body.translated_text: CANTO I
<s>Oṃ</s> — Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>.
CANTO I

children.text: gautamaḥ kapilo nāma muni dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ /
children.translated_text: There was a sage named <s>Kapila</s>, of the <s>Gautama</s> lineage, the best among upholders of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: babhūva tapasi śrāntaḥ kākṣīvān iva gautamaḥ // Saund_1.1 //
children.translated_text: who was devoted to austerity, like <s>Gautama Kākṣīvān</s>. (1.1)

children.text: aśiśriyad yaḥ satataṃ dīptaṃ kāśyapavat tapaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who constantly tended the blazing fire of <s>tapas</s> (austerity) like <s>Kaśyapa</s>,

children.text: āśiśrāya ca tadvṛddhau siddhim kāśyapavat parām // Saund_1.2 //
children.translated_text: and who, in its increase, attained the supreme <s>siddhi</s> (perfection) like <s>Kaśyapa</s>. (1.2)

children.text: haviḥṣu yaś ca svātmārthaṃ gām adhukṣad vasiṣṭhavat /
children.translated_text: He who, for the sake of his own spiritual goal, milked the cow into the oblation vessels like <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>,

children.text: tapaḥśiṣṭeṣu ca śiṣyeṣu gām adhukṣad vasiṣṭhavat /
children.translated_text: and who, among his disciples purified by austerity, milked the cow [of knowledge] like <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>;

children.text: māhātmyād dīrghatapaso yo dvitīya ivābhavat // Saund_1.3 //
children.translated_text: who, by the greatness of his long austerity, became as if a second [<s>Vasiṣṭha</s>]. (1.3)

body.text: tṛtīya iva yaś cābhūt kāyāṅgirasayor dhiyā // Saund_1.4 //
body.translated_text: And who became as if a third, by his wisdom, of <s>Kāya</s> and <s>Āṅgirasa</s>. (1.4)

children.text: tasya vistīrṇatapasaḥ pārśve himavataḥ śubhe /
children.translated_text: On the beautiful slope of the <s>Himavat</s> (Himālaya), that sage of vast austerity

children.text: kṣetraṃ cāyatanaṃ caiva tapasām āśramo 'bhavat // Saund_1.5 //
children.translated_text: had a hermitage (<s>āśrama</s>) that was both a field and a sanctuary of austerities. (1.5)

children.text: cāruvīruttaruvanaḥ prasnigdhamṛduśādvalaḥ /
children.translated_text: With lovely creepers, trees, and groves, with soft and smooth green grass,

children.text: havirdhūmavitānena yaḥ sadābhra ivābabhau // Saund_1.6 //
children.translated_text: it always appeared as if overcast by a canopy of smoke from oblations. (1.6)

children.text: mṛdubhiḥ saikataiḥ snigdhaiḥ kesarātarapāṇḍubhiḥ /
children.translated_text: With soft, smooth sandy stretches, pale as saffron pollen,

children.text: bhūmibhāgair asaṃkīrṇaiḥ sāṅgarāga ivābhavat // Saund_1.7 //
children.translated_text: it appeared, with its uncluttered patches of ground, as if adorned with cosmetic pigment. (1.7)

children.text: śucibhis tīrthasaṃkhyātaiḥ pāvanair bhāvanair api /
children.translated_text: With pure waters counted among sacred bathing places (<s>tīrthas</s>), purifying and inspiring,

children.text: bandhumān iva yas tasthau sarobhiḥ sasaraoruhaiḥ // Saund_1.8 //
children.translated_text: it stood as if surrounded by friends — with its lotus-bearing lakes. (1.8)

children.text: paryāptaphalapuṣpābhiḥ sarvato vanarājibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: With rows of forests on all sides, abundant in fruits and flowers,

children.text: śuśubhe vavṛdhe caiva naraḥ sādhanavān iva // Saund_1.9 //
children.translated_text: it shone and flourished, like a man endowed with resources. (1.9)

children.text: nīvāraphalasaṃtuṣṭaiḥ svasthaiḥ śāntair anutsukaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Though inhabited by ascetics contented with wild rice and fruits, healthy, peaceful, and free from longing,

children.text: akīrṇo 'pi tapobhṛdhibhiḥ śūnyaśūnya ivābhavat // Saund_1.10 //
children.translated_text: even when not crowded, it appeared as if empty and yet not empty. (1.10)

children.text: agnīnāṃ hūyamānānāṃ śikhinā kūjatām api /
children.translated_text: Of fires being offered into, of peacocks calling,

children.text: tīrthānāṃ cābhiṣekeṣu śuśruve yatra nisvanaḥ // Saund_1.11 //
children.translated_text: and of ablutions at the sacred fords — there the sound was heard. (1.11)

children.text: virejur hariṇā yatra suptā medhyāsu vediṣu /
children.translated_text: There, deer sleeping upon the pure sacrificial altars shone forth,

children.text: salājair mādhavīpuṣpair upahārāḥ kṛtā iva // Saund_1.12 //
children.translated_text: as if offerings had been made with parched grain and <s>mādhavī</s> flowers. (1.12)

children.text: api kṣudramṛgā yatra sāntāś ceruḥ samaṃ mṛgaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Even small animals there moved peacefully alongside the [wild] deer,

children.text: śarañyebhyas tapasvibhyo vinayaṅ śikṣitā iva // Saund_1.13 //
children.translated_text: as if they had learned gentleness from the ascetics who were their refuge. (1.13)

children.text: saṃdigdhe 'py apunarbhāve vidudhheṣv āgameṣv api /
children.translated_text: Even when the possibility of non-return [to existence] was doubtful and the scriptures were in dispute,

children.text: pratyakṣiṇa ivākurvaṃs tapo yatra tapodhanāḥ // Saund_1.14 //
children.translated_text: the ascetics rich in austerity there performed their <s>tapas</s> as if making it directly visible. (1.14)

children.text: yatra sma mīyate brahma kaiś cit kaiś cin na mīyate /
children.translated_text: There, by some, <s>Brahman</s> was ritually measured out, while by others it was not;

children.text: kāle nimīyate somo na cākāle pramīyate // Saund_1.15 //
children.translated_text: <s>Soma</s> was pressed at the proper time, and no creature was killed out of season. (1.15)

children.text: nirapekṣāḥ śarireṣu dharme yatra svabhuddhayaḥ /
children.translated_text: There, disregarding their bodies, with minds devoted to <s>dharma</s> of their own accord,

children.text: saṃhṛṣṭā iva yatnena tāpasās te pire tapaḥ // Saund_1.16
children.translated_text: the ascetics performed their austerities with effort, as if in joyful exertion. (1.16)

children.text: śrāmyanto munayo yatra svargāyodyuktacetasaḥ /
children.translated_text: There, the sages, toiling with minds intent on heaven,

children.text: taporāgeṇa dharmasya vilopam iva cakrire // Saund_1.17 //
children.translated_text: by their passion for austerity, seemed almost to violate <s>dharma</s> [itself]. (1.17)

children.text: atha tejavisadanaṃ tapaḥkṣetraṃ tam āśramam /
children.translated_text: Then, to that hermitage — that field of austerity, abode of radiant energy —

children.text: kecid ikṣvākavo jagmū rājaputrā vivatsavaḥ // Saund_1.18 //
children.translated_text: certain <s>Ikṣvāku</s> princes came, wishing to settle. (1.18)

children.text: suvarṇastambhavarṣmāṇaḥ siṃhoraskā mahābhujāḥ /
children.translated_text: With bodies like pillars of gold, lion-chested, great-armed,

children.text: pātraṃ śabdasya mahataḥ śriyāṃ ca vinayasya ca // Saund_1.19 //
children.translated_text: they were worthy of great fame, of splendor, and of discipline. (1.19)

children.text: arharūpā hy anarhasya mahātmānaś calātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Worthy in appearance yet [born] of an unworthy [brother], great-souled yet [related to one] of unsteady mind,

children.text: prājñāḥ prajñāvimuktasya bhrātṛyasya yavīyasaḥ // Saund_1.20 //
children.translated_text: wise yet [of the lineage of one] devoid of wisdom — [they were sons] of a younger brother. (1.20)

children.text: mātṛśulkād upagatāṃ te śriyaṃ na viṣehire /
children.translated_text: They could not endure the fortune that had come through the bride-price of their mother,

children.text: rarakṣuś ca pituḥ kautsās te bhavanti sma gautamāḥ // Saund_1.22 //
children.translated_text: and, protecting their father's [honor], the <s>Kautsas</s> became <s>Gautamas</s>. (1.22)

children.text: ekapitror yathā bhrātroḥ pṛthagguruparigrahāt /
children.translated_text: Just as two brothers born of the same father, through being under different preceptors,

children.text: rāma evābhavad gārgyo vāsubhadro 'pi gautamaḥ // Saund_1.23 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> became a <s>Gārgya</s> and <s>Vāsubhadra</s> became a <s>Gautama</s>. (1.23)

children.text: śākravṛkṣapraticchannaṃ vāsaṃ yasmāc ca cakrire /
children.translated_text: And because they settled under the shelter of the <s>Śākya</s> (teak) tree,

children.text: tasmād ikṣvākuvaṃśyās te bhuvi śākya iti smṛtāḥ // Saund_1.24 //
children.translated_text: therefore those descendants of <s>Ikṣvāku</s> are known on earth as <s>Śākyas</s>. (1.24)

children.text: sa teṣāṃ gautamaś cakre svavaṃśasadṛśīḥ kriyāḥ /
children.translated_text: That <s>Gautama</s> sage performed for them rites befitting their lineage,

children.text: munir ūrdhvaṃ kumārasya sagarasyeva bhārgavaḥ // Saund_1.25 //
children.translated_text: as the sage <s>Bhārgava</s> [did] for the young <s>Sagara</s> and after. (1.25)

children.text: kaṇvaḥ śākuntalasyeva bharatasya tarasviaḥ /
children.translated_text: Like <s>Kaṇva</s> for the impetuous <s>Bharata</s>, son of <s>Śakuntalā</s>,

children.text: vālmīkir iva dhīmāṃś ca dhīmator maithileyayoḥ // Saund_1.26 //
children.translated_text: and like the wise <s>Vālmīki</s> for the wise sons of <s>Maithilī</s>. (1.26)

children.text: tadvanaṃ muninā tena taiś ca kṣatriyapuṅgavaiḥ /
children.translated_text: That forest, with that sage and those bulls among <s>Kṣatriyas</s>,

children.text: śāntāṃ guptāṃ ca yugapad brahmakṣatraśriyaṃ dadhe // Saund_1.27 //
children.translated_text: simultaneously bore the serene and protected glory of both <s>Brahman</s> and <s>Kṣatra</s>. (1.27)

children.text: athodakalaśaṃ gṛhya teṣā vṛddhicikīrṣayā /
children.translated_text: Then, taking a water-pot, wishing for their prosperity,

children.text: muniḥ sa viyad utpatya tān uvāca nṛpātmajān // Saund_1.28 //
children.translated_text: the sage, rising into the sky, spoke to those princes. (1.28)

children.text: yā patet kalaśād asmād akṣayyasalilān mahīm /
children.translated_text: 'The stream that shall fall from this pot upon the earth of inexhaustible waters —

children.text: dhārā tām anatikramya mām anveta yathākramam // Saund_1.29 //
children.translated_text: follow me in proper order without crossing beyond it.' (1.29)

children.text: tataḥ paramam ity uktvā śirobhiḥ praṇipatya ca /
children.translated_text: Then, saying 'Very well,' and bowing with their heads,

children.text: rathān āruruhuḥ sarve śīghravāhān alaṅkrṛtān // Saund_1.30 //
children.translated_text: they all mounted their swiftly-drawn, decorated chariots. (1.30)

children.text: tataḥ sa tair anugataḥ syandanasthair nabhogataḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, followed by them standing in their chariots, he, moving through the sky,

children.text: tadāśramamahīprāntaṃ paricikṣepa vāriṇā // Saund_1.31 //
children.translated_text: encircled the boundary of that hermitage-land with water. (1.31)

children.text: aṣṭāpadam ivālikhya nimittaiḥ surbhīkṛtam /
children.translated_text: Having traced out [the ground] like a chessboard, consecrated with auspicious signs,

children.text: tān uvāca muniḥ sthitvā bhūmipālasutān idam // Saund_1.32 //
children.translated_text: the sage, standing still, spoke this to the sons of the king: (1.32)

children.text: asmin dhārāparikṣipte nemicihnitalakṣaṇe /
children.translated_text: 'Within this [boundary] encircled by the stream, marked by the wheel-track,

children.text: nirmimīdhvaṃ puraṃ yūyaṃ mayi yāte triviṣṭapam // Saund_1.33 //
children.translated_text: build a city, when I have departed to heaven.' (1.33)

children.text: tataḥ kadācit te vīrās tasmin pratigate munau /
children.translated_text: Then, in time, when that sage had departed, those heroes,

children.text: babhramur yauvanoddāmā gajā iva niraṅkuśāḥ // Saund_1.34 //
children.translated_text: wild with youth, roamed about like elephants without a goad. (1.34)

children.text: baddhagodhāṅgulītrāṇā hastaviṣṭhitakārmukāḥ /
children.translated_text: With leather guards fastened on their fingers, bows held in their hands,

children.text: śarādhmātamahātūṇā vyāyatābaddhavāsasaḥ // Saund_1.35 //
children.translated_text: with great quivers swollen with arrows, wearing garments drawn tight. (1.35)

children.text: jijñāsamānā nāgeṣu kauśalaṃ śvāpadeṣu ca /
children.translated_text: Seeking to test their skill against elephants and wild beasts,

children.text: anucakrur vanasthasya dauṣmanter devakramaṇaḥ // Saund_1.36 //
children.translated_text: they imitated the divine exploits of <s>Dauṣmanti</s> [<s>Bharata</s>] who dwelt in the forest. (1.36)

children.text: tān dṛṣṭvā prakṛtiṃ yātān vṛddhān vyāghraśiśūn iva /
children.translated_text: Seeing them reverted to their natural [warlike] state, like tiger cubs grown old,

children.text: tāpasās tadvanarh hitvā himavantarh siṣevire // Saund_1.37 //
children.translated_text: the ascetics abandoned that forest and resorted to the <s>Himavat</s>. (1.37)

children.text: tatas tadāśramasthānaṃ śūnyarh taiḥ śūnyacetasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, seeing that hermitage-site left empty by them, those of empty hearts,

children.text: paśyanto tadāśramasthānarṃ śūnyaṃ taiḥ niśaśvasuḥ // Saund_1.38 //
children.translated_text: seeing that hermitage-site empty of them, sighed deeply. (1.38)

children.text: atha te puṇyakarmāṇaḥ pratyupasthiravṛddhayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, those of meritorious deeds, their growth having come to fruition,

children.text: tatra tajjñair upākhyātān avāpur mahato nidhīn // Saund_1.39 //
children.translated_text: discovered there great treasures, pointed out by those who knew. (1.39)

children.text: alaṃ dharmārthakāmānāṃ nikhilānām svāptaye /
children.translated_text: Sufficient for the complete attainment of <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s> (wealth), and <s>kāma</s> (pleasure),

children.text: nidhayo naikavidhayo bhūrayas te gatārayaḥ // Saund_1.40 //
children.translated_text: those treasures were of many kinds, abundant, and their enemies were vanquished. (1.40)

children.text: tatas tatpratilambhāc ca pariṇāmāc ca karmaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, from obtaining those [treasures] and from the ripening of their merit,

children.text: tasmin vāstuni vāstujñāḥ puraṃ śrīman nyaveśayan // Saund_1.41 //
children.translated_text: experts in architecture established a splendid city on that site. (1.41)

children.text: saridvistīrṇaparikhaṃ spaṣṭāñcitamahāpatham /
children.translated_text: With a moat as wide as a river, with broad and well-decorated highways,

children.text: śailakalpamahāvapraṃ givirajam ivāparam // Saund_1.42 //
children.translated_text: with great ramparts massive as mountains — like another <s>Girivaja</s> (Rājagṛha). (1.42)

children.text: pāṇḍurāṭṭālasumukhaṃ suvibhaktāntarāpaṇam /
children.translated_text: With bright white watchtowers as its face, with well-arranged inner marketplaces,

children.text: harmyamālāparikṣiptaṃ kukṣiṃ himagirer iva // Saund_1.43 //
children.translated_text: encircled by rows of mansions — like the lap of the snow-mountain. (1.43)

children.text: vedavedāṅgaviduṣas tasthuṣaḥ ṣaṭsu karmasu /
children.translated_text: Brahmins learned in the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Vedāṅgas</s>, established in the six ritual duties,

children.text: śāntaye vṛddhaye caiva yatra viprān ajītjapan // Saund_1.44 //
children.translated_text: they had installed there for the sake of peace and prosperity. (1.44)

children.text: tadbhūmer abhiyoktṝṇāṃ prayuktān vinivṛttaye /
children.translated_text: To repel aggressors upon that land,

children.text: yatra svena prabhāvena bhṛtyadaṇḍān ajītjapan // Saund_1.45 //
children.translated_text: they maintained, by their own authority, troops of servants there. (1.45)

children.text: cāritradhansaṃpannān salajjān dīrghadarśinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Endowed with virtuous conduct and wealth, modest, and far-sighted,

children.text: arhato 'tiṣṭhipan yatra śūrān dakṣān kuṭumbinaḥ // Saund_1.46 //
children.translated_text: they appointed worthy men there — brave, capable householders. (1.46)

children.text: vyastais tais tair guñair yuktān mativāgvikramādibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Endowed severally with various qualities — intellect, eloquence, valor, and the like —

children.text: karmasu patirūpeṣu saicāṃs tān nyayūyujan // Saund_1.47 //
children.translated_text: they employed those capable men in tasks befitting them. (1.47)

children.text: vasumadbhir avibhrāntair alaṃvidyair avismitaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Filled with men who were wealthy yet unconfused, learned yet not arrogant,

children.text: yad babhāse naraiḥ kīrṇaṃ mandaraḥ kinnarair iva // Saund_1.48 //
children.translated_text: it shone like <s>Mandara</s> [mountain] thronged with <s>Kinnaras</s>. (1.48)

children.text: yatra te hṛṣṭamanasaḥ pauraprītickīrṣayā /
children.translated_text: There, with joyful hearts and desiring to please the citizens,

children.text: śrīmanty udyānasaṃjñāni yaśodhāmāny acīkaran // Saund_1.49 //
children.translated_text: they created glorious places known as gardens — abodes of renown. (1.49)

children.text: śvāḥ puṣkariṇīś caiva paramāgryaguṇāmbhasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Lakes and ponds too, with waters of the finest quality,

children.text: nājñāyā cetanotkarṣād dikṣu sarvāsv acīkhanan // Saund_1.50 //
children.translated_text: they dug in all directions, not by command but from the elevation of their own minds. (1.50)

children.text: manojñāḥ śrīmatiḥ praśṭhīḥ pathiṣūpavaneṣu ca /
children.translated_text: Delightful and glorious rest-houses along the roads and in the parks,

children.text: sabhāḥ kūpavatīś caiva samantāt pratyatiṣṭhipan // Saund_1.51 //
children.translated_text: and assembly-halls with wells — they established on all sides. (1.51)

children.text: hastyaśvarathasakīrṇam asaṃkīrṇam anākulam /
children.translated_text: Teeming with elephants, horses, and chariots, yet uncluttered and undisturbed,

children.text: anigūḍhārthivibhavaṃ nigūḍhajñānapauruṣam // Saund_1.52 //
children.translated_text: with wealth of petitioners unconcealed, yet with knowledge and valor concealed. (1.52)

children.text: saṃnidhānam ivārthānām ādhānam iva tejasām /
children.translated_text: It was as if a repository of riches, a storehouse of radiance,

children.text: niketam iva vidyānāṃ saṃketam iva saṃpadām // Saund_1.53 //
children.translated_text: a dwelling-place of learning, a rendezvous of prosperity. (1.53)

children.text: vāsavṛkṣaṃ guṇavatām āśrayaṃ śaraṇaiṣiām /
children.translated_text: A wishing-tree for the virtuous, a refuge for those seeking shelter,

children.text: ānartaṃ kṛtaśāstrāṇām ālānaṃ bābhuśālinām // Saund_1.54 //
children.translated_text: a stage for the learned, a tethering-post for the mighty. (1.54)

children.text: samājair utsavair dāyaiḥ kriyāvidhibhir eva ca /
children.translated_text: With assemblies, festivals, charitable gifts, and ritual observances,

children.text: alañcakrur alaṃvīryās te jagaddhāma tatpuram // Saund_1.55 //
children.translated_text: those heroes of sufficient valor adorned that city — a glory of the world. (1.55)

children.text: yasmād anyāyatas te ca kaṃ cin nācīkaran karam /
children.translated_text: And because they never levied any unjust tax,

children.text: tasmād alpena kālena tat tadāpūpuran puram // Saund_1.56 //
children.translated_text: therefore, in a short time, they filled that city. (1.56)

children.text: kapilasya ca tasyarṣes tasminn āśramavāstuni /
children.translated_text: And because of the sage <s>Kapila</s>, on that hermitage-site,

children.text: yasmāt te tatpuraṃ cakrus tasmāt kapilavāstu tat // Saund_1.57 //
children.translated_text: since they built that city, it was [called] <s>Kapilavastu</s>. (1.57)

children.text: kakandasya makandasya kuśāmbasyeva cāśrame /
children.translated_text: Just as, in the hermitages of <s>Kakanda</s>, <s>Makanda</s>, and <s>Kuśāmba</s>,

children.text: puryo yathā hi śrūyante tathaiva kapilasya tat // Saund_1.58 //
children.translated_text: cities are traditionally known, so too was [the city] of <s>Kapila</s>. (1.58)

children.text: āpuḥ puraṃ tatpuruhūtakalpās te tejasāryeṇa na vismayena /
children.translated_text: Those who rivaled <s>Indra</s> attained the city through splendor and noble conduct, not through pride,

children.text: āpur yaśogandham ataś ca śaśvat sutā yayāter iva kīrtimantaḥ // Saund_1.59 //
children.translated_text: and from that they won enduring fame, like the renowned sons of <s>Yayāti</s>. (1.59)

children.text: tannāthavṛttair api rājaputrair arājakaṃ naiva rarāja rāṣṭram /
children.translated_text: Even with those princes conducting themselves as lords, the kingdom without a [single] king did not shine,

children.text: tārāsahasrair api dīpyamānair anutthite candra ivāntarīkṣam // Saund_1.60 //
children.translated_text: like the sky without the moon risen, even when blazing with thousands of stars. (1.60)

children.text: yo jyāyān atha vayasā guṇaiś ca teṣāṃ bhrātṝṇāṃ vṛṣabha ivaujasā vṛṣāṇām /
children.translated_text: He who was eldest among those brothers in age and virtues, a bull in might like a bull among bulls —

children.text: te tatra priyaguruvas tam abhyaṣiñcann ādityā daśaśatalocanaṃ divīva // Saund_1.61 //
children.translated_text: there they, devoted to their elders, consecrated him, as the <s>Ādityas</s> [consecrated] the thousand-eyed [<s>Indra</s>] in heaven. (1.61)

children.text: ācāravān vinayavān nayavān kriyāvān dharmāya nendriyadukhāya dhṛtātparaḥ /
children.translated_text: Possessed of good conduct, discipline, statecraft, and ritual action; devoted to <s>dharma</s>, not to the pleasure of the senses, with steadfast resolve —

children.text: tadbhrātṛbhiḥ parivṛtaḥ sa jugopa rāṣṭraṃ saṃkrandano divam ivānuṣrto marudbhiḥ // Saund_1.62 //
children.translated_text: surrounded by his brothers, he governed the kingdom, as <s>Saṃkrandana</s> [<s>Indra</s>] governs heaven, attended by the <s>Maruts</s>. (1.62)

body.text: Saundaranada mahākāvye kapilavāstuvarṇano nāma prathamaḥ sargaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the first canto, entitled 'The Description of <s>Kapilavastu</s>,' in the <s>Saundarananda</s> <s>mahākāvya</s>.
CANTO II

children.text: tataḥ kadā cit kālena tad avāpa kulakramāt /
children.translated_text: Then, in the course of time, by hereditary succession, that [kingdom] was obtained by

children.text: rāja śuddhodhano nāma śuddhakarmā jitendriyaḥ // Saund_2.1 //
children.translated_text: a king named <s>Śuddhodana</s>, of pure deeds and conquered senses. (2.1)

children.text: yaḥ sasañje na kāmeṣu śrīpāptau na visismiye /
children.translated_text: He who did not cling to pleasures, did not grow arrogant at the attainment of royal fortune,

children.text: nāvamene parānṛddhyā parebhyo nāpi vivyathe // Saund_2.2 //
children.translated_text: did not look down upon others for their prosperity, nor did he tremble before others. (2.2)

children.text: balīyān sattvasaṃpannaḥ śrutavān buddhimān api /
children.translated_text: Strong, endowed with <s>sattva</s> (courage), learned, intelligent,

children.text: vikrānto nayvāṃś caiva dhīraḥ sumukha eva ca // Saund_2.3 //
children.translated_text: valorous, statesmanlike, steadfast, and gracious of countenance. (2.3)

children.text: vapuṣmāṃś ca na ca stabdho dakṣiṇo na ca nārajavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Handsome yet not haughty, courteous yet not slow,

children.text: tejasvī na ca na kṣāntaḥ kartā ca na ca vismitaḥ // Saund_2.4 //
children.translated_text: brilliant yet not lacking in patience, a man of action yet not boastful. (2.4)

children.text: ākṣiptaḥ śatrubhiḥ saṃkhye suhṛdbhiś ca vyapāśritaḥ /
children.translated_text: Assailed by enemies in battle and relied upon by friends,

children.text: abhavad yo na vimukhas tejasā ditsayaiva ca // Saund_2.5 //
children.translated_text: he was one who never turned away — by his splendor and his very generosity. (2.5)

children.text: yaḥ pūrvai rājabhir yātāṃ yiyāsur dharmapaddhatim /
children.translated_text: He who, wishing to follow the path of <s>dharma</s> trodden by former kings,

children.text: rājyaṃ dīkṣām iva vahan vṛttetānvagamat pitṝn // Saund_2.6 //
children.translated_text: bearing the kingdom as if it were a religious consecration (<s>dīkṣā</s>), followed his ancestors in conduct. (2.6)

children.text: yasya suvyahārāc ca rakṣanāc ca sukhaṃ prajāḥ /
children.translated_text: Through his good governance and protection, the subjects

children.text: śiśyire vigatodvegāḥ pitur aṅkagatā iva // Saund_2.7 //
children.translated_text: slept free from anxiety, as if on their father's lap. (2.7)

children.text: kṛtaśāstraḥ kṛtāstro vā jāto vā vipule kule /
children.translated_text: Whether learned in the sciences or skilled in arms, or born in a noble family,

children.text: akṛtārtho na dadṛśe yasya darśanameyivān // Saund_2.8 //
children.translated_text: no one who came into his presence was seen to remain without having his purpose fulfilled. (2.8)

children.text: hitaṃ vipriyam apy ukto yaḥ śuśrāva na cukṣubhe /
children.translated_text: He who, even when told something beneficial but unpleasant, listened and was not disturbed,

children.text: duṣkṛtaṃ bahv api tyaktvā sasmāra kṛtam aṇv api // Saund_2.9 //
children.translated_text: and who, abandoning even many misdeeds, remembered even a small kindness. (2.9)

children.text: praṇatān anujagrāha vijagrāha kuladviṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: He showed grace to the submissive, seized the enemies of his family,

children.text: āpannān parijagrāha nijagrāhāsthitān pathi // Saund_2.10 //
children.translated_text: rescued the distressed, and restrained those straying from the path. (2.10)

children.text: prāyeṇa viṣaye yasya tacchīlam anuvartinaḥ /
children.translated_text: In his realm, for the most part, [people] followed his character;

children.text: arjayanto dadṛśire dhanānīva guṇān api // Saund_2.11 //
children.translated_text: they were seen earning virtues just as [they earned] wealth.

children.text: adhyaiṣṭa yaḥ paraṃ brahma na vyaiṣṭa satataṃ dhṛteḥ /
children.translated_text: He who studied the supreme <s>Brahman</s> never wavered from steadfastness;

children.text: dānān yadita pātrebhyaḥ pāpaṃ nākṛta kiṃ cana // Saund_2.12 //
children.translated_text: he gave gifts to worthy recipients and committed no sin whatsoever.

children.text: dhṛtyāvākṣīt pratijñāṃ sa sadvājivodyatāṃ dhuram /
children.translated_text: With fortitude he upheld his vow, like a fine horse that has taken up the yoke;

children.text: na hy avānchīc eyutaḥ satyān muhūrtam api jīvitam // Saund_2.13 //
children.translated_text: for he did not desire life even for a moment apart from truth.

children.text: viduṣaḥ paryupāsiṣṭa vyakāśiṣṭātmavattayā /
children.translated_text: He attended upon the learned; he shone forth through self-mastery;

children.text: vyarociṣta ca śiṣṭebhyo māsīṣe candramā iva // Saund_2.14 //
children.translated_text: and he glowed brighter than the virtuous, like the moon [at its fullest].

children.text: avedīd buddhiśāstrābhyām iha cāmutra ca kṣamam /
children.translated_text: He discerned, through wisdom and the sciences, what was fitting in this world and the next;

children.text: arakṣīd dhairyavīryābhyām indriyāṇy api ca prajāḥ // Saund_2.15 //
children.translated_text: he guarded, through steadfastness and valor, both his senses and his subjects.

children.text: ahārṣīd duḥkham ārtānāṃ dviṣatāṃ corjitaṃ yaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: He removed the suffering of the afflicted and the swelling fame of enemies;

children.text: acaiṣte ca nayair bhūmiṃ bhūyasā yaśasaiva ca // Saund_2.16 //
children.translated_text: and he sought the earth through statesmanship and, even more, through glory alone.

children.text: apy āsīd duḥkhitān paśyan prakṛtyā karuṇātmakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Compassionate by nature even upon seeing the afflicted,

children.text: nāhauṣte ca yaśo lobhād anyāyādhigatair dhanaiḥ // Saund_2.17 //
children.translated_text: he did not covet glory through wealth acquired by unjust means.

children.text: sauhārdaṛḍhabhaktitvān maitreṣu viguṇeṣv api /
children.translated_text: Because of the firmness of his affection and devotion, [he did not abandon] even friends who had faults;

children.text: nādidāsīdaditsīt tu saumukhvāt svaṃ svam arthavat // Saund_2.18 //
children.translated_text: and with a gracious countenance, he wished to give away his own [possessions], each being of value.

children.text: anivedyāgram arhadbhyo nālikṣat hiṃ cid aplutaḥ /
children.translated_text: Without first offering the best portion to the worthy, he did not taste anything, [being] unwavering;

children.text: gām adharmeṇa nādhukṣat kṣīratarṣeṇa gām iva // Saund_2.19 //
children.translated_text: he did not milk the earth through unrighteousness, as one [might milk] a cow out of thirst for milk.

children.text: nāsṛkṣad balim aprāptaṃ nārukṣan mānam aiśvaram /
children.translated_text: He did not neglect the [proper] tribute, nor did he ascend to imperial pride;

children.text: āgamair buddhim āhikṣad dharmāya na tu kīrtaye // Saund_2.20 //
children.translated_text: he sharpened his intellect with the scriptures for the sake of <s>dharma</s>, not for fame.

children.text: kleśārhān api kāṃś ci tu nākliṣṭa kliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even those who deserved punishment for sinful deeds, he did not torment;

children.text: āryabhāvāc ca nāghukṣad dviṣato 'pi sato guṇān // Saund_2.21 //
children.translated_text: and out of noble nature, he did not belittle even the virtues of enemies.

children.text: ākṛṣad vapuṣā dṛṣṭīḥ prajānāṃ candramā iva /
children.translated_text: He attracted the gazes of his people with his beauty, like the moon;

children.text: parasvaṃ bhuvi nāmṛkṣan mahāviṣam ivoragam // Saund_2.22 //
children.translated_text: he did not touch another's property on earth, as [one would not touch] a great serpent's venom.

children.text: nākrukṣad viṣaye tasya kaś cit kaiś cit kva cit kṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: No one in his realm, harmed by anyone anywhere, cried out;

children.text: adikṣat tasya hastastham ārtebhyo hy abhayaṃ dhanuḥ // Saund_2.23 //
children.translated_text: for his bow, held in hand, bestowed fearlessness upon the distressed.

children.text: kṛtāgaso 'pi praṇatān prāg eva priyakāriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even those who had committed offenses, if they bowed — how much more those who had done pleasing deeds —

children.text: adarśat snighayā dṛṣṭyā ślakṣṇena vacasāsicat // Saund_2.24 //
children.translated_text: he regarded with an affectionate gaze and sprinkled [them] with gentle words.

children.text: bahvīr adhyagamad vidyā viṣayeṣv akutūhalaḥ /
children.translated_text: He mastered many sciences, [yet remained] without curiosity about sense pleasures;

children.text: adarśat kārtayuge dharme dharmāt kṛcchre 'pi nāsrasat // Saund_2.25 //
children.translated_text: he beheld <s>dharma</s> as in the <s>Kṛtayuga</s> (Golden Age), and did not slip from <s>dharma</s> even in adversity.

children.text: avardhiṣṭa guñaiḥ śaśvad avṛdhan mitrasaṃpadā /
children.translated_text: He grew constantly through virtues and increased in the wealth of friends;

children.text: avartiṣṭa ca vṛddheṣu nāvṛtad garhite pathi // Saund_2.26 //
children.translated_text: he moved among the elders and did not turn onto a blameworthy path.

children.text: śarair aśīśam acchatrūn guṇair bandhūn arīramat /
children.translated_text: With arrows he cut down enemies; with virtues he delighted kinsmen;

children.text: randhrair nācūcudad bhṛtyān karair nāpīpiḍat prajāḥ // Saund_2.27 //
children.translated_text: through weaknesses he did not provoke servants; with taxes he did not oppress his subjects.

children.text: rakṣaṇāc caiva śauryāc ca nikhilāṃ gām avīvapat /
children.translated_text: Through both protection and valor, he governed the entire earth;

children.text: spaṣṭayā daṇḍanītyā ca rātrisattrān avīvapat // Saund_2.28 //
children.translated_text: and through a clear policy of punishment, he dispelled nocturnal crimes.

children.text: kulaṃ rājarṣivṛttena yaśogandham avīvapat /
children.translated_text: Through conduct befitting a royal sage, he perfumed his dynasty with the fragrance of glory;

children.text: dīptyā tama ivādityas tejasārīn avīvapat // Saund_2.29 //
children.translated_text: like the sun [dispelling] darkness with its radiance, he outshone enemies with his splendor.

children.text: apaprathat pitṝṃś caiva satputradaṛśair guṇaiḥ /
children.translated_text: He gladdened his ancestors too through virtues worthy of a true son;

children.text: salileneva cāmbhodo vṛttenājihṇadat prajāḥ // Saund_2.30 //
children.translated_text: and like a rain cloud with water, he refreshed his subjects through [his righteous] conduct.

children.text: dānair ajasravipulaiḥ somaṃ viprān asūṣavat /
children.translated_text: Through gifts — ceaseless and abundant — he caused the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> to press the <s>Soma</s>;

children.text: rājadharmasthiatvāc ca kāle sasyam asūṣavat // Saund_2.31 //
children.translated_text: and through steadfastness in the duties of a king, he caused the crops to ripen in due season.

children.text: adharmiṣṭhām acakathan na kathām akathaṅkataḥ /
children.translated_text: Free from doubt, he did not speak an unrighteous word;

children.text: cakravartīva ca parān dharmāyābhyudasīṣahat // Saund_2.32 //
children.translated_text: and like a universal sovereign, he impelled others toward <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: rāṣṭram anyatra ca baler na sa kiṅ cid dadīdapat /

children.text: bhṛtyair eva ca sodyogaṃ dviṣaddarpam adīdapat // Saund_2.33 /
children.translated_text: and through his servants alone, with diligence, he crushed the pride of enemies.

children.text: svair evādīdapac cāpi bhūyo bhūyo guṇaiḥ kulam /
children.translated_text: Again and again he set his dynasty ablaze with his own virtues;

children.text: prajā nādīdapac caiva sarvadharmavyavasthayā // Saund_2.34 //
children.translated_text: and he did not oppress his subjects, [maintaining] the establishment of all [forms of] <s>dharma</s>.

body.translated_text: He did not steal anything in his realm except the share [owed as] tribute;

children.text: aśrāntaḥ samaye yajvā vajñabhūmim amīmapat /
children.translated_text: Unwearied, offering sacrifices at the proper times, he swept the sacrificial ground;

children.text: pālanāc ca cvijān brahma nirduvignān amīmapat // Saund_2.35 //
children.translated_text: and through protection, he enabled the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> to study <s>Brahman</s> free from danger.

children.text: gurubhir vidhivatkāle saumyaḥ somam amīmapat /
children.translated_text: Gentle, at the proper time, in the manner prescribed by his elders, he pressed the <s>Soma</s>;

children.text: tapasā tejasā caiva dviṣatsainyam amīmapat // Saund_2.36 //
children.translated_text: and through austerity and splendor, he crushed the armies of enemies.

children.text: prajāḥ paramadharmjñaḥ sūkṣmaṃ dharmam avīvasat /
children.translated_text: Knowing the supreme <s>dharma</s>, he taught his subjects the subtle <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: darśanāc caiva dharmasya kāle svargam avīvasat // Saund_2.37 //
children.translated_text: and through the vision of <s>dharma</s>, in due time he led [them] to heaven.

children.text: vyaktam apy arthakṛcchreṣu nādharmiṣṭham atiṣṭhipat /
children.translated_text: Even when clearly [facing] difficulties regarding wealth, he did not establish anything unrighteous;

children.text: priya ity eva cāśaktaṃ na saṃrāgād avīvṛdhat // Saund_2.38 //
children.translated_text: and merely because [someone was] dear, he did not promote an incompetent one out of partiality.

children.text: tejasā ca tviṣā caiva ripūn dṛptān abhībhasat /
children.translated_text: With his splendor and radiance, he overpowered proud enemies;

children.text: yaśodīpena dīptena pṛthivīṃ ca vyabhībhasat // Saund_2.39 //
children.translated_text: and with the blazing lamp of glory, he illuminated the earth.

children.text: ānṛśaṃsyān na yaśase tenādāyi sadārthine /
children.translated_text: Out of compassion, not for the sake of fame, he gave to those in perpetual need;

children.text: dravyaṃ mahad api tyaktvā na caivākīrti kiṃ cana // Saund_2.40 //
children.translated_text: and even having renounced great wealth, he did not proclaim anything [about it].

children.text: tenārir āpi duḥkhārto nātyāji śaraṇāgataḥ /
children.translated_text: By him, even an enemy afflicted with suffering was not turned away if he came seeking refuge;

children.text: jitvā dṛptān api ripūn na tenākāri vismayaḥ // Saund_2.41 //
children.translated_text: and having conquered even proud enemies, he did not indulge in arrogance.

children.text: na tenābhedi māryādā kāmād dveṣād bhayād api /
children.translated_text: He did not transgress boundaries out of desire, hatred, or fear;

children.text: tena satsv api bhogeṣu nāsevīndriyavṛttitā // Saund_2.42 //
children.translated_text: even though pleasures were available to him, he did not surrender to the ways of the senses.

children.text: na tenārdarśi viṣamaṃ kāryaṅ kva cana kiṃ cana /
children.translated_text: He never handled any matter anywhere in an improper way;

children.text: vipriyapriyayoḥ kṛtye na tenāgāmi nikriyāḥ // Saund_2.43 //
children.translated_text: in matters both unpleasant and pleasant, he did not resort to inaction.

children.text: tenāpāyi yathākalpaṃ somaś ca yaśa eva ca /
children.translated_text: He drank the <s>Soma</s> as prescribed and [won] glory as well;

children.text: vedaś cāmnāyi satataṃ vedokto dharma eva ca // Saund_2.44 //
children.translated_text: and he constantly recited the <s>Vedas</s> and [practiced] the very <s>dharma</s> taught in the <s>Vedas</s>.

children.text: evamādibhir atyakto babhūvāsulabhair guṇaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Endowed with such and other virtues, difficult to attain,

children.text: aśakyaśakyasāmantaḥ śākyarājaḥ sa śakravat // Saund_2.45 //
children.translated_text: that <s>Śākya</s> king, whose neighboring kings were both the [truly] powerful and the [merely] claiming power, was like <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) himself.

children.text: atha tasmin tathā kāle dharmakāmā divaukasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, at that time, the celestials, desirous of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: vicerur diśi lokasya dharmacaryā didṛkṣavaḥ // Saund_2.46 //
children.translated_text: roamed through the directions of the world, wishing to see the practice of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: dharmātmānaś carantas te dharmajijñāsayā jagat /
children.translated_text: Those righteous beings, wandering through the world in search of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: dadṛśus taṃ viśeṣeṇa dharmātmānaṃ narādhipam // Saund_2.47 //
children.translated_text: beheld especially that righteous king of men.

children.text: devebhyas tuṣitebhyo 'tha bodhisattvaḥ kṣitiṃ vrajan /
children.translated_text: Then, from the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, descending to the earth,

children.text: upapattiṃ praṇidadhe kule tasya mahīpateḥ // Saund_2.48 //
children.translated_text: resolved upon [his] birth in the family of that sovereign.

children.text: tasya devī nṛdevasya māyā nāma tadābhavat /
children.translated_text: The queen of that godlike king was then named <s>Māyā</s> —

children.text: vītakrodhatamomāyā māyeva divi devatā // Saund_2.49 //
children.translated_text: free from anger, darkness, and guile, like a divine <s>Māyā</s> in heaven.

children.text: svapne 'tha samaye garbham āviśantaṃ dadarśa sā /
children.translated_text: Then in a dream, at the [auspicious] time, she beheld entering her womb

children.text: ṣaḍdantaṃ vāraṇaṃ śvetam airāvatam ivaujasā // Saund_2.50 //
children.translated_text: a white elephant with six tusks, mighty as <s>Airāvata</s>.

children.text: taṃ vinirdidiṣuḥ śrutvā svapnaṃ svapnavido dvijāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard that dream, the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> skilled in interpreting dreams

children.text: tasya janma kumārasya lakṣmīdharmayaśobhṛtaḥ // Saund_2.51 //
children.translated_text: predicted the birth of a prince endowed with fortune, <s>dharma</s>, and fame.

children.text: tasya sattvaviśeṣasya jātau jātikṣayaiṣinaḥ /
children.translated_text: At the birth of that extraordinary being, who sought the destruction of [re]birth,

children.text: sācalā pracacālorvī taraṅgābhihateva nauḥ // Saund_2.52 //
children.translated_text: the earth with its mountains trembled, like a boat struck by waves.

children.text: sūryaraśmibhir akliṣṭaṃ puṣpavarṣaṃ papāta khāt /
children.translated_text: A rain of flowers, not burned by the rays of the sun, fell from the sky,

children.text: digvāraṇakarādhūtād vanāc caitrarathād iva // Saund_2.53 //
children.translated_text: as if from the <s>Caitraratha</s> garden shaken by the trunks of the guardian elephants of the directions.

children.text: divi dundubhayo nedur dīvyatāṃ marutām iva /
children.translated_text: Celestial drums resounded in the sky, as if the <s>Maruts</s> (storm gods) were sporting;

children.text: didīpe 'bhyadhiaṃ sūryaḥ śivaś ca pavano vavau // Saund_2.54 //
children.translated_text: the sun shone with surpassing brilliance, and a gentle, auspicious wind blew.

children.text: tutuṣus tuṣitāś caiva śuddhāvāsāś ca devatāḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Tuṣita</s> gods rejoiced, and the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (Pure Abode) deities too,

children.text: saddharmabahumānena sattvānāṃ cānukampayā // Saund_2.55 //
children.translated_text: out of great reverence for the true <s>dharma</s> and out of compassion for beings.

children.text: samāyayau yaśaḥketuṃ śreyaḥketukaraḥ paraḥ /
children.translated_text: The supreme one, who was to be the banner of welfare, came to the banner of glory;

children.text: babhrāje śāntayā lakṣmyā dharmo vigrahavān iva // Saund_2.56 //
children.translated_text: he shone with tranquil splendor, as if <s>Dharma</s> itself had taken bodily form.

children.text: devyām api yavīyasyām araṇyām iva pāvakaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the younger queen too, like fire in the fire-stick,

children.text: nando nāma suto jajñe nityānandakaraḥ kule // Saund_2.57 //
children.translated_text: a son named <s>Nanda</s> was born, a source of eternal joy to the family.

children.text: dīrghabāhur mahāvakṣāḥ siṃhāṃso vṛsabhekṣanaḥ /
children.translated_text: With long arms, a great chest, shoulders like a lion, and eyes like a bull,

children.text: vapuṣāgryeṇa yo nāma sundaropapadaṃ dadhe // Saund_2.58 //
children.translated_text: he bore the name '<s>Sundara</s>' (Handsome), befitting his supreme bodily form.

children.text: madhumāsa iva prāptaś candro naa ivoditaḥ /
children.translated_text: Like the arrival of the month of spring, like the rising of the [full] moon,

children.text: aṅgavān iva cānaṅgaḥ sa babhau kāntayā śriyā // Saund_2.59 //
children.translated_text: like <s>Anaṅga</s> (the bodiless Love-god) endowed with limbs — he shone with lovely splendor.

children.text: sa tau saṃvardhayāmāsa narendraḥ parayā mudā /
children.translated_text: The king raised them both with supreme delight,

children.text: arthaḥ sajjanahastastho dharmakāmau mahān iva // Saund_2.60 //
children.translated_text: like a great treasure in the hands of a virtuous person [that fosters] both <s>dharma</s> and <s>kāma</s>.

children.text: tasya kālena satputrau vavṛdhāte bhavāya tau /
children.translated_text: In time, those two true sons grew for the good [of the world],

children.text: āryasyārambhamahato darmārthāv iva bhūtaye // Saund_2.61 //
children.translated_text: like <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s> (righteousness and prosperity) for the welfare of a noble one who has commenced a great undertaking.

children.text: tayoḥ satputrayor madhye śākyarājo rarāja saḥ /
children.translated_text: Between those two true sons, that <s>Śākya</s> king shone resplendent,

children.text: madhyadeśa iva vyakto himavatpāripātrayoḥ // Saund_2.62 //
children.translated_text: like the clearly visible central region (<s>Madhyadeśa</s>) between the <s>Himavat</s> and <s>Pāripātra</s> [mountains].

children.text: tatas tayoḥ saṃskṛtayoḥ krameṇa narendrasūnvoḥ kṛtavidyayoś ca /
children.translated_text: Then, as those two sons of the king were duly consecrated and became learned,

children.text: kāmeṣv ajasraṅ pramamāda nandaḥ sarvārthasiddhas tu na saṃrarañja // Saund_2.63 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s> indulged ceaselessly in pleasures, while <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> (the Buddha-to-be) took no delight [in them].

children.text: sa prekśyaiva hi jīrṇam āturaṅ ca mṛtaṅ ca vimṛśan jagadanbhijñam ārtacittaḥ /
children.translated_text: For upon seeing an old man, a sick man, and a dead man, and reflecting on the world ensnared [in delusion], with a troubled heart,

children.text: hṛdayagataparaghṛṇo na viṣayaratim agamaj jananamaraṇabhayam abhito vijighāṃsuḥ // Saund_2.64 //
children.translated_text: with compassion arisen in his heart, he did not experience delight in sense pleasures, wishing everywhere to overcome the fear of birth and death.

children.text: udvegād apunarbhave manaḥ praṇidhāya sa yayau śayitavarāṅganādanāsthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having fixed his mind, out of revulsion, upon non-return [to rebirth], indifferent to the bed-chamber of beautiful women,

children.text: niśi nṛpatinilayanād vanagamankṛtmanāḥ sarasa iva mathitanalināt kalahaṃsaḥ // Saund_2.65 //
children.translated_text: he departed from the king's palace at night, his mind set on the forest, like a wild goose from a lake whose lotuses have been churned.

body.text: Saundaranande mahākāvye rājavarṇano nāma dvitīyaḥ sargaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the second canto, titled 'Description of the King,' in the <s>Saundarānanda</s> <s>mahākāvya</s>.
CANTO III

children.text: tapase tataḥ kapilavāstu hayagarathaughasaṃkulam /
children.translated_text: For the sake of austerity, leaving <s>Kapilavastu</s> — bustling with horses and chariots —

children.text: śrīmad abhayam anuraktajanaṃ sa vihāya viścitamanā vanaṃ yayau // Saund_3.1 //
children.translated_text: that glorious, fearless [city] with devoted people — he, with determined mind, went to the forest.

children.text: vividhāgmāṃs tapasi tāṃś ca vividhaniyamāśrayān munīn /
children.translated_text: Seeing ascetics of various scriptures in their austerities, following various rules,

children.text: prekṣya sa viṣayatṛākṛpaṇān anavasthitaṃ tapa iti nyavartata // Saund_3.2 //
children.translated_text: and [perceiving them as] pitiable in their thirst for sense objects, he turned back, [concluding] 'This austerity is unstable.'

children.text: atha mokṣavādinam arāḍam upaśamamatiṃ tathoḍrakam /
children.translated_text: Then, having attended upon <s>Arāḍa</s>, the teacher of liberation, and likewise <s>Uḍraka</s>, the teacher of tranquility,

children.text: tattvakṛtamatir upāsya jahāvayam apy amārga iti māgakovidaḥ // Saund_3.3 //
children.translated_text: with his mind set on truth, this one skilled in the path abandoned [them both], [concluding] 'This too is not the path.'

children.text: sa vicārayan jagati kiṃ nu paramam iti taṃ tam āgamam /
children.translated_text: Deliberating 'What then is the supreme [truth]?' and [examining] this and that scripture in the world,

children.text: niścayam anadhigataḥ parataḥ paramaṃ cacāra tapa eva duṣkaram // Saund_3.4 //
children.translated_text: not having attained certainty from another, he performed extremely difficult austerities.

children.text: atha naiṣa mārga iti vikṣya tad api vipulaṃ jahau tapaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, perceiving 'This is not the path,' he abandoned even that great austerity;

children.text: dhyānaviṣayam avagamya paraṃ bubhuje varānnam amṛtatvabuddhaye // Saund_3.5 //
children.translated_text: having understood the supreme object of meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), he partook of excellent food with the intention of [attaining] immortality.

children.text: sa suvarṇapīnayugabāhur ṛṣabhagatir āyatekṣaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: He, with golden, full, and paired arms, with the gait of a bull, and with wide eyes,

children.text: plakṣam avaniruham abhyagamat paramasya niścayavidher bubhutsayā // Saund_3.6 //
children.translated_text: approached the <s>Plakṣa</s> (fig) tree, a native of the earth, with the desire to know the supreme course of action.

children.text: upaviśya tatra kṛtabuddhir acaldhṛtir adrirājavat /
children.translated_text: Having sat there with resolute mind and immovable firmness like the king of mountains,

children.text: mārabalam ajayad ugram atho bubudhe padaṃ śivam ahāryam avyayam // Saund_3.7 //
children.translated_text: he conquered the fierce army of <s>Māra</s>, and then he awakened to the auspicious, unshakeable, imperishable state.

children.text: avagamya taṃ ca kṛtakāryam amṛtamanaso divaukasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having understood that he had accomplished his purpose, the celestials with joyful minds

children.text: harṣam atulam agaman muditā vimukhī tu mārapariṣat pracukṣubhe // Saund_3.8 //
children.translated_text: attained incomparable happiness and rejoiced; but <s>Māra</s>'s retinue, turning away, was thrown into turmoil.

children.text: sanagā ca bhūḥ pravicāla hutavahasakaḥ śivo vavau /
children.translated_text: The earth with its mountains trembled; a gentle wind blew, accompanied by fire;

children.text: nedur api ca suradundubhayaḥ pravavarṣa cāmbudharavarjitaṃ nabhaḥ // Saund_3.9 //
children.translated_text: and celestial drums resounded, and from the cloudless sky there fell rain.

children.text: avabudhya caiva paramārtham ajaram anukampayā vibhuḥ /
children.translated_text: And having awakened to the supreme truth — ageless — the all-powerful one, out of compassion,

children.text: nityam amṛtam upadarśyituṃ sa varāñasīparikarām ayāt purīm // Saund_3.10 //
children.translated_text: in order to reveal the eternal and immortal [truth], went to the city with <s>Vārāṇasī</s> as its environs.

children.text: atha dharmacakram ṛtanābhi dhṛtimatisamādhinemimat /
children.translated_text: Then the wheel of <s>dharma</s> — with truth as its hub, with firmness, wisdom, and <s>samādhi</s> as its rim —

children.text: tatra vinayanimāram ṛṣir jagato hitāya pariṣady avartayat // Saund_3.11 //
children.translated_text: there, the sage, for the welfare of the world, set in motion in the assembly, [the wheel that is] the subduer of <s>Māra</s>.

children.text: iti duḥkham etad iyam asya samudayalatā pravartikā /
children.translated_text: 'This is suffering; this is the creeper of its origination, the instigator;

children.text: śāntir iyam ayam upāya iti pravibhāgaśaḥ param idaṃ catuṣṭayam // Saund_3.12 //
children.translated_text: this is cessation; this is the path' — thus, distinctly, this is the supreme fourfold [truth].

children.text: abhidhāya ca triparivartam atulam anivartyam uttamam /
children.translated_text: Having proclaimed it with three turnings — incomparable, irreversible, supreme —

children.text: dvādaśaniyatavikalpam ṛṣir vinināya kauṇḍinasagotram āditaḥ // Saund_3.13 //
children.translated_text: with twelve determined aspects, the sage first guided the one of the <s>Kauṇḍinya</s> lineage.

children.text: sa hi doṣasāgaram agādham upadhijalam ādhijanutkam /
children.translated_text: For he crossed the fathomless ocean of defilements (<s>doṣa</s>) — with adventitious [impurities] as its waters, with afflictions (<s>ādhi</s>) as its crocodiles,

children.text: krodhamadabhayatarṅgacalaṃ pratatāra lokam api vyatārayat // Saund_3.14 //
children.translated_text: with anger, pride, and fear as its waves — and he also helped the world to cross over.

children.text: sa vinīya kāśiṣu gayeṣu bahujanam atho girivraje /
children.translated_text: Having disciplined many people in <s>Kāśī</s>, in <s>Gayā</s>, and then in <s>Girivraja</s> —

children.text: pitryam api paramakāruṇiko nagaraṃ yayāv anujighṛkṣayā tadā // Saund_3.15 //
children.translated_text: the supremely compassionate one then went to the paternal city, out of a desire to show favor. // Saund_3.15 //

children.text: viṣayātmakasya hi ianasya bahuvividhamārgasevinaḥ /
children.translated_text: For among the people who were devoted to sense-objects and who followed many diverse paths,

children.text: sūryasadṛśavapur abhyudito vijahāra sūrya iva gautamas tamaḥ // Saund_3.16 //
children.translated_text: <s>Gautama</s>, of sun-like form, having arisen, dispelled the darkness like the sun. // Saund_3.16 //

children.text: abhitas tataḥ kapilavāstu paramaśubhavāstusaṃstutam /
children.translated_text: Then, all around <s>Kapilavastu</s>, praised for its supremely auspicious dwellings,

children.text: vastumatiśuci śivopavanaṃ sa dadarśa niḥspṛhatayā yathā vanam // Saund_3.17 //
children.translated_text: he beheld the exceedingly pure city with its blessed groves, with detachment, as if it were a forest. // Saund_3.17 //

children.text: aparigrahaḥ sa hi babhūva niyatamatir ātmanīśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: For he was without possessions, of steadfast mind, master of himself,

children.text: naikavidhabhayakareṣu kim-u svajanasvadeśajanamitravastuṣu // Saund_3.18 //
children.translated_text: how much less [would he be attached] to kinsmen, countrymen, friends, and belongings, which cause manifold fears? // Saund_3.18 //

children.text: pratipūjayā na sa jaharṣa na ca śucam avajñayāgamat /
children.translated_text: He did not rejoice at honor, nor did he grieve at disrespect;

children.text: niścitamatir asicandanayor na jagāma duḥkhasukhayoś ca vikriyām // Saund_3.19 //
children.translated_text: of firm resolve regarding sword and sandal paste alike, he underwent no agitation from pain or pleasure. // Saund_3.19 //

children.text: atha pārthivaḥ samupalabhya sutam upagataṃ tathāgatam /
children.translated_text: Then the king, learning that his son had come as the <s>Tathāgata</s>,

children.text: tūrṇam ababhuturagānugataḥ sutadarśanotsukatayābhiniryayau // Saund_3.20 //
children.translated_text: swiftly went forth, followed by excellent horses, with eagerness to see his son. // Saund_3.20 //

children.text: sugatas tathāgatam avekṣya narapatim adhīram āśayā /
children.translated_text: The <s>Sugata</s>, seeing the king who had come thus, unsteady in disposition,

children.text: śeṣam api ca janam aśrumukhaṃ vinīṣaya gaganam utpapāta ha // Saund_3.21 //
children.translated_text: and the rest of the people too with tear-stained faces, in order to guide them, rose up into the sky. // Saund_3.21 //

children.text: sa vicakrame divi bhuvīva punar upaviveśa tasthivān /
children.translated_text: He strode through the sky as if on the ground, and sat down again, and stood;

children.text: niścalamatir aśayiṣṭa punar bahudhābhavat punar abhūt tathaikadhā // Saund_3.22 //
children.translated_text: with motionless mind he lay down, and then became manifold, and then became one again. // Saund_3.22 //

children.text: salile kṣitāv iva cacāra jalam iva viveṣa medinīm /
children.translated_text: He walked on water as if on earth, and entered the earth as if into water;

children.text: megha iva divi vavarṣa punaḥ punar ajvalan nava ivodito raviḥ // Saund_3.23 //
children.translated_text: like a cloud, he rained in the sky, and then blazed like the sun newly risen. // Saund_3.23 //

children.text: yugapaj jvalan jvalanavac ca jalam avasṛhaṃś ca meghavat /
children.translated_text: Blazing simultaneously like fire and releasing water like a cloud,

children.text: taptakanakasadṛśaprabhayā sa babhau pradīpta iva sandhyayā ghanaḥ // Saund_3.24 //
children.translated_text: with a radiance like heated gold, he shone like a cloud lit up by the sunset glow. // Saund_3.24 //

children.text: tam udīkṣya hemamaṇijālavalayinam ivotthitaṃ dhvajam /
children.translated_text: Beholding him like a banner raised aloft, encircled with nets of gold and jewels,

children.text: prītim agamad atulāṃ nṛpatir janatā natāś ca bahumānam abhyayuḥ // Saund_3.25 //
children.translated_text: the king attained incomparable joy, and the people, bowing, showed great reverence. // Saund_3.25 //

children.text: atha bhājanīkṛtam avekṣya manujapatim ṛddhisaṃpadā /
children.translated_text: Then, seeing that the lord of men had been made a worthy vessel through the display of supernatural powers,

children.text: paurajanam api ca tatpravaṇaṃ nijagāda dharmavinayaṃ vināyakaḥ // Saund_3.26 //
children.translated_text: and that the townspeople too were inclined toward him, the Guide (<s>Vināyaka</s>) taught the <s>Dharma</s> and discipline. // Saund_3.26 //

children.text: nṛpatis tataḥ prathamam āpa phalam amṛtadharmasiddhayoḥ /
children.translated_text: The king then first attained the fruit of the immortal <s>Dharma</s> and spiritual accomplishment;

children.text: dharmam atulam adhigamya muner munaye nanāma sa yato gurāv iva // Saund_3.27 //
children.translated_text: having realized the incomparable <s>Dharma</s> of the sage, he bowed to the sage as one would to a teacher. // Saund_3.27 //

children.text: bahavaḥ prasannamanaso 'tha jananamaraṇārtibhīravaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then many with serene minds, terrified of the sufferings of birth and death,

children.text: śākyatanayavṛṣabhāḥ kṛtino vṛṣabhā invānalabhayāt pravavrajuḥ // Saund_3.28 //
children.translated_text: bulls among the sons of the <s>Śākyas</s>, accomplished ones, went forth like bulls fleeing from the fear of fire. // Saund_3.28 //

children.text: vijahus tu ye 'pi na gṛhāṇi tanayapitṛmātrapekṣayā /
children.translated_text: But those who did not abandon their homes, out of regard for sons, fathers, and mothers,

children.text: te 'pi niyamavidhimāmaraṇāj jagṛhuś ca yuktamanasaś ca daghrire // Saund_3.29 //
children.translated_text: they too adopted the rules of restraint until death and, with concentrated minds, practiced austerity. // Saund_3.29 //

children.text: na jihiṃsa sūkṣmam api jantum api paravadhopajīvanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even one who lived by slaughtering others did not harm even the smallest creature —

children.text: kiṃ bata vipulaguñaḥ kulajaḥ sadayaḥ sadā kimu muner upāsayā // Saund_3.30 //
children.translated_text: how much more so one of great virtue, well-born, always compassionate, and especially one in the service of the sage! // Saund_3.30 //

children.text: akṛśodhyamaḥ kṛśadhano 'pi paraparibhavāsaho 'pi san /
children.translated_text: Though not lacking in energy, though poor in wealth, though unable to bear being humiliated by others,

children.text: nānyadhanam apajahāra tathā bhujagād ivānyavibhavād dhi vivyathe // Saund_3.31 //
children.translated_text: he did not steal another's property; for he recoiled from another's wealth as from a serpent. // Saund_3.31 //

children.text: vibhavānvito 'pi taruṇo 'pi viṣayacapalendriyo 'pi san /
children.translated_text: Though endowed with riches, though young, though having senses restless for sense-objects,

children.text: naiva ca parayuvatīr agamat paramaṃ hi tā dhanato 'py amanyata // Saund_3.32 //
children.translated_text: he did not approach other men's wives, for he considered them more [forbidden] even than wealth. // Saund_3.32 //

children.text: anṛtaṃ jagāda na ca kaś cid ṛtam api jajalpa nāpriyam /
children.translated_text: No one spoke untruth, nor did anyone utter even a truth that was unpleasant;

children.text: ślakṣṇam api ca na jagāv ahitaṃ hitam apy uvāca na ca paiśunāya yat // Saund_3.33 //
children.translated_text: nor did anyone say what was smooth but harmful; and he spoke what was beneficial, not for the sake of slander. // Saund_3.33 //

children.text: manasā lulobha na ca jātu paravasuṣu gṛddhamānasaḥ /
children.translated_text: No one whose mind was greedy ever coveted in thought another's possessions;

children.text: kāmasukham asukhato vimṛśan vijahāra tṛpta iva tatra sajjanaḥ // Saund_3.34 //
children.translated_text: reflecting on sensual pleasure as suffering, the good person lived there as though content. // Saund_3.34 //

children.text: na parasya kaś cid apaghātam api ca sgṛṇo vyacintayat /
children.translated_text: No compassionate person even thought of harming another;

children.text: mātṛpiṛsutasuhṛsadṛśaṃ sa dadarśa tatra hi paras paraṃ janaḥ // Saund_3.35 //
children.translated_text: for there the people regarded one another as mother, father, son, and friend. // Saund_3.35 //

children.text: niyataṃ bhaviṣyati paratra bhavad api ca bhūtam apy atho /
children.translated_text: 'What will certainly be in the hereafter, and what has been, and moreover

children.text: karmaphalam api ca lokagatir niyateti darśanam avāpa sādhu ca // Saund_3.36 //
children.translated_text: the fruit of <s>karma</s>, and the course of the world are fixed' — such right view they attained. // Saund_3.36 //

children.text: iti karmañā daśavidhena paramakuśalena bhūriṇā /
children.translated_text: Thus, through the tenfold supremely wholesome <s>karma</s> in abundance,

children.text: bhraṃśini śitahilaguṇo 'pi yuge vijahāra tatra munsaṃśrayaj janaḥ // Saund_3.37 //
children.translated_text: even in a degenerate age whose virtues of tranquility and mildness had declined, the people lived there by the influence of the sage. // Saund_3.37 //

children.text: na ca tatra kaś cid upapattisukham abhilalāṣa tair guṇaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Nor did anyone there desire the pleasures of rebirth through those virtues;

children.text: sarvam aśivam avagamya bhavaṃ bhavasaṃkṣayāya vavṛte na janmane // Saund_3.38 //
children.translated_text: having understood all existence as inauspicious, they turned toward the cessation of existence, not toward birth. // Saund_3.38 //

children.text: akathaṅkathā gṛhiṇa eva paramapariśuddhadṛṣtayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Free from doubt, householders themselves, with supremely purified vision —

children.text: srotasi hi vavṛtire bahavo rajasas tanutvam api cakrire pare // Saund_3.39 //
children.translated_text: many entered the stream, and others too attenuated the dust of passion. // Saund_3.39 //

children.text: vavṛte 'tra yo 'pi viṣameṣu vibhavadṛśeṣu kaś cana /
children.translated_text: Even one who was engaged in the uneven [paths] of wealth and status,

children.text: tyāgavinayaniyamābhirato vijahāra so 'pi na cacāla satpathāt // Saund_3.40 //
children.translated_text: delighting in generosity, humility, and restraint, lived [rightly] and did not stray from the true path. // Saund_3.40 //

children.text: api ca svato 'pi parato 'pi na bhayam abhavan na daivataḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, there was no fear from oneself, from others, or from the gods;

children.text: tatra ca susukhasubhikṣaguṇair jahṛṣuḥ prajāḥ kṛtayuge manor iva // Saund_3.41 //
children.translated_text: and there the people rejoiced with the virtues of great happiness and abundance, as in the <s>Kṛtayuga</s> of <s>Manu</s>. // Saund_3.41 //

children.text: iti muditam anāmayaṃ nirāpat kururaghupurupuropamaṃ puraṃ tat /
children.translated_text: Thus, that city, joyous, free from disease, free from calamity, comparable to the cities of the <s>Kuru</s>, <s>Raghu</s>, and <s>Puru</s> [dynasties],

children.text: abhavad abhayadaiśike maharṣau viharati tatra śivāya vītarāge // Saund_3.42 //
children.translated_text: became [blessed] while the great sage, the giver of fearlessness, passion-free, dwelt there for [the people's] welfare. // Saund_3.42 //

body.translated_text: CANTO IV

children.text: munau bruvāñe 'pi tu tatra dharmaṃ dharmaṃ prati jñātiṣu cādṛteṣu /
children.translated_text: But even while the sage was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> there, and while his kinsmen were devoted to the <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: prāsādasaṃstho madanaikakāryaḥ priyāsahāyo vijahāra nandaḥ // Saund_4.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s>, stationed in his palace, solely occupied with <s>Madana</s> (love), spent his time in the company of his beloved. // Saund_4.1 //

children.text: sa cakravākyeva hi cakravākas tayā sametaḥ priyayā priyārhaḥ /
children.translated_text: For he, worthy of love, united with his beloved like a <s>cakravāka</s> drake with his <s>cakravākī</s>,

children.text: nācintayad vaiśrmaṇaṃ na śakraṃ tasthānahetoḥ kuta eva dharmam // Saund_4.2 //
children.translated_text: thought neither of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> nor of <s>Śakra</s> — for the sake of that [pleasure], how much less of <s>Dharma</s>! // Saund_4.2 //

children.text: lakṣmyā ca rūpeṇa ca sundarīti stambhena garveṇa ca māninīti /
children.translated_text: Because of her beauty and form she was called <s>Sundarī</s> (the beautiful one), because of her pride and haughtiness she was <s>Māninī</s> (the proud one),

children.text: dīptyā ca mānena ca bhāminīti yato babhāṣe trividhena nāmnā // Saund_4.3 //
children.translated_text: because of her radiance and dignity she was <s>Bhāminī</s> (the resplendent one) — thus she was addressed by three names. // Saund_4.3 //

children.text: sā hāsahaṃsā nayandvirephā pīnastanātyunnatapadmakośā /
children.translated_text: She, whose laughter was like swans, whose eyes were like bees, whose full breasts were like lofty lotus buds,

children.text: bhūyo babhāse svakuloditena strīpadminī nandadivākareṇa // Saund_4.4 //
children.translated_text: shone all the more like a lotus-pool of women, with <s>Nanda</s> as the sun risen from her own lineage. // Saund_4.4 //

children.text: rūpeṇa cātyantamanohareṇa rūpānurūpeṇa ca ceṣṭitena /
children.translated_text: With her exceedingly captivating beauty, and with conduct befitting that beauty,

children.text: manuṣyaloke hi tadā babhūva sā sundarī strīṣu nareṣu nandaḥ // Saund_4.5 //
children.translated_text: she, <s>Sundarī</s>, was [the foremost] among women in the world of mortals at that time, and <s>Nanda</s> among men. // Saund_4.5 //

children.text: sā devatā nandanacāriṇīva kulasya nandījananaś ca nandaḥ /
children.translated_text: She was like a goddess wandering in <s>Nandana</s> [garden], and <s>Nanda</s> was the cause of joy to his family;

children.text: atītya martyān anupetya devān sṛṣṭāv abhūtām iva bhūtadhātrā // Saund_4.6 //
children.translated_text: surpassing mortals yet not quite reaching the gods, they seemed as if created [specially] by the Creator. // Saund_4.6 //

children.text: tāṃ sundarīṃ cen na labheta nandaḥ sā vā niṣeveta na taṃ natabhrūḥ /
children.translated_text: If <s>Nanda</s> had not obtained <s>Sundarī</s>, or if she of the curved brows had not attended upon him,

children.text: dvandaṃ dhruvaṃ tad vikalaṃ na śobhetānyonyahīnāv iva rātricandrau // Saund_4.7 //
children.translated_text: that couple, incomplete, would surely not have shone — like the night and the moon bereft of each other. // Saund_4.7 //

children.text: kandarparatyor iva lakṣyabhūtaṃ pramodanāndyor iva nīḍabhūtam /
children.translated_text: Having become the target, as it were, of <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love) and <s>Rati</s> (desire), having become the nest, as it were, of delight and bliss,

children.text: praharṣatuṣṭyor iva pātrabhūtaṃ dvandaṃ sahāraṃsta madāndhabhūtam // Saund_4.8 //
children.translated_text: having become the vessel, as it were, of joy and satisfaction, that couple reveled together, blinded by passion. // Saund_4.8 //

children.text: parasparodvīkṣaṇatatparākṣaṃ parasparavyāhṛtasaktacittam /
children.translated_text: With eyes intent on gazing at each other, with minds attached to each other's words,

children.text: parasparāśleṣahṛtāṇgarāgaṃ parasparaṃ tan mithunaṃ jahāra // Saund_4.9 //
children.translated_text: with body-ornaments smeared away by mutual embraces, that pair delighted in each other. // Saund_4.9 //

children.text: bhāvānuraktau girinirjharasthau tau kiṃnarīkiṃpuruṣāv ivobhau /
children.translated_text: Both of them, emotionally attached, like a <s>Kiṃnarī</s> and a <s>Kiṃpuruṣa</s> dwelling by a mountain waterfall,

children.text: cikrīḍatuś cābhivirejatuś ca rūpaśriyānyonyam ivākṣipantau // Saund_4.10 //
children.translated_text: they sported and shone, as if challenging each other with the splendor of their beauty. // Saund_4.10 //

children.text: anyonyasaṃrāgavivardhanena tad dvandvam anyonyam arīramac ca /
children.translated_text: Through the ever-increasing mutual passion, that couple delighted each other,

children.text: klamāntare 'nyonyavinodanena salīlam anyonyam amīmadac ca // Saund_4.11 //
children.translated_text: and in the intervals of weariness, through mutual entertainment, they playfully intoxicated each other. // Saund_4.11 //

children.text: vibhūṣayām āsa tataḥ priyāṃ sa siṣeviṣus tāṃ na mṛjāvahārtham /
children.translated_text: Then he adorned his beloved, desiring to attend upon her, not for the sake of cleansing;

children.text: svenaiva rūpeṇa vibhūṣitā hi vibhūṣaṇānām api bhuṣaṇaṃ sā // Saund_4.12 //
children.translated_text: for she, adorned by her own beauty alone, was indeed the ornament of ornaments. // Saund_4.12 //

children.text: dattvātha sā darpaṇam asya haste mamāgrato dhāraya tāvad enam /
children.translated_text: Then, placing the mirror in his hand, she said, 'Hold this before me

children.text: viśeṣakaṃ yāvad ahaṃ karomīty uvāca kāntaṃ sa ca taṃ babhāra // Saund_4.13 //
children.translated_text: while I apply the <s>viśeṣaka</s> (forehead mark)' — and to her beloved, and he held it. // Saund_4.13 //

children.text: bhartus tataḥ śmaśru nirīkṣamāṇā viśeṣakaṅ sāpi cakāra tādṛk /
children.translated_text: Then, looking at her husband's beard [reflected in the mirror], she drew a similar <s>viśeṣaka</s> [on the mirror];

children.text: niśvāsavātena ca darpañasya cikitsayitvā nijaghāna nandaḥ // Saund_4.14 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Nanda</s>, having fogged the mirror with a breath, wiped it off. // Saund_4.14 //

children.text: sā tena ceṣṭālalitena bhartuḥ śāṭhyena cāntarmanasā jahāsa /
children.translated_text: At that playful gesture of her husband and his inner mischievousness, she laughed;

children.text: bhavec ca ruṣṭā kila nāma tasmai lalāṭajihmāṃ bhṛkuṭiṃ cakāra // Saund_4.15 //
children.translated_text: and pretending to be angry with him, she drew a crooked frown upon her forehead. // Saund_4.15 //

children.text: cikṣepa karṇotpalam asya cāṃse kareña savyena madālasena /
children.translated_text: She tossed the ear-lotus from his [ear] onto his shoulder with her left hand, languid with passion,

children.text: pattrāṅguliṃ cārdhanimīlitākṣe vaktre 'sya tām eva vinirdudhāva // Saund_4.16 //
children.translated_text: and with her leaf-like finger, on his face with eyes half-closed, she smeared that very [mark] away. // Saund_4.16 //

children.text: tataś calannūpurayoktritābhyāṃ nakhaprabhodhāsitarāṅgulibhyām /
children.translated_text: Then, to the feet of his beloved — adorned with tinkling anklets,

children.text: padhyāṃ priyāyā nalinopamābhyāṃ mūrdhnā bhayān nāma nanāma nadaḥ // Saund_4.17 //
children.translated_text: with toes bright with nail-luster, and resembling lotuses — <s>Nanda</s> bowed his head, as if in fear. // Saund_4.17 //

children.text: sa muktapuṣponmiṣitena mūrdhnā tataḥ priyāyāḥ priyakṛd babhāse /
children.translated_text: Then, with his head from which flowers had fallen loose, making his beloved happy, he appeared

children.text: suvarṇavedyām anilāvabhagnaḥ puṣpātibhārād iva nāgavṛkṣaḥ // Saund_4.18 //
children.translated_text: like a <s>nāgavṛkṣa</s> (Mesua ferrea tree) on a golden platform, bent by the wind, as if overburdened with blossoms. // Saund_4.18 //

children.text: sā taṃ stanodvartitahāraṣṭir utthāpayām āsa nipīḍya dorbhyām /
children.translated_text: She, with the tip of her necklace pressed against her upraised breasts, raised him up, pressing him with her arms,

children.text: kathaṃ kṛto 'sīti jahāsa coccair mukhena sācīkṛtakuṇḍalena // Saund_4.19 //
children.translated_text: 'What have you done!' she laughed loudly, her face with its earring turned aside. // Saund_4.19 //

children.text: patyus tato darpaṇasaktapāṇer muhurmuhur vaktram avekṣamāṇā /
children.translated_text: Then, while her husband held the mirror in his hand, gazing again and again at his face,

children.text: tamālapattrārdratale kapole samāpayāmāsa viśeṣakaṃ tat // Saund_4.20 //
children.translated_text: on her cheek, its surface moist with <s>tamāla</s>-leaf [paste], she completed that <s>viśeṣaka</s>. // Saund_4.20 //

children.text: tasyā mukhaṅ tat satamālapattraṅ tāmrādharauṣṭhaṃ cikurāyatākṣam /
children.translated_text: Her face, with its <s>tamāla</s>-leaf [decoration], its lower lip copper-red, its eyes elongated with dark locks,

children.text: raktādhikāgraṃ patitadvirephaṅ saśaivalaṅ padmam ivābabhāse // Saund_4.21 //
children.translated_text: with a fallen bee at its reddened tip, appeared like a lotus with moss. // Saund_4.21 //

children.text: nandas tato darpaṇam ādareṇa bibhrat tadāmaṇḍanasākṣibhūtam /
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s>, then, reverently holding the mirror that was witness to her adornment,

children.text: viśeṣakāvekṣaṇakekarākṣo laḍat priyāyā vadanaṃ dadarśa // Saund_4.22 //
children.translated_text: with sidelong glances examining the <s>viśeṣaka</s>, playfully gazed at his beloved's face. // Saund_4.22 //

children.text: tat kuṇḍalādaṣṭaviśeṣakāntaṃ kāraṇḍavakliṣṭam ivāravindam /
children.translated_text: That [face], with the edge of its <s>viśeṣaka</s> grazed by the earring, like a lotus disturbed by a <s>kāraṇḍava</s> (duck),

children.text: nandaḥ priyāyā mukham īkṣamāṇo bhūyaḥ priyānandakaro babhūva // Saund_4.23 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s>, gazing at the face of his beloved, became ever more the cause of her delight. // Saund_4.23 //

children.text: vimānakalpe sa vimānagarbhe tatas tathā caiva nandana nandaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, in that palace-like chamber, while <s>Nanda</s> was thus delighting <s>Sundarī</s>,

children.text: tathāgataś cāgatabhaikṣakālo bhaikṣāya tasya praviveṣa veśma // Saund_4.24 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the time for his alms-round having come, entered his house for alms. // Saund_4.24 //

children.text: avāṅmukho niṣpraṇayaś ca tasthau bhrātu gṛhe 'nyasya gṛhe yathaiva /
children.translated_text: He stood with downcast face and without familiarity, in his brother's house as if in a stranger's house;

children.text: tasmād atho preṣyajanapramādād bhikṣām alabdhaiva punar jagāma // Saund_4.25 //
children.translated_text: and then, due to the negligence of the servants, without having received alms, he departed again. // Saund_4.25 //

children.text: kā cit pipeṣāṅgavilepanaṃ hi vāso 'ṅganā kā cid avāsayac ca /
children.translated_text: For one woman was grinding body-ointment, and another was scenting garments,

children.text: ayojayat snānavidhiṃ tathānyā jagranthur anyāḥ surabhīḥ srajaś ca // Saund_4.26 //
children.translated_text: and yet another was preparing the bathing ritual, and others were stringing fragrant garlands. // Saund_4.26 //

children.text: tasmin gṛhe bhartur ataś carantyaḥ krīḍānurūpaṃ lalitaṃ niyogam /
children.translated_text: Thus, the young women in that household, carrying out their master's graceful commands befitting his pleasures,

children.text: kāś cin na buddhaṃ dadṛśur yuvatyo buddhasya vaiṣā niyataṅ manīṣā // Saund_4.27 //
children.translated_text: some did not see the <s>Buddha</s> — though surely this was the <s>Buddha</s>'s intention. // Saund_4.27 //

children.text: kā cit sthitā tatra tu harmyapṛṣṭhe gavākṣapakṣe praṇidhāya cakṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: But a certain woman standing on the terrace of the palace, directing her gaze through the latticed window,

children.text: viniṣpatantaṃ sugataṃ dadarśa payodagarbhād iva dīptam arkam // Saund_4.28 //
children.translated_text: saw the <s>Sugata</s> departing, like the bright sun [emerging] from the womb of a cloud. // Saund_4.28 //

children.text: sā gauravaṃ tatra vicārya bhartuḥ svayā ca bhaktyārhatayārhataś ca /
children.translated_text: She, considering the reverence due to her master, and [motivated] by her own devotion and by the worthiness of the Worthy One,

children.text: nandasya tasthau purato vivakṣus tadājñayā ceti tadācacakṣe // Saund_4.29 //
children.translated_text: stood before <s>Nanda</s>, wishing to speak, and at his command, reported thus: // Saund_4.29 //

children.text: anugrahāyāsya janasya śaṅke gurur gṛhaṃ no bhagavān praviṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I think the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the teacher, has entered our house for the benefit of these people;

children.text: bhikṣām alabdhvā giram āsanaṃ vā sūnyād araṇyād iva yāti bhūyaḥ // Saund_4.30 //
children.translated_text: not having received alms, nor a word, nor a seat, he departs again as if from an empty wilderness.' // Saund_4.30 //

children.text: śrutvā maharṣeḥ sa gṛhapraveśaṃ satkārahīnaṃ ca punaḥprayāṇam /
children.translated_text: Hearing of the great sage's entrance into the house and his departure without having been honored,

children.text: cacāla citrābharaṇāmbarasrak kalpadrumo dhūta ivānilena // Saund_4.31 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Nanda</s>] trembled — with his marvelous ornaments, garments, and garlands — like a wishing-tree shaken by the wind. // Saund_4.31 //

children.text: kṛtvāñjaliṃ mūrdhani padmakalpaṃ tataḥ sa kāntāṃ gamanaṃ yayāce /
children.translated_text: Then, placing his lotus-like joined palms upon his head, he asked his beloved for permission to go.

children.text: kartuṃ gamiṣyāmi gurau praṇāmaṃ mām abhyanujñātum ihārhasīti // Saund_4.32 //
children.translated_text: "I shall go to pay obeisance to the teacher; please grant me leave here."

children.text: sā vepamānā parisasvaje taṃ śālaṃ latā vātasamīriteva /
children.translated_text: She, trembling, embraced him, like a creeper on a <s>śāla</s> tree swayed by the wind,

children.text: dadarśa cāśuplutalolanetrā dīrghaṃ ca niśvasya vaco 'bhyuvāca // Saund_4.33 //
children.translated_text: and gazed at him with eyes darting and brimming with tears, and having sighed deeply, spoke these words:

children.text: nāhaṃ yiyāsor gurudarśanārtham arhāmi kartuṃ tava dharmapīḍām /
children.translated_text: "I, who do not wish you to go, should not cause you distress from duty for the sake of seeing the teacher.

children.text: gacchāryaputraihi ca śīghram eva viśeṣako yāvad ayaṅ na śuṣkaḥ // Saund_4.34 //
children.translated_text: Go, noble son, and return quickly, while this <s>viśeṣaka</s> (ornamental mark) has not yet dried."

children.text: saced bhaves tvaṃ khalu dīrghasūtro daṇdaṃ mahāntaṃ tvayi pātayeyam /
children.translated_text: "Should you indeed be long in returning, I would inflict a great punishment upon you;

children.text: muhurmuhus tvāṃ śayitaṃ kucābhyāṃ vibodhayeyaṃ ca na cālapeyam // Saund_4.35 //
children.translated_text: again and again I would wake you as you sleep with my breasts, and yet I would not speak to you."

children.text: athāpy anāśyānaviśeṣakāyāṃ mayy eṣyasi tvaṃ tvaritaṃ tatas tvām /
children.translated_text: "But if you return swiftly while my <s>viśeṣaka</s> (ornamental mark) has not dried,

children.text: nipīḍayiṣyāmi bhujadvayena nirbhūṣañenārdravilepanena // Saund_4.36 //
children.translated_text: I shall press you with both my arms, bare of ornaments and moist with unguents."

children.text: ity evam uktaś ca nipīḍitaś ca tayāsavarṇasvanayā jagāda /
children.translated_text: Thus addressed and embraced by her whose voice was like a <s>kinnara</s>'s, he said:

children.text: evaṃ kariṣyāmi vimuñca caṇḍi yāvad gurur dūragato na me saḥ // Saund_4.37 //
children.translated_text: "I shall do so; release me, fierce one, lest my teacher has gone far away."

children.text: tataḥ stanodvartitacandanābhyāṃ mukto bhujābhyāṃ na tu mānasena /
children.translated_text: Then, released from her arms — smeared with sandal paste from her breasts — but not from her heart,

children.text: vihāya veṣaṃ madanānurūpaṃ satkārayogyaṃ sa vapur babhāra // Saund_4.38 //
children.translated_text: setting aside his attire suited to love, he assumed a form worthy of paying respects.

children.text: sā taṃ prayāntaṃ ramaṇaṃ pradadhyau pradhyānaśūnyasthitaniścalākṣī /
