children.translated_text: She watched her departing lover with unblinking eyes, standing still, absorbed in thought,

children.text: sthitoccakarṇā vyapaviddhaśaṣpā bhrāntasṃ mṛgaṃ bhrāntaṃ mṛgaṅ bhrāntaṃ mukhī mṛgīva // Saund_4.39 //
children.translated_text: like a doe standing with ears pricked up, grass abandoned from her mouth, watching a departing stag.

children.text: didṛkṣayākṣiptamanā munes tu nandaḥ prayāṇaṃ prati tatvare ca /
children.translated_text: But <s>Nanda</s>, his mind captivated by the desire to see the sage, hastened toward the departure,

children.text: vivṛttadṛṣṭiś ca śanair yayau tāṃ karīva paśyan sa laḍatkareñum // Saund_4.40 //
children.translated_text: yet turning his gaze back slowly, he went toward her, like an elephant looking back at a playful she-elephant.

children.text: chātodariṃ pīnapayodharoruṃ sa sundarīṃ rukmadarīm ivādreḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s>, looking sidelong at <s>Sundarī</s> — slender-waisted, with full breasts and thighs — like a golden cave on a mountain,

children.text: kākṣeṇa paśyan na tatarpa nandaḥ pibann ivaikena jalaṃ kareṇa // Saund_4.41//
children.translated_text: was not satisfied, like one drinking water with only one trunk.

children.text: taṅ gauravaṃ buddhagataṃ cakarṣa bhāryānurāgaḥ punar ācakarṣa /
children.translated_text: Reverence for the <s>Buddha</s> drew him forward, while love for his wife pulled him back;

children.text: sa 'niścayān nāpi yayau na tasthau turaṃs taraṅgeṣv iva rājahaṃsaḥ // Saund_4.42 //
children.translated_text: unable to resolve, he neither went nor stayed, like a royal swan on turbulent waves.

children.text: adarśanaṃ tūpagataś ca tasyā harmyāt tataś cāvatatāra tūrṇam /
children.translated_text: But when he had passed beyond sight of her, she quickly descended from the upper palace,

children.text: śrutvā tato nūpuranisvanaṃ sa punar lalambe hṛdaye gṛhītaḥ // Saund_4.43 //
children.translated_text: and then, hearing the sound of her anklets, he was seized in his heart and clung [to the spot] again.

children.text: sa kāmarāgeña nigṛhyamāṇo dharmānurāgeña ca kṛṣyamāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Held back by the passion of desire, yet drawn forward by devotion to <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: jagāma duḥkhena vivartyamānaḥ plavaḥ pratisrota ivāpagāyāḥ // Saund_4.44 //
children.translated_text: he went forth in anguish, turning back and forth, like a raft against the current of a river.

children.text: tataḥ kramair dīrghatamaiḥ pracakrame kataṃ nu yāto na gurur bhaved iti /
children.translated_text: Then he proceeded with extremely long strides, thinking, 'Has the teacher perhaps already gone far?'

children.text: svajeya tāṃ caiva viśeṣakapriyāṃ kathaṃ priyām ārdraviśeṣakām iti // Saund_4.45 //
children.translated_text: and 'Shall I embrace that beloved one who loves the ornamental mark, my darling with the moist <s>viśeṣaka</s>?'

children.text: atha sa pathi dadarśa muktamānaṃ pitṛnagare 'pi tathāgatābhimānam /
children.translated_text: Then on the road he saw, even in his ancestral city, the banner of pride in the <s>Tathāgata</s>, set free [from worldly attachment],

children.text: daśabalam abhito vilambamānaṃ dhvajam anuyāna ivaindram arcyamānam // Saund_4.46 //
children.translated_text: hanging on all sides around the <s>Daśabala</s> (the Ten-Powered One), being honored as if following <s>Indra</s>'s banner.

body.text: Saundaranande mahākāvye bhāryāyācitako nāma caturthaḥ sargaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth canto named 'The Entreaty of the Wife' in the <s>Saundarananda</s> <s>mahākāvya</s>.
CANTO V

children.text: athāvatīryāśvarathadvipebhyaḥ śākyā yathāsvarddhi gṛhītaveṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Śākyas</s>, having dismounted from horses, chariots, and elephants, dressed according to their respective wealth,

children.text: mahāpaṇebhyo vyavahāriṇaś ca mahāmunau bhaktivaśāt praṇemuḥ // Saund_5.1 //
children.translated_text: and traders from the great markets, bowed before the great sage out of devotion.

children.text: ke cit praṇamyānuyayur mhūrtaṅ ke cit praṇamyārthavaśena jagmuḥ /
children.translated_text: Some, having bowed, followed for a while; some, having bowed, went about their business;

children.text: ke cit svakeṣv āvastheṣu tastuḥ kṛtvāñjalīn vikṣaṇatatparākṣāḥ // Saund_5.2 //
children.translated_text: some stood at their own stations, with palms joined and eyes intent on gazing.

children.text: buddhas tatas tatra narendramārga sroto mahadbhaktimato janasya /
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> then proceeded along the royal highway there, through the great stream of devoted people,

children.text: jagāma duūkhena vigāhamāno jalāgame srota ivāpagāyāḥ // Saund_5.3 //
children.translated_text: making his way with difficulty, like a river's current at the onset of the rains.

children.text: atho mahadbhiḥ pathi saṃpatadbhiḥ saṃpūjyamānāya tathāgatāya /
children.translated_text: Then, as the <s>Tathāgata</s> was being honored by great ones thronging on the path,

children.text: kartuṃ prañāmaṃ na śaśāka nandas tenābhireme tu guror mahimnā // Saund_5.4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s> was unable to make his obeisance, yet he delighted in the majesty of the teacher.

children.text: svaṃ cāvasaṅgaṃ pathi nirmumukṣur bhaktiṃ janasyānyamateś ca rakṣan /
children.translated_text: Wishing to free himself from his own attachment on the path, protecting the devotion of the people and the respect of others,

children.text: nandaṃ ca gehābhimukhaṃ jighṛkṣan mārgaṃ tato 'nyaṃ sugataḥ prapede // Saund_5.5 //
children.translated_text: and wishing to take hold of <s>Nanda</s> who was turning homeward, the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) took another road.

children.text: tato viviktaṃ ca viviktacetāḥ sanmārgavin mārgam abhipratasthe /
children.translated_text: Then the pure-minded knower of the true path set out upon a secluded path,

children.text: gatvāgrataś cāgryatamāya tasmai nāndīvimuktāya nanāma nadnaḥ // Saund_5.6 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Nanda</s>, going ahead, bowed before that foremost one, who was freed from [worldly] joy.

children.text: śanair vrjann eva sa gauraveṇa paṭāvṛtāṃso vinatārdhakāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Walking slowly with reverence, his shoulder covered with cloth, his upper body bent,

children.text: adhonibaddhāñjalir ūrdhvanetraḥ sagadgadaṃ vākyam idaṃ babhāṣe // Saund_5.7 //
children.translated_text: his palms joined below, his eyes raised upward, he spoke these words in a faltering voice:

children.text: prāsādasaṃstho bhavantam antaḥpraviṣṭam aśrauṣam anugrahāya /
children.translated_text: "Standing in the upper palace, I heard that you had entered the city for the purpose of bestowing grace.

children.text: atas tvarāvān aham abhyupeto gṛhasya kakṣyāmahato 'bhasūyan // Saund_5.8 //
children.translated_text: Therefore I have come in haste, resenting [the delay caused by] the enclosures of this great house."

children.text: tat sādhu sādhupriya matpriyārthaṃ tatrāstu bikṣūttama bhaikṣakālsaḥ /
children.translated_text: "So then, O best of monks, dear friend of the good, for my sake, let the time for alms be there,

children.text: asau hi madhyaṃ nabhaso yiyāsuḥ kālaṃ pratismārayatīva sūryaḥ // Saund_5.9 //
children.translated_text: for that sun, wishing to reach the middle of the sky, seems to remind [us] of the time."

children.text: ity evam uktaḥ praṇatena tena snehābhimānonmukhalocanena /
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by him who was bowing, whose eyes were raised with affection and pride,

children.text: tādṛṅnimittaṃ sugataś cakāra nāhārakṛtyaṃ sa yathā viveda // Saund_5.10 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Sugata</s> created such circumstances that he [<s>Nanda</s>] did not understand it as a matter concerning food.

children.text: tataḥ sa kṛtvā munaye praṇāmaṃ gṛhaprayāṇāya matiṃ cakāra /
children.translated_text: Then he, having made obeisance to the sage, set his mind on returning home,

children.text: anugrahārthaṃ sugatas tu tasmai pātraṃ dadau puṣkarapattranetraḥ // Saund_5.11 //
children.translated_text: but the <s>Sugata</s>, the lotus-petal-eyed one, gave him the alms-bowl for the purpose of grace.

children.text: tataḥ sa loke dadataḥ phalārthaṃ pātrasya tasyāpratimasya pātram /
children.translated_text: Then he, who in this world gives for the sake of fruit, the worthy vessel of that incomparable vessel,

children.text: jagrāha cāpagrahaṇakṣaṃābhyāṃ padmopamābhyāṃ prayataḥ karābhyām // Saund_5.12 //
children.translated_text: received it reverently with both hands, lotus-like, fit for receiving and not receiving.

children.text: parāṅmukhas tv anyamanaskam ārād vijñāya nandaḥ sugataṃ gatāstham /
children.translated_text: But <s>Nanda</s>, perceiving from afar that the <s>Sugata</s> had turned away and become absent-minded,

children.text: hastasthapātro 'pi gṛha yiyāsuḥ sasāra mārgān munim īkṣamāṇaḥ // Saund_5.13 //
children.translated_text: though holding the bowl in hand, wishing to go home, departed along the road, watching the sage.

children.text: bhāryānurāgeṇa yadā gṛhaṃ sa pātraṃ gṛhītvāpi yiyāsur eva /
children.translated_text: When, out of love for his wife, he wished to go home even after receiving the bowl,

children.text: vimohayām āsa munis tatas taṃ rathyāmukhasyāvaraṇena tasya // Saund_5.14 //
children.translated_text: the sage then bewildered him by blocking the entrance to his street.

children.text: nirmokṣabījaṃ hi dadarśa tasya jñanaṃ mṛdu kleśarajaś ca tīvram /
children.translated_text: For he saw in him the seed of liberation, soft knowledge, and intense dust of affliction,

children.text: kleśānukūlaṃ viṣayātmakaṅ ca nandaṃ yatas taṃ munir ācakarṣa // Saund_5.15 //
children.translated_text: and [saw] <s>Nanda</s> as inclined toward affliction, with sense-objects as his nature — therefore the sage drew him [away].

children.text: saṃkleśapakṣo dvividhaś ca dṛṣṭas tathā dvikalpo vyavadānapakṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: The side of defilement is seen to be twofold, and likewise the side of purification is of two kinds:

children.text: ātmāśrayo hetubalādhikasya bāhyāśrayaḥ pratyayagauravasya // Saund_5.16 //
children.translated_text: self-dependent for one in whom the force of the cause predominates, and externally dependent for one in whom the weight of conditions is greater.

children.text: ayatnato hetubalādhikas tu nirmucyate ghaṭṭitamātra eva /
children.translated_text: One in whom the force of the cause predominates is liberated effortlessly, merely upon being touched [by the teaching],

children.text: yatnena tu pratyayaneyabuddhir vimokṣam āpnoti parāśrayeṇa // Saund_5.17 //
children.translated_text: but one whose understanding must be guided by conditions attains liberation through external support, with effort.

children.text: nandaḥ sa ca pratyayaneyacetā yaṃ śiśriye tanmayatām avāpa /
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s>, whose mind was to be guided by conditions, became absorbed in whatever he resorted to;

children.text: yasmād imaṃ tatra cakāra yatnaṃ taṃ snehapaṅkān munir ujjihīrṣam // Saund_5.18 //
children.translated_text: therefore the sage made this effort there, wishing to lift him from the mire of attachment.

children.text: nandas tu duḥkhena viceṣṭamānaḥ śanair agatyā gurum anvagacchat /
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s>, however, struggling in anguish, slowly and reluctantly followed the teacher,

children.text: bhāryāmukhaṃ vīkṣaṇalolanetraṃ vicintayann ādraviśeṣakaṃ tat // Saund_5.19 //
children.translated_text: thinking of his wife's face, with eyes restless with longing, and that moist ornamental mark.

children.text: tato munis taṃ priyamālyahāraṃ vasantamāsena kṛtābhihāram /
children.translated_text: Then the sage led him — who loved garlands and necklaces, who had been adorned by the spring month,

children.text: nināya bhagnapramadāvihāraṃ vidyāvihārābhimataṃ vihāram // Saund_5.20 //
children.translated_text: whose pleasure with women was broken — to the monastery (<s>vihāra</s>) intended for the pursuit of learning.

children.text: dīnaṃ mahākāruṇikas tatas taṃ dṛṣṭvā muhūrtaṃ karuṇāyamānaḥ /
children.translated_text: The greatly compassionate one, seeing him dejected, feeling compassion for a moment,

children.text: kareṇa cakdrāṅkatalena mūrdhni pasparśa caivedam uvāca cainam // Saund_5.21 //
children.translated_text: touched his head with his hand marked with the moon-sign, and said this to him:

children.text: yāvan na hiṃsraḥ samupaiti kālaḥ śamāya tāvat kuru saumya buddhim /
children.translated_text: "Before the violent time [of death] approaches, cultivate the intention for peace, gentle one;

children.text: sarvāsv avasthāsv iha vartamānaḥ sarvābhisāreṇa nihanti mṛtyuḥ // Saund_5.22 //
children.translated_text: death strikes down [all beings] existing in every state here, with every assault."

children.text: sādhāraṇāt svapnanibhādasārāl lolaṃ manaḥ kāmasukhān niyaccha /
children.translated_text: "Restrain the fickle mind from sensual pleasures, which are shared by all, dream-like, and without essence,

children.text: havyair ivāgneḥ pavaneritasya lokasya kāmair na hi tṛptir asti // Saund_5.23 //
children.translated_text: for the world is never satiated with pleasures, like a fire [fed] by oblations and fanned by wind."

children.text: śraddhādhanaṃ śreṣṭhatamaṃ dhanebhyaḥ prajñārasas tṛptir rasebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: "The wealth of faith is the most excellent of all riches; the savor of wisdom is the most satisfying of all savors;

children.text: pradhānamadhyātmasukhaṃ sukhebhyo vidyāratir duḥkhatatmā ratibhyaḥ // Saund_5.24 //
children.translated_text: the highest happiness is the inner happiness of the self; delight in knowledge is the most free from suffering of all delights."

children.text: hitasya vaktā pravaraḥ suṛdbhyo dharmāya khedo guṇavān śramebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: "A speaker of what is beneficial is the best of friends; toil for <s>dharma</s> is the most virtuous of all labors;

children.text: jñānāya kṛtyaṃ paramaṃ kriyābhyaḥ kim indriyāṇām upagamya dāsyam // Saund_5.25 //
children.translated_text: the supreme act among all activities is for the sake of knowledge — why submit to the slavery of the senses?"

children.text: tan niścitaṃ bhīklamaśugviyuktaṃ pareṣv anāyattam ahāryam anyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: "Therefore choose that which is certain, free from fear, fatigue, and sorrow, independent of others, and unassailable by any —

children.text: nityaṃ śivaṃ śāntisukhaṃ vṛṇīṣva kim indriyārthārtham anartham ūḍhvā // Saund_5.26 //
children.translated_text: the eternally auspicious, the bliss of peace. Why bear calamity for the sake of sense-objects?"

children.text: jarāsamā nāsty amṛjā prajānāṃ vyādheḥ samo nāsti jagaty anarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: "There is no defilement for beings equal to old age; there is no misfortune in the world equal to disease;

children.text: mṛtyoḥ samaṃ nāsti bhayaṃ pṛthivyām etat trayaṃ khalv avaśena sevyam // Saund_5.27 //
children.translated_text: there is no fear on earth equal to death — yet this triad must be served perforce."

children.text: snehena kaś cin na samo 'sti pāśaḥ sroto na tṛṇāsamam asti hāri /
children.translated_text: "No bond equals attachment; no current is as captivating as craving;

children.text: rāgāgninā nāsti samas tathāgnis tac cet trayaṃ nāsti sukhaṃ ca te 'sti // Saund_5.28 //
children.translated_text: no fire equals the fire of passion — but if that triad [of attachment, craving, passion] is absent, happiness is yours."

children.text: avaśyabhāvi priyaviprayogas tasmāc ca śoko niyataṃ viṣevyaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Separation from the beloved is inevitable; therefore grief must invariably be endured;

children.text: śokena conmādam upeyivāṃso rājarṣayo 'nye 'py avaśā viceluḥ // Saund_5.29 //
children.translated_text: and royal sages and others, driven to madness by grief, have helplessly wandered astray."

children.text: prajñāmayaṃ varma badhāna tasmān no kṣāntinighnasya hi śokabāṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, put on the armor of wisdom, for the arrows of sorrow cannot slay one who possesses forbearance;

children.text: mahac ca dagdhuṃ bhavakakṣajālaṃ saṃdhukṣayālpāgnim ivātmatejaḥ // Saund_5.30 //
children.translated_text: and kindle your own spiritual fire like a small flame to burn the great thicket of worldly existence."

children.text: yathauṣadhair hastagataiḥ savidyo na daśyate kaś cana pannagena /
children.translated_text: "Just as one who is skilled, holding herbs in hand, is not bitten by any serpent,

children.text: tathānapekṣo jitalokamoho na daśyate śokabhujaṅgamena // Saund_5.31 //
children.translated_text: so one who is free from regard [for worldly things] and has conquered the world's delusion is not bitten by the serpent of sorrow."

children.text: āsthāya yogaṃ parigamya tattvaṃ na trāsam āgacchati mṛtyukāle /
children.translated_text: "Having resorted to <s>yoga</s> and comprehended the truth, one does not become frightened at the time of death,

children.text: ābaddhavarmā sudhanuḥ kṛtāstro jigīṣayā śūra ivāhavasthaḥ // Saund_5.32 //
children.translated_text: like a warrior standing in battle, having put on his armor, with a fine bow and arrows prepared, with the desire to conquer."

children.text: ity evam uktaḥ sa tathāgatena sarveṣu bhūteṣv anukampakena /
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, who has compassion for all beings,

children.text: dhṛṣṭaṃ girāntarhṛdayena sīdaṃs tatheti nandaḥ sugataṃ babhāṣe // Saund_5.33 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s>, sinking in his heart while bold in speech, said 'So be it' to the <s>Sugata</s>.

children.text: atha pramādāc ca tam ujjihīrṣan matvāgamasyaiva ca pātrabhūtam /
children.translated_text: Then, wishing to lift him from heedlessness, and considering him a worthy vessel for the teaching,

children.text: pravrājayānanda śamāya nandam ity abravīn maitramanā maharṣiḥ // Saund_5.34 //
children.translated_text: the great sage, with a benevolent mind, said: '<s>Ānanda</s>, ordain <s>Nanda</s> for the sake of peace.'

children.text: nandaṃ tato 'ntarmanasā rudantam ehīti vaidehamunir jagāda /
children.translated_text: Then the sage of <s>Vaideha</s> said 'Come' to <s>Nanda</s>, who was weeping inwardly,

children.text: śanais tatas taṃ samupetya nando na pravrajiṣyāmy aham ity uvāca // Saund_5.35 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Nanda</s>, slowly approaching him, said: 'I will not go forth [into the renunciant life].'

children.text: śrutvātha nandasya manīṣitaṃ tad buddhāya vaidehamuniḥ śaśaṃsa /
children.translated_text: Then the sage of <s>Vaideha</s>, having heard <s>Nanda</s>'s intention, reported it to the <s>Buddha</s>,

children.text: saṃśrutya tasmād api tasya bhāvaṃ mahāmunir nandam uvāca bhūyaḥ // Saund_5.36 //
children.translated_text: and having understood his disposition from him as well, the great sage again spoke to <s>Nanda</s>:

children.text: mayy agraje pravrajite 'jitātman bhrātṣṛv anupravrajiteṣu cāsmān /
children.translated_text: "Since I, your elder brother, have gone forth, O uncontrolled one, and since your brothers have followed us into renunciation,

children.text: jñātīṃś tasmād api tasya bhāvaṃ mahāmunir nandam uvāca bhūyaḥ // Saund_5.37 //
children.translated_text: therefore, knowing the disposition [of <s>Nanda</s>], the great sage again spoke to <s>Nanda</s>."

children.text: rājarṣayas te viditā na nūnaṃ vanāni ye śiśriyire hasantaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Surely those royal sages are not known to you, who laughingly resorted to the forests,

children.text: niṣṭhīvya kāmān upaśāntikāmāḥ kāmeṣu naivaṃ kṛpaṇeṣu saktāḥ // Saund_5.38 //
children.translated_text: spitting out pleasures, desiring tranquility — not thus attached to wretched pleasures."

children.text: bhūyaḥ samālokya gṛheṣu doṣān niśāmya tattyāgakṛtaṃ ca śarma /
children.translated_text: "Once more, having considered the faults in household life and observed the peace achieved by renunciation,

children.text: naivāsti moktuṃ maitrālayaṃ te deśaṃ mumūrṣor iva sopasargam // Saund_5.39 //
children.translated_text: there is no reason not to leave the abode of attachment — like a dying man [leaving] a plague-ridden place."

children.text: saṃsārakāntāraparāyaṇasya śive kathaṃ te pathi nārurukṣā /
children.translated_text: "How is it that you, bound for the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s>, have no desire to ascend the auspicious path,

children.text: āropyamāṇasya tam eva mārgaṃ bhraṣṭasya sārthād iva sārthikasya // Saund_5.40 //
children.translated_text: being led onto that very road, like a merchant who has strayed from the caravan?"

children.text: yaḥ sarvato veśmani dahyamāne śayita mohān na tato vyapeyāt /
children.translated_text: "He who, when his house is burning on all sides, would lie there in delusion and not flee,

children.text: kālāgninā vyādhijarāśikhena loke pradīpte sa bhavet pramattaḥ // Saund_5.41 //
children.translated_text: would be heedless indeed when the world is ablaze with the fire of time, whose flames are disease and old age."

children.text: prañīyamānaś ca yathā vadhāya matto hasec ca pralapec ca vadhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: And just as a condemned man being led to execution might laugh in his madness and babble,

children.text: mṛtyau tathā tiṣṭhati pāśahaste śocyaḥ pramādyan viparītacetāḥ // Saund_5.42 //
children.translated_text: So too, pitiable is the one who revels heedlessly with confused mind while <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death) stands with noose in hand. // 5.42 //

children.text: yadā narendrāś ca kuṭumbinaś ca vihāya badhūṃś ca parigrahāṃś ca /
children.translated_text: When kings and householders alike, having abandoned their wives and possessions,

children.text: yayuś ca yāsyanti ca yānti caiva priyeṣv anityeṣv kuto 'nurodhaḥ // Saund_5.43 //
children.translated_text: Have gone, will go, and are even now going — what point is attachment to impermanent loved ones? // 5.43 //

children.text: kiṃ cin na paśyāmi ratasya yatra tad anyabhāvena bhaven na duḥkham /
children.translated_text: I see nothing in which one who delights does not [eventually] suffer through its transformation;

children.text: tasmāt kva cin na kṣamate prasktir yadi kṣamas tadvigamān na śokaḥ // Saund_5.44 //
children.translated_text: Therefore attachment to anything is unfit — if one is capable [of seeing this], there is no grief at its departure. // 5.44 //

children.text: tat saumya lolaṃ parigamya lokaṃ māyopamaṃ citram ivendrajālam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, O gentle one, having recognized this fickle world, illusory like a magician's spectacle,

children.text: priyābhidhāntaṃ tayja mohajālaṃ chettuṃ matis te yadi duḥkhajālam // Saund_5.45 //
children.translated_text: Abandon this net of delusion called 'the beloved' — if you have the resolve to cut through the net of suffering. // 5.45 //

children.text: varaṃ hitodarkam aniṣṭam annaṃ na svādu yat syād ahitānubaddham /
children.translated_text: Better is unpleasant food that leads to benefit than what is sweet but bound to harm;

children.text: yasmād ahaṃ tvā viniyojayāmi śive śucau vartmani vipriye 'pi // Saund_5.46 //
children.translated_text: For I am directing you onto the auspicious and pure path, even though it is unpleasant. // 5.46 //

children.text: bālasya dhārtrī vinigṛhya loṣṭaṃ yathoddharaty āsyapuṭapraviṣṭam /
children.translated_text: Just as a nurse, restraining a child, removes a clod that has entered its mouth,

children.text: tathojjihīrṣuḥ khalu rāgaśalyaṃ tat tvām avocaṃ paruṣaṃ hitāya // Saund_5.47 //
children.translated_text: So too, wishing to extract the thorn of passion, I have spoken harshly to you for your benefit. // 5.47 //

children.text: aniṣṭam apy auṣadham āturāya dadāti vaidyaś ca yathā nigṛhya /
children.translated_text: Just as a physician forcibly gives even unpleasant medicine to a sick person,

children.text: tadvan mayoktaṃ pratikūlam etat tubhyaṃ hitodarkam anugrahāya // Saund_5.48 //
children.translated_text: So this disagreeable [speech] has been spoken by me for you, leading to benefit, out of kindness. // 5.48 //

children.text: tad yāvad eva kṣañasaṃnipāto na mṛtyur āgacchati yāvad eva /
children.translated_text: Therefore, as long as the moment has not yet slipped away, as long as death has not yet arrived,

children.text: yāvad vayo yogavidhau samarthaṃ buddhiṃ kuru śreyasi tāvad eva // Saund_5.49 //
children.translated_text: As long as your youth is capable of the discipline of practice — set your mind on the highest good just so long. // 5.49 //

children.text: ity evam uktaḥ sa vināyakena hitaiṣinā kāruṇikena nandaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by the Guide, who wished his welfare and was compassionate, <s>Nanda</s>

children.text: kartāsmi sarvaṃ bhagavan vacas te tathā yathājñāpaysīty uvāca // Saund_5.50 //
children.translated_text: Said: 'I shall do everything as you command, O <s>Bhagavān</s> — just as you instruct.' // 5.50 //

children.text: ādāya vaidehamunis tatas taṃ nināya saṃśliṣya viceṣṭamānam /
children.translated_text: Then the sage of <s>Videha</s> lineage took him up and led him, embracing the struggling [<s>Nanda</s>],

children.text: vyayojayac cāsrupariplutākṣaṃ keśaśriyaṃ chattranibhasya mūrdhnaḥ // Saund_5.51 //
children.translated_text: And removed the glory of hair from the head of him whose eyes were flooded with tears, [the head] resembling an umbrella. // 5.51 //

children.text: atho nataṃ tasya mukhaṃ sabāṣpaṃ pravāsyamāneṣu śiroruheṣu /
children.translated_text: And then his face, downcast and tearful as the locks were being removed,

children.text: vakrāgranālaṃ nalinaṃ taḍāge varṣodakalinnam ivābabhāse // Saund_5.52 //
children.translated_text: Appeared like a lotus in a pond with curved stem-tip, drenched by rainwater. // 5.52 //

children.text: nandas tatas tarukaṣāyaviraktavāsāś cintāvaśo navagṛhita iva dvipendraḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s>, then, wearing ochre-dyed garments made from tree bark, absorbed in thought like a newly captured lordly elephant,

children.text: pūrṇaḥ śaśī bahulapakṣagataḥ kṣapānte bālātpena pariṣikta ivābabhāse // Saund_5.53 //
children.translated_text: Appeared like the full moon entering the dark fortnight, at the end of night, as if sprinkled with a thin [veil of] cloud. // 5.53 //

body.text: Saundaranande mahākāvye nandapravrājano nāma pañcamaḥ sargaḥ /
body.translated_text: In the <s>Saundarananda Mahākāvya</s>, this is the Fifth Canto, called 'The Going Forth of <s>Nanda</s>.'
CANTO VI

children.text: tato hṛte bhartari gauraveṇa prītau hṛtāyām aratau kṛtāyām /
children.translated_text: Then, when her husband had been taken away by [the Buddha's] authority, her joy stolen and discontent created,

children.text: tatraiva harmyopari vartamānā na sundarī saiva tadā babhāse // Saund_6.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>Sundarī</s>, remaining there on top of the palace, no longer shone as before. // 6.1 //

children.text: sā bhartur abhyāgamanapratīkṣā gavākṣam ākramya payodharābhyām /
children.translated_text: She, awaiting her husband's return, pressing her breasts against the window,

children.text: dvāronmukhī calayoktrakā lalambe mukhena tiryaṅnatakuṇḍalena // Saund_6.2 //
children.translated_text: Hung facing the door, with swaying ornamental cords, her face tilted sideways with dangling earrings. // 6.2 //

children.text: vilambhaārā calayoktrakā sā tasmād vimānād vinatā cakāśe /
children.translated_text: She with the swaying ornamental cords, leaning from that palace, appeared

children.text: tapaḥksayād apsarasāṃ vareva cyutaṃ vimānāt priyam īkṣamāṇā // Saund_6.3 //
children.translated_text: Like the foremost of <s>Apsaras</s> (celestial nymphs), gazing at a beloved who has fallen from an aerial chariot due to the exhaustion of merit. // 6.3 //

children.text: sā khedasaṃsvinnalalāṭakena niśvāsanīṣpītaviśeṣakeṇa /
children.translated_text: She stood with her face — its forehead moist with the sweat of distress, its ornamental mark absorbed by her sighs,

children.text: cintācalākṣeṇa mukhena tasthau bartāram anyatra viśaṅkamānā // Saund_6.4 //
children.translated_text: Its eyes restless with anxiety — suspecting her husband to be elsewhere. // 6.4 //

children.text: tataś cirasthānaparśrameña sthitaiva paryaṅkatale papāta /
children.translated_text: Then, exhausted from standing so long, while still standing she fell onto the surface of the couch,

children.text: tiryak ca śiśye pravikīrṇahārā sapādukaikārthavilambapādā // Saund_6.5 //
children.translated_text: And lay on her side, her necklace scattered, one foot dangling with its sandal hanging down. // 6.5 //

children.text: athātra kā cit pramadā sabāṣpāṃ tāṃ duḥkhitāṃ draṣṭum anīpsamānā /
children.translated_text: Then a certain woman, tearful, not wishing to see her in such distress,

children.text: prāsādasopānatalapraṇādaṃ cakāra padbhyāṃ sahasā rudantī // Saund_6.6 //
children.translated_text: Made a sound on the stairway landing of the palace with her feet, weeping suddenly. // 6.6 //

children.text: tasyāś ca sopānatalapraṇādaṃ śrutaiva tūrṇaṃ punar utpapāta /
children.translated_text: And hearing the sound on the stairway landing, she [<s>Sundarī</s>] quickly sprang up again,

children.text: prītyā prasaktaiva ca saṃjaharṣa priyopayānaṃ pariśaṅkamānā // Saund_6.7 //
children.translated_text: And was seized with joy, eagerly thrilled, suspecting it to be her beloved's approach. // 6.7 //

children.text: sā trāsayantī valabhīpuṭasthān pārāvatān nūpuranisvanena /
children.translated_text: She, startling the pigeons perched on the balcony ledges with the jingling of her anklets,

children.text: sopānakukṣiṅ prasasāra harṣād bhraṣṭaṃ dukūlāntam acintayantī // Saund_6.8 //
children.translated_text: Rushed along the stairway corridor in her joy, heedless of the trailing edge of her garment slipping. // 6.8 //

children.text: tām aṅganāṃ prekṣya ca vipralabdhā niśvasya bhūyaḥ śayanaṃ prapede /
children.translated_text: But seeing that woman and realizing she had been deceived, she sighed and returned to her bed,

children.text: vivarṇavaktrā na rarāja cāśu vivarṇacandreva himāgame dyauḥ // Saund_6.9 //
children.translated_text: And with her pallid face she did not shine — like the sky with a pale moon at the onset of winter. // 6.9 //

children.text: sā duḥkhitā bhartur adarśanena kāmena kopena ca dahyamānā /
children.translated_text: She, grieving at not seeing her husband, burning with desire and anger,

children.text: kṛtvā kare vaktram upopaviṣṭā cintānadīṃ śokajalāṃ tatāra // Saund_6.10 //
children.translated_text: Sat with her face in her hands and crossed the river of anxiety with its waters of sorrow. // 6.10 //

children.text: tasyā mukhaṃ padmasapatnabhūtaṃ pāṇau sthitaṅ pallavarāgatāmre /
children.translated_text: Her face, which rivaled the lotus, resting on her hand with its coppery-red tender palm,

children.text: chāyāmayasyāmbhasi paṅkajasya babhau nataṃ padmam ivopariṣṭāt // Saund_6.11 //
children.translated_text: Appeared like a lotus bent over above a shadowy lotus reflected in water. // 6.11 //

children.text: sā strīsvabhāvena vicintya tat tad dṛṣṭānurāge 'bhimukhe 'pi patyau /
children.translated_text: She, by feminine nature imagining various things, even though her husband's affection was visibly directed toward her,

children.text: dharmāśrite tattvam avindamānā saṃkalpya tat tad vilalāpa tat tat // Saund_6.12 //
children.translated_text: Not discerning the truth because he had resorted to <s>Dharma</s>, imagined various things and lamented variously: // 6.12 //

children.text: eṣyāmy anāśyānaviśeṣakāyāṃ tvayīti kṛtvā mayi tāṃ pratijñām /
children.translated_text: 'Having made that promise to me — "I shall return before the ornamental mark on your forehead has dried" —

children.text: kasmān nu hetor dayitapratijñaḥ so 'dya priya me vitathapratijñaḥ // Saund_6.13 //
children.translated_text: For what reason has my beloved, once true to his word, today become false to his promise?' // 6.13 //

children.text: āryasya sādhoḥ karuṇātmakasya mannityabhīror atidakṣiṇasya /
children.translated_text: 'In one who is noble, virtuous, compassionate by nature, always devoted to me, and exceedingly generous,

children.text: kuto vikāro 'yam abhūtapūrvaḥ svenāparāgeṇa mamāpacārāt // Saund_6.14 //
children.translated_text: Whence comes this unprecedented change — through his own indifference, or through my fault?' // 6.14 //

children.text: ratipriyasya priyavartino me priyasya nūnaṃ hṛdayaṃ viraktam /
children.translated_text: 'The heart of my beloved, who delights in love and is attentive to me, must surely have become disenchanted;

children.text: tathāpi rāgo yadi tasya hi syān maccittarakṣī na sa nāgataḥ syāt // Saund_6.15 //
children.translated_text: Yet if he still had affection for me, being mindful of my feelings, he would not have failed to return.' // 6.15 //

children.text: rūpeṇa bhāvena ca madviśiṣtā priyeṇa dṛṣṭā niyataṃ tato 'nyā /
children.translated_text: 'Surely another woman, superior to me in beauty and character, has been seen by my beloved;

children.text: tathā hi kṛtvā mayi moghasāntvaṃ lagnāṃ satīṃ mām agamad vihāya // Saund_6.16 //
children.translated_text: For thus, having offered me empty consolation, he departed abandoning me though I clung to him.' // 6.16 //

children.text: bhaktiṃ sa buddhaṃ prati yām avocat tasya prayātuṃ mayi sopadeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The devotion he professed toward the <s>Buddha</s> was his pretext for leaving me;

children.text: munau prasādo yadi tasya hi syān mṛtyor ivogrād anṛtād bibhīyāt // Saund_6.17 //
children.translated_text: For if he truly had reverence for the sage, he would shrink from falsehood as from terrible death.' // 6.17 //

children.text: lekārtham ādarśanam anyacitto vibhūṣayantya mama dhārayitvā /
children.translated_text: 'Having held my mirror while I adorned myself for applying the forehead mark, though his mind was elsewhere —

children.text: bibharti so 'nyasya janasya taṅ cen namo 'stu tasmai calasauhṛdāya // Saund_6.18 //
children.translated_text: If he now carries it for another person, salutations to that one of fickle friendship!' // 6.18 //

children.text: necchanti yāḥ śokam avāptum evaṃ śraddhātum arhanti na tā narāṇām /
children.translated_text: 'Those women who do not wish to obtain such grief should not place their trust in men;

children.text: kva cānuvṛttir mayi sāsya pūrvaṃ tyāgaḥ kva cāyaṃ janavat kṣaṇena // Saund_6.19 //
children.translated_text: Where now is his former devotion to me, and where this abandonment in an instant, as if I were a stranger?' // 6.19 //

children.text: ity evamādi priyaviprakutā priye 'nyad āśaṅkya ca sā jagāda /
children.translated_text: Thus and more she spoke, suspecting her beloved of another [woman], distressed by separation from her beloved,

children.text: saṃbhrāntam āruhya ca tad vimānaṃ tāṃ strī sabāṣpā giram ity uvāca // Saund_6.20 //
children.translated_text: And a tearful woman, having hastily ascended that palace, spoke these words to her: // 6.20 //

children.text: yuvāpi tāvat priyadarśano 'pi saubhāgyabhāgvyābhijanānvito 'pi /
children.translated_text: 'Though he is young, handsome, blessed with good fortune, noble birth, and lineage,

children.text: yas tvāṃ priyo nābhyacarat kadā cit tam anyathā yāsyatikātarāsi // Saund_6.21 //
children.translated_text: Your beloved who never once behaved improperly toward you — you are anxious that he will become otherwise! // 6.21 //

children.text: mā svāminaṃ svāmini doṣato gāḥ priyaṃ priyārhaṃ priyakāriṇaṃ tam /
children.translated_text: 'Do not, O lady, attribute fault to your lord — to that beloved who is worthy of love and who acts lovingly;

children.text: na sa tvad anyāṃ pramadām avaiti svacakravākyā iva cakravākaḥ // Saund_6.22 //
children.translated_text: He knows no woman other than you, like a <s>cakravāka</s> (sheldrake) with his own mate.' // 6.22 //

children.text: sa tu tvadarthaṃ gṛhavāsam īpsan jijīviṣus tvatparitoṣahetoḥ /
children.translated_text: 'But he, desiring household life for your sake, wishing to live for your happiness,

children.text: bhrātrā kilāryeṇa tathāgatena pravrājito netrajalārdravaktraḥ // Saund_6.23 //
children.translated_text: Was, it is said, made to go forth by his noble brother, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, with his face wet with tears.' // 6.23 //

children.text: śrutvā tato bhartari tāṃ pravṛttiṃ savepathuḥ sā sahasotpapāta /
children.translated_text: Then, hearing that news about her husband, she [<s>Sundarī</s>] sprang up suddenly, trembling,

children.text: pragṛhya bāhū virurāva coccair hṛdīva digdhābhihatā kareṇuḥ // Saund_6.24 //
children.translated_text: And raising her arms, wailed aloud, like a she-elephant struck in the heart by a poisoned arrow. // 6.24 //

children.text: sā rdoanāroṣitaraktadṛṣṭiḥ saṃtāpasaṃkṣobhitagātrayaṣṭiḥ /
children.translated_text: She, her reddened eyes inflamed by grief and anger, her body-stalk shaken by burning anguish,

children.text: papāta śīrṇākulahārayaṣṭiḥ phalātibhārād iva cūtayaṣṭiḥ // Saund_6.25 //
children.translated_text: Fell, her string of pearls broken and disheveled, like a mango branch under the excessive weight of fruit. // 6.25 //

children.text: sā padmarāgaṃ vasanaṃ vasānā padmānanā padmadalāyatākṣī /
children.translated_text: She, wearing a garment of ruby-red, lotus-faced, with eyes long as lotus petals,

children.text: padmā vipadmā patiteva lakṣmīḥ śuśoṣa padmasrag ivātapena // Saund_6.26 //
children.translated_text: Withered like <s>Padmā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) without her lotus, fallen — like a lotus garland [withered] by the sun. // 6.26 //

children.text: saṃcintya saṃcintya guṇāṃś ca bhartur dīrghaṃ niśaśavāsa tatāma caiva /
children.translated_text: Thinking again and again of her husband's virtues, she sighed deeply and became rigid,

children.text: vibhūṣaśrīnihite prakoṣṭhe tāmre karāgre ca vinirdudhāva // Saund_6.27 //
children.translated_text: And wept bitterly, with her forearms where ornaments and beauty were placed, and with her coppery-red fingertips. // 6.27 //

children.text: na bhuṣaṇārtho mama saṃpratīti sā dikṣu cikṣepa vibhūṣaṇāni /
children.translated_text: 'I have no use for ornaments now' — saying this, she flung her ornaments in all directions;

children.text: nirbhuṣaṇā sā patitā cakāśe viśīrṇapuṣpastabakā lateva // Saund_6.28 //
children.translated_text: Without ornaments she lay fallen, appearing like a vine whose clusters of blossoms have been scattered. // 6.28 //

children.text: dhṛtaḥ priyeṇāyam abhūn mameti rukmatsaruṃ darpaṇam āliliṅge /
children.translated_text: 'This was held by my beloved for me' — and she embraced the gold-handled mirror;

children.text: yatnāc ca vinyastatamālapattrau ruṣṭeva dhṛṣṭaṃ pramamārja gaṇḍau // Saund_6.29 //
children.translated_text: And with effort, she angrily and boldly wiped away the <s>tamālapattra</s> (decorative leaf-marks) that had been carefully applied to her cheeks. // 6.29 //

children.text: sā cakravākvīka bhṛśaṃ cukūja śyenāgrapakṣakṣatacakravākā /
children.translated_text: She wailed piteously like a <s>cakravākī</s> (female sheldrake) whose <s>cakravāka</s> mate has been wounded by a hawk's talons,

children.text: vispardhamāneva vimānasaṃstahiḥ pārāvataiḥ kūjanalokaṇṭhaiḥ // Saund_6.30 //
children.translated_text: As if competing with the pigeons perched on the palace, whose throats were [likewise] cooing. // 6.30 //

children.text: vicitramṛdvāstaraṇe 'pi suptā vaiḍūryavajrapratimaṇḍite 'pi /
children.translated_text: Though she lay on a couch of varied and soft coverings, adorned with <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl) and diamond,

children.text: rukmāṅgapāde śayane mahārhe na śarma lebhe pariceṣṭamānā // Saund_6.31 //
children.translated_text: With golden-legged bedstead of great worth, she found no comfort, tossing restlessly. // 6.31 //

children.text: saṃdṛṣya bhartuś ca vibhūṣañāni vāsāṃsi vīṇāprabhṛtiṃś ca līlāḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing her husband's ornaments, garments, and amusements such as the <s>vīṇā</s> (lute) and the like,

children.text: tamo viveśābhinanāda coccaiḥ paṅkāvatīrṇeva ca saṃsasāda // Saund_6.32 //
children.translated_text: She entered into darkness and wailed aloud, and sank down as if mired in mud. // 6.32 //

children.text: sā sundarī śvāsacalodarī hi vajrāgnisaṃbhinnadarīguheva /
children.translated_text: <s>Sundarī</s>, with her belly heaving with sighs, like a mountain cavern split open by thunderbolt and fire,

children.text: śokāgnināntardhṛdi dahyamānā vibhrāntacitteva tadā babhūva // Saund_6.33 //
children.translated_text: Burning within her heart with the fire of grief, became as if bewildered in mind. // 6.33 //

children.text: ruroda mamlau virurāva jaglau babhrāma tasthau vilalāpa dadhyau /
children.translated_text: She wept, she wilted, she wailed, she swallowed [her cries], she wandered, she stood still, she lamented, she brooded,

children.text: cakāra roṣaṃ vicakāra mālyaṃ cakarta vaktraṃ vicakarṣa vastram // Saund_6.34 //
children.translated_text: She showed anger, she tore apart her garland, she scratched her face, she pulled at her garment. // 6.34 //

children.text: tāṃ cārudantīṃ prasabhaṃ rudantīṃ saṃśrutya nāryaḥ paramābhitaptāḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing her — beautiful-toothed, weeping violently — the women, deeply distressed,

children.text: antargṛhād āruruhur vimānaṃ trāsena kiṃnarya ivādripṛṣṭham // Saund_6.35 //
children.translated_text: Ascended from the inner chambers to the palace roof, like <s>Kinnarī</s> women [ascending] a mountain peak in alarm. // 6.35 //

children.text: bāṣpeṇa tāḥ klinnaviṣaṇṇavaktrā varṣeṇa padminya ivārdrapadmāḥ /
children.translated_text: They, with tear-stained and dejected faces, like lotuses in a pool moist with rain,

children.text: sthānānurūpeṇa yathābhimānaṃ nililyire tām anu dahyamānāḥ // Saund_6.36 //
children.translated_text: Concealed themselves according to their station and as befitting their dignity, burning in sympathy with her. // 6.36 //

children.text: tābhir vṛtā harmyatale 'ṅganābhiś cintātanuḥ sā sutanur babhāse /
children.translated_text: Surrounded by those women on the palace terrace, she, slender with grief, appeared

children.text: śatahradābhiḥ pariveṣṭiteva śaśāṅkalekhā śaradbhramadhye // Saund_6.37 //
children.translated_text: Like a crescent of the moon in the middle of an autumn cloud, encircled by streaks of lightning. // 6.37 //

children.text: yā tatra tāsāṃ vacasopapannā mānyā ca tasyā vayasādhikā ca /
children.translated_text: One among them who was endowed with eloquence, respected, and senior in age to her,

children.text: sā pṛṣṭhatas tāṃ tu samāliliṅge pramṛhya cāśrūṇi vacāṃsy uvāca // Saund_6.38 //
children.translated_text: Embraced her from behind, and wiping away her tears, spoke these words: // 6.38 //

children.text: rājarṣivadhvās tava nānurūpo dharmāśrite bhartari jātu śokaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For the wife of a royal sage, grief is never fitting when her husband has resorted to <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: ikṣvākuvaṃśe hy abhikāṅkṣitāni dāyādyabhūtāni tapovanāni // Saund_6.39 //
children.translated_text: For in the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> lineage, retreats in the forest are coveted as hereditary inheritance.' // 6.39 //

children.text: prāyeṇa mokṣāya viniḥsṛtānāṃ śākyarṣabhāṇāṃ viditāḥ striyas te /
children.translated_text: 'You must surely know the women of the foremost <s>Śākya</s> bulls who have gone forth for liberation,

children.text: tapovanānīva gṛhāṇi yāsāṃ sādhvīvrataṃ kāmavadāsritānām // Saund_6.40 //
children.translated_text: Whose homes were like hermitages, who were devoted to the vow of chastity even while living amid pleasures.' // 6.40 //

children.text: yady anyayā rūpaguṇādhikatvād bhartā hṛtas te kuru bāṣpamokṣam /
children.translated_text: 'If your husband has been taken by another woman superior in beauty and virtue, then let your tears flow;

children.text: manasvinī rūpavatī guṇādhyā hṛdi kṣate kātra hi nāśru muñcet // Saund_6.41 //
children.translated_text: For what woman of pride, beauty, and virtue would not shed tears when wounded in the heart?' // 6.41 //

children.text: athāpi kiṃ cid vyasanaṃ prapanno mā caiva tad bhūt sadṛśo 'tra bāṣpaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'But if he has encountered some misfortune — may that not be so! — then tears would be appropriate;

children.text: ato viśiṣṭaṃ na hi duḥkham asti kulodgatāyāḥ patidevatāyāḥ // Saund_6.42 //
children.translated_text: For there is no greater sorrow than this for a woman of noble birth whose husband is her deity.' // 6.42 //

children.text: atha tv idānīṃ laḍitaḥ sukhena svasthaḥ phalastho vyasnāny adṛṣtvā /
children.translated_text: 'But if now, having been pampered with comforts, sound in health, established in fruition, not having seen misfortunes,

children.text: vītaspṛho dharmam anuprapannaḥ kiṃ viklave rodiṣi harṣakāle // Saund_6.43 //
children.translated_text: He has followed <s>Dharma</s>, free from craving — why do you weep in distress, when this is a time for rejoicing?' // 6.43 //

children.text: ity evam uktāpi bahuprakāraṃ snehāt tayā naiva dhṛtiṃ cakāra /
children.translated_text: Though addressed thus in many ways, she [<s>Sundarī</s>] out of affection showed no composure from that [woman's words];

children.text: athāparā tāṃ manaso 'nukūlaṃ kālopapannaṃ praṇayād uvāca // Saund_6.44 //
children.translated_text: Then another woman spoke to her affectionately, with words agreeable to her mind and suited to the occasion: // 6.44 //

children.text: bravīmi satyaṃ suviniścitaṃ me prāptaṃ priyaṃ drakṣyasi śīghram eva /
children.translated_text: 'I speak the truth — I am firmly convinced — you will see your beloved return very soon;'

children.text: tvayā vinā sthāsyati tatra nāsau sattvāṣrayaś cetanayeva hīnaḥ // Saund_6.45 //
children.translated_text: Without you, he will not remain there, deprived of the support of his being, as if bereft of consciousness. // Saund_6.45 //

children.text: aṅke 'pi lakṣmyā na sa nirvṛtaḥ syāt tvaṃ tasya pārśve yadi tatra na syāḥ /
children.translated_text: Even in the lap of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, he would not find contentment if you were not by his side;

children.text: āpatsu kṛcchrāsv api cāgatāsu tvāṃ paśyatas tasya bhaven na duḥkham // Saund_6.46 //
children.translated_text: And even when dire calamities befall, there would be no sorrow for him as long as he sees you. // Saund_6.46 //

children.text: tvaṃ nirvṛtiṃ gaccha niyaccha bāṣpaṃ taptāśrumokṣāt parirakṣa cakṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: Find your peace, restrain your tears, and protect your eyes from the shedding of hot tears;

children.text: yas tasya bhāvas tvayi yaś ca rāgo na raṃsyate tvadvirahāt sa dharme // Saund_6.47 //
children.translated_text: The affection and passion he has for you — he will not delight in the <s>Dharma</s> while separated from you. // Saund_6.47 //

children.text: syād atra nāsau kulasattvagoyāt kāṣāyam ādāya vihāsyatīti /
children.translated_text: If you think, 'He will not, out of the nobility of his family and character, cast aside the ochre robe' —

children.text: anātmanādāya gṛhonmukhasya punar vimoktuṃ ka ivāsti doṣaḥ // Saund_6.48 //
children.translated_text: what fault is there if one who took it unwillingly and is inclined toward home should give it up again? // Saund_6.48 //

children.text: ity yuvatijanena sāntvyamānā hṛtahṛdayā ramaṇena sundarī sā /
children.translated_text: Thus consoled by the company of young women, that <s>Sundarī</s>, whose heart had been stolen by her beloved,

children.text: dramiḍam abhimukhī pureva rambhā kṣitim agamat parivāritāpsarobhiḥ // Saund_6.49 //
children.translated_text: went to the ground like <s>Rambhā</s> once faced <s>Dramiḍa</s>, surrounded by <s>Apsarases</s>. // Saund_6.49 //

body.text: Saundaranande mahākāvye bhāryāvilāpo nāma ṣaṣṭaḥ sargah //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth canto, named 'The Lamentation of the Wife,' in the <s>Saundarānanda</s> <s>mahākāvya</s>.
CANTO VII

children.text: liṅgaṃ tataḥ śāstṛvidhipradiṣṭaṃ gātreṇa bibhran na tu cetasā tat /
children.translated_text: Then, bearing on his body the monastic marks (<s>liṅga</s>) prescribed by the Master's rule, but not in his heart,

children.text: bhāryāgatair eva manovitakair jehrīyamāṇo na nananda nandaḥ // Saund_7.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s>, tormented by thoughts of his wife, found no joy. // Saund_7.1 //

children.text: sa puṣpamāsasya ca puṣpalakṣmyā sarvābhisāreṇa ca puṣpaketoḥ /
children.translated_text: With the splendor of blossoms in the month of flowers, with the universal onset of <s>Puṣpaketu</s> (the flower-bannered god of love),

children.text: yānīyabhāvena ca yauvanasya vihārasaṃstho na śamaṃ jagāma // Saund_7.2 //
children.translated_text: and with the intoxicating power of youth, he found no peace while dwelling in the monastery. // Saund_7.2 //

children.text: sthitaḥ sa dīnaḥ sahakāravīthyām ālīnasaṃmūrchitaṣatpadāyām /
children.translated_text: Standing forlorn in a row of mango trees where bees clung and swarmed together,

children.text: bhṛśaṃ jajṛmbhe yugadīrghabāhur dhyātvā priyāṃ cāpam ivācakarṣa // Saund_7.3 //
children.translated_text: he yawned deeply, and with arms long as a yoke, thinking of his beloved, drew back as if pulling a bow. // Saund_7.3 //

children.text: sa pitakṣodam iva pratīcchan cūtadrumbheyas tanupuṣpavarṣam /
children.translated_text: Receiving, as it were, a shower of fine blossoms from the young shoots of the mango tree, like a sprinkling of yellow powder,

children.text: dīrghaṃ niśaśvāsa vicintya bhāryāṃ navagraho nāga ivāvaruddhaḥ // Saund_7.4 //
children.translated_text: he heaved a long sigh thinking of his wife, like an elephant newly captured and confined. // Saund_7.4 //

children.text: śokasya hartā śaraṇāgatānāṃ śokasya kartā pratigarvitānām /
children.translated_text: He who removes the sorrow of those who seek refuge, who creates sorrow for the arrogant —

children.text: aśokam ālambya sa jātaśokaḥ priyāṃ priyāśokavanāṃ śuśoca // Saund_7.5 //
children.translated_text: leaning against an <s>Aśoka</s> tree, he who was born to sorrow grieved for his beloved who loved the <s>Aśoka</s> groves. // Saund_7.5 //

children.text: priyāṃ priyāyāḥ pratanuṃ priyaṇguṃ niśāmya bhītām iva niṣpatantim /
children.translated_text: Seeing a slender <s>Priyangu</s> creeper, dear to his beloved, trembling as if in fear,

children.text: sasmāra tām aśrumukhīṃ sabāṣpaḥ priyāṃ priyaṅguprasavāvadātām // Saund_7.6 //
children.translated_text: he, tearful himself, remembered her with her tear-stained face, beautiful as the blossoms of the <s>Priyangu</s>. // Saund_7.6 //

children.text: puṣpāvanaddhe tilakadrumasya dṛṣṭvānyapuṣṭāṃ śikhare niviṣṭām /
children.translated_text: Seeing a cuckoo perched atop a <s>Tilaka</s> tree laden with blossoms, reared by another,

children.text: saṃkalpayām āsa śikhāṃ priyāyāḥ śuklāṃśuke 'ṭṭālam apāsritāyāḥ // Saund_7.7 //
children.translated_text: he imagined the crest of his beloved, leaning on a balcony in her white garment. // Saund_7.7 //

children.text: latāṃ praphullām atimuktakasya cūtasya pārśve parirabhya jātām /
children.translated_text: Seeing a blossoming <s>Atimuktaka</s> creeper growing beside a mango tree, clinging to it in embrace,

children.text: niśāmya cintām agamat tadaivaṃ śliṣṭābhavan mām api sundarīti // Saund_7.8 //
children.translated_text: he fell into brooding: 'Thus did <s>Sundarī</s> too embrace me.' // Saund_7.8 //

children.text: puṣpotkarālā api nāgavṛkṣā dāntaiḥ samudgair iva hemagarbhaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Even the <s>Nāga</s> trees, laden with clusters of blossoms, with ivory-like caskets filled with golden [pollen],

children.text: kāntāravṛkṣā iva duḥkhitasya na cakṣur ācikṣipur asya tatra // Saund_7.9 //
children.translated_text: did not please his eye there, as if they were trees in a desolate forest to one in distress. // Saund_7.9 //

children.text: gandhaṃ vasanto 'pi ca gandhaparṇā gandharvaveṣyā iva gandhapūrṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: And the <s>Gandhaparṇā</s> plants, though filled with fragrance in spring, like the perfumed chambers of <s>Gandharva</s> women,

children.text: tasyānyacittasya śugātmakasya ghrāṇaṃ na jahrur hṛdayaṃ pratepuḥ // Saund_7.10 //
children.translated_text: did not delight the nose of him whose mind was elsewhere and whose nature was sorrow — they only scorched his heart. // Saund_7.10 //

children.text: saṃraktakaṇṭhaiś ca vinīlakaṇṭhais tuṣṭaiḥ prahṛṣṭair api cānyapuṣṭaiḥ /
children.translated_text: By the red-throated ones, by the blue-necked [peacocks], by the contented and joyous cuckoos reared by others,

children.text: lelihyamānaiś ca madhu dvirepaiḥ svanadvanaṃ tasya mano nunoda // Saund_7.11 //
children.translated_text: and by the bees repeatedly licking honey — the resounding forest drove his mind away. // Saund_7.11 //

children.text: sa tatra bhāryāraṇisaṃbhavena vitarkadhūmena tamaḥśikhena /
children.translated_text: There, burned within his heart by the fire of <s>Kāma</s> — born from the fire-stick of his wife, with the smoke of anxious thoughts and flames of darkness —

children.text: kāmāgnināntarhṛdi dahyamāno vihāya dhairyaṃ vilalāpa tat tat // Saund_7.12 //
children.translated_text: abandoning his composure, he lamented this and that. // Saund_7.12 //

children.text: adyāvagacchāmi suduṣkaraṃ te cakruḥ kariṣyanti ca kurvate ca /
children.translated_text: 'Now I understand how difficult is what they have done, will do, and are doing —

children.text: tyaktvā priyām aśrumukhīṃ tapo ye ceruś cariṣyanti caranti caiva // Saund_7.13 //
children.translated_text: those who, abandoning their tear-faced beloveds, have practiced, will practice, and practice austerities. // Saund_7.13 //

children.text: tāvad dṛḍhaṃ bandhanam asti loke na dāravaṃ tāntavam āyasaṃ vā /
children.translated_text: There is no bond in the world so firm — not one of wood, nor of cord, nor of iron —

children.text: yāvad dṛḍhaṃ bandhanam etad eva mukhaṃ calśkṣaṃ lalitaṃ ca vākyam // Saund_7.14 //
children.translated_text: as this firm bond: a beautiful face and charming words. // Saund_7.14 //

children.text: chittvā ca bhittvā ca hi yānti tāni svapauruṣāc caiva suhṛdbalāc ca /
children.translated_text: For those [bonds of wood and the like] are cut and broken through one's own valor and the strength of friends,

children.text: jñānāc ca raukṣyāc ca vinā vimoktuṃ na śakyate snehamayas tu pāśaḥ // Saund_7.15 //
children.translated_text: but the noose made of affection cannot be loosened without knowledge and harshness. // Saund_7.15 //

children.text: jñānaṃ na me tac ca śamāya yat syān na cāsti raukṣyaṃ karuṇātmako 'smi /
children.translated_text: I have neither that knowledge which would bring me peace, nor do I possess harshness, for I am of compassionate nature;

children.text: kāmātmakaś cāsmi guruś ca buddhaḥ sthito 'ntare cakragater ivāsmi // Saund_7.16 //
children.translated_text: and I am given to desire, while the <s>Buddha</s> is my teacher — I am caught between, like one standing in the path of a wheel. // Saund_7.16 //

children.text: ahaṃ gṛhītvāpi hi bhikṣuliṅgaṃ bhrātṝṣiṇā dvirguruṇānuśiṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: For though I have taken the mendicant's garb and am instructed by a brother-sage who is doubly a teacher,

children.text: sarvāsv avasthāsu labhe na śāntiṃ priyāviyogād iva cakravākaḥ // Saund_7.17 //
children.translated_text: I find no peace in any state, like a <s>Cakravāka</s> bird separated from its mate. // Saund_7.17 //

children.text: adyāpi tan me hṛdi vartate ca yad darpaṇe vyākulite mayā sā /
children.translated_text: Even now it stays in my heart — how, when the mirror was knocked aside by me,

children.text: kṛtānṛtakrodhakam abravīn māṃ kathaṃ kṛto 'sīti śaṭhaṃ hasantī // Saund_7.18 //
children.translated_text: she, laughing mischievously with feigned anger, said to me: "What have you done?" // Saund_7.18 //

children.text: yathaiṣy anāśyānaviśeṣakāyāṃ mayīti yan mām avadac ca sāśru /
children.translated_text: And what she said to me tearfully, with wavering eyes and a young face:

children.text: pāriplavākṣeṇa mukhena bālā tan me vaco 'dyāpi mano ruṇaddhi // Saund_7.19 //
children.translated_text: "You will leave me with my ornamental marks still fresh" — that speech blocks my mind even now. // Saund_7.19 //

children.text: baddhvāsanaṃ parvatanirjharasthaḥ svastho yathā dhyāyati bhikṣur eṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: How this monk, seated on a mountain stream-bank, composed, meditates calmly;

children.text: saktaḥ kva cin nāham ivaiṣa nūnaṃ śāntas tathā tṛpta ivopaviṣṭaḥ // Saund_7.20 //
children.translated_text: surely he is not attached anywhere as I am — so tranquil, he sits as if satisfied. // Saund_7.20 //

children.text: puṃskokilānām avicintya ghoṣaṃ vasantalakṣmyām avicārya cakṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: Without giving thought to the call of the male cuckoo, without turning his eye to the beauty of spring,

children.text: śāstraṃ yathābhyasyati caiṣa yuktaḥ śaṅke priyākarṣati nāsya cetaḥ // Saund_7.21 //
children.translated_text: how diligently he studies the scripture — I suspect his beloved does not pull at his heart. // Saund_7.21 //

children.text: asmai namo 'stu sthiraniścayāya nivṛttakautūhalavismayāya /
children.translated_text: Salutation to this one of firm resolve, free from curiosity and wonder,

children.text: śāntātmane 'ntargatamānasāya caṅkramyamāṇāya nirutsukāya // Saund_7.22 //
children.translated_text: of tranquil self, with mind turned inward, walking in meditation without longing! // Saund_7.22 //

children.text: nirīkṣamāṇāya jalaṃ sapadmaṃ vanaṃ ca phullaṃ parapuṣṭajuṣṭam /
children.translated_text: Who, gazing upon lotus-filled waters and blossoming forests frequented by cuckoos,

children.text: kasyāsti dhairyaṃ navayauvanasya māse madhau dharmasapatnabhūte // Saund_7.23 //
children.translated_text: has the fortitude, in the freshness of youth, in the month of spring — the very enemy of <s>Dharma</s>? // Saund_7.23 //

children.text: bhāvena garveṇa gatena lakṣmyā smitena kopena madena vāgbhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Through their demeanor, their pride, their grace, their beauty, their smiles, their anger, their intoxication, and their words,

children.text: jahruḥ striyo devanṛparṣisaṃghān kasmād dhi nāsmadvidham āṣipeyuḥ // Saund_7.24 //
children.translated_text: women have conquered hosts of gods, kings, and sages — why then would they not overpower one such as me? // Saund_7.24 //

children.text: kāmābhibhūto hi hiraṇyaretāḥ svāhāṃ siṣeve maghavān ahalyām /
children.translated_text: For even <s>Hiraṇyaretas</s> (the golden-seed, i.e., <s>Brahmā</s>/<s>Agni</s>), overpowered by desire, courted <s>Svāhā</s>; <s>Maghavān</s> (<s>Indra</s>) courted <s>Ahalyā</s>;

children.text: sattvena sargeña ca tena hīnaḥ strīnirjitaḥ kiṃ bata mānuṣo 'ham // Saund_7.25 //
children.translated_text: how much more then I, a mere human, inferior to them in strength and creative power, conquered by women! // Saund_7.25 //

children.text: sūryaḥ saraṇyūṃ prati jātarāgas tatprītaye taṣṭa iti śrutaṃ naḥ /
children.translated_text: It is heard that <s>Sūrya</s>, having conceived passion for <s>Saraṇyū</s>, had himself pared down to please her,

children.text: yām aśvabhūto 'śvavadhuṃ sametya yato 'śvinau tau janayāṃ babhūva // Saund_7.26 //
children.translated_text: and in the form of a horse, joining the mare, he begot the two <s>Aśvins</s>. // Saund_7.26 //

children.text: strīkāraṇaṃ vairaviṣaktabuddhyor vaivasvatāgnyoś calitātmadhṛtyoḥ /
children.translated_text: On account of a woman, between <s>Vaivasvata</s> and <s>Agni</s>, whose minds were gripped by enmity and whose self-composure wavered,

children.text: bahūni varṣāṇi babhūva yuddhaṃ kaḥ strīnimittaṃ na caled ihānyaḥ // Saund_7.27 //
children.translated_text: there was war for many years — who else in this world would not be shaken on account of a woman? // Saund_7.27 //

children.text: bheje śvapākīṃ munir akṣamālāṃ kāmād vaiṣṭhaś ca sa sadvariṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: The sage <s>Vāsiṣṭha</s>, the best among the good, out of desire took <s>Akṣamālā</s>, a woman of the <s>Śvapāka</s> caste,

children.text: yasyāṃ vivasvān iva bhūjalādaḥ sutaḥ prasūto 'sya kapiñjalādaḥ // Saund_7.28 //
children.translated_text: in whom, like the sun [born] from a water-born [lotus], his son <s>Kapiñjalāda</s> was born. // Saund_7.28 //

children.text: parāśaḥ śāpaśaras taharṣiḥ kālīṃ siṣeve jhaṣagarbhayonim /
children.translated_text: The sage <s>Parāśara</s>, whose arrow is his curse, courted <s>Kālī</s>, born from the womb of a fish,

children.text: suto 'sya yasyāṃ suṣuve mahātmā dvaipāyano vedavibhāgakartā // Saund_7.29 //
children.translated_text: in whom was born his great-souled son <s>Dvaipāyana</s>, the divider of the <s>Vedas</s>. // Saund_7.29 //

children.text: dvaipāyano dharmaparāyañaś ca reme samaṃ kāśiṣu veśyavadhva /
children.translated_text: <s>Dvaipāyana</s> too, though devoted to <s>Dharma</s>, sported with a courtesan's daughter in <s>Kāśī</s>,

children.text: yayā hato 'bhūc calanūpureña pādena vidyullatayeva meghaḥ // Saund_7.30 //
children.translated_text: by whom he was struck with her foot adorned with tinkling anklets, like a cloud [struck] by a streak of lightning. // Saund_7.30 //

children.text: tathāñgirā rāgaparītacetāḥ sarasvatīṃ brahmasutaḥ siṣeve /
children.translated_text: Likewise <s>Aṅgiras</s>, the son of <s>Brahmā</s>, with his heart overcome by passion, courted <s>Sarasvatī</s>,

children.text: sārasvato yatra suto 'sya jajñe naṣṭasya vedasya punaḥpravaktā // Saund_7.31 //
children.translated_text: in whom his son <s>Sārasvata</s> was born, who re-proclaimed the lost <s>Vedas</s>. // Saund_7.31 //

children.text: tathā nṛparṣer dilipasya yajñe svargastriyāṃ kāśyapa āgatāsthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Likewise, at the sacrifice of the royal sage <s>Dilīpa</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, overcome with desire for a celestial woman,

children.text: srucaṃ gṛhītvā sravad ātmatejaś cikṣepa vahnāv asito yato 'bhūt // Saund_7.32 //
children.translated_text: seized the sacrificial ladle and, his own vital energy flowing, cast [it] into the fire — whence <s>Asita</s> was born. // Saund_7.32 //

children.text: tathāṅgado 'ntaṃ tapaso 'pi gatvā kāmābhibhūto yamunām agacchat /
children.translated_text: Likewise <s>Aṅgada</s>, though he had gone to the very end of austerity, overcome by desire, went to the <s>Yamunā</s>,

children.text: dhīmattaraṃ yatra rahītaraṃ sa sāraṅgajuṣṭaṃ janayāṃ babhūva // Saund_7.33 //
children.translated_text: where he, more intelligent [than others], in a more secluded spot frequented by deer, begot [a son]. // Saund_7.33 //

children.text: niśāmya śāntāṃ naradevakanyāṃ vane 'pi śānte 'pi ca vartamānaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even while dwelling in a tranquil forest, upon seeing a serene princess,

children.text: cacāla dhairyān munir ṛṣyaṣṛṅgaḥ śailo mahīkampa ivoccaśṛṅgaḥ // Saund_7.34 //
children.translated_text: the sage <s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s> shook from his composure, like a high-peaked mountain during an earthquake. // Saund_7.34 //

children.text: brahmarṣibhāvārtham apāsya rājyaṃ bheje vanaṃ yo viṣayeṣv anāsthaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who had renounced his kingdom for the sake of attaining the status of a <s>Brahmarṣi</s>, indifferent to worldly pleasures, and taken to the forest —

children.text: sa gādhijaś cāpahṛto ghṛtācyā samā daśaikaṃ divasaṃ viveda // Saund_7.35 //
children.translated_text: that son of <s>Gādhi</s> (<s>Viśvāmitra</s>), carried away by <s>Ghṛtācī</s>, knew ten years as a single day. // Saund_7.35 //

children.text: tathaiva kandarpaśarābhimṛṣṭo rambhāṃ prati stuḥilaśirā mumūrcha /
children.translated_text: Likewise, struck by the arrow of <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love), he became slack-headed and fainted toward <s>Rambhā</s>,

children.text: yaḥ kāmaroṣātmatayānapekṣaḥ śaśāpa tām apratigṛhyamāṇaḥ // Saund_7.36 //
children.translated_text: he who, being of the nature of desire and wrath and [thus] indifferent, cursed her when she would not accept him. // Saund_7.36 //

children.text: pramadvarāyāṃ ca ruruḥ priyāyāṃ bhujaṅgamenāpahṛtendriyāyām /
children.translated_text: And <s>Ruru</s>, when his beloved <s>Pramadvarā</s> was struck by a serpent and lost consciousness,

children.text: saṃdṛśya saṃdṛśya jaghāna sarpān priyaṃ na roṣeṇa tapo rarakṣa // Saund_7.37 //
children.translated_text: seeing serpent after serpent, slew them — he did not guard his austerity, out of love, with anger. // Saund_7.37 //

children.text: naptā śaśāṅkasya yaśoguṇāṅko budhasya sūnur vibhudhaprabhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: The grandson of the moon, marked by fame and virtue, the son of <s>Budha</s>, possessed of divine power,

children.text: tathorvaśīm apsarasaṃ vicintya rājarṣir unmādam agacchad aiḍaḥ // Saund_7.38 //
children.translated_text: that royal sage <s>Aila</s> (<s>Purūravas</s>), brooding on the <s>Apsaras</s> <s>Urvaśī</s>, went mad. // Saund_7.38 //

children.text: rakto girer mūrdhani menakāyāṃ kāmātmakatvāc ca sa tāljaṅghaḥ /
children.translated_text: Passionate toward <s>Menakā</s> on the mountain peak, and being of amorous nature, that <s>Tālajaṅgha</s> [sage],

children.text: pādena viśvāvasunā saroṣaṃ vajreṇa hintāla ivābhijaghne // Saund_7.39 //
children.translated_text: was furiously struck on the foot by <s>Viśvāvasu</s>, as a palmyra is struck by a thunderbolt. // Saund_7.39 //

children.text: nāśaṃ gatāyāṃ paramāṅganāyāṃ gaṅgājale 'naṅgaparītacetāḥ /
children.translated_text: When the supreme woman had disappeared, King <s>Jahnu</s>, his mind seized by bodiless <s>Kāma</s>,

children.text: jahnuś ca gaṅgāṃ nṛpatir bhujābhyāṃ rurodha maināka ivācalendraḥ // Saund_7.40 //
children.translated_text: held back the <s>Gaṅgā</s> with his arms, like <s>Maināka</s>, the lord of mountains. // Saund_7.40 //

children.text: nṛpaś ca gaṅgāvirahāj jughūrṇa gaṅgāmbhasā sāla ivāttamūlaḥ /
children.translated_text: And the king, reeling from separation from the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, like a <s>Sāla</s> tree uprooted by the waters of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> —

children.text: kulapradīpaḥ pratipasya sūnuḥ śrīmattanuḥ śantanur asvatantraḥ // Saund_7.41 //
children.translated_text: the lamp of his dynasty, the son of <s>Pratīpa</s>, the glorious <s>Śantanu</s>, [was] not his own master. // Saund_7.41 //

children.text: hṛtāṃ ca saunandakinānuśocan prāptām invorvīṃ striyam urvaśīṃ tām /
children.translated_text: And <s>Somavarmā</s>, grieving over his wife who had been taken away by [the king] of <s>Saunandakinī</s>, like <s>Urvaśī</s> once restored to earth,

children.text: sadvṛttavarmā kila somavarmā babhrāma cittodhavabhinnavarmā // Saund_7.42 //
children.translated_text: wandered about, they say, with his armor broken by the agitation of his heart, though he was one of virtuous conduct and firm armor. // Saund_7.42 //

children.text: bhāryāṃ mṛtāṃ cānumamāra rājā bhīmaprabhāvo bhuvi bhīmakaḥ saḥ /
children.translated_text: And King <s>Bhīmaka</s>, of terrible power on earth, followed his dead wife in death,

children.text: balena senāka iti prakāśaḥ senāpatir deva ivāttasenaḥ // Saund_7.43 //
children.translated_text: he who was famous as a general named <s>Senāka</s> by his strength, like a god who had seized an army. // Saund_7.43 //

children.text: svargaṃ gate bhartari śantanau ca kālīṃ jihirṣan janamejayaḥ saḥ /
children.translated_text: And when his lord <s>Śantanu</s> had gone to heaven, that <s>Janamejaya</s>, desiring to seize <s>Kālī</s>,

children.text: avāpa bhīṣmāt samavetya mṛtyuṃ na tadgataṃ manmhatham utsasarje // Saund_7.44 //
children.translated_text: met his death at the hands of <s>Bhīṣma</s>, [yet] he did not abandon the passion directed toward her. // Saund_7.44 //

children.text: śaptaś ca pāṇḍur madanena nūnaṃ strīṇāṃ vaśaṃ kāmavaśena jagmuḥ /
children.translated_text: And <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, surely cursed by <s>Madana</s> (the god of love), [who had fallen] under the power of women through being subject to desire,

children.text: jagāma mādrīṃ na maharṣiśāpād asevyasevī vimamarśa mṛtyum // Saund_7.45 //
children.translated_text: went to <s>Mādrī</s> and, having consorted with one who should not have been approached, contemplated death because of the great sage's curse. // Saund_7.45 //

children.text: evaṃvidhā devanṛparṣisaṅghaḥ strīṇāṃ vaśaṃ kāmavaśena jagmuḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus hosts of gods, kings, and sages of such stature fell under the power of women through being subject to desire;

children.text: dhiyā ca sāreṇa ca durbalaḥ san priyām apaśyan kimu viklavo 'ham // Saund_7.46 //
children.translated_text: how much more I, weak in wisdom and in strength, bereft of seeing my beloved — how could I not be distressed? // Saund_7.46 //

children.text: yāsyāmi tasmād gṛham eva bhūyaḥ kāmaṃ kariṣye vidhivat sakāmam /
children.translated_text: Therefore I shall return home again and fulfill my desire in the proper way;

children.text: na hy anyacittasya calendriyasya liṅgaṃ kṣamaṃ dharmapathāc cyutasya // Saund_7.47 //
children.translated_text: for the monastic garb is not fitting for one whose mind is elsewhere, whose senses are unsteady, and who has fallen from the path of <s>Dharma</s>. // Saund_7.47 //

children.text: pāṇau kapālam avadhāya vidhāya mauṇḍyaṃ māna nidhāya vikṛtaṃ paridhāya vāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: Placing a begging bowl in hand, having his head shaved, setting aside his honor, wearing disfigured garments —

children.text: yasyoyoddhavo na dhṛtir asti na śānti asti citrapradīpa iva so 'sti ca nāsti caiva // Saund_7.48 //
children.translated_text: he who has neither fortitude nor peace is like a painted lamp: he both is and is not. // Saund_7.48 //

children.text: yo niḥsṛtaś ca na ca niḥsṛtakāmarāgaḥ kāṣāyam udvahati yo na ca niṣkasāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who has gone forth yet has not gone forth from desire and passion, who bears the ochre robe yet is not free from defilements,

children.text: pātraṃ bibharti ca guṇair na ca pātrabhūto kiṅgaṃ vahann api sa naiva gṛhī na bhikṣuḥ // Saund_7.49 //
children.translated_text: who carries a bowl yet is not a worthy vessel by his qualities — bearing the monastic mark, he is neither a householder nor a mendicant. // Saund_7.49 //

children.text: na nyāyyam anvayavataḥ parigṛhya liṅgaṃ bhūyo vimoktum iti yo 'pi hi me vicāraḥ /
children.translated_text: My reflection that it would not be proper for one of [noble] lineage to abandon the monastic mark once assumed —

children.text: so 'pi praṇaśyati vicintya nṛpapravīrāṃs tān ye tapovanaṃ apāsya gṛhāṇy atīyuḥ // Saund_7.50 //
children.translated_text: even that vanishes when I think of those mighty kings who, forsaking the ascetic grove, crossed over to their homes.' // Saund_7.50 //

children.text: śālvādhipo hi sasuto 'pi tathāmbarīṣo rāmo 'ndhva eva sa ca sāṃkṛtir antidevaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the king of the <s>Śālvas</s> together with his son, and likewise <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Andhva</s> himself, and that <s>Sāṃkṛti</s> <s>Antideva</s>,

children.text: cīrāṇy apāsya dadhire punar aṃśukāni chittvā jaṭāṣ ca kuṭilā mukuṭāni babhruḥ // Saund_7.51 //
children.translated_text: casting off their bark garments, they again wore fine cloth, and cutting their matted locks, they bore crowns. // Saund_7.51 //

children.text: tasmād bhikṣārthaṃ mama gurur ito yāvad eva prayātas tyaktvā kāṣāyaṃ gṛham aham itas tāvad eva prayāsye /
children.translated_text: Therefore, as soon as my teacher has gone from here to beg for alms, I shall cast off this saffron robe and go home from here;

children.text: pūjyaṃ liṅgaṃ hi skalitamanaso bibhrataḥ kliṣṭabuddher nāmutrārthaḥ syād upahatamater nāpy ayaṃ jīvalokaḥ // Saund_7.52 //
children.translated_text: for one whose mind has slipped, who bears the venerable insignia with a troubled intellect, whose understanding is impaired — neither the goal of the next world is achieved, nor is this world of the living. // Saund_7.52 //

body.text: Saundarananda mahākāvye nandivlāpo nāma saptamaḥ sargaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the seventh canto called "<s>Nandavilāpa</s>" (The Lament of <s>Nanda</s>) in the <s>Saundarananda</s> <s>mahākāvya</s>.
CANTO VIII

children.text: atha nandam adhīralocanaṃ gṛhayānotsukam utsukotuskam /
children.translated_text: Then, a certain <s>śramaṇa</s> (ascetic) approached <s>Nanda</s>, whose eyes were unsteady, who was eager to go home, consumed by longing,

children.text: abhigamya śivena cakṣuṣā śramaṇaḥ kaś cid uvāca maitrayā // Saund_8.1 //
children.translated_text: and with a benevolent gaze, spoke to him with friendliness: // Saund_8.1 //

children.text: kim idaṃ mukham aśrudurinaṃ hṛdayasthaṃ vivṛṇoti te tamaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Why is this face stained with tears, revealing the darkness dwelling in your heart?

children.text: dhṛtim ehi niyaccha vikriyāṃ na hi bāṣpaś ca śamaś ca śobhate // Saund_8.2 //
children.translated_text: Summon your composure, restrain this agitation — for weeping and tranquility do not become each other. // Saund_8.2 //

children.text: dvividhā samudeti vedanā niyataṃ cetasi deha eva ca /
children.translated_text: Suffering arises in two forms: inevitably in the mind and in the body;

children.text: śrutavidhyupacārakovidā dvividhā eva tayoś cikitsakāḥ // Saund_8.3 //
children.translated_text: and the physicians for these two are likewise of two kinds — those skilled in learning, rules, and treatment. // Saund_8.3 //

children.text: tad iyaṃ yadi kāyikī rujā bhiṣaje tūrṇam anūnam ucyatām /
children.translated_text: If this is a bodily affliction, let it be told fully and at once to a physician;

children.text: viniguhya hi rogam āturo nacirāt tīvram anartham ṛcchati // Saund_8.4 //
children.translated_text: for a sick person who conceals his disease soon meets with severe calamity. // Saund_8.4 //

children.text: atha duḥkham idaṃ manomayaṃ vada vakṣyāmi yad atra bheṣajam /
children.translated_text: But if this suffering is born of the mind, speak — I shall tell you the remedy for it;

children.text: manaso hi rajastamasvino bhiṣajo 'dhyātmavidaḥ parīkṣakāḥ // Saund_8.5 //
children.translated_text: for the physicians of a mind afflicted by <s>rajas</s> (passion) and <s>tamas</s> (darkness) are those who examine the inner self. // Saund_8.5 //

children.text: nikhilena ca satyam ucyatāṃ yadi vācyaṃ mayi saumya manyaste /
children.translated_text: And let the truth be told in full, if you think it fit to confide in me, O gentle one;

children.text: gatayo vividhā hi cetasāṃ bahuguhyāni madākulāni ca // Saund_8.6 //
children.translated_text: for the ways of minds are manifold, deeply hidden, and clouded by intoxication. // Saund_8.6 //

children.text: iti tena sa coditas tadā vyavasāyaṃ pravivakṣur ātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus urged by him, <s>Nanda</s>, wishing to disclose his intention,

children.text: avalambya kare kareṇa taṃ pravivakṣur ātmanaḥ // Saund_8.7 //
children.translated_text: grasping the other's hand in his own, wished to speak of his inner state. // Saund_8.7 //

children.text: atha tatra śucau latāgṛhe kusumodgāriṇi tau niṣedatuḥ /
children.translated_text: Then in that clean bower of creepers, fragrant with blossoming flowers, the two sat down,

children.text: mṛdubhir mṛdumāruteritair upagūdhāv iva bālapallavaiḥ // Saund_8.8 //
children.translated_text: as if embraced by soft young shoots stirred by gentle breezes. // Saund_8.8 //

children.text: sa jagāda tataś cikīṣitam ghananiśvāsagṛhītam antarā /
children.translated_text: He then spoke of his purpose, his words interrupted by deep sighs,

children.text: śrutavāgviśadāya bhikṣave viduṣā pravrajitena durvacam // Saund_8.9 //
children.translated_text: saying to the monk of clear speech and learning what is hard for a wise renunciant to say: // Saund_8.9 //

children.text: sadṛśaṃ yadi dharmacāriṇaḥ satataṃ prāṇiṣu maitracetasaḥ /
children.translated_text: "If it befits one who practises <s>dharma</s>, who always has a friendly mind toward living beings,

children.text: adhṛtau yad iyaṃ hitaiṣitā mayi te syāt karuṇātmanaḥ sataḥ // Saund_8.10 //
children.translated_text: then may this well-wishing compassion of yours, O virtuous one of compassionate nature, be directed toward me in my distress. // Saund_8.10 //

children.text: ata eva ca me viśeṣataḥ pravivakṣā kṣamavādini tvayi /
children.translated_text: And for this very reason I especially wish to confide in you, who speak with patience;

children.text: na hi bhāvam imaṃ calātmane kathayeyaṃ bruvate 'py asādhave // Saund_8.11 //
children.translated_text: for I would not reveal this state of mind to one of fickle nature, even if he spoke well, nor to a wicked person. // Saund_8.11 //

children.text: tad idaṃ śṛṇu me samāsato na rame dharavidhāv ṛte priyām /
children.translated_text: Then hear this from me in brief: I find no joy in the monastic life without my beloved,

children.text: girisānuṣu kāminīm ṛte kṛtaretā iva kiṃnaraś caran // Saund_8.12 //
children.translated_text: like a <s>kiṃnara</s> (celestial musician), maddened with desire, wandering on the mountain slopes without his mate. // Saund_8.12 //

children.text: vanavāsasukhāt parāṅmukhaḥ prayiyāsā gṛham eva yena me /
children.translated_text: Turned away from the joys of forest dwelling, my desire is only to go home;

children.text: na hi śarma labhe tayā vinā nṛpatir hīna ivottamaśriyā // Saund_8.13 //
children.translated_text: for I find no peace without her, like a king deprived of his supreme glory." // Saund_8.13 //

children.text: atha tasya niśamya tadvacaḥ priyabhāryābhimukhasya śocataḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, having heard those words of him who grieved, longing for his dear wife,

children.text: śramaṇaḥ sa śiraḥ prakampayan nijagādātmagataṃ śanair idam // Saund_8.14 //
children.translated_text: that <s>śramaṇa</s>, shaking his head, slowly spoke these words to himself: // Saund_8.14 //

children.text: kṛpaṇaṃ bata yūthalālaso mahato vyādhabhayād viniḥsṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Pitiable indeed! A creature, languishing for the herd, having escaped from the great terror of the hunter,

children.text: pravivikṣati vāgurāṃ mṛgaś capalo gītaraveṇa vañcitaḥ // Saund_8.15 //
children.translated_text: the restless deer, deceived by the sound of song, seeks to enter the snare! // Saund_8.15 //

children.text: vihagaḥ khalu jālasaṃvṛto hitakāmena janena mokṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Indeed, a bird trapped in a net, freed by a person wishing its welfare,

children.text: vicaran phalapuṣpavadvanaṃ pravivikṣuḥ svayam eva pañjaram // Saund_8.16 //
children.translated_text: roaming through a forest rich with fruit and flowers, wishes of its own accord to enter the cage again! // Saund_8.16 //

children.text: kalabhaḥ kariṇā khalūddhṛto bahupaṅkād viṣamān nadītalāt /
children.translated_text: Indeed, an elephant calf, pulled out by an elephant from deep mud on a treacherous riverbank,

children.text: jalatarṣavaśena tāṃ punaḥ saritaṃ grāhavatī titīrṣati // Saund_8.17 //
children.translated_text: driven by thirst for water, wishes to cross that very river full of crocodiles again! // Saund_8.17 //

children.text: śaraṇe sabhujaṅgame svapan pratibuddhena pareña bodhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who slept in a shelter infested with serpents, awakened and alerted by another,

children.text: taruṇaḥ khalu jātavibhramaḥ svayam ugraṃ bhujagaṃ jighṛkṣati // Saund_8.18 //
children.translated_text: the young man, indeed becoming bewildered, himself seeks to seize the fierce serpent! // Saund_8.18 //

children.text: mahatā khalu jātavedasā jvalitād utpatito vanadrumāt /
children.translated_text: Indeed, a bird that has flown up from a forest tree set ablaze by a great fire,

children.text: punar icchati nīḍatṛṣṇayā patituṃ tatra gatavyatho dvijaḥ // Saund_8.19 //
