children.translated_text: wishes to fall back there again out of longing for its nest, its pain forgotten! // Saund_8.19 //

children.text: avaśaḥ khalu kāmamūrchayā priyayā śyenabhayād vinākṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Indeed, helpless with the swoon of desire, the <s>jīvajīvaka</s> bird, separated from its mate by fear of a hawk,

children.text: na dhṛtiṃ samupaiti na hriyaṃ karuṇaṃ jīvati jīvajīvakaḥ // Saund_8.20 //
children.translated_text: finds neither composure nor shame, and lives pitifully! // Saund_8.20 //

children.text: akṛtātmatayā tṛṣānvito ghṛṇayā caiva dhiyā ca varjitaḥ /
children.translated_text: With an undisciplined self, driven by craving, devoid of both disgust and discernment,

children.text: aśanaṃ khalu vāntam ātmanā kṛpañaḥ śvā punar attum icchati // Saund_8.21 //
children.translated_text: indeed a wretched dog wishes to eat again the food it has itself vomited! // Saund_8.21 //

children.text: iti manmathaśokakarṣitaṃ tam anudhyāya muhur nirīkṣya ca /
children.translated_text: Thus, reflecting upon him who was tormented by love's grief, gazing at him again and again,

children.text: śramaṇaḥ sa hitābhikāṅkṣayā guṇavadvākyam uvāca vipriyam // Saund_8.22 //
children.translated_text: that <s>śramaṇa</s>, desiring his welfare, spoke words that were virtuous yet unwelcome: // Saund_8.22 //

children.text: avicārayataḥ śubhāśubhaṃ viṣayeṣv eva niviṣṭacetasaḥ /
children.translated_text: "For one who does not discern the auspicious from the inauspicious, whose mind is fixed only on sensory objects,

children.text: upapannam alabdhacakusuṣo na ratiḥ śreyasi ced bhavet tava // Saund_8.23 //
children.translated_text: it is fitting that if you have not gained insight, you should have no delight in the higher good. // Saund_8.23 //

children.text: śravaṇe grahaṇe 'tha dhāraṇe paramārthāvagame manaḥśame /
children.translated_text: In hearing, grasping, retaining, comprehending the ultimate truth, and calming the mind,

children.text: aviṣaktamateś calātmano na hi dharme 'bhiratir vidhīyate // Saund_8.24 //
children.translated_text: for one whose intellect is unattached yet whose self is fickle, delight in the <s>dharma</s> is not established. // Saund_8.24 //

children.text: viṣayeṣu tu doṣadarśinaḥ parituṣṭasya śucer amāninaḥ /
children.translated_text: But for one who sees faults in sensory objects, who is contented, pure, and free from pride,

children.text: śamakarmasu yuktacetasaḥ kṛtabuddher na ratir na vidyate // Saund_8.25 //
children.translated_text: whose mind is engaged in the practice of tranquility, whose understanding is firm — how can there be no delight? // Saund_8.25 //

children.text: ramate tṛṣito dhanaśriyā ramate kāmasukhen bāliśaḥ /
children.translated_text: The thirsty man delights in the splendor of wealth; the fool delights in the pleasure of desires;

children.text: ramate praśamena sajjanaḥ paribhogān paribhūya vidyayā // Saund_8.26 //
children.translated_text: but the virtuous person delights in tranquility, having surpassed worldly enjoyments through wisdom. // Saund_8.26 //

children.text: api ca prathitasya dhīmataḥ kulajasyārcitaliṅgadhāriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, for one who is renowned, wise, of noble birth, and bears the honored insignia,

children.text: sadṛśī na gṛhāya cetanā praṇatir vāyuvaśād girer iva // Saund_8.27 //
children.translated_text: the inclination toward household life is not fitting — like the bowing of a mountain before the wind. // Saund_8.27 //

children.text: spṛhyet parasaṃśritāya yaḥ paribhūyātmavaśāṃ svatantratām /
children.translated_text: He who would desire dependence on another, scorning the self-mastery of independence,

children.text: upaśāntipathe śive sthitaḥ spṛhayed doṣavate gṛhāya saḥ // Saund_8.28 //
children.translated_text: though established on the auspicious path of tranquility — he would desire the household life full of faults. // Saund_8.28 //

children.text: vyasanābhihato yathā viśet parmuktaḥ punar eva bandhanam /
children.translated_text: Just as one struck by misfortune, having been freed, might enter bondage again,

children.text: samupetya vanaṃ tathā punar gṛhasaṃjñaṃ mṛgayeta bandhanam // Saund_8.29 //
children.translated_text: so having reached the forest, one would again seek bondage in what is called the household. // Saund_8.29 //

children.text: puruṣaś ca vihāya yaḥ kaliṃ punar icchet kalim eva sevitum /
children.translated_text: And a man who, having abandoned strife, would again wish to pursue strife,

children.text: sa vihāya bhajeta bāliṣaḥ kalibhūtām ajitendriyaḥ priyām // Saund_8.30 //
children.translated_text: that fool, with uncontrolled senses, having abandoned it, would embrace his wife who is the source of strife. // Saund_8.30 //

children.text: saviṣā iva saṃśritā latāḥ parimṛṣṭā iva soragā guhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Like poisonous creepers clinging to trees, like caves inhabited by serpents,

children.text: vivṛtā iva cāsayo dhṛtā vyasanāntā hi bhavanti yoṣitaḥ // Saund_8.31 //
children.translated_text: like concealed diseases held within — women bring ruin in the end. // Saund_8.31 //

children.text: pramadāḥ samadā madapradāḥ pramadā vītamadā bhayapradāḥ /
children.translated_text: Intoxicating women are equal to intoxication and givers of madness; beyond their allure, they inspire fear;

children.text: iti doṣabhayāvahāś ca tāḥ katham arhanti niṣevanaṃ nu tāḥ // Saund_8.32 //
children.translated_text: thus, being bringers of both fault and danger, how can they deserve to be pursued? // Saund_8.32 //

children.text: svajanaḥ svajanena bhidyate suhṛdaś cāpi suhṛjjanena yat /
children.translated_text: Kinsmen are divided from kinsmen, and friends from friends,

children.text: paradoṣavikṣaṇāḥ śaṭhās tadanāryāḥ pracaranti yoṣitaḥ // Saund_8.33 //
children.translated_text: because women, who are deceitful, who see faults in others, act ignobly. // Saund_8.33 //

children.text: kulajāḥ kṛpaṇībhavanti yad yad ayuktaṃ pracaranti sāhasam /
children.translated_text: That men of noble birth become wretched, that they commit unjust acts of violence,

children.text: praviśanti ca yac camūmukhaṃ rabhasās tatra nimittam aṅganāḥ // Saund_8.34 //
children.translated_text: and that they rush into the front of battle — in all these, women are the cause. // Saund_8.34 //

children.text: vacanena haranati valgunā niśitena praharanti cetasā /
children.translated_text: They captivate with sweet words, and they strike with a sharpened mind;

children.text: madhu tiṣṭhati vāci yoṣitāṃ hṛdaye hālahalaṃ mahadviṣam // Saund_8.35 //
children.translated_text: honey rests on the lips of women, but in their hearts is <s>hālāhala</s> (deadly poison). // Saund_8.35 //

children.text: pradahan dahano 'pi gṛhyate viśarīraḥ pavano 'pi gṛhyate /
children.translated_text: Even burning fire can be seized; even bodiless wind can be seized;

children.text: kupito bhujago 'pi gṛhyate pradānāṃ tu mano na gṛhyate // Saund_8.36 //
children.translated_text: even an enraged serpent can be seized — but the mind of women cannot be grasped. // Saund_8.36 //

children.text: na vapur vimṛśanti na śriyaṃ na matiṃ nāpi kulaṃ na vikramam /
children.translated_text: They regard neither beauty, nor fortune, nor intellect, nor lineage, nor valor;

children.text: praharanty aviśeṣataḥ striyaḥ sarito grāhakulākulā iva // Saund_8.37 //
children.translated_text: women strike indiscriminately, like rivers teeming with crocodiles. // Saund_8.37 //

children.text: na vaco madhuraṃ na lālanaṃ smarati strī na ca suahṛdaṃ kva cit /
children.translated_text: A woman remembers neither sweet words, nor caresses, nor a friend;

children.text: kalitā vanitaiva cañcalā tad ihāriṣv iva nāvalambyate // Saund_8.38 //
children.translated_text: fickle as a painted woman, she is not to be relied upon — as with enemies. // Saund_8.38 //

children.text: adadatsu bhavanti narmadāḥ pradadatsu praviśanti vibhramam /
children.translated_text: With those who do not give, they are playful; with those who give, they become capricious;

children.text: praṇateṣu bhavanti garvitāḥ pramadās tṛptatarāś ca māniṣu // Saund_8.39 //
children.translated_text: toward the humble they are haughty; and with the proud, women are even more full of themselves. // Saund_8.39 //

children.text: guṇavatsu caranti bhartṛvad guṇahīneṣu caranti putravat /
children.translated_text: Toward men of virtue they act as husbands; toward the virtueless, they act as toward sons;

children.text: dhanavatsu caranti tṛṣṇayā dhanahīneṣu caranty avajñayā // Saund_8.40 //
children.translated_text: toward the wealthy they act with greed; toward the poor they act with contempt. // Saund_8.40 //

children.text: viṣayād viṣayāntaraṃ gatā pracaraty eva yathā hṛtāpi gauḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a cow, even when seized, wanders from one pasture to another,

children.text: anavekṣitapūrvasauhṛdā ramate 'nyatra gatā tathāṅganā // Saund_8.41 //
children.translated_text: so a woman, gone elsewhere, disregarding former affection, takes delight in another. // Saund_8.41 //

children.text: praviśanty api hi striyaś citām anubhadhnanty api muktajīvtāḥ /
children.translated_text: For women may even enter the funeral pyre, they may even follow in death with their lives released,

children.text: api bibhrati naiva yantraṇā na tu bhāvena vahanti sāhṛdam // Saund_8.42 //
children.translated_text: they may even bear harsh restraints — yet they do not truly carry affection with sincerity. // Saund_8.42 //

children.text: ramayanti patīn kathaṃ cana pramadā yāḥ patidevatāḥ kva cit /
children.translated_text: Those women who somehow please their husbands, and who in some cases regard their husband as a god,

children.text: calacittatayā sahasraśo ramayante hṛdayaṃ svan eva tāḥ // Saund_8.43 //
children.translated_text: they, with their fickle minds, please their own hearts a thousandfold more. // Saund_8.43 //

children.text: śvapacaṃ kila senajitsutā cakame mīnaripuṃ kumudvatī /
children.translated_text: The daughter of <s>Senajit</s> reportedly desired an outcaste; <s>Kumudvatī</s> desired the enemy of fish;

children.text: mṛgarājam atho bṛhadrathā pramadānām agatir na vidyate // Saund_8.44 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Bṛhadratā</s> desired the king of beasts — there is no limit to where women may go. // Saund_8.44 //

children.text: kuruhaihayavṛṣṇivaṃśajā bahumāyākavaco 'tha śambaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Those born of the <s>Kuru</s>, <s>Haihaya</s>, and <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> lineages, and <s>Śambara</s> of many illusions and armor,

children.text: munir ugratapāś ca gautamaḥ samavāpur vanitoddhataṃ rajaḥ // Saund_8.45 //
children.translated_text: and the sage <s>Gautama</s> of fierce austerities — all suffered the dust raised by women. // Saund_8.45 //

children.text: akṛtajñam anāryam asthiraṃ vanitānām ida īdṛśaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: Ungrateful, ignoble, and inconstant — such is the mind of women;

children.text: katham arhati tāsu paṇḍito hṛdayaṃ sañjayituṃ calātmasu // Saund_8.46 //
children.translated_text: how can a wise man deserve to fix his heart upon those of fickle nature? // Saund_8.46 //

children.text: atha sūkṣmamati dvayāśivaṃ laghu tāsāṃ hṛdayaṃ na paśyasi /
children.translated_text: Now, if with your subtle intellect you do not perceive the inauspicious and fickle heart of women,

children.text: kimu kāyam asadgṛhaṃ sravad vaintānām aśuciṃ na paśyasi // Saund_8.47 //
children.translated_text: why do you not at least see the impure body of women — that wretched dwelling, always oozing? // Saund_8.47 //

children.text: anulepanam añjanaṃ srajo maṇimuktātapanīyam aṃśukam /
children.translated_text: Ointments, collyrium, garlands, jewels, pearls, gold, and fine cloth —

children.text: yad ahany ahani pradhāvanair vasanaiś cābharaṇaiś ca saṃskṛtam /
children.translated_text: that which day after day is embellished with washings, garments, and ornaments,

children.text: aśubhaṃ tamasāvṛtekṣaṇaḥ śubhato gacchasi nāvagacchasi // Saund_8.48 //
children.translated_text: you regard as beautiful what is in truth foul, your eyes veiled by darkness — you do not perceive it. // Saund_8.48 //

children.text: atha vā samavaiṣi tattanūm aśubhāṃ tvaṃ na tu saṃvid asti te /
children.translated_text: Or perhaps you do recognize that body as impure, but you have no true awareness;

children.text: surabhiṃ vidadhāsi hi kriyām aśuces tatprabhavasya śāntaye // Saund_8.49 //
children.translated_text: for you perform fragrant rites to quell the impurity that is its very source. // Saund_8.49 //

children.text: malapañkadharā digambarā prakṛtisthair nakhadantaromabhiḥ /
children.translated_text: If women were seen in their natural state — bearing dirt and filth, unclothed, with nails, teeth, and body hair as nature made them —

children.text: yadi sādhu kim atra yoṣitāṃ sahajaṃ tāsu vicīyatāṃ śuci // Saund_8.50 //
children.translated_text: then what beauty would there be in women? Let what is naturally pure in them be sought out! // Saund_8.50 //

children.text: malapaṅkadharā digambarā prakṛtisthair nakhadantaromabhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Bearing dirt and filth, unclothed, with nails, teeth, and body hair in their natural state —

children.text: yadi sā tava sundarī bhaven niyataṃ te 'dya na sundarī bhavet // Saund_8.51 //
children.translated_text: if your <s>Sundarī</s> (beautiful one) were thus, surely she would not be beautiful to you today. // Saund_8.51 //

children.text: sravatīm aśuciṃ spṛśec ca kaḥ saghuṇo jarjarabhāṇḍavat striyam /
children.translated_text: Who of good character would touch a woman — oozing, impure, like a cracked vessel —

children.text: yadi kevalayā tvacāvṛtā na bhaven makṣikapattramātrayā // Saund_8.52 //
children.translated_text: if she were not covered by skin alone, thin as a fly's wing? // Saund_8.52 //

children.text: tvacaveṣṭhitam astipañjaraṃ yadi kāyaṃ samavaiṣi yoṣitām /
children.translated_text: If you recognize the body of women as a cage of bones wrapped in skin,

children.text: madanena ca kṛṣyase balād aghṛṇaḥ kāyaṃ samvaiṣi yoṣitām // Saund_8.53 //
children.translated_text: and yet you are forcibly dragged by desire, O shameless one, you do indeed know the body of women! // Saund_8.53 //

children.text: śubhatām aśubheṣu kalpayan nakhadantatvacakeśaromasu /
children.translated_text: Imagining beauty in what is foul — in nails, teeth, skin, hair, and body hair —

children.text: avicakṣaṇa kiṃ na paśyasi prakṛtiṃ ca prabhavaṃ ca yoṣitām // Saund_8.54 //
children.translated_text: O undiscerning one, why do you not see the true nature and origin of women? // Saund_8.54 //

children.text: tad avetya manaḥśarīrayor vanitā doṣavatīr viśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, having recognized that women are especially full of faults in both mind and body,

children.text: capalaṃ bhavanotsukaṃ manaḥ pratisaṃkhyānabalena vāryatām // Saund_8.55 //
children.translated_text: let the fickle mind, eager for the household, be restrained by the power of reflection. // Saund_8.55 //

children.text: śrutavān matimān kulodgataḥ paramasya praśamasya bhājanam /
children.translated_text: You are learned, wise, of noble birth, a vessel for the supreme tranquility;

children.text: upagamya yathā tathā punar na hi behttuṃ niyamaṃ tvam arhasi // Saund_8.56 //
children.translated_text: having undertaken it thus, you should not break your vow and turn back. // Saund_8.56 //

children.text: abhijanamahato manasvinaḥ priyayaśaso bahumānam icchataḥ /
children.translated_text: For a high-born, resolute man of firm character, who desires honor and cherishes his good name,

children.text: nidhanam api varaṃ sthirātmanaś cyutavinayasya na caiva jīvitam // Saund_8.57 //
children.translated_text: death is preferable to a life in which discipline has been abandoned." // Saund_8.57 //

children.text: baddhvā yathā hi kavacaṃ pragṛhītacāpo nindyo bhavaty apasṛtaḥ samarād rathasthaḥ /
children.translated_text: For just as a warrior who has donned his armor and taken up his bow becomes contemptible when he retreats from battle while standing on his chariot,

children.text: bhaikṣākam abhyupagataḥ parigṛhya liṅgaṃ nindyas tathā bhavati kāmarhṛtendriyāśvaḥ // Saund_8.58 //
children.translated_text: so too one who has taken up the mendicant's guise and adopted the religious mark becomes contemptible when his sense-horses are seized by desire. (8.58)

children.text: hāsyo yathā ca paramābharaṇāmbarasrag bhaikṣaṃ caran dhṛtadhanuś calacitramauliḥ /
children.translated_text: And just as one wearing the finest ornaments, garments, and garlands, going about begging with bow in hand and a trembling, colorful crest, would be laughable,

children.text: vairūpyam abhyupagataḥ paraiṇḍabhojī hāsyas tathā gṛhasukhābhimukhaḥ satṛṣṇaḥ // Saund_8.59 //
children.translated_text: so too one who has adopted ugliness yet eats from another's bowl becomes laughable when he faces homeward, full of craving. (8.59)

children.text: yathā svannaṃ bhuktvā paramaśyanīye 'pi śayito varāho nirmuktaḥ punar aśuci dhāvet paricitam /
children.translated_text: Just as a boar, having eaten its own food and lain down in the most excellent bedding, when released runs again to filth out of familiarity,

children.text: tathā śreyaḥ śṛṇvan praśamasukham āsvādya guṇavad vanaṃ śāntaṃ hitvā gṛham abhilaṣet kāmatṛṣitaḥ // Saund_8.60 //
children.translated_text: so too one who hears the teachings, having tasted the excellent pleasure of tranquility, would, if tormented by desire, abandon the peaceful forest and long for the household. (8.60)

children.text: yatholkā hastasthā dahati pavanapreritaśikhā yathā pādākrānto daśati bhujagaḥ krodharabhasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a torch held in the hand burns with its flame fanned by the wind, just as a serpent trodden upon bites in a frenzy of rage,

children.text: yathā hanti vyāghraḥ śiśur api gṛhīto gṛhagataḥ tathā strīsaṃsargo bhuvidham anarthāya bhavati // Saund_8.61 //
children.translated_text: just as even a young tiger, captured and brought home, kills — so too association with women leads to manifold calamity. (8.61)

children.text: tad vijñāya manaḥśarīraniyatān nāriṣu doṣān imān matvā kāmasukhaṃ nadījalacalaṃ kleśāya śokāya ca /
children.translated_text: Therefore, having understood these faults toward women, which are rooted in the mind and body, having recognized that the pleasure of desire is as fleeting as river water, leading to affliction and sorrow,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā durbalam āmapatrasadṛśaṃ mṛtyūpasṛṣṭaṃ jagan nirmokṣāya kuruṣva buddhim atulām utkaṇṭhituṃ nārhasi // Saund_8.62 //
children.translated_text: having seen the world as feeble as a wet leaf and surrendered to death — apply your incomparable mind toward liberation; you ought not to pine. (8.62)

body.translated_text: Thus ends the eighth canto, titled "The Discouragement Concerning Women," in the <s>Saundarananda</s> <s>mahākāvya</s>.
CANTO IX

children.text: athaivam ukto 'pi sa tena bhiṣuṇā jagāma naivopaśamaṃ priyāṃ prati /
children.translated_text: Then, though thus admonished by that monk, he found no peace regarding his beloved;

children.text: tathā hi tām eva tadā sa cintayan na tasya śuśrāva visaṃjñavad vacaḥ // Saund_9.1 //
children.translated_text: for thinking of her alone at that time, he did not hear his words, as if unconscious. (9.1)

children.text: yathā hi vaidyasya cikīrṣataḥ śivaṃ vaco na gṛhnāti mumūrṣur āturaḥ /
children.translated_text: For just as a patient on the verge of death does not heed the words of a physician who wishes to do good,

children.text: tathaiva matto balarūpayauvanair hitaṃ na jagrādha sa tasya tadvacaḥ // Saund_9.2 //
children.translated_text: so too he, intoxicated by strength, beauty, and youth, did not grasp those beneficial words of his. (9.2)

children.text: na cātra citraṃ yadi rāgapāpmanā mano 'bhibhūyeta tamovṛtāmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: And it is no wonder if a mind enveloped in darkness is overwhelmed by the evil of passion,

children.text: narasya pāpmā hi tadā nivartate yadā bhavaty antagataṃ tamas tanu // Saund_9.3 //
children.translated_text: for the evil of a person ceases only when that darkness becomes thin and reaches its end. (9.3)

children.text: tatas tathākṣiptam avekṣya taṃ tadā balena rūpeṇa ca yauvanena ca /
children.translated_text: Then, seeing him at that time so agitated by strength, beauty, and youth,

children.text: gṛhaprayāṇaṃ prati ca vyavasthitaṃ śaśāsa nandaṃ śramaṇaḥ sa śantaye // Saund_9.4 //
children.translated_text: and resolved upon returning home, that ascetic instructed <s>Nanda</s> for the sake of tranquility. (9.4)

children.text: balaṃ ca rūpaṃ ca navaṃ ca yauvanaṃ tathāvagacchāmi yathāvagacchasi /
children.translated_text: "I understand strength, beauty, and fresh youth just as you understand them;

children.text: ahaṃ iv idaṃ te trayam avyavastitaṃ yathāvabuddho na tathāvabudhyase // Saund_9.5 //
children.translated_text: but I know these three to be unstable, whereas you, though [seemingly] enlightened, do not understand them so. (9.5)

children.text: idaṃ hi rogāyatanaṃ jarāvaśaṃ nadītaṭānokahavac calācalam /
children.translated_text: For this body is an abode of disease, subject to old age, unsteady as a tree on a riverbank,

children.text: na vetsi dehaṃ jalaphenadurbalaṃ balasthatām ātmani yena manyase // Saund_9.6 //
children.translated_text: feeble as water-foam — yet you do not realize this and consider yourself endowed with strength. (9.6)

children.text: yadānnapānāsanayānakarmaṇām asevanād apy atisevanād api /
children.translated_text: When the body is seen to be on the verge of ruin from either the non-use or the overuse

children.text: śarīram āsannavipatti dṛśyate bale 'bhimānas tava kena hetunā // Saund_9.7 //
children.translated_text: of food, drink, sitting, travel, and work — on what ground is your pride in strength? (9.7)

children.text: himātapavyādhijarākṣudādibhir yadāpy anarthair upamīyate jagat /
children.translated_text: When the world is beset by calamities such as cold, heat, disease, old age, and hunger,

children.text: jalaṃ śucau māsa ivārkaraśmibhiḥ kṣayaṃ vrajan kiṃ baladṛpta manyase // Saund_9.8 //
children.translated_text: waning like water in a clean [vessel] under the sun's rays in summer — what do you, proud of strength, imagine? (9.8)

children.text: tvagasthimāṃsakṣatajātmakaṃ yada śarīram āhāravaśena tiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: When a body made of skin, bone, flesh, and blood subsists only by the power of food,

children.text: ajasram ārtaṃ satatapratikriyaṃ balānvito 'smīti kathaṃ vihanyase // Saund_9.9 //
children.translated_text: constantly afflicted and requiring perpetual remedies — how can you delude yourself saying "I am endowed with strength"? (9.9)

children.text: yathā ghaṭaṃ mṛnmayam āmam āśrito naras titīrṣet kṣubhitaṃ mahārṇavam /
children.translated_text: Just as a man clinging to an unbaked clay pot would try to cross the turbulent great ocean,

children.text: samucchrayaṃ tadvad asāram udvahan balaṃ vyavasyed viṣayārtham udyataḥ // Saund_9.10 //
children.translated_text: so too one who, carrying this lofty but insubstantial [body], would rely on strength intent upon sense objects. (9.10)

children.text: śariram āmād api mṛnmayam āmam āśrito naras titīrṣet kṣubhitaṃ mahārṇavam /
children.translated_text: The body is even more fragile than an unbaked clay pot — for a pot, when properly maintained, might surprisingly endure,

children.text: citraṃ hi tiṣṭhed vidhivaddhṛto ghaṭād idaṃ nu niḥsāratmaṃ mataṃ mama // Saund_9.11 //
children.translated_text: but this [body] I consider to be utterly without substance. (9.11)

children.text: yadāmbubhūvāyvanalāś ca dhātavaḥ sadā viruddhā viṣamā ivoragāḥ /
children.translated_text: When the bodily constituents — water, earth, wind, and fire — always in conflict like hostile serpents,

children.text: bhavanty anarthāya śarīram āśritāḥ kathaṃ balaṃ rogavidho vyavasyasi // Saund_9.12 //
children.translated_text: bring calamity while residing in the body, how do you, who know the course of disease, presume there is strength? (9.12)

children.text: prāyanti mantraiḥ praśamaṃ bhujaṅgamā na mantrasādhyās tu bhavanti dhātavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Snakes can be pacified by mantras, but the bodily humors cannot be subdued by mantras;

children.text: kva cic ca kiṃ cic ca daśanti pannagāḥ sadā ca sarvaṃ ca tudanti dhātavaḥ // Saund_9.13 //
children.translated_text: serpents bite only sometimes and only in some places, but the humors afflict always and everywhere. (9.13)

children.text: idaṃ hi śayyāsanapānabhojanair guṇaiḥ śariraṃ ciram apy avekṣitam /
children.translated_text: For this body, though long tended with beds, seats, drinks, and foods of excellent quality,

children.text: na marṣayaty ekam api vytikramaṃ yato mahāśiviṣavat prakupyati // Saund_9.14 //
children.translated_text: does not forgive even a single transgression, wherefore it rages like a great venomous serpent. (9.14)

children.text: yadā himārto jvalanaṃ niṣevate himaṃ nidāghābhihato 'bhikāṅkṣati /
children.translated_text: When one afflicted by cold resorts to fire, when one oppressed by heat longs for coolness,

children.text: kṣudhānivto 'nnaṃ salilaṃ tṛṣānvito balaṃ kutaḥ kiṃ ca kathaṃ ca kasya ca // Saund_9.15 //
children.translated_text: when one pressed by hunger [seeks] food and one pursued by thirst [seeks] water — where, what, how, and whose is strength? (9.15)

children.text: tad evam ajñāya śarīram āturaṃ balānvito 'smīti na mantum arhasi /
children.translated_text: Therefore, having understood the body to be afflicted thus, you ought not to think "I am endowed with strength";

children.text: asāram asvantam aniścitaṃ jagaj jagaty anitye balam avyavasthitam // Saund_9.16 //
children.translated_text: the world is insubstantial, impermanent, and uncertain — in an impermanent world, strength is unstable. (9.16)

children.text: kva kārtavīryasya balābhimāninaḥ shasrabāhor balam arjunasya tat /
children.translated_text: Where is the strength of <s>Kārtavīrya</s> <s>Arjuna</s>, who was proud of his strength and had a thousand arms?

children.text: cakarta bāhūn yudhi yasya bhārgavo mahānti śṛṅgāṇy aśanir girer iva // Saund_9.17 //
children.translated_text: Whose arms <s>Bhārgava</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>) cut off in battle, as a thunderbolt [shatters] the great peaks of a mountain. (9.17)

children.text: kva tadbalaṃ kaṃsavikarṣiṇo hares turaṅgarājasya puṭāvabhedinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Where is the strength of <s>Hari</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), the subduer of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, who split open the mouth of the king of horses (<s>Keśin</s>)?

children.text: yam ekabāṇena nijaghinvān jarāḥ kramāgatā rūpam ivottamaṃ jarā // Saund_9.18 //
children.translated_text: Whom old age, arriving gradually, laid low with a single arrow, as [it destroys] the finest beauty. (9.18)

children.text: diteḥ sutasyāmararoṣakāriṇaś camūrucer vā namuceḥ kva tadbalam /
children.translated_text: Where is the strength of <s>Namuci</s>, son of <s>Diti</s>, who provoked the wrath of the gods, or of the army-splendid one?

children.text: yam āhave kruddham ivāntakaṃ sthitaṃ jaghāna phenāvayavena vāsavaḥ // Saund_9.19 //
children.translated_text: Whom <s>Vāsava</s> (<s>Indra</s>), standing in battle like furious Death, slew with a weapon [made of] foam. (9.19)

children.text: balaṃ kurūṇāṃ kva ca tat tadābhavad yudhi jvalitvā tarasaujasā ca ye /
children.translated_text: And where was the strength of the <s>Kurus</s>, who, having blazed in battle with speed and might,

children.text: samitsammidhā jvalanā ivādhvare hatāsavo bhasmani paryavasthitāḥ // Saund_9.20 //
children.translated_text: like fires kindled at a sacrifice, lay lifeless, reduced to ashes? (9.20)

children.text: ato viditvā balvīryamānināṃ balānvitānām avamarditaṃ balam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, knowing that the strength of those who prided themselves on strength, valor, and pride has been crushed,

children.text: jagaj jarāmṛtyuvaśaṃ vicārayan bale 'bhimānaṃ na vidhātum arhasi // Saund_9.21 //
children.translated_text: reflecting that the world is subject to old age and death, you ought not to entertain pride in strength. (9.21)

children.text: balaṃ mahad vā yadi vā na manyase kuruṣva yuddhaṃ saha tāvad indriyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Whether you consider your strength great or not, wage war first with your senses;

children.text: jayaś ca te 'trāsti mahac ca te balaṃ parājayaś ced vitathaṃ ca te balam // Saund_9.22 //
children.translated_text: if you are victorious therein, then your strength is great; but if defeated, then your strength is hollow. (9.22)

body.text: tathā matā vīratarā manīṣiṇo jayanti lohāni ṣaśindriyāṇi ye // Saund_9.23 //
body.translated_text: Thus the wise regard as more heroic those who conquer the six senses, hard as iron. (9.23)

children.text: ahaṃ vapuṣmān iti yac ca manyase vicakṣaṇaṃ naitad idaṃ ca gṛhyatām /
children.translated_text: And as for your thinking "I am handsome" — this is not discerning, and consider this:

children.text: kva tad vapuḥ sā ca vapuṣmatī tanur gadasya sāmyasya ca sāraṇasya ca // Saund_9.24 //
children.translated_text: where is that beauty and that handsome body of <s>Gada</s>, <s>Sāmba</s>, and <s>Sāraṇa</s>? (9.24)

children.text: yathā mayūraś calacitracandrako bibharti rūpaṃ guṇavat svabhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a peacock with its trembling, colorful, moon-spotted [tail] bears its beauty by nature,

children.text: śarīrasaṃskāraguṇād ṛte tathā bibharṣi rūpaṃ yadi rūpavān asi // Saund_9.25 //
children.translated_text: if you bear beauty without the aid of bodily adornment, then you are truly handsome. (9.25)

children.text: yadi pratīpaṃ vṛṇuyān na vāsasā na śaucakāle yadi saṃspṛśed apaḥ /
children.translated_text: If one were to choose unbecoming garments, if one did not touch water at the time of cleansing,

children.text: mṛjāviśeṣaṃ yadi nādadīta vā vapur vapuṣman vada kīdṛśaṃ bhavet // Saund_9.26 //
children.translated_text: if one did not apply special grooming — tell me, what kind of beauty would the body of a "handsome one" have? (9.26)

children.text: navaṃ vayaś cātmagataṃ niśāmya yad gṛhonmukhaṃ te viṣayāptaye manaḥ /
children.translated_text: And seeing that your youth is new and your mind faces homeward for the attainment of sense pleasures,

children.text: niyaccha tac chailanadīrayopamaṃ drutaṃ hi gacchaty anvirati yauvanam // Saund_9.27 //
children.translated_text: restrain it, for like a mountain torrent, youth passes swiftly without pause. (9.27)

children.text: ṛtur vyatītaḥ parivartate punaḥ kṣayaṅ prayātaḥ punar eti candramāḥ /
children.translated_text: A season that has passed returns again; the moon that has waned waxes once more;

children.text: gataṃ gataṃ naiva tu saṃnivartate jalaṃ nadīnāṃ ca nṛṇāṃ ca yauvanam // Saund_9.28 //
children.translated_text: but what has gone, gone, never returns — neither the water of rivers nor the youth of men. (9.28)

children.text: vivarṇitaśmaśru valīvikuñcitaṃ viśīrṇadantaṃ śithilabhru niṣprabham /
children.translated_text: When you shall see your face withered — with discolored beard, wrinkled with creases,

children.text: yadā mukhaṃ drakṣyasi jarjaraṃ tadā jarābhibhūto vimado bhaviṣyasi // Saund_9.29 //
children.translated_text: with teeth fallen out, with sagging brows, without luster — then, overcome by old age, you will be stripped of pride. (9.29)

children.text: niṣevya pānaṃ madanīyam uttamaṃ niśāvivāseṣu cirād vimādyati /
children.translated_text: A man who has drunk the finest intoxicating drink eventually becomes sober after nights of revelry;

children.text: naras tu matto balarūpayauvanair na kaś cid aprāpya jarāṃ vimādyati // Saund_9.30 //
children.translated_text: but one intoxicated by strength, beauty, and youth — no one becomes sober without reaching old age. (9.30)

children.text: yathekṣur atyantarasaprapīḍito bhuvi praviddho dahanāya śuṣyate /
children.translated_text: Just as a sugarcane, utterly crushed of its juice, is cast on the ground and dries up for burning,

children.text: tathā jarāyantraniīḍitā tanur nipītasārā maraṇāya tiṣṭhati // Saund_9.31 //
children.translated_text: so too the body, pressed in the mill of old age, its essence drained, stands ready for death. (9.31)

children.text: yathā hi nṛbhyāṃ karapattram īritaṃ samucchritaṃ dāru bhinatty anekadhā /
children.translated_text: Just as a two-man saw, set in motion, splits a tall tree into many pieces,

children.text: tathocchritāṃ pātayati prajām imām aharniśābhyām upasaṃhitā jarā // Saund_9.32 //
children.translated_text: so too old age, joined with day and night, topples this lofty population. (9.32)

children.text: smṛteḥ pramoṣo vapuṣaḥ parābhavo rateḥ kṣayo vācchruticakṣuṣāṃ grahaḥ /
children.translated_text: Robbery of memory, decline of the body, loss of passion, impairment of speech, hearing, and sight,

children.text: śramasya yonir balvīryayor vadho jarāsamo nāsti śarīriṇāṃ ripuḥ // Saund_9.33 //
children.translated_text: source of weariness, destruction of strength and vigor — there is no enemy of embodied beings equal to old age. (9.33)

children.text: idaṃ viditvā nidhanasya daiśikaṃ jarābhidahānaṃ jagato mahadbhayam /
children.translated_text: Knowing this — that old age, which guides to destruction and burns the world, is a great terror —

children.text: ahaṃ vapuṣmān balavān yuveti vā na mānam āroḍhum anāryam arhasi // Saund_9.34 //
children.translated_text: you ought not to mount the ignoble pride of [thinking] "I am handsome, strong, and young." (9.34)

children.text: ahaṃ mamety eva ca raktacetasāṃ śarīrasaṃjñā tava yaḥ kalau grahaḥ /
children.translated_text: The attachment to the body of those whose minds are colored by "I" and "mine" — the demon that afflicts you in this evil [age] —

children.text: tam utsṛjaivaṃ yadi śāmyatā bhaved bhayaṃ hy ahaṃ ceti mameti cārchati // Saund_9.35 //
children.translated_text: abandon that, if there could be peace; for fear arises from [the notions of] "I" and "mine." (9.35)

children.text: yadā śarīre na vaśo 'sti kasya cin nirasyamāne vividhair upaplavaiḥ /
children.translated_text: When no one has control over the body as it is assailed by various calamities,

children.text: kathaṃ kṣamaṃ vettum ahaṃ mameti vā śarīrasaṃjñaṃ gṛham āpadām idam // Saund_9.36 //
children.translated_text: how is it fitting to know as "I" or "mine" this abode of misfortunes called the body? (9.36)

children.text: sapannage yaḥ kugṛhe sadāśucau rameta nityaṃ pratisaṃskṛte 'bale /
children.translated_text: One who would delight in a wretched house — always impure, infested with serpents, always requiring repair, and structurally weak —

children.text: sa duṣṭadhātāv aśucau calācale rameta kāye viparītdarśanaḥ // Saund_9.37 //
children.translated_text: he, with perverted vision, would delight in a body of corrupt humors, impure, unsteady, and unstable. (9.37)

children.text: yathā prarohanti tṛṇāny ayatnataḥ kṣitau prayatnāt tu bhavnti śālayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as weeds sprout effortlessly on the ground, while rice grows only with effort,

children.text: tathaiva duḥkhāni tṛñāny ayatnataḥ kṣitau pryatnāt tu bhavanti vā na vā // Saund_9.39 //
children.translated_text: so too sufferings arise effortlessly like weeds, while [pleasures on the ground] come about with effort — or perhaps not at all. (9.39)

children.text: śarīram ārtaṃ parikarṣataś calaṃ na cāsti kiṃ cit paramārthataḥ sukham /
children.translated_text: One drags about an afflicted, unsteady body, and there is no pleasure whatsoever in the ultimate sense;

children.text: sukhaṃ hi duḥkhapratikārasevayā sthite ca duḥkhe tanuni vyasvasyati // Saund_9.40 //
children.translated_text: for what is called pleasure is merely the practice of counteracting pain, and when even a slight pain persists, one imagines [it as pleasure]. (9.40)

children.text: yathānapekṣyāgryam apīsitaṃ sukhaṃ prabādhate duḥkham upetam aṇv api /
children.translated_text: Just as even a trifling pain, when it arrives, overwhelms [a person] regardless of the highest desired pleasure,

children.text: tathānapekṣyātmani duḥkham āgataṃ na vidyate kiṃ cana kasya cit sukham // Saund_9.41 //
children.translated_text: so too, regardless of suffering that has come upon oneself, there is no pleasure whatsoever for anyone. (9.41)

children.text: śarīram īdṛgbhahuduḥkham adhruvaṃ phalānurodhāh atha nāvagacchasi /
children.translated_text: The body is such — full of much suffering and impermanent. If you do not understand [this] connection with consequences,

children.text: dravat phalebhyo dhṛtiraśmibhir mano nigṛhyatāṃ gaur iva śasyalālasā // Saund_9.42 //
children.translated_text: then let your mind, rushing toward sense objects, be restrained with the reins of resolve, like a cow greedy for crops. (9.42)

children.text: na kāmabhogā hi bhavanti tṛptaye havīṃṣi dīptasya vibhāvasor iva /
children.translated_text: For the enjoyment of desires does not lead to satisfaction, like oblations [poured] into a blazing fire;

children.text: yathā yathā kāmasukheṣu vartate tathā tathecchā viṣayeṣu vardhate // Saund_9.43 //
children.translated_text: the more one indulges in the pleasures of desire, the more craving for sense objects increases. (9.43)

children.text: yathā ca kuṣṭhavyasanena duḥkhitaḥ pratāpanān naiva śamaṃ nigacchati /
children.translated_text: And just as one afflicted by the misery of leprosy finds no relief from heated application,

children.text: tathendriyārtheṣv ajitendriyaś caran na kāmabhogair upaśāntim ṛcchati // Saund_9.44 //
children.translated_text: so too one with unconquered senses, indulging in sense objects, does not attain peace through the enjoyment of desires. (9.44)

children.text: yathā hi bhaiṣajyasukhābhikāṅkṣayā bhajeta rogān na bhajeta tatkṣamam /
children.translated_text: Just as one who, out of desire for the pleasure of medicine, would cultivate diseases rather than what cures them,

children.text: tathā śarīre bahuduḥkhabhājane rameta mohād viṣayābhikāṅkṣayā // Saund_9.45 //
children.translated_text: so too one would, out of delusion and desire for sense objects, take delight in a body that is a vessel of much suffering. (9.45)

children.text: anarthakāmaḥ puruṣasya yo janaḥ sa tasya śatruḥ kila tena karmaṇā /
children.translated_text: A person who desires another's harm is indeed his enemy by that very action;

children.text: anarthamūlā viṣayāś ca kevalā nanu praheyā viṣamā yathārayaḥ // Saund_9.46 //
children.translated_text: and since sense objects are nothing but the root of harm, should they not be abandoned like hostile foes? (9.46)

children.text: ihaiva bhūtvā ripavo vadhātmakāḥ prayānti kāle puruṣasya mitratām /
children.translated_text: Even in this world, enemies who are intent on killing may in time become friends;

children.text: paratra caiveha ca duḥkhahetavo bhavanti kāmā na tu kasya cic chivāḥ // Saund_9.47 //
children.translated_text: but desires, causing suffering both here and hereafter, are never auspicious for anyone. (9.47)

children.text: yathopayuktaṃ rasavarṇagandhavad vadhāya kiṃpākaphalaṃ na puṣṭaye /
children.translated_text: Just as a <s>kiṃpāka</s> (poison) fruit, though endowed with taste, color, and fragrance when consumed, leads to death and not to nourishment,

children.text: niṣevyamāṇā viṣayāś calātmano bhavanty anarthāya tathā na bhūtaye // Saund_9.48 //
children.translated_text: sense objects, when indulged in by one of unsteady mind, lead to ruin and not to prosperity. (9.48)

children.text: tat etad ājñāya vipāpmanātmanā vimokṣadharmādyupasaṃhitaṃ hitam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, knowing this, with a sinless self, [accept] this beneficial [teaching] beginning with the <s>dharma</s> of liberation —

children.text: juṣasva me sajjanasaṃmataṃ mataṃ pracakṣva vā niścayam udgiran giram // Saund_9.49 //
children.translated_text: embrace my view, approved by the virtuous, or declare your resolution, uttering your word. (9.49)

children.text: iti hitam api bahv apīdam uktaḥ śrutamahatā śramaṇena tena nandaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, though told much that was beneficial by that monk of great learning,

children.text: na dhṛtim upayayau na śarma lebhe dvirada ivātimado madāndhacetāḥ // Saund_9.50 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s> neither attained composure nor found peace — like an elephant excessively intoxicated, blinded by rut. (9.50)

children.text: nandasya bhāvam avagamya tataḥ sa bhikṣuḥ pāriplavaṃ gṛhasukhābhimukhaṃ na dharme /
children.translated_text: Then, perceiving <s>Nanda</s>'s disposition — wavering, inclined toward domestic pleasures, not toward the <s>dharma</s> —

children.text: sattvāśayānuśayabhāvaparkṣakāya buddhāya tattvadiuṣe kathayāṃ cakāra // Saund_9.51 //
children.translated_text: that monk reported [it] to the <s>Buddha</s>, the knower of truth, who examines the natures, dispositions, and latent tendencies of beings. (9.51)

body.text: Saundaranande mahākāvye madāpavādo nāma navamaḥ sargaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth canto, entitled 'The Censure of Intoxication,' in the <s>Saundarananda</s> <s>mahākāvya</s>.
CANTO X

children.text: śrutvā tataḥ sadvratam utsisṛkṣuṃ bhāryāṃ didṛkṣuṃ bhavanaṃ vivikṣum /
children.translated_text: Then, hearing that [<s>Nanda</s>] wished to abandon his good vows, wished to see his wife, wished to enter his home —

children.text: nandaṃ nirānandam apetadhairyam abhyujjihīrṣur munir ājuhāva // Saund_10.1 //
children.translated_text: the sage, wishing to uplift <s>Nanda</s>, joyless and bereft of fortitude, summoned him. (10.1)

children.text: taṃ prāptam aprāptavimokṣamārgaṃ papraccha cittaskhalitaṃ sucittaḥ /
children.translated_text: When he arrived — having not yet attained the path of liberation, his mind faltering — the clear-minded [<s>Buddha</s>] questioned him,

children.text: sa hrīmate hrīvinato jagāda svaṃ niścayaṃ niścayakovidāya // Saund_10.2 //
children.translated_text: and he, abashed before the venerable one, bowing with modesty, declared his resolution to the one skilled in resolutions. (10.2)

children.text: nandaṃ viditvā sugatas tatas taṃ bhāryābhidhāne tamasi bhramantam /
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), knowing that <s>Nanda</s> was wandering in the darkness called 'wife,'

children.text: pāṇau gṛhītvā viyad utpapāta maṇiṃ jale sādhur ivojjihīrṣuḥ // Saund_10.3 //
children.translated_text: seized him by the hand and flew up into the sky — like a good man wishing to retrieve a jewel from the water. (10.3)

children.text: kāṣāyavastrau kanakāvadātau virejatus tau nabhasi prasanne /
children.translated_text: Clad in saffron robes, radiant as gold, the two shone in the clear sky,

children.text: anyonyasaṃśliṣṭavikīrṇapakṣau saraḥprakīrṇāv iva cakravākau // Saund_10.4 //
children.translated_text: like a pair of <s>cakravāka</s> birds, wings interlocked and spread, released over a lake. (10.4)

children.text: tau devadārūttamagandhavantaṃ nadīsaraḥprasravaṇaughavantam /
children.translated_text: They swiftly reached the <s>Himavat</s> (Himālaya), fragrant with the finest <s>devadāru</s> (deodar) trees,

children.text: ājagmatuḥ kāñcanadhātumantaṃ devarṣimantaṃ himavantam āśu // Saund_10.5 //
children.translated_text: abounding in rivers, lakes, and cascading streams, rich in veins of gold, and frequented by divine sages. (10.5)

children.text: tasmin girau cārañasiddhajuṣṭe śive havir dhūmakṛttottarīye /
children.translated_text: On that auspicious mountain, frequented by <s>Cāraṇa</s> adepts, wearing the smoke of oblations as an upper garment,

children.text: āgamya pārasya nirāśrayasya tau tasthatur dvīpa ivāmbarasya // Saund_10.6 //
children.translated_text: having arrived, those two stood like an island, as it were, of the supportless expanse of the sky. (10.6)

children.text: śāntendriye tatra munau sthite tu savismayaṃ dikṣu dadarśa nandaḥ /
children.translated_text: While the sage stood there with senses stilled, <s>Nanda</s> gazed about in all directions with wonder,

children.text: darīś ca kuñjāṃś ca vanaukasaś ca vibhūṣaṇaṃ rakṣaṇam eva cādreḥ // Saund_10.7 //
children.translated_text: [beholding] caves and bowers and forest-dwellers — both the ornament and the guardians of the mountain. (10.7)

children.text: bahvāyate tatra site hi śṛṅge saṃkṣiptabarhaḥ śayito mayūraḥ /
children.translated_text: For on a long, white peak there, a peacock with its tail folded lay sleeping,

children.text: bhuje balasyāyatapīnabāhor vaiḍūryakeyūra ivābabhāse // Saund_10.8 //
children.translated_text: and appeared like a <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl) armlet on the outstretched, massive arm of <s>Bala</s> [<s>Indra</s>]. (10.8)

children.text: manaḥśilādhātuśilāśrayeṇa pītākṛtāṃso virarāja siṃhaḥ /
children.translated_text: A lion, its shoulder yellowed from resting against rocks rich in <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar) ore, shone splendidly,

children.text: saṃtaptacāmīkarabhaktcitraṃ rūpyāṅgadaṃ śīrṇam ivāmbikasya // Saund_10.9 //
children.translated_text: like a fallen silver armlet of <s>Śiva</s>, painted with figures of molten gold. (10.9)

children.text: vyāghraḥ klavyāyatakhelagāmī lāṅgūlacakreṇa kṛtāpasvyaḥ /
children.translated_text: A tiger, moving with a slow, drawn-out, lazy gait, making a circle with its tail,

children.text: babhau gireḥ prasravaṇaṃ pipāsur ditsan pitṛbhyo 'mbha ivāvatirṇaḥ // Saund_10.10 //
children.translated_text: shone forth, thirsting for the mountain stream — as if it had descended to offer water to the ancestors. (10.10)

children.text: calatkadambe himvannitambe tarau pralambe camaro lalambe /
children.translated_text: On the slope of the <s>Himavat</s>, where <s>kadamba</s> trees swayed, a <s>camara</s> (yak) hung from a low-hanging branch,

children.text: chettuṃ vilagnaṃ na śaśāka bālaṃ kulodgatāṃ prītim ivāryavṛttaḥ // Saund_10.11 //
children.translated_text: unable to cut loose its entangled young — like a man of noble conduct unable to abandon affection born of his family. (10.11)

children.text: suvarṇagaurāś ca kirātasaṃghā mayūrapattrojjvalagātralekhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Groups of <s>Kirātas</s> (mountain tribesmen), golden-complexioned, with limbs streaked bright as peacock plumes,

children.text: sārdūlapātapratimā guhābhayo niśeptur udgāra ivācalasya // Saund_10.12 //
children.translated_text: with the pounce of leopards, slept [emerging] from caves — like eruptions of the mountain. (10.12)

children.text: darīcarīṇām atisundariṇāṃ manoharaśroṇikucodharīṇām /
children.translated_text: Groups of <s>Kiṃnarī</s> women, exceedingly beautiful, wandering through the caves, with captivating hips and breasts,

children.text: vṛdndāni rejur diśi kiṃnarīṇāṃ puṣpotkacānām iva vallarīṇām // Saund_10.13 //
children.translated_text: shone in every direction — like clusters of creepers blossoming with flowers. (10.13)

children.text: nagān nagasyopari devadārūn āyāsayantaḥ kapayo viceruḥ /
children.translated_text: Monkeys roamed about, troubling the <s>devadāru</s> trees atop the mountain peaks,

children.text: tebhyaḥ phalaṃ nāpurato 'pajagmur moghaprasādebhya iveśvarebhyaḥ // Saund_10.14 //
children.translated_text: but obtained no fruit from them in return — as from lords whose favors are fruitless. (10.14)

children.text: tasmāt tu yūthād apasāryamāṇāṃ niṣpīditālaktakaraktavaktrām /
children.translated_text: Then, [seeing] a female monkey being driven away from a troop, her face red as if smeared with <s>alaktaka</s> (lac),

children.text: śākhāmṛgīm ekavipannadṛṣṭiṃ dṛṣṭvā munir nandam idaṃ babhāṣe // Saund_10.15 //
children.translated_text: with one eye ruined, the sage spoke thus to <s>Nanda</s>: (10.15)

children.text: kā nanda rūpeṇa ca ceṣṭayā ca saṃpaśyataś cārutarā matā te /
children.translated_text: 'Who, <s>Nanda</s>, in your view, is more lovely in form and movement as you look upon them —

children.text: eṣā mṛgī viakavipanndṛṣṭiḥ sa vā jano yatra gatā taveṣṭiḥ // Saund_10.16 //
children.translated_text: this she-monkey with one eye ruined, or that person toward whom your desire is directed?' (10.16)

children.text: ity evam uktaḥ sugatena nandaḥ kṛtvā smitaṃ kiṃ cid idaṃ jagāda /
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by the <s>Sugata</s>, <s>Nanda</s>, with a slight smile, said this:

children.text: kva cottamastrī bhagavan badhūs te mṛgi nagakleśkarī kva caiṣā // Saund_10.17 //
children.translated_text: 'How can you compare, <s>Bhagavan</s>? Where is the supreme woman, your daughter-in-law, and where is this she-monkey, a torment of the mountain?' (10.17)

children.text: tato munis tasya niśamya vākyaṃ hetvantaraṃ kiṃ cid avekṣamāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, hearing his words, the sage, contemplating another means,

children.text: ālambya nandaṃ prayayau tathaiva krīḍāvanaṃ vajradharasya rājñaḥ // Saund_10.18 //
children.translated_text: took hold of <s>Nanda</s> and proceeded in the same manner to the pleasure-grove of king <s>Vajradhara</s> [<s>Indra</s>]. (10.18)

children.text: ṛtāv rtāv ākṛtim eka eke kṣaṇe kṣaṇe bibhrati yatra vṛkṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: Where some trees bear a different form in each successive season, at each successive moment,

children.text: citrāṃ samastām api ke cid anye ṣaṇṇām ṛtūnāṃ śriyam udvahanti // Saund_10.19 //
children.translated_text: while certain others bear simultaneously the complete, variegated splendor of all six seasons. (10.19)

children.text: puṣyanti ke cit surabhīr udārā mālāḥ srajaś ca grathitā vicitrāḥ /
children.translated_text: Some produce fragrant, magnificent garlands, woven wreaths of varied [colors],

children.text: karṇānukūlān avataṃsakāṃṣ ca pratyarthibhūtān iva kuṇḍalānām // Saund_10.20 //
children.translated_text: and ear-ornaments pleasing to the ear — as if rivals of earrings. (10.20)

children.text: raktāni phullāḥ kamalāni yatra pradīpavṛkṣā iva bhānti vṛkṣā /
children.translated_text: Where some trees, bearing red, full-blown lotuses, shine like lamp-trees,

children.text: praphullanīlotpalarohiṇo 'nye sonmīlitākṣā iva bhānti vṛkṣā // Saund_10.21 //
children.translated_text: and others, bearing full-blown blue lotuses, shine as if with half-opened eyes. (10.21)

children.text: atāntavāny ekaghanāni yatra sūkṣmāṇi vāsāṃsi phalanti vṛkṣā // Saund_10.22 /
children.translated_text: unwoven, of a single density, and fine. (10.22)

children.text: hārān maṇīn uttamakuṇḍalāni keyūravaryāṇy atha nūpurāṇi /
children.translated_text: Necklaces, jewels, finest earrings, excellent armlets, and anklets —

children.text: evaṃvidhāny ābharaṇāni yatra svargānurūpāṇi phalanti vṛkṣaḥ // Saund_10.23 //
children.translated_text: ornaments of such kinds, befitting heaven, the trees bear as fruit there. (10.23)

body.translated_text: There, trees bear garments of various faded colors, white, shining with golden patterns,

children.text: vaiḍūryanālāni ca kāñcanāni padmāni vajrāṅkurakesarāṇi /
children.translated_text: Lotuses with stalks of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl) and petals of gold, with pistils and stamens of diamond,

children.text: sparśakṣamāṇy uttamagandhavanti rohanti niṣkampatalā nalinyaḥ // Saund_10.24 //
children.translated_text: pleasant to touch and supremely fragrant, grow in ponds with motionless surfaces. (10.24)

children.text: yatrāyatāṃś caiva tatāṃś ca tāṃs tān vādyasya hetūn suṣirān ghanāṃś ca /
children.translated_text: Where trees, adorned with jewels and gold of varied [hues], bear as fruit all manner of

children.text: phalanti vṛkṣā maṇihemacitrāḥ krīḍāsahāyās tridaśālayānām // Saund_10.25 //
children.translated_text: musical instruments — elongated, flat, hollow, and solid — playthings of the celestial dwellers. (10.25)

children.text: mandāravṛkṣāṃś ca kuśeśayāṃś ca puṣpānatān kokanadāṃś ca vṛkṣān /
children.translated_text: <s>Mandāra</s> trees, <s>kuśeśaya</s> lotuses, <s>kokanada</s> trees bowed with blossoms —

children.text: ākramya māhātmyaguṇair virājan rājāyate yatra sa pārijātaḥ // Saund_10.26 //
children.translated_text: surpassing them all by its qualities of greatness, the <s>Pārijāta</s> reigns supreme there. (10.26)

children.text: kṛṣṭe tapaḥṣīlahalair akhinnais tripiṣṭapakṣetratale prasūtāḥ /
children.translated_text: In the field of heaven, ploughed by the unwearying ploughshares of austerity and moral discipline,

children.text: evaṃvidhā yatra saānuvṛttā divaukasāṃ bhogavidhānavṛkṣāḥ // Saund_10.27 //
children.translated_text: such trees, compliant [to the gods' wishes], grow — trees that provide for the enjoyments of the celestials. (10.27)

children.text: manaḥśilābhair vadanair vihaṅgā yatrākṣibhiḥ spāṭikasaṃnibhaiś ca /
children.translated_text: There, birds with faces [bright] as <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar), with eyes resembling crystal,

children.text: śāvaiś ca pakṣair abhilohitāntair māñjiṣṭhakair ardhasitaiś ca pādaiḥ // Saund_10.28 //
children.translated_text: with tawny wings tipped with red, and with <s>māñjiṣṭhaka</s>-colored feet that are half-white — (10.28)

children.text: citraiḥ suvarṇacchadanais tathānye vaiḍuryavarṇābhir nayanaiḥ prasannaiḥ /
children.translated_text: And other birds with variegated golden plumage, with serene eyes the color of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl),

children.text: vihaṅgamā śiñjirikābhidhānā rutair manaḥśrotaharair bhramanti // Saund_10.29 //
children.translated_text: called <s>śiñjirikā</s>, wander about with calls that captivate the mind and ears. (10.29)

children.text: raktābhir agreṣu ca vallarībhir madhyeṣu cāmīkarapiñjarābhiḥ /
children.translated_text: With red creepers at their tips, with <s>cāmīkara</s>-gold-yellow ones in the middle,

children.text: vaiḍūryavarṇābhir upāntamadhyeṣv alaṅkṛtā yatra khagāś caranti // Saund_10.30 //
children.translated_text: and with <s>vaiḍūrya</s>-colored ones at the inner edges — adorned thus, the birds move about there. (10.30)

children.text: rociṣṇavo nāma patratriṇo 'nye dīptāgnivarṇā jvalitair ivāsyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Other resplendent birds, blazing with the color of fire, with mouths as if aflame,

children.text: bhramanti dṛṣṭīr vapuṣākṣipantaḥ svanaiḥ śubhair apsaraso harantaḥ // Saund_10.31 //
children.translated_text: roam about, captivating the sight with their beauty and charming the <s>Apsarases</s> with their auspicious calls. (10.31)

children.text: yatreṣṭaceṣṭāḥ satataprahṛṣṭā nirartayo nirjaraso viśokāḥ /
children.translated_text: Where those who act as they please, forever delighted, free from suffering, free from aging, free from grief,

children.text: svaiḥ karmabhir hīnaviśiṣṭtamadhyāḥ svayaṃprabhāḥ puṇyakṛto ramante // Saund_10.32 //
children.translated_text: distinguished as low, middle, or high by their own deeds, self-luminous, the meritorious ones sport. (10.32)

children.text: pūrvaṃ tapomūlyaparigraheṇa svargakrayārthaṃ kṛtaniścayānāṃ /
children.translated_text: The hearts of ascetics, wearied by the exertion of purchasing heaven with the price of austerity,

children.text: manāṃsi khinnāni tapodhanānāṃ haranti yatrāpsaraso laḍantyāḥ // Saund_10.33 //
children.translated_text: are there captivated by the frolicking <s>Apsarases</s>. (10.33)

children.text: nityotsavaṃ taṃ ca niśāmya lokaṃ nistandrinidrāratiśokarogam /
children.translated_text: And seeing that world of perpetual festivity, free from drowsiness, sleep, weariness, grief, and disease,

children.text: nando jarāmṛtyuvaśaṃ sadārtaṃ mene śmaśānapratimaṃ nṛlokam // Saund_10.34 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s> considered the human world — ever afflicted, subject to old age and death — as resembling a cremation ground. (10.34)

children.text: aindraṃ vanaṃ tac ca dadarśa nandaḥ samantato vismayaphulladṛṣṭiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s> beheld that grove of <s>Indra</s>, looking all around with eyes wide with amazement,

children.text: harṣānvitāś cāpsarasaḥ parīyuḥ sagarvam anyonyam avekṣamāṇāḥ // Saund_10.35 //
children.translated_text: and the <s>Apsarases</s>, filled with joy, came around, casting proud glances at one another. (10.35)

children.text: sadā yuvatyo madanaikakāryāḥ sādhāraṇāḥ puṇyakṛtāṃ vihārāḥ /
children.translated_text: Forever youthful, devoted solely to the work of love, common to all the meritorious as their recreation,

children.text: divyāś ca nirdoṣaparigrahāś ca tapaḥphalasyāśrayaṇaṃ surāṇām // Saund_10.36 //
children.translated_text: divine, possessing faultless retinues — they are the reward of austerity for the gods. (10.36)

children.text: tāsāṃ jagur dhīram udāttam anyāḥ padmāni kāś cil lalitaṃ labhañjuḥ /
children.translated_text: Some among them sang with depth and grandeur; some gracefully plucked lotuses;

children.text: anyonyaharṣān nanṛtus tathānyāś cirāṅgahārāḥ stanabhinnabhārāḥ // Saund_10.37 //
children.translated_text: others danced in mutual delight, with long-drawn movements of their limbs, their burdens [of breasts] splitting. (10.37)

children.text: kāsāṃ cid āsāṃ vadanāni rejur vanāntarebhyaś calakuṇḍalāni /
children.translated_text: The faces of some among them, with swinging earrings, shone forth from the forest clearings,

children.text: vyāviddhaparṇebhya ivākarebhyaḥ padmāni kāraṇḍavaghaṭṭitāni // Saund_10.38 //
children.translated_text: like lotuses disturbed by <s>kāraṇḍava</s> ducks, [emerging] from clefts between the rocks with leaves displaced. (10.38)

children.text: tāḥ niḥsṛtāḥ prekṣya vanāntarebhyas taḍitpatākā iva toyadebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing them emerge from the forest clearings like streaks of lightning from rain clouds,

children.text: nandasya rāgeṇa tanur vivepe jale cale candramasaḥ prabheva // Saund_10.39 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s>'s body trembled with desire — like the reflection of the moon in rippling water. (10.39)

children.text: vapuś ca divyaṃ lalitāś ca ceṣṭās tataḥ sa tāsāṃ manasā jahāra /
children.translated_text: He then mentally absorbed the divine beauty and graceful movements of those [<s>Apsarases</s>],

children.text: kautūhalāvarjitayā ca dṛṣṭyā saṃśleṣatarṣād iva jātarāgaḥ // Saund_10.40 //
children.translated_text: and with his gaze drawn by curiosity, he became inflamed with passion, as if from a thirst for union. (10.40)

children.text: sa jātatarṣo 'psarasaḥ pipāsus tatprāptaye 'dhiṣṭhitaviklavārtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Seized with longing, thirsting for the <s>Apsarases</s>, distressed and agitated for their attainment,

children.text: lolendriyāśvena manorathena jehriyamāṇo na dhṛtiṃ cakāra // Saund_10.41 //
children.translated_text: carried away by the chariot of fantasy drawn by the unruly steeds of the senses, he lost all composure. (10.41)

children.text: yathā manuṣyo malinaṃ hi vāsaḥ kṣāreṇa bhūyo malinīkaroti /
children.translated_text: Just as a man makes a dirty garment still dirtier with lye —

children.text: malakṣayārthaṃ na malodbhavārtaṃ rajas tathāsmai munir ācakarṣa // Saund_10.42 //
children.translated_text: not to increase the dirt but to destroy it — so the sage drew out passion [in <s>Nanda</s>]. (10.42)

children.text: doṣāṃś ca kāyād bhiṣaguj jihīrṣur bhūyo yathā kleśayituṃ yateta /
children.translated_text: Just as a physician, wishing to extract impurities from the body, would endeavor to aggravate them further,

children.text: rāgaṃ tathā tasya munir jighāṃsur bhūyastaraṃ rāgam upānināya // Saund_10.43 //
children.translated_text: so the sage, wishing to destroy <s>Nanda</s>'s passion, introduced even greater passion. (10.43)

children.text: dīpaprabhāṃ hanti yathāndhakāre sahasraraśmer uditasya dīptiḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the radiance of the thousand-rayed [sun], when risen, eclipses the light of a lamp in darkness,

children.text: manuṣyaloke dyutim aṅganānām antardadhāty apsarasāṃ tathā śrīḥ // Saund_10.44 //
children.translated_text: so the splendor of the <s>Apsarases</s> eclipses the beauty of women in the mortal world. (10.44)

children.text: mahac ca rūpaṃ svaṇu hanti rūpaṃ śabdo mahān hanti ca śabdam alpam /
children.translated_text: A great beauty eclipses a small beauty, a great sound drowns out a faint sound,

children.text: gurvī rujā hanti rujāṃ ca mṛdviṃ sarvo mahān hetur aṇor vadhāya // Saund_10.45 //
children.translated_text: a severe pain suppresses a mild pain — every great cause serves to destroy the small. (10.45)

children.text: muneḥ prabhāvāc ca śaśāka nandas taddarśanaṃ soḍhum asahyam anyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: And by the power of the sage, <s>Nanda</s> was able to endure that sight, unbearable to others;

children.text: avitarāgasya hi durbalasya mano dahed apsarasāṃ vapuḥṣrīḥ // Saund_10.46 //
children.translated_text: for the bodily splendor of the <s>Apsarases</s> would burn the mind of one who is weak and has not abandoned passion. (10.46)

children.text: matvā tato nandam udīrṇarāgaṃ bhāryānurodhād apavṛttarāgam /
children.translated_text: Then, perceiving that <s>Nanda</s>'s passion was inflamed — his attachment to his wife having been displaced by [this greater] passion —

children.text: rāgeṇa rāgaṃ pratihantukāmo munir virāgo giram ity uvāca // Saund_10.47 //
children.translated_text: the sage, himself passionless, wishing to counter passion with passion, spoke these words: (10.47)

children.text: etāḥ strīyaḥ paśya divaukasas tvaṃ nirīkṣya ca brūhi yathārthattvam /
children.translated_text: 'Behold these celestial women, and having observed them, speak the truth:

children.text: etāḥ kathaṃ rūpaguṇair matās te sa vā jano yatra gataṃ manas te // Saund_10.48 //
children.translated_text: how do you regard these in beauty and qualities — or that person toward whom your mind is directed?' (10.48)

children.text: athāpsaraḥs eva niviṣṭadṛṣtī rāgāgnināntarhṛdaye pradīptaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, with his gaze fixed upon the <s>Apsarases</s>, burning within his heart with the fire of desire,

children.text: sagadgagadaṃ kāmaviṣaktacetāḥ kṛtāñjalir vākyam uvāca nandaḥ // Saund_10.49 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s>, his mind ensnared by lust, with faltering voice, spoke with joined palms: (10.49)

children.text: haryaṅganāsau muṣitaikadṛṣṭir yadantare syāt tava nātha vadhvāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'That she-monkey with one eye ruined — what your daughter-in-law would be in comparison to them, O Lord,

children.text: tadantare 'sau kṛpaṇā vadhūs te vauṣmatīr apsarasaḥ pratītya // Saund_10.50 //
children.translated_text: that is what your pitiable daughter-in-law is, compared to these <s>Apsarases</s>.' (10.50)

children.text: āsthā yathā pūrvam abhūn na kā cid anyāsu me striṣu niśāmya bhāryām /
children.translated_text: 'Just as formerly I had no regard for other women upon seeing my wife,

children.text: tasyāṃ tataḥ samprati kā cid āsthā na me niśāmyaiva hi rūpam āsām // Saund_10.51 //
children.translated_text: so now I have no regard for her, having seen the beauty of these.' (10.51)

children.text: yathā pratapto mṛdunātapena dahyeta kaś cin mahatānalena /
children.translated_text: 'Just as one who was gently warmed by a mild heat would be burned by a great fire,

children.text: rāgeṇa pūrvaṃ mṛdunābhitapto rāgāninānena tathābhidahye // Saund_10.52 //
children.translated_text: so I, who was formerly scorched by a gentle passion, am now consumed by this blazing passion.' (10.52)

children.text: vāgvāriṇā māṃ pariṣiñca tasmād yāvan na dahye sa ivāhjaśatruḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, sprinkle me with the water of your words, lest I burn like <s>Anjaśatru</s> [<s>Arjuna</s>];'

children.text: rārāgnir adyaiva hi māṃ didhakṣuḥ kakṣaṃ savṛkṣāgram ivotthito 'gniḥ // Saund_10.53 //
children.translated_text: for the fire of passion, desiring to burn me this very day, has risen like a fire that has reached the dry grass and treetops. (10.53)

children.text: prasīda sīdāmi vimuñca mā mune vasundharādhairya na dhairyam asti me /
children.translated_text: Be gracious, O sage — I am sinking! Release me! You who have the steadfastness of the earth — I have no steadfastness;

children.text: asūn vimokṣyāmi vimuktamānasa prayccha vā vāgamṛtaṃ mumūrṣave // Saund_10.54 //
children.translated_text: I shall give up my life, O you of liberated mind — or else administer the nectar of words to one who is about to die! (10.54)

children.text: anarthabhogena vighātaydṛṣtinā pramādadaṃśṭreṇa tamoviṣāgninā /
children.translated_text: For I have been bitten in the heart by the serpent of <s>Manmatha</s> (Love) — whose fangs are heedlessness, whose venom-fire is darkness, whose gaze brings ruin, who feeds on purposeless pleasures —

children.text: ahaṃ hi daṣṭo hṛdi manmathāhinā vidhatsya tasmād agadaṃ mahābhiṣak // Saund_10.55 //
children.translated_text: therefore, O great physician, administer the antidote! (10.55)

children.text: anena daṣṭo madanāhinā hi nā na kaś cid ātmany anavasthitaḥ sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: For no one bitten by this serpent of <s>Madana</s> (Love) has remained established in himself;

children.text: mumoha vodhyor hy acalātmano mano babhūva dhīmāṃś ca sa śantanus tanuḥ // Saund_10.56 //
children.translated_text: even the mind of <s>Vodhra</s> (the sage), who was firm as a mountain, was deluded, and the wise <s>Śantanu</s> became wasted. (10.56)

children.text: sthite viśiṣṭe tvayi saṃśraye śraye yathā na yāmīha vasan diśaṃ diśam /
children.translated_text: Since you, an excellent refuge, stand firm, may I find shelter such that, living here, I do not wander from quarter to quarter,

children.text: yathā ca labdhvā vyasanakṣayaṃ kṣayaṃ vrajāmi tan me kuru śaṃsataḥ sataḥ // Saund_10.57 //
children.translated_text: and such that, having found the destruction of affliction, I reach a [lasting] abode — grant this to me who speaks truly! (10.57)

children.text: tato jighāṃsur hṛdi tasya tattamas tamonudo naktam ivotthitaṃ tamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, desiring to destroy that deep darkness in his heart — darkness [arisen] at night, as it were, for the dispeller of darkness —

children.text: maharṣicandro jagatas tamonudas tamaḥprahīṇo nijagāda gautamaḥ // Saund_10.58 //
children.translated_text: that moon among great sages, the dispeller of the world's darkness, <s>Gautama</s> who had abandoned darkness, spoke: (10.58)

children.text: dhṛtiṃ pariṣvajya vidhūya vikriyāṃ nigṛhya tāvac chrutacetasī śṛṇu /
children.translated_text: "Embrace fortitude, shake off agitation, restrain your hearing and mind, and listen for now;

children.text: imā yadi prārthayase tvam aṅganā vidhatsva śulkārtham ihottamaṃ tapaḥ // Saund_10.59 //
children.translated_text: if you desire these women, then undertake the highest austerity here as the bride-price. (10.59)

children.text: imā hi śakyā na balān na sevayā na saṃpradānena na rūptavattayā /
children.translated_text: "For these [celestial women] cannot be won by force, nor by service, nor by gifts, nor by beauty;

children.text: imā hriyante khalu dharmacaryayā sacet praharṣaś cara dharmam ādṛtaḥ // Saund_10.60 //
children.translated_text: these are won indeed only by the practice of <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) — if you are delighted, then practice <s>dharma</s> with devotion. (10.60)

children.text: ihādhivāso divi daivataiḥ samaṃ vanāni ramyāṇy ajarāś ca yoṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: "[The reward is] dwelling here [in heaven] together with the gods, delightful groves, and ageless women —

children.text: idaṃ phalaṃ svasya śubhasya karmaṇo na dattam anyena na cāpy ahetutaḥ // Saund_10.61 //
children.translated_text: this is the fruit of one's own meritorious action, not given by another, nor arising without cause. (10.61)

children.text: kṣitau manuṣyo dhanurādhibhiḥ śramaiḥ striyaḥ kadā cid dhi labheta vā na vā /
children.translated_text: "On earth, a man, through the toils of hunting and the like, might or might not obtain women;

children.text: asaṃśayaṃ yat tv iha dharmacaryayā bhaveyur etā divi puṇakarmaṇaḥ // Saund_10.62 //
children.translated_text: but these [<s>Apsarases</s>] would undoubtedly come into being in heaven through the practice of <s>dharma</s>, for one of meritorious deeds. (10.62)

children.text: tad apramatto niyame samudyato ramasva yady apsaraso 'bhilipsase /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, being vigilant, striving in self-restraint, enjoy yourself if you desire the <s>Apsarases</s>;

children.text: ahaṃ ca te 'tra pratibhūḥ sthire vrate yathā tvam ābhir niyataṃ sameṣyasi // Saund_10.63 //
children.translated_text: and I am your guarantor in this firm vow — that you will assuredly unite with them." (10.63)

children.text: ataḥparaṃ paramam iti vyavasthitaḥ parāṃ dhṛtim paramamunau cakāra saḥ /
children.translated_text: Resolving 'henceforth, the supreme [goal],' he placed supreme trust in the supreme sage;

children.text: tato muniḥ pavana ivāmbarāt patan pragṛhya taṃ punar agaman mahītalam // Saund_10.64 //
children.translated_text: then the sage, like the wind descending from the sky, took hold of him and returned to the surface of the earth. (10.64)

body.text: Saundaranande mahākāvye svarganidarśano nāma daśamaḥ sargaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the tenth canto, entitled 'The Showing of Heaven,' in the <s>Saundarananda</s> <s>mahākāvya</s>.
CANTO XI

children.text: tatas tā yoṣito dṛṣṭvā nando nandanacāriṇīḥ /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Nanda</s>, having seen those women strolling in <s>Nandana</s> (the divine garden),

children.text: babandha niyamastambhe durdamaṃ capalaṃ manaḥ // Saund_11.1 //
children.translated_text: bound his restless, unruly mind to the pillar of self-restraint. (11.1)

children.text: so 'niśṭaniaiṣkramyaraso mlānatāmarasopamaḥ /
children.translated_text: He, who had lost all savor for going forth [from worldly life], resembling a wilting lotus,

children.text: cacāra viraso dharmaṃ niveśyāpsaraso hṛdi // Saund_11.2 //
children.translated_text: practiced <s>dharma</s> without relish, having placed the <s>Apsarases</s> in his heart. (11.2)

children.text: tathā lolendriyo bhūtvā dayitendriyagocaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, having been one of unsteady senses, given to the sensory domain of his beloved,

children.text: indriyārthavaśād eva babhūva niyatendriyaḥ // Saund_11.3 //
children.translated_text: through the very force of sense-objects he became one of restrained senses. (11.3)

children.text: kāmacaryāsu kuśalo bhikṣucaryāsu viklavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Skilled in the practices of desire, yet faltering in the practices of a mendicant,

children.text: paramācāryaviṣṭabdho brahmacaryaṃ cacāra saḥ // Saund_11.4 //
children.translated_text: held firm by the supreme teacher, he practiced <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy). (11.4)

children.text: saṃvṛtena ca śāntena tīvreṇa madanena ca /
children.translated_text: With passion both suppressed and tranquil yet also fierce,

children.text: jalāgner iva saṃsargāc chaśāma ca śuśoṣa ca // Saund_11.5 //
children.translated_text: like the contact of water and fire, he both cooled and burned. (11.5)

children.text: svabhāvadarśanīyo 'pi vairūpyam agamat param /
children.translated_text: Though naturally handsome, he arrived at the utmost disfigurement

children.text: cintayāpsarasāṃ caiva niyamenāyatena ca // Saund_11.6 //
children.translated_text: through brooding over the <s>Apsarases</s> and through prolonged self-restraint. (11.6)

children.text: prastaveṣv api bhāryāyāṃ priyabhāryas tathāpi saḥ /
children.translated_text: Even when occasions arose to mention his wife, he who loved his wife

children.text: vītarāga ivottasthau na jaharṣa na cukṣubhe // Saund_11.7 //
children.translated_text: rose up as if free from passion — he neither rejoiced nor was agitated. (11.7)

children.text: taṃ vyavasthitam ājñāya bhāryārāgāt parāṅmukham /
children.translated_text: Knowing him to be established [in restraint], his face turned away from passion for his wife,

children.text: abhigamyābhravīn nandam ānandaḥ praṇayād idam // Saund_11.8 //
children.translated_text: <s>Ānanda</s> approached <s>Nanda</s> and spoke this out of affection: (11.8)

children.text: aho sadṛśam ārabdhaṃ śrutasyābhijanasya ca /
children.translated_text: "Ah, how fitting for one of your learning and noble birth —

children.text: nigṛhītendriyaḥ svastho niyame yadi saṃsthitaḥ // Saund_11.9 //
children.translated_text: if, with senses restrained and self-composed, you are established in discipline! (11.9)

children.text: abhiṣvaktasya kāmeṣu rāgiṇo viṣayātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: "For one who was attached to pleasures, passionate, devoted to sense-objects,

children.text: yad iyaṃ saṃvid utpannā neyam alpena hetunā // Saund_11.10 //
children.translated_text: this transformation of awareness has arisen [in you] — this is not from a small cause. (11.10)

children.text: vyādhir alpena yatnena mṛduḥ pratinivāryate /
children.translated_text: "A mild disease is averted with little effort;

children.text: prabalaḥ prabalair eva yatnair naśyatti vā na vā // Saund_11.11 //
children.translated_text: a powerful one, only with powerful efforts — and even then, it may or may not be destroyed. (11.11)

children.text: durharo mānaso vyādhir balavāṃś ca tavābhavat /
children.translated_text: "The mental disease [you had] was hard to remove and was powerful;

children.text: vinivṛtto yadi sa te sarvathā dhṛtimānasi // Saund_11.12 //
children.translated_text: if it has turned away from you, then you are truly steadfast in every way. (11.12)

children.text: duṣkaraṃ sādhv anāryeṇa māninā caiva mārdavam /
children.translated_text: "Virtue is difficult for an ignoble person; gentleness for a proud one;

children.text: atisargaś ca lubdhena bramacaryaṃ ca rāgiṇā // Saund_11.13 //
children.translated_text: generosity for a miser; and <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) for one filled with passion. (11.13)

children.text: ekas tu mama saṃdehas tavāsyāṃ niyame dhṛtau /
children.translated_text: "But I have one doubt regarding this discipline of yours;

children.text: atrānunayam icchāmi vaktavyaṃ yadi manase // Saund_11.14 //
children.translated_text: I wish for a clarification here — if it may be spoken to [your] mind. (11.14)

children.text: ārjavābhihitaṃ vākyaṃ na ca gantavyam anyathā /
children.translated_text: "A word spoken in candor should not be taken amiss;

children.text: rūkṣam apy āśaye śuddhe rūkṣato naiti sajjanaḥ // Saund_11.15 //
children.translated_text: even if harsh, a good person does not take it harshly when the intention is pure. (11.15)

children.text: spriyaṃ hi hitaṃ snigdham asnigdham ahitaṃ priyaṃ /
children.translated_text: "For what is beneficial is not [always] agreeable, and what is agreeable is not [always] beneficial;

children.text: durlabhaṃ tu priyahitaṃ svādu pathyam ivauṣadham // Saund_11.16 //
children.translated_text: but that which is both agreeable and beneficial is rare — like medicine that is both palatable and wholesome. (11.16)

children.text: viśvāsaś cārthacaryā ca sāmānyaṃ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ /
children.translated_text: "Trust, conduct in mutual interest, sharing of joy and sorrow,

children.text: marṣaṇaṃ praṇayaś caiva mitravṛttir iyaṃ satām // Saund_11.17 //
children.translated_text: forbearance, and affection — this is the conduct of friendship among the good. (11.17)

children.text: tad idaṃ tvā vivakṣāmi praṇayān na jīghāṃsayā /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, I wish to say this to you out of affection, not from a desire to harm;

children.text: tvacchreyo hi vivakṣā me yato nārhāmy upekṣitum // Saund_11.18 //
children.translated_text: for my desire to speak concerns your welfare, which I cannot simply overlook. (11.18)

children.text: apsarobhṛtako dharmaṃ carasīty abhidīyase /
children.translated_text: "It is said that you practice <s>dharma</s> as a hireling of the <s>Apsarases</s> —

children.text: kim idaṃ bhūtam āhosvit prarihāso 'yam īdṛśaḥ // Saund_11.19 //
children.translated_text: is this true, or is it a jest of this kind? (11.19)

children.text: yadi tāvad idaṃ satyaṃ vakṣyāmy atra yudaṣadham /
children.translated_text: "If this is indeed true, I shall state what is fitting as a remedy here;

children.text: auddhatyam atha vaktṝmā, abhidāsyāmi tattvataḥ // Saund_11.20 //
children.translated_text: if it is mere frivolous gossip, I shall address it truthfully. (11.20)

children.text: ślakṣṇapūrvam atho tena hṛdi so 'bhihatas tadā /
children.translated_text: Struck then in the heart by those words, gently spoken at first,

children.text: dhyātvā dīrghaṃ niśaśvāsa kiṃ cic cāvāñmukho 'bhavat // Saund_11.21 //
children.translated_text: he pondered, heaved a long sigh, and became somewhat downcast. (11.21)

children.text: tatas tasyeṅgitaṃ jñātvā manaḥsaṃkalpasūcakam /
children.translated_text: Then, knowing his gesture — indicative of his mind's intention —

children.text: babhāṣe vākyam ānando madhurodarkam apriyam // Saund_11.22 //
children.translated_text: <s>Ānanda</s> spoke words that were unpleasant but whose outcome was sweet: (11.22)

children.text: ākāreṇāvagacchāmi tava dharmaprayojanam /
children.translated_text: "From your bearing I understand the motive of your <s>dharma</s>-practice,

children.text: yaj jñātvā tvayi jātaṃ me hāsyaṃ kāuṇyam eva ca // Saund_11.23 //
children.translated_text: and knowing this, there has arisen in me both laughter and pity toward you. (11.23)

children.text: yathāsanārthaṃ skandhena kaś cid gurvīṃ śilāṃ vahet /
children.translated_text: "Just as someone might carry a heavy stone on his shoulder for the sake of sitting down [later],

children.text: tadvat tvam api kāmārthaṃ niyamaṃ voḍhum udyataḥ // Saund_11.24 //
children.translated_text: so too you are determined to bear self-restraint for the sake of desire. (11.24)

children.text: titāḍayiṣayāsṛpto yathā meṣo 'pasarpati /
children.translated_text: "Just as a ram retreats from a desire to butt [harder],

children.text: tadvad abrahmacaryāya brahmacaryam idaṃ tava // Saund_11.25 //
children.translated_text: so this <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) of yours is [actually] for the sake of non-celibacy. (11.25)

children.text: cikrīṣanti yathā paṇyaṃ vaṇijo lābhalipsayā /
children.translated_text: "Just as merchants sell their wares out of desire for profit,

children.text: dharmacaryā tava tathā paṇyabhūtā na śāntaye // Saund_11.26 //
children.translated_text: so your practice of <s>dharma</s> is a commodity — not for the sake of peace. (11.26)

children.text: yathā phalaviśeṣārthaṃ bījaṃ vapati kārṣakaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Just as a farmer sows seed for the sake of a specific fruit,

children.text: tadvad viṣayakārpaṇyād viṣayāṃs tyaktavān asi // Saund_11.27 //
children.translated_text: so, out of wretchedness for sense-objects, you have renounced sense-objects [only to regain them]. (11.27)

children.text: ākāṅkṣec ca yathā rogaṃ pratīkārasukhepsayā /
children.translated_text: "Just as one might welcome a disease for the sake of the pleasure of its cure,

children.text: duḥkham anvicchati bhavāṃs tathā viṣayatṛśṇayā // Saund_11.28 //
children.translated_text: so you, through thirst for sense-objects, seek suffering. (11.28)

children.text: yathā paśyati madhv eva na prapātam avekṣate /
children.translated_text: "Just as one sees only the honey and does not look at the precipice,

children.text: paśyasy apsarasas tadvad bhraṃśam ante na paśyasi // Saund_11.29 //
children.translated_text: so you see the <s>Apsarases</s> but do not see the fall at the end. (11.29)

children.text: hṛdi kāmāgninā dīpte kāyena vahato vratam /
children.translated_text: "When the fire of desire is blazing in your heart, while your body carries the vow,

children.text: kim idaṃ brahmacaryaṃ te manasābrahmacāriṇaḥ // Saund_11.30 //
children.translated_text: what kind of <s>brahmacarya</s> is this of yours — you who are not a celibate in mind? (11.30)

children.text: saṃsāre vartamānena yadā cāpsarasas tvayā /
children.translated_text: "Moreover, while revolving in <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), you have obtained and lost

children.text: prāptās tyaktāś ca śataśas tābhyaḥ kim iti te spṛhā // Saund_11.31 //
