children.translated_text: <s>Apsarases</s> by the hundreds — why then this craving for them? (11.31)

children.text: tṛptir nāstīndhanair agner nāmbhasā lavaṇāmbhasaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Fire is not sated by fuel; the salt ocean not by water;

children.text: nāpi kāmaiḥ satṛṣṇasya tasmāt kāmā na tṛptaye // Saund_11.32 //
children.translated_text: nor the thirsty one by desires — therefore, desires do not lead to satisfaction. (11.32)

children.text: atṛptau ca kutaḥ śāntir aśāntau ca kutaḥ sukham /
children.translated_text: "And without satisfaction, where is peace? Without peace, where is happiness?

children.text: asukhe ca kutaḥ pṛtir aprītau ca kuto ratiḥ // Saund_11.33 //
children.translated_text: Without happiness, where is contentment? Without contentment, where is delight? (11.33)

children.text: riraṃsā yadi te tasmād adhyātme dhīyatāṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: "If you desire true enjoyment, therefore, let your mind be fixed on the inner self (<s>adhyātma</s>);

children.text: praśānta cānavadyā ca nāsty adhyātmasamā ratiḥ // Saund_11.34 //
children.translated_text: for there is no delight equal to the delight of the inner self — tranquil and blameless. (11.34)

children.text: na tatra kāryaṃ tūryais te na strībhir na vibhūṣanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: "There you have no need of musical instruments, nor of women, nor of ornaments;

children.text: ekas tvaṃ yatratrasthas tayā ratyābhiraṃsyase // Saund_11.35 //
children.translated_text: alone, wherever you may be, you will delight in that pleasure. (11.35)

children.text: mānasaṃ balavad duḥkhaṃ tarṣe tiṣṭhati tiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: "Powerful mental suffering persists as long as craving persists;

children.text: taṃ tarṣaṃ chindhi duḥkhaṃ hi tṛṣṇā cāsti ca nāsti ca // Saund_11.36 //
children.translated_text: cut that craving — for suffering truly exists and does not exist [depending on] <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (thirst). (11.36)

children.text: saṃpattau vā vipattau vā divā vā naktam eva vā /
children.translated_text: "Whether in prosperity or adversity, by day or by night,

children.text: kāmeṣu hi saṭṛṣñasya na śāntir upadadyate // Saund_11.37 //
children.translated_text: for one who thirsts after desires, no peace is to be found. (11.37)

children.text: kāmānāṃ prārthanā duḥkhā prāptau tṛptir na vidyate /
children.translated_text: "The pursuit of desires is suffering; in their attainment there is no satisfaction;

children.text: viyogān niyataḥ śoko viyogaś ca dhruvo divi // Saund_11.38 //
children.translated_text: from separation comes inevitable grief, and separation in heaven is certain. (11.38)

children.text: kṛtvāpi duṣkaraṃ karma svargaṃ labdhvāpi durlabham /
children.translated_text: "Even after performing the most difficult austerities and obtaining the hard-to-attain heaven,

children.text: nṛlokaṃ punar evaiti pravāsāt svagṛhaṃ yathā // Saund_11.39 //
children.translated_text: one returns again to the world of mortals, just as one returns home from a sojourn abroad. (11.39)

children.text: yadā bhraṣṭasya kuśalaṃ śiṣṭaṃ kiṃ cin na vidyate /
children.translated_text: "When the merit of the fallen one is exhausted, and nothing remains,

children.text: triyakṣu pitṛloke vā narake vopapadyate // Saund_11.40 //
children.translated_text: he is reborn among animals, in the world of the ancestors, or in hell. (11.40)

children.text: tasya bhuktavataḥ svarge viṣayān uttamān api /
children.translated_text: "For one who has enjoyed even the highest pleasures in heaven,

children.text: bhraṣṭasyārtasya duḥkhena kim āsvādaḥ karoti saḥ // Saund_11.41 //
children.translated_text: and then falls, stricken with suffering — what good does that former savoring do him? (11.41)

children.text: śyenāya prāṇivātsalyāt svamāṃsāny api dattavān /
children.translated_text: "<s>Śibi</s>, out of compassion for living beings, gave even his own flesh to a hawk,

children.text: śibhiḥ svargāt paribhraṣṭas tādṛk kṛtvāpi duṣkaram // Saund_11.42 //
children.translated_text: yet fell from heaven — even after performing such a difficult deed. (11.42)

children.text: śakrasyārdhāsanaṃ gatvā pūrvapārthiva eva yaḥ /
children.translated_text: "He who, as a former king, attained half the throne of <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>),

children.text: sadevataṃ gate kāle māndhātādhaḥ punar yayau // Saund_11.43 //
children.translated_text: <s>Māndhātṛ</s>, when his time came, fell down again, together with the gods. (11.43)

children.text: rājyaṃ kṛtvāpi devānāṃ papāta nahuṣo bhuvi /
children.translated_text: "<s>Nahuṣa</s>, even after ruling the kingdom of the gods, fell to earth;

children.text: prāptaḥ kila bjuaṅgatvaṃ nādyāpi parimucyate // Saund_11.44 //
children.translated_text: having obtained the state of a serpent, he is said to be not yet liberated. (11.44)

children.text: tathaivelivilo rāja rājavṛttena saṃskṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Likewise, King <s>Elivilā</s> (Purūravas), refined by royal conduct,

children.text: svargaṃ gatvā punar bhraṣṭaḥ kūrmībhūtaḥ kilārṇave // Saund_11.45 //
children.translated_text: having gone to heaven, fell again and became a tortoise in the ocean, it is said. (11.45)

children.text: bhūrdiyumno yayātiś ca te cānye ca nṛparṣabhāḥ /
children.translated_text: "<s>Bhūridyumna</s>, <s>Yayāti</s>, and those other bull-like kings

children.text: karmabhir dyām abhikrīya tatkṣayāt punar atyajan // Saund_11.46 //
children.translated_text: purchased heaven through their deeds, and upon the exhaustion of those [deeds], abandoned it again. (11.46)

children.text: asurāḥ pūrvadvās tu surair apahṛtaśriyaḥ /
children.translated_text: "The <s>Asuras</s>, who formerly were gods, their glory seized by the <s>Suras</s> (gods),

children.text: śriyaṃ samanuśocantaḥ pātālaṃ śarañaṃ yayuḥ // Saund_11.47 //
children.translated_text: lamenting over their lost glory, took refuge in the netherworld. (11.47)

children.text: kiṃ ca rājarṣibhis tāvad asurair vā surādibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: "But what of royal sages, or <s>Asuras</s>, or gods and the like?

children.text: mahendrāḥ śataśaḥ petur māhātmyam api na sthiram // Saund_11.48 //
children.translated_text: Hundreds of <s>Mahendras</s> (<s>Indras</s>) have fallen — even [divine] greatness is not permanent. (11.48)

children.text: saṃsadaṃ śobhayitvaindrīm upendraś ca trivikramaḥ /
children.translated_text: "And <s>Upendra</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), the <s>Trivikrama</s> (Three-Strider), having adorned <s>Indra</s>'s assembly,

children.text: kṣīṇakarmā papātovriṃ madhyād apsarasāṃ rasan // Saund_11.49 //
children.translated_text: when his merit was exhausted, fell to earth from amidst the <s>Apsarases</s>. (11.49)

children.text: hā caitraratha hā vāpi hā mandākini hā priye /
children.translated_text: "'Alas, <s>Caitraratha</s> (the garden of Kubera)! Alas, the lake! Alas, <s>Mandākinī</s>! Alas, beloved!'

children.text: ity ārtā vilapanto 'pi gāṃ patanti divaukasaḥ // Saund_11.50 //
children.translated_text: — thus lamenting in anguish, the celestial beings fall to earth. (11.50)

children.text: tīvraṃ hy uptadyate duḥkham iha tāvan mumūrṣatām /
children.translated_text: "For even here [on earth], intense suffering arises for those about to die;

children.text: kiṃ punaḥ patatāṃ svargād evānte sukhasevinām // Saund_11.51 //
children.translated_text: how much more so for those who fall from heaven, pleasure-seekers, at the very end! (11.51)

children.text: rajo gṛhṇanti vāsāṃsi mlāyanti paramāḥ srajaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Their garments gather dust, their supreme garlands wilt,

children.text: gātrebhyo jāyate svedo ratir bhavati nāsane // Saund_11.52 //
children.translated_text: sweat arises on their limbs, and delight in their seats ceases. (11.52)

children.text: etāny ādau nimittāni cyutau svargād divaukasām /
children.translated_text: "These are the first omens of the fall of celestial beings from heaven —

children.text: aniṣṭāniva martyānām ariṣṭāni mumūrṣatām // Saund_11.53 //
children.translated_text: like the unwelcome portents of death for mortals about to die. (11.53)

children.text: sukham utpadyate yac ca divi kāmān upāśnatām /
children.translated_text: "And the happiness that arises in heaven for those enjoying desires,

children.text: yac ca duḥkhaṃ nipatatāṃ duḥkham eva viṣiṣyate // Saund_11.54 //
children.translated_text: and the suffering of those who fall — the suffering is far greater. (11.54)

children.text: tasmād asvantam atrāṇam aviśvāsyam atarpakam /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, knowing heaven to be impermanent, without protection, untrustworthy, unsatisfying,

children.text: vijñāya kṣayiṇaṃ svargam apavarge matiṃ kuru // Saund_11.55 //
children.translated_text: and perishable — set your mind on <s>apavarga</s> (final liberation). (11.55)

children.text: aśarīraṃ bhavāgraṃ hi gatvāpi munir udrakaḥ /
children.translated_text: "For even the sage <s>Udraka</s>, having gone to <s>Bhavāgra</s> (the summit of existence), which is bodiless —

children.text: karmaṇo 'nte cyutas tasmāt tiryagyoniṃ prapatsyate // Saund_11.56 //
children.translated_text: at the end of [his] <s>karma</s>, having fallen from there, he will be reborn in the animal realm. // Saund_11.56 //

children.text: maitrayā sptavārṣikyā brahmalokam ito gataḥ /
children.translated_text: Having gone from here to the <s>Brahmaloka</s> through seven years of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness),

children.text: sunetraḥ punar āvṛtto garbhavāsam upeyivān // Saund_11.57 //
children.translated_text: <s>Sunetra</s> returned again and entered the state of dwelling in a womb. // Saund_11.57 //

children.text: yada caiśvcaryavanto 'pi kṣayiñaḥ svargavāsinaḥ /
children.translated_text: When even the powerful inhabitants of heaven are subject to decay,

children.text: ko nāma svargavāsāya kṣeṣṇave spṛhayed budhaḥ // Saund_11.58 //
children.translated_text: what wise person would desire residence in heaven, which is perishable? // Saund_11.58 //

children.text: sūtreṇa baddho hi yathā vihaṅgo vyāvartate dūragato 'pi bhūyaḥ /
children.translated_text: For just as a bird tied by a string returns even after going far away,

children.text: ajñānasūtreṇa tathāvabaddho gato 'pi dūraṃ punar eti lokaḥ // Saund_11.59 //
children.translated_text: so too the world, bound by the string of ignorance, returns again even after going far. // Saund_11.59 //

children.text: kṛtvā kālavilakṣañaṃ pratibhuvā mukto yathā bandhanād bhuktvā veśmasukhāny atītya samayaṃ bhūyo viśed bandhanam /
children.translated_text: Just as one who, having committed a breach of terms, is released from prison on surety, and after enjoying the comforts of home, when the time has passed, enters prison again —

children.text: tadvad dyāṃ pratibhūvad ātmaniyamair dhyānādibhiḥ prāptavān kāle karmasu teṣu bhuktaviṣayeṣv ākṛṣyate gāṃ punaḥ // Saund_11.60 //
children.translated_text: so too, one who has reached heaven as if on surety through self-restraints such as <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and the like, when those <s>karmas</s> are exhausted and their fruits consumed, is dragged back to earth again. // Saund_11.60 //

children.text: antarjālagatāḥ pramattamanaso minās taḍāge yathā jānantī vyasanaṃ na rodhajanitaṃ svasthāś caranty ambhasi /
children.translated_text: Just as fish inside a net in a pond, their minds heedless, unaware of the calamity caused by the enclosure, move about freely in the water,

children.text: antarlokagatāḥ kṛtārthamatayas tadvad divi dhyāyino manyante śivam acyutaṃ dhruvam iti svaṃ sthānam āvartakam // Saund_11.61 //
children.translated_text: so too, meditators in heaven, situated within the [cycle of the] world, thinking themselves accomplished, consider their own abode — which is subject to return — as auspicious, permanent, and everlasting. // Saund_11.61 //

children.text: tajjanmavyādhimṛtyuvyasanaparigataṃ matvā jagad idaṃ saṃsāre bhrāmyamāṇaṃ divi nṛṣu narake tiryakpitṛṣu ca /
children.translated_text: Knowing this world to be beset by the calamities of birth, disease, and death, wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s> — among gods, humans, in hell, among animals, and among the departed ancestors —

children.text: yat trāṇaṃ nirbhayaṃ yac chivam amarajaraṃ niḥṣokam amṛtaṃ taddhetor brahmacaryaṃ cara jahihi calaṃ svargaṃ prati rucim // Saund_11.62 //
children.translated_text: for the sake of that which is protection, fearlessness, auspiciousness, freedom from aging and death, sorrowlessness, and immortality — practice <s>brahmacarya</s> (the holy life), and abandon your inclination toward the unstable heaven. // Saund_11.62 //

body.translated_text: In the <s>Saundarananda</s> <s>mahākāvya</s>, this is the eleventh canto, called 'The Deprecation of Heaven.'
CANTO XII

children.text: apsarobhṛtako dharmaṃ carasīty atha coditaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, having been told by <s>Ānanda</s> that he was practicing <s>dharma</s> as a hired servant of the <s>apsarases</s>,

children.text: ānandena tadā nandaḥ paraṃ vrīḍam upāgamat // Saund_12.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s> was overcome by extreme shame. // Saund_12.1 //

children.text: tasya vriḍena mahatā pramodo hṛdi nābhavat /
children.translated_text: Due to that great shame, joy did not arise in his heart;

children.text: aprāmodyena vimukhaṃ nāvatasthe vrate manaḥ // Saund_12.2 //
children.translated_text: and due to the absence of joy, his mind turned away and did not remain steadfast in the vow. // Saund_12.2 //

children.text: kāmarāgapradhāno 'pi parihāsasamo 'pi san /
children.translated_text: Though predominantly [subject to] passion for sensual pleasures, and though equal [in bearing] to ridicule,

children.text: paripākagate hetau na sa tan mamṛṣe vacaḥ // Saund_12.3 //
children.translated_text: when the cause had reached maturity, he could not endure those words. // Saund_12.3 //

children.text: aparīkṣabkabhāvāc ca pūrvaṃ matvā divaṃ dhruvam /
children.translated_text: And because he had not investigated before and had considered heaven to be permanent,

children.text: tasmāt kṣeṣṇuṃ pariśrutya bhṛśaṃ saṃvegam eyivān // Saund_12.4 //
children.translated_text: having learned that it was perishable, he was overcome by intense spiritual urgency (<s>saṃvega</s>). // Saund_12.4 //

children.text: tasya svargān nivavṛte saṃkalpāśvo manorathaḥ /
children.translated_text: His desire, whose steed was imagination, turned back from heaven,

children.text: mahāratha ivonmārgād apramattasya sāratheḥ // Saund_12.5 //
children.translated_text: like a great chariot [turned back] from a wrong path by an attentive charioteer. // Saund_12.5 //

children.text: svargatarṣān nivṛttaś ca sadyaḥ svastha ivābhavat /
children.translated_text: Having turned back from the craving for heaven, he immediately became, as it were, healthy,

children.text: mṛṣṭād apathyād virato jijīvṣur ivāturaḥ // Saund_12.6 //
children.translated_text: like a sick man who wishes to live and has given up rich but unwholesome food. // Saund_12.6 //

children.text: visasmāra priyāṃ bhāryāṃ aspsarodarśanād yathā /
children.translated_text: Just as he had forgotten his dear wife upon seeing the <s>apsarases</s>,

children.text: tathānityatayodvignas tatyājāpsaraso 'pi saḥ // Saund_12.7 //
children.translated_text: so too, being agitated by impermanence, he abandoned even the <s>apsarases</s>. // Saund_12.7 //

children.text: mahatām api bhūtānām āvṛtti iti cintayan /
children.translated_text: Reflecting that even great beings are subject to return [to <s>saṃsāra</s>],

children.text: saṃvegāc ca sarāgo 'pi vītarāga ivābhavat // Saund_12.8 //
children.translated_text: even though still attached, he became, as it were, free from attachment, due to spiritual urgency. // Saund_12.8 //

children.text: babhūva sa hi saṃvegaḥ śreyasas tasya vṛddhaye /
children.translated_text: For that spiritual urgency served the growth of his spiritual welfare,

children.text: dhātur edhir ivākhyāte paṭhito 'kṣaracintakaiḥ // Saund_12.9 //
children.translated_text: like the root <s>edh</s> ('to grow'), recited by grammarians, stated in the [grammatical] element [list]. // Saund_12.9 //

children.text: na tu kāmānmanas tasya kena cij jagṛhe dhṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: But no firmness held his mind back from sensual desires

children.text: triṣu kāleṣu sarveṣu nipāto 'stir iva smṛtaḥ // Saund_12.10 //
children.translated_text: at any of the three times whatsoever, just as the particle <s>asti</s> ('is') is remembered [as applying] in all [tenses]. // Saund_12.10 //

children.text: khelagāmī mahābāhur gajendra iva nirmadaḥ /
children.translated_text: Moving with a slow gait, mighty-armed, like a great elephant without rut,

children.text: so 'bhyagacchad guruṃ kale vivakṣur bhāvam ātmanaḥ // Saund_12.11 //
children.translated_text: he approached his teacher at the right time, wishing to express his inner state. // Saund_12.11 //

children.text: praṇamya ca gurau mūrdhnā bāṣpavyākulalocanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Bowing his head before the teacher, his eyes filled with tears,

children.text: kṛtvānjalim uvācedaṃ hriyā kiṃ cid avāñmukhaḥ // Saund_12.12 //
children.translated_text: with palms joined, he spoke thus, his face slightly downcast with shame: // Saund_12.12 //

children.text: apsaraḥprāptaye yan me bhagavan pratibhūr asi /
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Bhagavān</s>, you who are my surety for attaining the <s>apsarases</s> —

children.text: nāpsarobhir mamārtho 'sti pratibhūtvaṃ tyajāmy aham // Saund_12.13 //
children.translated_text: I have no desire for the <s>apsarases</s>; I release you from your suretyship. // Saund_12.13 //

children.text: śrutvā hy āvartakaṃ svargaṃ saṃsārasya ca citratām /
children.translated_text: For having heard that heaven is subject to return, and [having heard] of the diversity of <s>saṃsāra</s>,

children.text: na martyeṣu na deveṣu pravṛttir mama rocate // Saund_12.14 //
children.translated_text: engagement neither among mortals nor among gods appeals to me. // Saund_12.14 //

children.text: yadi prāpya divaṃ yatnān niyamena damena ca /
children.translated_text: If, having reached heaven through effort, restraint, and self-control,

children.text: avitṛptāḥ patanaty ante svargāya tyāgine namaḥ // Saund_12.15 //
children.translated_text: they fall at the end, unsatiated — homage to the one who renounces for the sake of heaven! // Saund_12.15 //

children.text: ataś ca nikhilaṃ lokaṃ vidibā sacarācaram /
children.translated_text: And therefore, knowing the entire world, with all its moving and unmoving [beings],

children.text: sarvaduḥkhakṣayakare tvaddharme parame rame // Saund_12.16 //
children.translated_text: I delight in your supreme <s>Dharma</s>, which removes all suffering. // Saund_12.16 //

children.text: tasmād vyāsamāsābhyāṃ tan me vyākhyātum arhasi /
children.translated_text: Therefore, please explain to me, in summary and in detail,

children.text: yac chrutvā śṛṇvatāṃ śreṣṭha paramaṃ prāpnuyāṃ padam // Saund_12.17 //
children.translated_text: that by hearing which, O best of hearers, I may attain the supreme state.' // Saund_12.17 //

children.text: tatas tasyāśayaṃ jñātvā vipakṣāṇindriyāṇi ca /
children.translated_text: Then, knowing his disposition and [that] his faculties were opposed [to defilements],

children.text: śreyaś caivāmukhībhūtaṃ nijagāda tathāgataḥ // Saund_12.18 //
children.translated_text: and that [his] spiritual welfare had become manifest, the <s>Tathāgata</s> spoke: // Saund_12.18 //

children.text: aho pratyavamarśo 'yaṃ śreyasas te purojavaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Ah, this reflection of yours runs ahead of your spiritual welfare,

children.text: araṇyāṃ mathyamānāyām agner dhūma ivotthitaḥ // Saund_12.19 //
children.translated_text: like smoke rising when the fire-drill is being churned. // Saund_12.19 //

children.text: ciram unmārgavihṛto lolair indiyavājibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Long carried along the wrong path by the fickle horses of the senses,

children.text: avatirṇo 'si panthānaṃ diṣṭyā dṛśtyāvimūḍhayā // Saund_12.20 //
children.translated_text: you have fortunately descended onto the [right] road, with your vision undeluded. // Saund_12.20 //

children.text: adya te saphalaṃ janma lābho 'dya sumahāṃs tava /
children.translated_text: Today your birth is fruitful; today your gain is supremely great,

children.text: yasya kāmarasjñasya naiṣkramyāyotsukaṃ manaḥ // Saund_12.21 //
children.translated_text: you whose mind, though you know sensual pleasures, is eager for renunciation. // Saund_12.21 //

children.text: loke 'sminn ālayārāme nivṛttau durlabhā ratiḥ /
children.translated_text: In this world that delights in attachment, delight in cessation is hard to find;

children.text: vyathante hy apunarbhāvāt prapātād iva bāliśāḥ // Saund_12.22 //
children.translated_text: for the childish are distressed by non-return [to existence], as from a precipice. // Saund_12.22 //

children.text: duḥkhaṃ na syāt sukhaṃ me syād iti prayatate janaḥ /
children.translated_text: People strive [thinking] "May I have no suffering, may I have happiness,"

children.text: atyantaduḥkhoparamaṃ sukhaṃ tac ca na budhyate // Saund_12.23 //
children.translated_text: yet they do not understand that happiness which is the complete cessation of suffering. // Saund_12.23 //

children.text: airbhūteṣv anityeṣu satataṃ duḥkhahetuśu /
children.translated_text: Attached to sensual pleasures and the like, which arise, are impermanent, and are constantly causes of suffering,

children.text: kāmādiṣu jagat saktaṃ na vetti sukham avyayam // Saund_12.24 //
children.translated_text: the world does not know imperishable happiness. // Saund_12.24 //

children.text: sarvaduḥkhāpahaṃ tat tu hastatham amṛtaṃ tava /
children.translated_text: But that [happiness] which removes all suffering — that nectar is within your reach,

children.text: viṣaṃ pītvā yad agadaṃ samaye pātum icchasi // Saund_12.25 //
children.translated_text: since, having drunk poison, you now wish to drink the remedy at the right time. // Saund_12.25 //

children.text: anarhasaṃsārabhayaṃ mānārhaṃ te cikīrṣitam /
children.translated_text: Worthy of honor is your intention, which fears the unworthy <s>saṃsāra</s>;

children.text: rāgāgnis tādṛṣo yasya dharmonmukha parāṇmukhaḥ // Saund_12.26 //
children.translated_text: [for you are one] whose fire of passion, so formidable, is turned away, [now] turned toward <s>dharma</s>. // Saund_12.26 //

children.text: rāgoddāmena manasā sarvathā duṣkarā dhṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: With a mind unrestrained by passion, firmness is by all means difficult to attain,

children.text: sadoṣam salilaṃ dṛṣṭvā pathineva pipāsunā // Saund_12.27 //
children.translated_text: like [self-restraint for] a thirsty person on a road who sees water, even if polluted. // Saund_12.27 //

children.text: īdṛśī nāma buddhis te niruddhā rajasābhavat /
children.translated_text: Such was your intellect, which had been obstructed by <s>rajas</s> (passion),

children.text: rajasā caṇḍavātena vivasvata iva prabhā // Saund_12.28 //
children.translated_text: like the radiance of the sun [obscured] by the fierce wind of <s>rajas</s> (dust). // Saund_12.28 //

children.text: sā jighāṃsus tamo hārdaṃ yā saṃprati vijṛmbhate /
children.translated_text: That [intellect] which now expands, intent on destroying the darkness of the heart,

children.text: tamo naiśaṃ prabhā saurī vinirgīrṇeva meruṇā // Saund_12.29 //
children.translated_text: [is] like the solar radiance, as if poured forth by <s>Meru</s>, [destroying] the darkness of night. // Saund_12.29 //

children.text: yuktarūpam idaṃ caiva śuddhasattvasya cetasaḥ /
children.translated_text: And this is fitting for a mind whose <s>sattva</s> is pure —

children.text: yat te syān naiṣṭhike sūkṣme śreyasi śraqddadhānatā // Saund_12.30 //
children.translated_text: that you should have faith in the ultimate, subtle spiritual good. // Saund_12.30 //

children.text: dharmacchandam imaṃ tasmād vivardhayitum arhasi /
children.translated_text: Therefore, you should cultivate this desire for <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: sarvadharmā hi dharmajña niyamācx chandahetavaḥ // Saund_12.31 //
children.translated_text: for all <s>dharmas</s>, O knower of <s>dharma</s>, invariably have desire as their cause. // Saund_12.31 //

children.text: satyāṃ gamanabuddhau hi gamanāya pravartate /
children.translated_text: For when there is the intention to go, one proceeds to go;

children.text: śayyābuddhau ca śayanaṃ sthānabuddhau tathā sthitiḥ // Saund_12.32 //
children.translated_text: when there is the intention to lie down, one lies down; and likewise, when there is the intention to stand, one stands. // Saund_12.32 //

children.text: antarbhūmigataṃ hy ambhaḥ śraddadhāti naro yadā /
children.translated_text: For when a person has faith that water lies beneath the ground,

children.text: arthitve sati yatnena tadā khanati gām imām // Saund_12.33 //
children.translated_text: then, when the need exists, he digs this earth with effort. // Saund_12.33 //

children.text: nārthi yady agninā vā syāc chraddadhyāt taṃ na vāraṇau /
children.translated_text: If one were not in need of fire, or had no faith in it within the wood,

children.text: mathnīyān nāraṇiṃ kaś cit tadbhāve sati mathyate // Saund_12.34 //
children.translated_text: no one would churn the fire-drill; but when that [faith and need] exist, it is churned. // Saund_12.34 //

children.text: sasyotpattiṃ yadi na vā śraddadhyāt kārṣakaḥ kṣitau /
children.translated_text: If a farmer had no faith in the production of crops from the earth,

children.text: arthī sasyena vā na syād bhījāni na vaped bhuvi // Saund_12.35 //
children.translated_text: or were not in need of crops, he would not sow seeds in the ground. // Saund_12.35 //

children.text: ataś ca hasta ity uktā mayā śraddhā viśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: And therefore, faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) has been called by me especially a "hand,"

children.text: yasmād gṛhnāti saddharmaṃ dāyaṃ hasta ivākṣataḥ // Saund_12.36 //
children.translated_text: because, like an unimpaired hand, it grasps the true <s>dharma</s> as a gift. // Saund_12.36 //

children.text: prādhānyād indriyam iti shtiratvād balam ity ataḥ /
children.translated_text: Because of its primacy, it is called a "faculty" (<s>indriya</s>); because of its steadfastness, it is called "strength" (<s>bala</s>);

children.text: guṇadāridryaśamanād dhanam ity abhivarṇitā // Saund_12.37 //
children.translated_text: and because it removes the poverty of virtues, it has been described as "wealth" (<s>dhana</s>). // Saund_12.37 //

children.text: rakṣaṇārthena dharmasya tatheṣīkety udāhṛtā /
children.translated_text: For the purpose of protecting <s>dharma</s>, it is likewise called a "shaft" (<s>iṣīkā</s>);

children.text: loke 'smin durlabhatvāc ca ratnam ity abhihāṣitā // Saund_12.38 //
children.translated_text: and because of its rarity in this world, it is called a "jewel" (<s>ratna</s>). // Saund_12.38 //

children.text: punaś ca bījam ity uktā nimittaṃ śreyasotpadā /
children.translated_text: And again, it is called a "seed" (<s>bīja</s>), as the cause of the arising of spiritual welfare;

children.text: pāvanārthena pāpasya nadīty abhihitā punaḥ // Saund_12.39 //
children.translated_text: and again, for the purpose of purifying sin, it is called a "river" (<s>nadī</s>). // Saund_12.39 //

children.text: yasmād dharmasya cottpattau śraddhā kāraṇam uttamam /
children.translated_text: Since faith is the supreme cause for the arising of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: mayoktā kāryatas tasmāt tatra tatra tathā tathā // Saund_12.40 //
children.translated_text: it has been spoken of by me accordingly, in various ways, in terms of its effects. // Saund_12.40 //

children.text: śraddhāñkuram imaṃ tasmāt saṃvardhayitum arhasi /
children.translated_text: Therefore, you should nurture this sprout of faith;

children.text: tad vṛddhau vardhate dharmo mūlavṛddhau yathā drumaḥ // Saund_12.41 //
children.translated_text: when it grows, <s>dharma</s> grows, as a tree [grows] when its root grows. // Saund_12.41 //

children.text: vyākulaṃ darśanaṃ yasya durbalo yasya niścayaḥ /
children.translated_text: One whose view is confused and whose resolve is weak —

children.text: tasya pāriplavā śraddhā na hi kṛtāya vartate // Saund_12.42 //
children.translated_text: his faith is wavering, for it does not operate for what has been accomplished. // Saund_12.42 //

children.text: yāvat tattvaṃ na bhavati hi dṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ vā tāvac chraddhā na bhavati balasthā sthirā vā /
children.translated_text: For as long as the truth has not been seen or heard,

children.text: dṛṣṭe tattve niyamaparibhūtendriyasya śraddhāvṛkṣo bhavati saphalaś cāśrayās ca // Saund_12.43 //
children.translated_text: so long faith does not become strong or firm; but when the truth is seen, for one whose senses are conquered by discipline, the tree of faith becomes fruitful and a [firm] support. // Saund_12.43 //

body.text: Saundaranande mahākāvye paryavamarśo nāma dvādaśaḥ sargaḥ /
body.translated_text: In the <s>Saundarananda</s> <s>mahākāvya</s>, this is the twelfth canto, called 'Reflection.'
CANTO XIII

children.text: atha saṃrādhito nandaḥ śraddhāṃ prati maharṣinā /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Nanda</s>, having been gladdened by the great sage regarding faith,

children.text: parikṣikto 'mṛteneva yuyuje parayā mudā // Saund_13.1 //
children.translated_text: as though sprinkled with nectar, was united with supreme joy. // Saund_13.1 //

children.text: kṛtārtham iva taṃ mene saṃbuddhaḥ śraddhayā tayā /
children.translated_text: The fully awakened one (<s>Saṃbuddha</s>) considered him accomplished through that faith;

children.text: mene prāptam iva śreyaḥ sa ca buddhena saṃskṛtaḥ // Saund_13.2 //
children.translated_text: and he, refined by the <s>Buddha</s>, considered [his] spiritual welfare as attained. // Saund_13.2 //

children.text: ślakṣṇena vacasā kāṃś cit kāṃś cit paruṣayā girā /
children.translated_text: Some through gentle speech, some through harsh words,

children.text: kāṃś cid ābhyām upāyābhyāṃ sa vininye vināyakaḥ // Saund_13.3 //
children.translated_text: and some through both methods — thus did the Guide (<s>Vināyaka</s>) discipline [beings]. // Saund_13.3 //

children.text: pāṃsubhyaḥ kāñcanaṃ jātaṃ viśuddhaṃ nirmalaṃ śuci /
children.translated_text: Just as gold, born from dust, purified, stainless, and clean,

children.text: sthitaṃ pāṃsuṣv api yathā pāṃsudoṣair na lipyate // Saund_13.4 //
children.translated_text: even while resting in the dust, is not stained by the faults of the dust, // Saund_13.4 //

children.text: padmaparṇaṃ yathā caiva jale jātaṃ jale sthitham /
children.translated_text: and just as a lotus leaf, born in water and resting in water,

children.text: upariṣṭād adhastād vā na jalendopalipyate // Saund_13.5 //
children.translated_text: is not soiled by water, whether from above or below, // Saund_13.5 //

children.text: tadval loke munir jāto lokasyānugrahaṃ caran /
children.translated_text: so too the sage, born in the world and acting for the benefit of the world,

children.text: kṛtitvān nirmalatvāc ca lokadharmair na liyate // Saund_13.6 //
children.translated_text: because of his accomplishment and purity, is not stained by the ways of the world. // Saund_13.6 //

children.text: śleṣaṃ tyāgaṃ priyaṃ rūkṣaṃ kathāṃ ca dhyānam eva ca /
children.translated_text: Attachment and renunciation, the pleasant and the harsh, discourse and meditation —

children.text: mantukāle cikitsārthaṃ cakre nātmānuvṛttaye // Saund_13.7 //
children.translated_text: he employed [these] at the time of treatment for the purpose of healing, not for self-indulgence. // Saund_13.7 //

children.text: ataś ca saṃdadhe dāyaṃ mahākaruṇayā tayā /
children.translated_text: And thus, with that great compassion, he conferred the gift [of teaching],

children.text: mocayeyaṃ kathaṃ duḥkhāt sattvānīty anukampakaḥ // Saund_13.8 //
children.translated_text: compassionate, [thinking] 'How may I liberate beings from suffering?' // Saund_13.8 //

children.text: atha saṃharṣaṇān nadaṃ viditvā bhājanīkṛtam /
children.translated_text: Then, knowing that <s>Nanda</s> had been made a worthy vessel through encouragement,

children.text: abravīd bruvatāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ kramajñaḥ śreyasāṃ kramam // Saund_13.9 //
children.translated_text: the best of speakers, who knew the [proper] sequence, spoke the sequence of spiritual goods: // Saund_13.9 //

children.text: ataḥ prabhṛti bhūyas tvaṃ śraddhendriyapuraḥsaraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'From now on, you, O gentle one, with the faculty of faith as your forerunner,

children.text: amṛtasyāptaye saumya vṛttaṃ rakṣitum arhasi // Saund_13.10 //
children.translated_text: should protect your conduct for the attainment of the deathless (<s>amṛta</s>). // Saund_13.10 //

children.text: prayogaḥ kāyavacasoḥ śuddho bhavati te yathā /
children.translated_text: So that the practice of your body and speech becomes pure,

children.text: uttāno nivṛto gupto 'navacchidras tathā kuru // Saund_13.11 //
children.translated_text: make it open, transparent, guarded, and without gaps. // Saund_13.11 //

children.text: uttāno bhāvakarañād vivṛtaś cāpy agūhanāt /
children.translated_text: Open through sincerity of disposition, transparent through non-concealment,

children.text: gupto rakṣaṇatātparyād acchidraś cānavadyataḥ // Saund_13.12 //
children.translated_text: guarded through devotion to protection, and without gaps through blamelessness. // Saund_13.12 //

children.text: śarīravacasoḥ śuddhau saptāṅge cāpi karmaṇi /
children.translated_text: In the purity of body and speech, and in the sevenfold action,

children.text: ājīvasamudācāraṃ śaucāt saṃskartum arhasi // Saund_13.13 //
children.translated_text: you should purify your livelihood and conduct through [ethical] purity. // Saund_13.13 //

children.text: doṣānāṃ kuhanādīnāṃ pañcānām aniṣevaṇāt /
children.translated_text: Through not engaging in the five faults such as deception and the like,

children.text: tyāgāc ca jyotiṣādīnāṃ caturṇāṃ vṛttighātinām // Saund_13.14 //
children.translated_text: and through the abandonment of the four destroyers of livelihood such as fortune-telling and the like, // Saund_13.14 //

children.text: prāṇidhānyadhanādīnāṃ varjyānām apratigrahāt /
children.translated_text: through not accepting what is to be avoided — living beings, grain, wealth, and the like —

children.text: bhaiṣāṅgānāṃ nisṛṣṭānāṃ niyatānāṃ pratigrahāt // Saund_13.15 //
children.translated_text: and through accepting what is permitted, fixed, and [pertaining to] the requisites of medicine, // Saund_13.15 //

children.text: partiuṣṭaḥ śucir mañjuś caukṣayā jīvasaṃpadā /
children.translated_text: being content, pure, and agreeable, with a fine and proper livelihood,

children.text: kuryā duḥkhapratīkāraṃ yāvad eva vimuktaye // Saund_13.16 //
children.translated_text: one should practice the remedy for suffering, even unto liberation. // Saund_13.16 //

children.text: karmaño hi yathādṛṣtāt kāyavākprabhavād api /
children.translated_text: For although livelihood springs from the visible actions of body and speech,

children.text: ājīvaḥ pṛthag evokto duḥṣodhatvād ayaṃ mayā // Saund_13.17 //
children.translated_text: it has been stated separately by me because it is difficult to purify. // Saund_13.17 //

children.text: gṛhasthena hi duḥśobdhā dṛṣṭir vividhadṛṣṭinā /
children.translated_text: For right view is difficult to purify for a householder who holds various views —

children.text: ājīvo bhikṣuṇā caiva pareṣṭāyattavṛttinā // Saund_13.18 //
children.translated_text: and the livelihood of a monk is dependent on what is offered by others.

children.text: etāvac chīlam ity uktam ācāaro 'yaṃ samāsataḥ /
children.translated_text: This much has been called <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct); this is the practice (<s>ācāra</s>), in brief.

children.text: asya nāśena naiva syāt pravrajyā na gṛhasthatā // Saund_13.19 //
children.translated_text: Without it, there can be neither the life of a renunciant nor that of a householder.

children.text: tasmāc cāritrasaṃpanno brahmacaryam idaṃ cara /
children.translated_text: Therefore, endowed with good conduct, practice this holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>),

children.text: aṇumātreṣv avadyeṣu bhayadarśi dṛḍhavrataḥ // Saund_13.20 //
children.translated_text: seeing danger in even the slightest faults, firm in your vows.

children.text: śīlam āsthāya vartante sarvā hi śreyasi kriyāḥ /
children.translated_text: For all actions leading to the good proceed based on moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>),

children.text: sthānādyāniva kāryāṇi pratiṣṭhāya vasundharām // Saund_13.21 //
children.translated_text: just as standing, walking, and other activities rest upon the earth.

children.text: mokṣasyopaniṣat saumya vairāgyam iti gṛhyatām /
children.translated_text: "Understand, gentle one, that dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) is the prerequisite for liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>);

children.text: vairāgasyāpi saṃvedaḥ saṃvido jñānardarśanam // Saund_13.22 //
children.translated_text: and the prerequisite for dispassion is insight (<s>saṃveda</s>), and for insight — knowledge and vision (<s>jñānadarśana</s>)."

children.text: jñānasyopaniṣac caiva samādhir upadhāryatām /
children.translated_text: "And understand that <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) is the prerequisite for knowledge;

children.text: samādher apy upaniṣat sukhaṃ śarīramānasam // Saund_13.23 //
children.translated_text: and the prerequisite for <s>samādhi</s> is bodily and mental happiness."

children.text: paśrabdhiḥ kāyamanasaḥ sukhasyopaniṣatparā /
children.translated_text: "Tranquility (<s>praśrabdhi</s>) of body and mind is the supreme prerequisite for happiness;

children.text: praśabdher apy upaniṣat prāmodyaṃ paramaṃ mamatam // Saund_13.24 //
children.translated_text: and the prerequisite for tranquility is supreme delight (<s>prāmodya</s>)."

children.text: tathaḥ prīter upaniṣat prāmodyaṃ paramaṃ matam /
children.translated_text: "Likewise, supreme delight (<s>prāmodya</s>) is considered the prerequisite for joy (<s>prīti</s>);

children.text: prāmodyasyāpy ahṛllekhaḥ kukṛteṣv akṛteṣu vā // Saund_13.25 //
children.translated_text: and the prerequisite for delight is the absence of remorse (<s>ahṛllekha</s>) regarding things done or left undone."

children.text: ahṛllekhasya manasaḥ śīlaṃ tūpaniṣac chuci /
children.translated_text: "Pure moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) is the prerequisite for a mind free from remorse;

children.text: ataḥ śīlaṃ nayaty agryam iti śīlaṃ viśodhaya // Saund_13.26 //
children.translated_text: therefore, since moral conduct leads to the highest, purify your moral conduct."

children.text: śīlanāc chīlam ity uktaṃ śīlanaṃ sevanād api /
children.translated_text: "<s>Śīla</s> (moral conduct) is so called from <s>śīlana</s> (habitual practice); and <s>śīlana</s> from repeated cultivation (<s>sevana</s>);

children.text: sevanaṃ tannideśāc ca nideśaś ca tadāśrayāt // Saund_13.27 //
children.translated_text: and cultivation from instruction (<s>nideśa</s>); and instruction from reliance upon that [teaching]."

children.text: śīlaṃ hi śaraṇaṃ saumya kāntāra iva daiśikaḥ /
children.translated_text: "For moral conduct is a refuge, gentle one, like a guide in the wilderness,

children.text: mitraṃ bandhuś ca rakṣā ca dhanaṃ ca balam eva ca // Saund_13.28 //
children.translated_text: a friend, a kinsman, a protector, wealth, and strength indeed."

children.text: yataḥ śīlam ataḥ saumya śīlaṃ saṃskartum arhasi /
children.translated_text: "Since [all good] comes from moral conduct, you should, gentle one, cultivate moral conduct;

children.text: etat sthānam athānye ca mokṣārambheṣu yogināṃ // Saund_13.29 //
children.translated_text: this is the foundation, and so too the other [foundations], in the undertakings of <s>yogins</s> toward liberation."

children.text: tataḥ smṛtim adhiṣṭhāya capalāni svabhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: "Then, having established mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>), you should restrain the senses,

children.text: indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyo nivārayitum arhasi // Saund_13.30 //
children.translated_text: which are fickle by nature, from sense-objects."

children.text: bhetavyaṃ na tathā śatror nāgner nāher na cāśaneḥ /
children.translated_text: "One should not fear an enemy, fire, a serpent, or a thunderbolt as much

children.text: indriyebhyo yathā svebhyas tair ajasraṃ hi hanyate // Saund_13.31 //
children.translated_text: as one's own senses, for one is constantly slain by them."

children.text: dviṣabdhiḥ śatrubhiḥ kaś cit kadā cit pīḍyate na vā /
children.translated_text: "A person who hates may sometimes be harassed by enemies, or may not;

children.text: indriyair bādhyate sarvaḥ sarvatra ca sadaiva ca // Saund_13.32 //
children.translated_text: but everyone is afflicted by the senses, everywhere and always."

children.text: na ca prayāti narakaṃ śatruprabhṛthibhir hataḥ /
children.translated_text: "One slain by enemies and the like does not go to hell;

children.text: kṛṣyate tatra nighnas tu capalair indriyair hataḥ // Saund_13.33 //
children.translated_text: but one slain by the fickle senses is certainly dragged there."

children.text: hanyamānasya tair duḥkhaṃ hārdaṃ bhavati vā na vā /
children.translated_text: "For one slain by them, the suffering may or may not be of the heart;

children.text: indriyair bādhyamānasya hārdaṃ śārīram eva ca // Saund_13.34 //
children.translated_text: but for one afflicted by the senses, it is both of the heart and of the body."

children.text: saṃkalpaviṣadigdhā hi pañcendriyamayāḥ śarāḥ /
children.translated_text: "For the arrows made of the five senses, smeared with the poison of imagination (<s>saṃkalpa</s>),

children.text: cintāpuṅkhā raiphalā viṣayākāśagocarāḥ // Saund_13.35 //
children.translated_text: feathered with anxiety, tipped with passion, ranging through the space of sense-objects,

children.text: manuṣyahariṇān ghnanti kāmavyādheritā hṛdi /
children.translated_text: shot by the hunter of desire, strike the human deer in the heart;

children.text: vihanyante yadi na te tataḥ patanti taiḥ kṣatāḥ // Saund_13.36 //
children.translated_text: if they are not repelled, those struck by them fall."

children.text: niyamājirasaṃsthena dhairyakārmukadhāriṇā /
children.translated_text: "Standing in the courtyard of discipline, bearing the bow of steadfastness,

children.text: nipatanto nivāryās te mahatā smṛtivarmaṇā // Saund_13.37 //
children.translated_text: those [arrows] as they fall should be warded off with the great armor of mindfulness."

children.text: indriyāṇām upaśamād arīṇāṃ nigrahād iva /
children.translated_text: "Through the pacification of the senses, as through the subjugation of enemies,

children.text: sukhaṃ svapiti vāste vā yatra tatra gatoddhavaḥ // Saund_13.38 //
children.translated_text: one sleeps or dwells in happiness, wherever one may be, free from agitation."

children.text: teṣāṃ hi satataṃ loke viṣayāṇ abhikāṅkṣatām /
children.translated_text: "For those who constantly crave sense-objects in this world,

children.text: saṃvin naivāsti kārpaṇyāc chunām āśāvatām iva // Saund_13.39 //
children.translated_text: there is no contentment in their wretchedness, like dogs full of expectation."

children.text: viṣayair indriyagrāmo na tṛptim adhigacchati /
children.translated_text: "The aggregate of senses is never satiated by sense-objects,

children.text: ajasraṃ pūryamāṇo 'pi samudraḥ salilair iva // Saund_13.40 //
children.translated_text: though constantly being filled, like the ocean by waters."

children.text: avaśyaṃ gocare sve sve vartitavyam ihendriyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: "The senses must inevitably operate in their respective domains here;

children.text: nimittaṃ tatra na grāhyam anuvyañjanam eva ca // Saund_13.41 //
children.translated_text: but one should not grasp at the general sign (<s>nimitta</s>) or the secondary features (<s>anuvyañjana</s>) therein."

children.text: ālokya cakṣuṣā rūpaṃ dhātumātre vyavasthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Having seen a form with the eye, established merely in the elements (<s>dhātu</s>),

children.text: strī veti puruṣo veti na kalpayitum arhasi // Saund_13.42 //
children.translated_text: you should not conceptualize it as 'a woman' or 'a man.'"

children.text: sacet strīpuruṣagrāhaḥ kva cid vidyeta kās cana /
children.translated_text: "If somewhere there should arise a perception of woman or man,

children.text: śubhataḥ keśadantādīn nānuprasthātum arhasi // Saund_13.43 //
children.translated_text: you should not pursue hair, teeth, and the like as beautiful."

children.text: nāpaneyaṃ bhūtato bhūtaṃ śaśvad indiyagocare /
children.translated_text: "What truly exists in the range of the senses should not be cast aside;

children.text: draṣṭavyaṃ bhūtato bhūtaṃ yādṛṣaṃ ca yathā ca yat // Saund_13.44 //
children.translated_text: what truly exists should be seen as it truly is — whatever it is and however it is."

children.text: evaṃ te paśyatas tattvaṃ śaśvad indriyagocare /
children.translated_text: "Thus, when you constantly see the truth in the domain of the senses,

children.text: bhaviṣyati padasthānaṃ nābhiyādaurmanasyayoḥ // Saund_13.45 //
children.translated_text: there will be no foothold for either covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>) or despondency (<s>daurmanasya</s>)."

children.text: abhidhyā priyarūpeṇa hanti kāmātmakaṃ jagat /
children.translated_text: "Covetousness, in the form of what is pleasing, destroys the world that is given to desire,

children.text: arir mitramukheneva priyavākkaluṣāśayaḥ // Saund_13.46 //
children.translated_text: like an enemy wearing the face of a friend, with sweet words and a corrupt heart."

children.text: daurmanasyābhidhānas tu pratigho viṣayāśritaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Ill-will (<s>pratigha</s>), called despondency, is rooted in sense-objects;

children.text: mohād yenānuvṛttena paratreha ca hanyate // Saund_13.47 //
children.translated_text: through delusion, by following it, one is destroyed both here and hereafter."

children.text: anurodhavirodhābhyāṃ śitoṣṇābhyām ivārditaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Afflicted by attraction and aversion, as by cold and heat,

children.text: śarma nāpnoti na śreyaś calendricam ato jagat // Saund_13.48 //
children.translated_text: the world, with its fickle senses, attains neither comfort nor the highest good."

children.text: nendriyaṃ viṣaye tāvat pravṛttam api sajjate /
children.translated_text: "A sense organ, even when engaged with an object, does not become attached

children.text: yāvan na manasas tatra parikalpaḥ pravartate // Saund_13.49 //
children.translated_text: so long as mental conceptualization does not operate with regard to it."

children.text: indhane sati vāyau ca yathā jvalati pāvakaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Just as a fire blazes when there is fuel and wind,

children.text: viṣayāt parikalpāc ca kleśāgnir jāyate tathā // Saund_13.50 //
children.translated_text: so the fire of affliction (<s>kleśa</s>) arises from sense-objects and conceptualization."

children.text: abhūtaparikalpena viṣayasya hi badhyate /
children.translated_text: "For one is bound by false conceptualization of the sense-object;

children.text: tam eva viṣayaṃ paśyan bhūtataḥ parimucyate // Saund_13.51 //
children.translated_text: seeing that very sense-object as it truly is, one is liberated."

children.text: dṛṣṭvaikaṃ rūpam anyo hi rajyate 'nyaḥ praduṣyati /
children.translated_text: "Having seen one and the same form, one person is attracted, another is repulsed,

children.text: kaś cid bhavati madhyasthas tatraivānyo ghṛṇāyate // Saund_13.52 //
children.translated_text: someone becomes indifferent, and yet another feels disgust toward that very [form]."

children.text: ato na viṣayo hetur bandhāya na vimuktaye /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, the sense-object is not the cause of either bondage or liberation;

children.text: parikalpaviṣeṣeṇa saṃgo bhavati vā na vā // Saund_13.53 //
children.translated_text: it is through the particular conceptualization that attachment arises or does not arise."

children.text: kāryaḥ paramayatnena tasmād indiyasaṃvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, sense-restraint (<s>indriyasaṃvara</s>) should be practiced with the utmost effort,

children.text: indriyāṇi hy aguptāni duḥkhāya ca bhavāya ca // Saund_13.54 //
children.translated_text: for unguarded senses lead to suffering and continued existence."

children.text: kāmabhogabhogavadbhir āmadṛṣṭidṛṣṭibhiḥ pramādanaikamūrdhabhiḥ praharṣalolajivaiḥ /
children.translated_text: "By the sense-serpents — whose fangs are sense-enjoyments, whose gaze is fixed with wrong views, whose raised hoods are heedlessness, whose flickering tongues are excitement,

children.text: indriyoragair manobilaśayaiḥ spṛhāviṣaiḥ śamāgadā ṛte na daṣṭam asti yac cikitset // Saund_13.55 //
children.translated_text: whose lairs are in the mind, whose venom is craving — there is no cure for one bitten, except the medicine of tranquility."

children.text: tasmād eṣām akuṣalakarāṇām arīṇāṃ cakṣurghrāṇaśravañarasanasparśanānām /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, with respect to these evil-doing enemies — the eye, nose, ear, tongue, and touch —

children.text: sarvāvasthaṃ bhava viniyamād apramatto māsminn arthe kṣaṇam api kṛthāsa tvaṃ pramādaṃ // Saund_13.56 //
children.translated_text: be heedful at all times through restraint; do not be negligent in this matter for even a moment."

body.text: Saundaranande mahākāvye śīlendriyajayo nāma trayodaśaḥ sargaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the thirteenth canto named 'The Conquest of the Senses through Moral Conduct' in the <s>Saundarananda</s> <s>mahākāvya</s>.
CANTO XIV

children.text: atha smṛtikavāṭena pidhāyendriyasaṃvaram /
children.translated_text: "Then, having closed the door of sense-restraint with the bolt of mindfulness,

children.text: bhojane bhava mātrājño dhyānāyānāmayāya ca // Saund_14.1 //
children.translated_text: be moderate in food, for the sake of meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) and good health."

children.text: prāṇāpānau nigṛhṇāti glāninidre prayacchati /
children.translated_text: "Excessive food restrains the in-breath and out-breath, produces sluggishness and drowsiness,

children.text: kṛto hy atyartham āhāro vihanti ca parākramam // Saund_14.2 //
children.translated_text: and when food is taken in excess, it impairs one's capacity for exertion."

children.text: yathā cātyartham āhāraḥ kṛto 'narthāya kalpate /
children.translated_text: "And just as food taken in excess leads to harm,

children.text: upayuktas tathātyalpo na sāmarthyāya kalpate // Saund_14.3 //
children.translated_text: so too food taken in too little quantity does not conduce to strength."

children.text: ācayaṃ dyutim utsāhaṃ prayogaṃ balam eva ca /
children.translated_text: "Food taken in too little quantity diminishes the body's

children.text: bhojanaṃ kṛtam atyalpaṃ śarīrasyāpakarṣati // Saund_14.4 //
children.translated_text: nourishment, radiance, enthusiasm, capacity, and strength."

children.text: yathā bhāreṇa namate laghunonnamate tulā /
children.translated_text: "Just as a scale tips down with a heavy weight and rises with a light one,

children.text: samā tiṣṭhati yuktena bhojyeneyaṃ tathā tanuḥ // Saund_14.5 //
children.translated_text: so this body [is balanced] with the right amount of food."

children.text: tasmād abhyavahartavyaṃ svaśaktim anupaśyatā /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, one who considers one's own capacity should eat

children.text: nātimātraṃ na cātyalpaṃ meyaṃ mānavaśād api // Saund_14.6 //
children.translated_text: neither too much nor too little — the measure should be determined according to proper reckoning."

children.text: atyākrānto hi kāyāgnir guruṇānnena śāmyati /
children.translated_text: "For the digestive fire of the body, overwhelmed by heavy food, is extinguished,

children.text: avacchan na ivālpo 'gniḥ sahasā mahatendhasā // Saund_14.7 //
children.translated_text: like a small fire suddenly [smothered] by a great mass of fuel."

children.text: atyantam api saṃhāro nāhārasya praśasyate /
children.translated_text: "Excessive restriction of food is also not praiseworthy,

children.text: anāhāro hi nirvāti nirindhana ivānalaḥ // Saund_14.8 //
children.translated_text: for one without food is extinguished, like a fire without fuel."

children.text: yasmān nāsti vināhārāt sarvaprāṇabhṛtāṃ sthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: "Since the sustenance of all living beings is impossible without food,

children.text: tasmād duṣyati nāhāro vikalpo 'tra tu vāryate // Saund_14.9 //
children.translated_text: food itself is not blameworthy; rather, it is the wrong attitude toward it that should be checked."

children.text: na hy evakviṣaye 'nyatra sajyante prāṇinas tathā /
children.translated_text: "For living beings are not so attached in any other domain

children.text: avijñāte yathāhāre boddhavyaṃ tatra kāraṇam // Saund_14.10 //
children.translated_text: as they are in the matter of food, which is not [properly] understood — the cause therein should be recognized."

children.text: cikitsārthaṃ yathā dhatte vraṇasyālepanaṃ vraṇī /
children.translated_text: "Just as one with a wound applies a salve for the purpose of healing,

children.text: kṣudvighātārtham āhāras tadvat sevyo mumukṣunā // Saund_14.11 //
children.translated_text: so food should be taken by one who seeks liberation, for the purpose of warding off hunger."

children.text: bhārasyodvahanārthaṃ ca rathākṣo 'bhyajyate yathā /
children.translated_text: "And just as an axle of a chariot is greased for the purpose of bearing the load,

children.text: bhojanaṃ prāṇayātrārthaṃ tadvad vidvān niṣevate // Saund_14.12 //
children.translated_text: so the wise one takes food for the purpose of sustaining life."

children.text: samatikramaṇārthaṃ ca kāntārasya yathādhvagau /
children.translated_text: "And just as two travelers, in order to cross a wilderness,

children.text: putramāṃsāni khādetāṃ dampatī bhṛṣaduḥkhitau // Saund_14.13 //
children.translated_text: a husband and wife, deeply distressed, would eat the flesh of their own child,"

children.text: evam abhyavahartavyaṃ bhojanaṃ pratisaṃkhyayā /
children.translated_text: "so food should be taken with reflection,

children.text: na bhūṣārthaṃ na vapuṣe na madāya na dṛptaye // Saund_14.14 //
children.translated_text: not for adornment, not for physical beauty, not for intoxication, not for arrogance."

children.text: dhāraṇārthaṃ śarīrasya bhojanaṃ hi vidhiyate /
children.translated_text: "For food is prescribed for the maintenance of the body,

children.text: upastambhaḥ pipatiṣor durbalasyeva veśmanaḥ // Saund_14.15 //
children.translated_text: as a support for a weak house that is about to fall."

children.text: plavaṃ yatnād yathā kaś cid badhnīyād dhārayed api /
children.translated_text: "Just as someone would carefully build and maintain a raft,

children.text: na tatsnehena yāvat tu mahaughasyottīrṣayā // Saund_14.16 //
children.translated_text: not out of attachment to it, but for the purpose of crossing a great flood,"

children.text: tathopakaraṇaiḥ kāyaṃ dhārayanti parikṣakāḥ /
children.translated_text: "so the discerning ones maintain the body with requisites,

children.text: na tatsnehena yāvat tu duḥkhaughasya titīrṣayā // Saund_14.17 //
children.translated_text: not out of attachment to it, but for the purpose of crossing the flood of suffering."

children.text: śocatā pīḍyamānena dīyate śatrave yathā /
children.translated_text: "Just as one who is distressed and oppressed gives [tribute] to an enemy,

children.text: na bhaktyā nāpi tarṣena kevalaṃ prāṇaguptaye // Saund_14.18 //
children.translated_text: not out of devotion or desire, but solely for the protection of life,"

children.text: yogācāras tathāhāraṃ śarirāya payacchati /
children.translated_text: "so the practitioner of <s>yoga</s> gives food to the body,

children.text: kevalaṃ kṣudvighātārthaṃ na rāgeṇa na bhaktaye // Saund_14.19 //
children.translated_text: solely for the purpose of warding off hunger, not out of passion or devotion."

children.text: manodhāraṇayā caiva pariṇāmyātmavān ahaḥ /
children.translated_text: "And with mental concentration, the self-possessed one should spend the day,

children.text: vidhūya nidrāṃ yogena niśām apy atināmayeḥ // Saund_14.20 //
children.translated_text: and having shaken off drowsiness through <s>yoga</s>, should also pass the night."

children.text: hṛrdi yatsaṃjñinaś caiva nidrā prādurbhavet tava /
children.translated_text: "And even while conscious, if sleep should arise in your heart,

children.text: guṇavatsaṃjñitāṃ saṃjñāṃ tadā manasi mā kṛthāḥ // Saund_14.21 //
children.translated_text: do not at that time entertain in your mind a perception associated with virtuous qualities."

children.text: dhātur ārambhadhṛtyoś ca sthāmavikramayor api /
children.translated_text: "The elements (<s>dhātu</s>), initiative, fortitude,

children.text: nityaṃ manasi kāryas te bādhyamānena nidrayā // Saund_14.22 //
children.translated_text: stamina, and vigor — these should always be kept in mind by one who is being overcome by sleep."

children.text: āmnātavyāś ca viśadaṃ te dharmā ye pariśrutāḥ /
children.translated_text: "The teachings (<s>dharma</s>) that have been heard should be clearly recited,

children.text: parebhyaś copadeṣṭavyāḥ saṃcintyāḥ svayam eva ca // Saund_14.23 //
children.translated_text: and should be taught to others, and also reflected upon by oneself."

children.text: prakledyamadbhir vadanṃ vilokyāḥ sarvato diśaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Sprinkling the face with water, looking in all directions,

children.text: cāryā dṛṣṭiś ca tārāsu jijāgariṣuṇā sadā // Saund_14.24 //
children.translated_text: and directing the gaze at the stars — these should always [be done] by one who wishes to stay awake."

children.text: antargatair acapalair vaśasthāyibhir indriyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: "With the senses turned inward, steady, under control, and stable,

children.text: avikṣiptena manasā caṅkramyavāsva vā niśi // Saund_14.25 //
children.translated_text: with an undistracted mind, you should walk or sit during the night."

children.text: bhaye prītau ca śoke ca nidrayā nābhibhūyate /
children.translated_text: "In fear, in delight, and in grief, one is not overcome by sleep;

children.text: tasmān nidrābhiyogeṣu sevitavyam idaṃ trayam // Saund_14.26 //
children.translated_text: therefore, in the practice of wakefulness, this triad should be cultivated."

children.text: bhayam āgamanān mṛtyoḥ prītiṃ dharmaparigrahāt /
children.translated_text: "You should develop fear from the approach of death, delight from the attainment of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: janmaduḥkhād aparyantāc chokam āgantum arhasi // Saund_14.27 //
children.translated_text: and grief from the endless suffering of [repeated] birth."

children.text: evamādi kramaḥ saumya kāryo jāgaraṇaṃ prati /
children.translated_text: "Such and similar is the method, gentle one, with regard to wakefulness;

children.text: vandhyaṃ hi śayanād āyuḥ kaḥ prājñaḥ kartum arhati // Saund_14.28 //
children.translated_text: for what wise person would render life barren through sleep?"

children.text: doṣavyālān atikramya vyālān gṛhagatān iva /
children.translated_text: "Having passed beyond the serpent-like faults, as one would pass serpents within a house,

children.text: kṣamaṃ prājñasya na svaptuṃ nistīrṣor mahadbhayam // Saund_14.29 //
children.translated_text: it is not fitting for a wise person seeking to cross over the great danger to sleep."

children.text: pradīpte jīvaloke hi mṛtyuvyādhijarāgnibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: "When the world of the living is ablaze with the fires of death, disease, and old age,

children.text: kaḥ śayīta nirudvegaḥ pradīpta iva veśmani // Saund_14.30 //
children.translated_text: who would lie undisturbed, as if in a burning house?"

children.text: tasmāt tama iti jñātvā nidrāṃ nāveṣṭum arhasi /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, knowing sleep to be darkness (<s>tamas</s>), you should not resort to it,

children.text: apraśānteṣu doṣeṣu saśastreṣv iva śatgruṣu // Saund_14.31 //
children.translated_text: while afflictions remain unextinguished — like [dwelling with] enemies bearing weapons."

children.text: pūrvaṃ yāmaṃ triyāmāyāḥ prayogeṇātināmya tu /
children.translated_text: "Having spent the first watch of the three-watch night in practice,

children.text: sevyā śayyā śarīrasya viśrāmārthaṃ svatantriṇā // Saund_14.32 //
children.translated_text: the bed should be used by the self-disciplined one for the purpose of resting the body."

children.text: dakṣiṇena tu pārśvena sthitayālokasaṃjñayā /
children.translated_text: "Lying on the right side, with the perception of light established,

children.text: prabodhaṃ hṛdaye kṛtvā śayīthāḥ śāntamānasaḥ // Saund_14.33 //
children.translated_text: having placed the intention to awaken in your heart, you should sleep with a tranquil mind."

children.text: yāme tṛtīye cotthāya carann āsīna eva vā /
children.translated_text: And in the third watch of the night, having risen, whether walking or seated,

children.text: bhūyo yogaṃ mahaḥśuddhau kurvīthā niyatendriyaḥ // Saund_14.34 //
children.translated_text: You should again practice <s>yoga</s> for the purification of the mind, with senses controlled. // 14.34 //

children.text: athāsanagatasthānaprekṣitavyāhṛtādiṣu /
children.translated_text: In sitting, standing, looking, speaking, and other [activities],

children.text: saṃprajānan kriyāḥ sarvāḥ smṛtim ādhātum arhasi // Saund_14.35 //
children.translated_text: You should maintain <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), being fully aware in all actions. // 14.35 //

children.text: dvārādhyakṣa iva dvāri yasya praṇihitā smṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: He whose <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) is stationed like a gatekeeper at the gate —

children.text: dharṣayanti na taṃ doṣāḥ puraṃ guptam ivārayaḥ // Saund_14.36 //
children.translated_text: The faults do not assail him, like enemies [cannot assail] a well-guarded city. // 14.36 //

children.text: na tasyotpadyate kleśo yasya kāyagatā smṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: No <s>kleśa</s> (affliction) arises in one whose <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) is directed toward the body;

children.text: cittaṃ sarvāsv avasthāsu bālaṃ dhātrīva rakṣati // Saund_14.37 //
children.translated_text: It protects the mind in all conditions, like a nurse [protects] a child. // 14.37 //

children.text: śaravyaḥ sa tu doṣāṇāṃ yo hīnaḥ smṛtivarmaṇā /
children.translated_text: But he who is devoid of the armor of <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) is a target for the faults,

children.text: raṇasthaḥ pratiśatrūṇāṃ vihīna iva varmaṇā // Saund_14.38 //
children.translated_text: Like one standing in battle before enemies, deprived of armor. // 14.38 //

children.text: anāthaṃ tan mano jñeyaṃ yat smṛtir nābhirakṣati /
children.translated_text: That mind should be known as unprotected which <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) does not guard —

children.text: nirṇetā dṛṣṭirahito viṣameṣu carann iva // Saund_14.39 //
children.translated_text: Like a guide without sight, walking on uneven ground. // 14.39 //

children.text: anartheṣu prasaktāś ca svārthebhyaś ca parāṅmukhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who are attached to harmful things and turn away from what is beneficial,

children.text: yad bhaye sati nodvignāḥ smṛtināśo 'tra kāraṇam // Saund_14.40 //
children.translated_text: Who are not alarmed when there is cause for alarm — the loss of <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) is the cause of this. // 14.40 //

children.text: svabhūmiṣu guṇāḥ sarve ye ca śīlādayaḥ sthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: All virtues, beginning with <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) and the rest, that are established in their respective domains —

children.text: vikīrṇā iva gā gopaḥ smṛtis tān anugacchati // Saund_14.41 //
children.translated_text: <s>Smṛti</s> (mindfulness) follows after them, like a cowherd [follows] scattered cattle. // 14.41 //

children.text: pranaṣṭam amṛtaṃ tasya yasya kviprasṛtā smṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: The immortal nectar is lost for one whose <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) has strayed far;

children.text: hastastham amṛtaṃ tasya yasya kāyagatā smṛtiḥ // Saund_14.42 //
children.translated_text: The immortal nectar is in the hand of one whose <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) is directed toward the body. // 14.42 //

children.text: āryo nyāyaḥ kutas tasya smṛtir yasya na vidyate /
children.translated_text: Whence comes the noble path for one in whom <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) is absent?

children.text: yasyāryo nāsti ca nyāyaḥ pranaṣṭas tasya satpathaḥ // Saund_14.43 //
children.translated_text: And for one who lacks the noble path, the true way is lost. // 14.43 //

children.text: pranaṣṭo yasya sanmārgo naṣṭaṃ tasyāmṛtaṃ padam /
children.translated_text: For one whose true way is lost, the immortal state is lost;

children.text: pranaṣṭam amṛtaṅ yasya sa duḥkhān na vimucyate // Saund_14.44 //
children.translated_text: And one whose immortal [state] is lost is not freed from suffering. // 14.44 //

children.text: tasmāc caran caro 'smīti sthito 'smiti ca dhiṣṭhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, while walking, [thinking] 'I am walking,' and while standing, firmly [aware] 'I am standing' —

children.text: evamādiṣu kāleṣu smṛtim ādhātum arhasi // Saund_14.45 //
children.translated_text: In these and other occasions, you should maintain <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness). // 14.45 //

children.text: yagānulomaṃ vijanaṃ viśabdaṃ śayyāsanaṃ saumya tathā bhajasva /
children.translated_text: O gentle one, thus resort to a bed and seat that is solitary, quiet, and conducive to <s>yoga</s>;

children.text: kāyasya kṛtvā hi vivekam ādau sukho 'dhigantuṃ manaso vivekaḥ // Saund_14.46 //
children.translated_text: For having first achieved seclusion of the body, seclusion of the mind is easy to attain. // 14.46 //

children.text: alabdhacetaḥpraśamaḥ sarāgo yo na pracāraṃ bhajate viviktam /
children.translated_text: One who has not attained tranquility of mind, who is still passionate, and who does not frequent a secluded place,

children.text: sa kṣaṇyate hy apartilabdhamārgaś carann ivoryāṃ bahukaṇṭakāyām // Saund_14.47 //
children.translated_text: Is injured, like one walking on thorny ground who has not yet found the path. // 14.47 //

children.text: adṛṣṭatattvena parīkṣakeṇa sthitena citre viṣayapracāre /
children.translated_text: By one who has not seen the truth, who is an examiner [still] situated in the varied range of sense-objects,

children.text: cittaṃ niṣeddhuṃ na sukhena śkyaṃ kṛśṭādako gaur iva sasyamadhyāt // Saund_14.48 //
children.translated_text: The mind cannot easily be restrained — like an ox accustomed to plowed [fields] from the midst of crops. // 14.48 //

children.text: anīryamāṇas tu yathānilena praśāntim āgacchati citrabhānuḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as fire, when not fanned by wind, comes to quiescence,

children.text: alpena yatnena tathā vivikteṣv aghaṭṭitaṃ śāntim upaiti cetaḥ // Saund_14.49 //
children.translated_text: So too in solitary places, the undisturbed mind attains peace with little effort. // 14.49 //

children.text: kva cid bhuktvā yat tad vasanam api yat tat parihito
children.translated_text: Having eaten whatever [food is available], wearing whatever garment [he has],

children.text: vasann ātmārāmaḥ kva cana vijane yo 'bhiramate /
children.translated_text: Dwelling self-delighted in some solitary place, he who rejoices [therein] —

children.text: kṛtārthaḥ saj ñeyaḥ śamasukharasajñaḥ kṛtamatiḥ
children.translated_text: He should be known as one who has accomplished his purpose, possessed of the taste of the bliss of tranquility, with mind fulfilled,

children.text: pareṣāṃ saṃsargaṃ pariharati yaḥ kaṇṭakam iva // Saund_14.50 //
children.translated_text: Who avoids the company of others as if it were thorns. // 14.50 //

children.text: yadi dvandvārāme jagati viṣayavyagrahṛdaye
children.translated_text: If in this world where people delight in dualities and whose hearts are seized by sense-objects,

children.text: vivikte nirdvando viharati kṛtī śāntahṛdayaḥ /
children.translated_text: One lives in seclusion, free from dualities, accomplished, with a tranquil heart —

children.text: tataḥ pītvā prajñārasam amṛtavat tṛptahṛdayo
children.translated_text: Then, having drunk the nectar-like taste of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), with a satisfied heart,

children.text: viviktaḥ saṃsaktaṃ viṣayakṛpaṇaṃ śocati jagat // Saund_14.51 //
children.translated_text: He, secluded, looks with compassion upon the attached world, wretched in its pursuit of sense-objects. // 14.51 //

children.text: vasañ śuṇyāgāre yadi satatam eko 'bhiramate
children.translated_text: If, dwelling in an empty abode, one constantly delights in solitude,

children.text: yadi kleśotpādaiḥ saha na ramate śatrubhir iva /
children.translated_text: If one does not delight in the arising of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) as if they were enemies,

children.text: carann ātmārāmo yadi ca pibati prītisalilaṃ
children.translated_text: If, wandering self-delighted, one drinks the water of joy (<s>prīti</s>) —

children.text: tato bhuṅkte śreṣṭhaṃ tridaśapatirājyād api sukham // Saund_14.52 //
children.translated_text: Then one enjoys a happiness superior even to the sovereignty of <s>Tridaśapati</s> (<s>Indra</s>). // 14.52 //

body.text: Saundaranande mahākāvya ādiprasthāno nāma caturdaśaḥ sargaḥ /
body.translated_text: In the <s>Saundarananda Mahākāvya</s>, this is the Fourteenth Canto, called 'The Initial Setting Forth.'
CANTO XV

children.text: yatra tatra vivikte tu baddhvā paryaṅkam uttamam /
children.translated_text: In any secluded place, having assumed the supreme cross-legged posture,

children.text: ṛjuṃ kāyaṃ samādhāya smṛtyābhimukhayānvitaḥ // Saund_15.1 //
children.translated_text: Holding the body upright, endowed with mindfulness directed toward [the meditation object] — // 15.1 //

children.text: nāsāgre vā lalāṭe vā bhruvor antara eva vā /
children.translated_text: At the tip of the nose, or at the forehead, or between the eyebrows —

children.text: kurvīthāś capalaṃ cittam ālambanaparāyaṇam // Saund_15.2 //
children.translated_text: You should make the restless mind intent upon its support (<s>ālambana</s>). // 15.2 //

children.text: sacet kāmavitarkas tvāṃ dharṣayen mānaso jvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: If a thought of desire (<s>kāmavitarka</s>), a mental fever, should assail you,

children.text: kṣeptavyo nādhivāsyaḥ sa vastre reṇur ivāgataḥ // Saund_15.3 //
children.translated_text: It should be cast away and not tolerated — like a speck of dust that has fallen on a garment. // 15.3 //

children.text: yady api pratisaṃkhyānāt kāmān utsṛṣṭavān asi /
children.translated_text: Even if through deliberation you have abandoned desires,

children.text: tamāṃsīva prakāśena pratipakṣeṇa tāñ jahi // Saund_15.4 //
children.translated_text: Destroy them with their antidote — as darkness [is destroyed] by light. // 15.4 //

children.text: tiṣṭhaty anuśayas teṣāṃ channo 'gnir iva bhasmanā /
children.translated_text: Their latent tendency (<s>anuśaya</s>) remains, hidden like fire beneath ashes;

children.text: sa te bhāvanayā saumya praśāmyo 'gnir ivāmbunā // Saund_15.5 //
children.translated_text: That, O gentle one, must be quenched by meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) — as fire [is quenched] by water. // 15.5 //

children.text: te hi tasmāt pravartante bhūyo bījād ivāṅkurāḥ /
children.translated_text: For they [the desires] sprout again from that [latent tendency], like shoots from a seed;

children.text: tasya nāśena te na syur bījanāśād ivāṅkurāḥ // Saund_15.6 //
children.translated_text: Through its destruction, they would cease to exist — like shoots through the destruction of the seed. // 15.6 //

children.text: arjanādīni kāmebhyo dṛṣṭvā duḥkhāni kāminām /
children.translated_text: Seeing the sufferings — acquisition and the rest — that befall those who desire, arising from desires,

children.text: tasmāt tān mūlataś chindhi mitrasaṃjñān arīn iva // Saund_15.7 //
children.translated_text: Therefore cut them down at the root — those enemies who bear the name of friends. // 15.7 //

children.text: anityā moṣadharmāṇo riktā vyasanahetavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Impermanent, subject to deprivation, empty, causes of calamity,

children.text: bahusādhāraṇāḥ kāmā barhyā hy āśiviṣā iva // Saund_15.8 //
children.translated_text: Shared by many — desires should be cast out like venomous serpents. // 15.8 //

children.text: ye mṛgyamāṇā duḥkhāya rakṣyamāṇā na śāntaye /
children.translated_text: Those which when sought lead to suffering, when guarded do not lead to peace,

children.text: bhraṣṭāḥ śokāya mahate prāptāś ca na vitṛptaye // Saund_15.9 //
children.translated_text: When lost lead to great sorrow, and when obtained do not lead to satisfaction — // 15.9 //

children.text: tṛptiṃ vittaprakarṣeṇa svargāvāptyā kṛtārthatām /
children.translated_text: He who sees contentment in abundance of wealth, fulfillment in the attainment of heaven,

children.text: kāmebhyaś ca sukhotpattiṃ yaḥ paśyati sa naśyati // Saund_15.10 //
children.translated_text: And the arising of happiness from desires — that person perishes. // 15.10 //

children.text: calān apariniṣpannān asārān anavasthitān /
children.translated_text: Fickle, unfinished, without essence, unstable,

children.text: parikalpasukhān kāmān na tān smartum ihārhasi // Saund_15.11 //
children.translated_text: Offering only imagined pleasure — you should not call such desires to mind here. // 15.11 //

children.text: vyāpādo vā vihiṃsā vā kṣobhayed yadi te manaḥ /
children.translated_text: If ill-will or the intention to harm should agitate your mind,

children.text: prasādyaṃ tad vipakṣena maṇinevākulaṃ jalam // Saund_15.12 //
children.translated_text: It should be purified by the antidote — like turbid water by a jewel. // 15.12 //

children.text: pratipakṣas tayor jñeyo maitrī kāruṇyam eva ca /
children.translated_text: The antidote to those two should be known as loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) and compassion (<s>kāruṇya</s>);

children.text: virodho hi tayor nityaṃ prakāśatamasor iva // Saund_15.13 //
children.translated_text: For the opposition between them is perpetual, like that of light and darkness. // 15.13 //

children.text: nivṛttaṃ yasya duḥśīlyaṃ vyāpādaś ca pravartate /
children.translated_text: One whose misconduct has ceased but in whom ill-will still operates

children.text: hanti pāṃsubhir ātmānāṃ sa snāta iva vāraṇaḥ // Saund_15.14 //
children.translated_text: Injures himself with filth — like an elephant that has bathed. // 15.14 //

children.text: duḥkhitebhyo hi martyebhyo vyādhimṛtyujarādibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: To mortals who are afflicted by disease, death, old age, and the like —

children.text: āryaḥ ko duḥkham aparaṃ saghṛṇo dhātum arhati // Saund_15.15 //
children.translated_text: What noble person with compassion could inflict additional suffering? // 15.15 //

children.text: duṣṭena ceha manasā bādhyate vā paro na vā /
children.translated_text: Whether or not another is harmed by a corrupted mind here,

children.text: sadyas tu dahyate tāvat svaṃ mano duṣṭacetasaḥ // Saund_15.16 //
children.translated_text: At least the mind of the one with corrupt thoughts is immediately burned. // 15.16 //

children.text: tasmāt sarveṣu bhūteṣu maitrīṃ kāruṇyam eva ca /
children.translated_text: Therefore, toward all beings, loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) and compassion (<s>kāruṇya</s>) —

children.text: na vyāpādaṃ vihiṃsāṃ vā vikalpayitum arhasi // Saund_15.17 //
children.translated_text: Not ill-will or the intention to harm — should you cultivate. // 15.17 //

children.text: yad yad eva prasaktaṃ hi vitarkayati mānavaḥ /
children.translated_text: For whatever a person habitually thinks about,

children.text: abhyāsāt tena tenāsya natir bhavati cetasaḥ // Saund_15.18 //
children.translated_text: Through repeated practice, the mind develops an inclination in that very direction. // 15.18 //

children.text: tasmād askuśalaṃ tyaktvā kuśalaṃ dhyātum arhasi /
children.translated_text: Therefore, abandoning the unwholesome (<s>akuśala</s>), you should contemplate the wholesome (<s>kuśala</s>),

children.text: yat te syād iha cārthāya paramārthasya cāptaye // Saund_15.19 //
children.translated_text: Which would serve you both in this world and for the attainment of the highest good. // 15.19 //

children.text: saṃvardhante hy akuśalā vitarkāḥ saṃbhṛtā hṛrdi /
children.translated_text: For unwholesome thoughts (<s>vitarka</s>), when nurtured in the heart, grow,

children.text: anarthajanakās tulyam ātmanaś ca parasya ca // Saund_15.20 //
children.translated_text: Producing harm equally to oneself and to others. // 15.20 //

children.text: śreyaso vighnakaraṇād bhavanty ātmavipattaye /
children.translated_text: By obstructing what is beneficial, they lead to one's own ruin;

children.text: pātrībhāvopaghātāt tu parabhaktivipattaye // Saund_15.21 //
children.translated_text: And by destroying one's fitness as a worthy recipient, they lead to the ruin of others' offerings. // 15.21 //

children.text: manaḥkarmasv avikṣepam api cābhyastum arhasi /
children.translated_text: You should also practice non-distraction in the activities of the mind,

children.text: na tv evākuśalaṃ saumya vitarkayitum arhasi // Saund_15.22 //
children.translated_text: But you should never, O gentle one, think unwholesome thoughts. // 15.22 //

children.text: yā trikāmopabhogāya cintā manasi vartate /
children.translated_text: The anxious thought that arises in the mind for the enjoyment of the three kinds of desire

children.text: na ca taṃ guṇam āpnoti bandhanāya ca kalpate // Saund_15.23 //
children.translated_text: Does not attain that [desired] quality and serves only as a fetter. // 15.23 //

children.text: sattvānām upaghātāya parikleṣāya cātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the harm of beings and for one's own affliction,

children.text: mohaṃ vrajati kāluṣyaṃ narakāya ca vartate // Saund_15.24 //
children.translated_text: It leads to delusion and corruption, and tends toward hell. // 15.24 //

children.text: tadvitarkair akuśalair nātmānaṃ hantum arhasi /
children.translated_text: Therefore, you should not destroy yourself with unwholesome thoughts —

children.text: suśastraṃ ratnavikṛtaṃ mṛddhato gāṃ khanann iva // Saund_15.25 //
children.translated_text: Like one digging up the ground from beneath a jewel-encrusted, well-fashioned building. // 15.25 //

children.text: anabhijño yathā jātaṃ dahed aguru kāṣṭhavat /
children.translated_text: Just as an ignorant person would burn <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood) that has grown, treating it like common firewood,

children.text: anyāyena manuṣyatvam upahanyād idaṃ tathā // Saund_15.26 //
children.translated_text: So would one improperly destroy this human existence. // 15.26 //

children.text: tyaktvā ratnaṃ yathā loṣṭaṃ ratnadvīpāc ca saṃharet /
children.translated_text: Just as one might abandon a jewel and collect a clod of earth from a jewel-island,

children.text: tyaktvā naiḥśreyasaṃ dharmaṃ cintayed aśubhaṃ tathā // Saund_15.27 //
children.translated_text: So would one abandon the <s>Dharma</s> leading to the highest good and contemplate what is inauspicious. // 15.27 //

children.text: himavantaṃ yathā gatvā viṣaṃ bhuñjīta nauṣadham /
children.translated_text: Just as one who has gone to the <s>Himavān</s> (Himalayas) would consume poison rather than medicine,

children.text: manuṣyataṃ tathā prāpya pāpaṃ seveta no śubham // Saund_15.28 //
children.translated_text: So, having obtained human birth, one would pursue evil rather than good. // 15.28 //

children.text: tad buddhvā pratikaṣeṇa vitarkaṃ kṣeptum arhasi /
children.translated_text: Therefore, understanding this, you should cast out unwholesome thought with its antidote —
