children.text: sūkṣmeṇa parikīlena kilaṃ dārvantarād iva // Saund_15.29 //
children.translated_text: Like [driving out] a wedge from within wood by means of a fine counter-wedge. // 15.29 //

children.text: vṛdhhyavṛddhyor atha bhavec cintā jñātijanaṃ prati /
children.translated_text: And if anxious thought should arise regarding your kinfolk, about their prosperity or adversity,

children.text: svabhāvo jīvalokasya parīkṣyas tannivṛttaye // Saund_15.30 //
children.translated_text: The nature of the world of the living should be examined for its cessation. // 15.30 //

children.text: saṃsāre kṛṣyamāṇānāṃ sattvānāṃ svena karmaṇā /
children.translated_text: Of beings who are being dragged through <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth) by their own <s>karma</s> (actions) —

children.text: ko janaḥ svajanaḥ ko vā mohāt sakto jane janaḥ // Saund_15.31 //
children.translated_text: What person is 'one's own' and what person is 'another'? It is out of delusion that a person is attached to people. // 15.31 //

children.text: atīte 'dhvani saṃvṛttaḥ svajano hi janas tava /
children.translated_text: In a past period, a stranger became your kinsman;

children.text: aprāpte cādhvani janaḥ svajanas te bhaviṣyti // Saund_15.32 //
children.translated_text: And in a future period yet to come, a stranger will become your kinsman. // 15.32 //

children.text: vihagānā yathā sāyaṃ tatra tatra samāgamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as birds gather here and there in the evening,

children.text: jātau jātau tathā śleṣo janasya svajanasya ca // Saund_15.33 //
children.translated_text: So in birth after birth is the union of kinsmen and strangers. // 15.33 //

children.text: pariśrayaṃ abhuvidhaṃ saṃśrayanti yathādhvagāḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as travelers resort to various shelters

children.text: prātiyānti punas tyaktvā tadvaj jñātisamāgamaḥ // Saund_15.34 //
children.translated_text: And depart again having abandoned them — such is the gathering of relatives. // 15.34 //

children.text: loke prakṛtibhinne 'smin na kaś cit kasya cit priyaḥ /
children.translated_text: In this world, essentially divided, no one is truly dear to anyone;

children.text: kāryakārañasaṃbaddhaṃ bālukāmuṣṭivaj jagat // Saund_15.35 //
children.translated_text: The world is bound by cause and effect, like a handful of sand. // 15.35 //

children.text: bibharti hi sutaṃ mātā dharayiṣyati mām iti /
children.translated_text: A mother supports her son [thinking] 'he will support me';

children.text: mātaraṃ bhajate putṛo garbheṇādhatta mām iti // Saund_15.36 //
children.translated_text: A son serves his mother [thinking] 'she carried me in her womb.' // 15.36 //

children.text: anukūlaṃ pravartante jñātiṣu jñātayo yadā /
children.translated_text: When kinsmen behave agreeably toward kinsmen,

children.text: tadā snehaṃ prakurvanti riputvaṃ tu viparyayāt // Saund_15.37 //
children.translated_text: Then they develop affection; but enmity arises from the reverse. // 15.37 //

children.text: ahito dṛṣyate jñātir ajñātir hitaḥ /
children.translated_text: A kinsman is seen to be harmful, and a non-kinsman beneficial;

children.text: snehaṃ kāryāntarāl lokaś chinatti ca karoti ca // Saund_15.38 //
children.translated_text: The world, due to ulterior motives, both severs and creates affection. // 15.38 //

children.text: svayam eva yathālikya rajyec citrakaraḥ striyam /
children.translated_text: Just as a painter himself falls in love with a woman he has painted,

children.text: tathā kṛtvā svayaṃ snehaṃ saṃgameti jane janaḥ // Saund_15.39 //
children.translated_text: So, having created affection themselves, people become attached to people. // 15.39 //

children.text: yo 'bhavad bāndhavajanaḥ paraloke priyas tava /
children.translated_text: The person who was your kinsman, dear to you in a former life —

children.text: sa te kam arthaṃ kurute tvaṃ vā tasmai karoṣi kam // Saund_15.40 //
children.translated_text: What purpose does he serve you, and what do you do for him? // 15.40 //

children.text: tasmāj jñātvitarkeṇa mano nāveṣṭum arhasi /
children.translated_text: Therefore, you should not entangle your mind with thoughts about kinsmen;

children.text: vyavasthā nāsti saṃsāre svajanasya janasya ca // Saund_15.41 //
children.translated_text: In <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth), there is no fixed distinction between kinsmen and strangers. // 15.41 //

children.text: asau kṣemo janapadaḥ subhikṣo 'sāv asau śivaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'That country is safe, that one is prosperous, that one is auspicious' —

children.text: ity evam atha jāyeta vitarkas tava kaś cana // Saund_15.42 //
children.translated_text: If some such thought should arise in you — // 15.42 //

children.text: praheyaḥ sa tvayā saumya nādhivāsyaḥ kathaṃ cana /
children.translated_text: It should be abandoned by you, O gentle one, and never indulged,

children.text: viditvā sarvam ādīptaṃ tais tair doṣāgnibhir jagat // Saund_15.43 //
children.translated_text: Knowing the entire world to be ablaze with the various fires of faults. // 15.43 //

children.text: ṛtucakranivartāc ca kṣutpipāsāklamād api /
children.translated_text: Due to the revolving cycle of seasons and also from the fatigue of hunger and thirst,

children.text: sarvatra niyataṃ duḥkhaṃ na kva cid vidyate śivam // Saund_15.44 //
children.translated_text: Suffering is certain everywhere — nowhere is there true well-being. // 15.44 //

children.text: kva cic chitaṃ kva cid dharmaḥ kva cid rogo bhayaṃ kva cit /
children.translated_text: In some places cold, in some places heat, in some places disease, in some places fear —

children.text: bādhate 'bhyadhikaṃ loke tasmād aśaraṇaṃ jagat // Saund_15.45 //
children.translated_text: Afflicts excessively in the world — therefore the world is without refuge. // 15.45 //

children.text: jarā vyādhiś ca mṛtyuś ca lokasyāsya mahadbhayam /
children.translated_text: Old age, disease, and death — this is the great terror of this world;

children.text: nāsti deśaḥ sa yatrāsya tadbhayaṃ nopapadyate // Saund_15.46 //
children.translated_text: There is no place where this terror does not arise. // 15.46 //

children.text: yatra gacchati kāyo 'yaṃ duḥkhaṃ tatrānugacchati /
children.translated_text: Wherever this body goes, suffering follows;

children.text: nāsti kā cid gatir loke gato yatra na bādhayte // Saund_15.47 //
children.translated_text: There is no destination in the world where one who has gone is not afflicted. // 15.47 //

children.text: ramaṇīyo 'pi deśaḥ san dubhikṣaḥ kṣema eva ca /
children.translated_text: A place that is delightful, prosperous, and safe —

children.text: kudeśa iti vijñeyo yatra kleśair vidhayate // Saund_15.48 //
children.translated_text: Should be known as a bad place if one is tormented by <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) there. // 15.48 //

children.text: lokasyābhyāhatsyāsya duḥkhaiḥ śarīramānasaiḥ /
children.translated_text: For this world, beset by bodily and mental sufferings,

children.text: kṣemaḥ kaś cin na deśo 'sti svastho yatra gato bhavet // Saund_15.49 //
children.translated_text: There is no safe place where one who has gone would be at ease. // 15.49 //

children.text: duḥkhaṃ sarvatra sarvasya vartate sarvadā yadā /
children.translated_text: Since suffering exists everywhere, for everyone, at all times —

children.text: chandarāgam ataḥ saumya likacitreṣu mā kṛthāḥ // Saund_15.50 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, O gentle one, do not cultivate desire and passion toward painted images! // Saund_15.50 //

children.text: yadā tasmān nivṛttas te chandarāgo bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: When your desire and passion for those have ceased,

children.text: jīvalokaṃ tadā sarvam ādīptam iva maṃsyase // Saund_15.51 //
children.translated_text: then you will regard the entire world of the living as if ablaze. // Saund_15.51 //

children.text: athas kaś cid vitarkas te bhaved amaraṇāśrayaḥ /
children.translated_text: And if any thought should arise in you that rests on the assumption of not dying,

children.text: yatnena sa vihantavyo vyādhir ātmagato yathā // Saund_15.52 //
children.translated_text: that must be destroyed with effort, like a disease that has entered the body. // Saund_15.52 //

children.text: muhūrtam api viśrambhaḥ kāryo na khalu jīvite /
children.translated_text: Not even for a moment should confidence be placed in life,

children.text: nilīna iva hi vyāghraḥ kālo viśvastaghātakaḥ // Saund_15.53 //
children.translated_text: for time is a killer of the unsuspecting, lurking like a tiger. // Saund_15.53 //

children.text: balastho 'haṃ yuvā veti na te bhavitum arhati /
children.translated_text: 'I am strong, I am young' — such a thought should not arise in you,

children.text: mṛtyuḥ sarvāsv avasthāsu hanti nāvekṣate vayaḥ // Saund_15.54 //
children.translated_text: for death strikes in all states and does not regard age. // Saund_15.54 //

children.text: kṣetrabhūtam anarthānāṃ śarīraṃ parikarṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: For one who drags along the body — the field of misfortunes —

children.text: svāsthyāśā jivitāśa vā na dṛṣṭārthasya jāyate // Saund_15.55 //
children.translated_text: no hope of health or hope of life arises for one who has seen the truth. // Saund_15.55 //

children.text: nivṛtaḥ ko bhavet kāyaṃ mahābhūtāśrayaṃ vahan /
children.translated_text: Who could be at ease while carrying this body, a receptacle of the great elements,

children.text: parasparaviruddhānām ahinām iva bhājanam // Saund_15.56 //
children.translated_text: which is like a vessel of mutually hostile serpents? // Saund_15.56 //

children.text: praśvasity ayam anvakṣa yad ucchvasiti mānavaḥ /
children.translated_text: That a person breathes out again right after breathing in —

children.text: avagaccha tad āścaryam aviśvāsyaṃ hi jīvitam // Saund_15.57 //
children.translated_text: understand this as a wonder, for life is truly unreliable. // Saund_15.57 //

children.text: idam āścaryam aparaṃ yat suptaḥ pratibudhyate /
children.translated_text: This is another wonder — that one who has fallen asleep wakes up,

children.text: svapity utthāya vā bhūyo bahvamitrā hi dehinaḥ // Saund_15.58 //
children.translated_text: or, having risen, sleeps again, for embodied beings have many enemies. // Saund_15.58 //

children.text: garbhāt prabhṛti yo lokaṃ jighāṃsur anugacchati /
children.translated_text: Death, who follows the world from birth onward, seeking to kill —

children.text: kas tasmin viśvasen mṛtyāv udyatāsāv arāv iva // Saund_15.59 //
children.translated_text: who would trust in that [death], as in a foe with raised weapon? // Saund_15.59 //

children.text: prasūtaḥ puruṣo loke śrutavān balavān api /
children.translated_text: Though a person born in the world be learned and strong,

children.text: na jayaty antakaṃ kaś cin nājayan nāpi jeṣyati // Saund_15.60 //
children.translated_text: no one conquers the Ender — no one has conquered, nor will anyone conquer. // Saund_15.60 //

children.text: sāmnā dānena bhedena daṇḍena niyamena vā /
children.translated_text: By conciliation, by gifts, by stratagem, by force, or by restraint —

children.text: prāpto hi rabhaso mṛtyuḥ pratihantuṃ na śakyate // Saund_15.61 //
children.translated_text: death, once arrived with impetuosity, cannot be repelled. // Saund_15.61 //

children.text: tasmān nāyuṣi viśvāsaṃ cañcale kartum arhasi /
children.translated_text: Therefore you should not place trust in this fickle lifespan,

children.text: nityaṃ harati kālo hi sthāviryaṃ na pratīkṣate // Saund_15.62 //
children.translated_text: for time constantly carries [beings] away and does not wait for old age. // Saund_15.62 //

children.text: niḥsāraṃ paśyato lokaṃ toyabudbudadurbalam /
children.translated_text: For one who sees the world as substanceless, fragile as a water bubble —

children.text: kasyāmaravitarko hi syād anunmattacetasaḥ // Saund_15.63 //
children.translated_text: how could the thought of immortality arise in one of sound mind? // Saund_15.63 //

children.text: tasmād eṣāṃ vitarkāṇāṃ prahāṇārthaṃ samāsataḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, O gentle one, for the purpose of abandoning these [unwholesome] thoughts,

children.text: ānāpānasmṛtiṃ saumya viṣayīkartum arhasi // Saund_15.64 //
children.translated_text: in brief, you should take up <s>ānāpānasmṛti</s> (mindfulness of breathing). // Saund_15.64 //

children.text: ity anena prayogeṇa kāle sevitum arhasi /
children.translated_text: By this method, you should apply at the proper time

children.text: pratipakṣān vitarkāṇāṃ gadānām agadān iva // Saund_15.65 //
children.translated_text: the antidotes to [unwholesome] thoughts, as remedies to diseases. // Saund_15.65 //

children.text: suvarṇahetor api pāṃsudhāvako vihāya pāṃsūn bṛhato yathāditaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a gold-washer, for the sake of gold, first removes the large pieces of dirt,

children.text: jahāti sūkṣmān api tadviśuddhaye viśodhya hemāvayavān niyacchati // Saund_15.66 //
children.translated_text: then discards even the fine [impurities] for its purification, and having refined it, secures the particles of gold;

children.text: vimokṣahetor api yuktamānaso vihāya doṣā bṛhatas tathāditaḥ /
children.translated_text: so too one of yoked mind, for the sake of liberation, first abandons the great faults,

children.text: jahāti sūkṣmān api tadviśuddhaye viśodhya dharmāvayān niyacchati // Saund_15.67 //
children.translated_text: then discards even the subtle ones for its purification, and having refined them, secures the elements of <s>Dharma</s>. // Saund_15.67 //

children.text: kraeṇādbhiḥ śuddhaṃ kanakam iha pāṃsuvyavahitaṃ
children.translated_text: Just as gold intermixed with dirt is here [first] purified with water in stages,

children.text: yathāgnau karmāraḥ pacati bhṛṣam āvartayati ca /
children.translated_text: and then the goldsmith heats it intensely in fire and turns it over and over;

children.text: tathā yogācāro nipuñam iha doṣavyavahitaṃ
children.translated_text: so too the practitioner of <s>yoga</s>, [working on] the mind here, intermixed with faults,

children.text: viśodhya kleśebhyaḥ śamayati manaḥ saṃkṣipati ca // Saund_15.68 //
children.translated_text: having carefully purified it from the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), pacifies the mind and concentrates it. // Saund_15.68 //

children.text: yathā ca svacchandād upanayati karmāśrayasukhaṃ
children.translated_text: And just as a goldsmith, at will, employs gold — amenable to working and easy to handle —

children.text: suvarṇaṃ karmāro bahuṃvidham alaṅkāravidhiṣu /
children.translated_text: in various forms of ornamental design;

children.text: manaḥśuddho bhikṣur vaśagatam abhijñāsv api tathā
children.translated_text: so too the monk of purified mind, with [his] mind under control, in the <s>abhijñās</s> (higher knowledges),

children.text: yathecchaṃ yatrecchaṃ śamayati manaḥ prerayati ca // Saund_15.69 //
children.translated_text: pacifies and directs the mind wherever he wishes, as he wishes. // Saund_15.69 //

body.text: Saundaranande mahākāvye vitarkaprahāṇo nāma pañcadaśaḥ sargaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fifteenth canto, named 'The Abandonment of [Unwholesome] Thoughts,' in the <s>Saundarānanda</s> <s>mahākāvya</s>.
CANTO XVI

children.text: evaṃ manodhāraṇayā krameṇa vyapohya kiṃ cit samupohya kiṃ cit /
children.translated_text: Thus, through mental fixation (<s>dhāraṇā</s>), step by step, putting aside some things and taking up others,

children.text: dhyānāni catvāry adhigamya yogī prāpnoty abhijñā niyamena pañca // Saund_16.1 //
children.translated_text: the <s>yogin</s>, having attained the four <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions), necessarily achieves the five <s>abhijñās</s> (higher knowledges). // Saund_16.1 //

children.text: ṛddhipravekaṃ ca bahuprakāraṃ parasya cetaś caritāvabodham /
children.translated_text: Foremost among them is <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernatural power) of many kinds, the understanding of others' minds and conduct,

children.text: atītajanmasmaraṇaṃ ca dīrghaṃ divye viśuddhe śruticakṣuṣī ca // Saund_16.2 //
children.translated_text: the long recollection of past births, and the purified divine ear and eye. // Saund_16.2 //

children.text: ataḥparaṃ tattvaparīkṣaṇena mano dadhāty āsravasaṃkṣayāya /
children.translated_text: Beyond this, through the examination of reality, the mind applies itself to the destruction of the <s>āsravas</s> (influxes),

children.text: tato hi duḥkhaprabhṛtīni samyak catvāri satyāni padāny avaiti // Saund_16.3 //
children.translated_text: for then one rightly comprehends the four truths beginning with suffering. // Saund_16.3 //

children.text: bādhātmakaṃ duḥkham idaṃ prasaktaṃ duḥkhasya hetuḥ prabhavātmako 'yam /
children.translated_text: This suffering, whose nature is affliction, is ever-present; this is the cause of suffering, whose nature is origination;

children.text: duḥkhakṣayo niḥsaraṇātmako 'yaṃ trāṇātmako 'yaṃ praśamāya mārgaḥ // Saund_16.4 //
children.translated_text: this is the cessation of suffering, whose nature is release; this is the path leading to peace, whose nature is protection. // Saund_16.4 //

children.text: ity āryasaryāny avabudhya buddhyā catvāri samyak pratividhya caiva /
children.translated_text: Having understood the four <s>Āryasatyas</s> (Noble Truths) with wisdom, and having rightly penetrated them,

children.text: sarvāsravān bhāvanayābhibhūya na jāyate śāntim avāpya bhūyaḥ // Saund_16.5 //
children.translated_text: one overcomes all <s>āsravas</s> through contemplation and, having attained peace, is not born again. // Saund_16.5 //

children.text: abodhato hy aprativedhataś ca tattvātmakasyāsya catuṣṭayasya /
children.translated_text: For without understanding and without penetrating this fourfold [truth],

children.text: bhāvad bhavaṃ yāti na śāntim eti saṃsāradolām adhiruhya lokaḥ // Saund_16.6 //
children.translated_text: the world, having mounted the swing of <s>saṃsāra</s>, goes from existence to existence and does not reach peace. // Saund_16.6 //

children.text: tasmāj jarāder vyasanasya mūlaṃ samāsato duḥkham avaihi janma /
children.translated_text: Therefore, know in brief that birth is the root of calamity beginning with old age — that is suffering;

children.text: sarvauṣadhīnām iva bhūr bhavāya sarvāpadāṃ kṣetram idaṃ hi janma // Saund_16.7 //
children.translated_text: for birth is the field of all misfortunes, just as the earth is [the field] of all plants that lead to existence. // Saund_16.7 //

children.text: yaj janma rūpasya hi sendriyasya duḥkhasya tan naikavidhasya janma /
children.translated_text: For the birth of [a being] endowed with form and senses is the birth of manifold suffering;

children.text: yaḥ saṃbhavaś cāsya samucchrayasya mṛtyoṣ ca rogasya ca saṃbhavaḥ saḥ // Saund_16.8 //
children.translated_text: and what is the arising of this growth is also the arising of death and disease. // Saund_16.8 //

children.text: sad vāpy asad vā viṣamiṣram annaṃ yathā vināśāya na dhāraṇāya /
children.translated_text: Just as food — whether good or bad or mixed with poison — leads to destruction, not to sustenance,

children.text: loke tathā tiryag uparyadho vā duḥkhāya sarvaṃ na sukḥāya janma // Saund_16.9 //
children.translated_text: so too in the world — whether in animal realms, above, or below — all birth leads to suffering, not to happiness. // Saund_16.9 //

children.text: jarādayo naikavidhā parajānāṃ satyāṃ pravṛttau prabhavanty anarthāḥ /
children.translated_text: The manifold misfortunes of beings, such as old age and the rest, arise when there is [continued] activity;

children.text: pravātsu ghoeṣv api māruteṣu na hy aprasūtās taravaś calanti // Saund_16.10 //
children.translated_text: for trees do not shake in fierce winds unless they have sprouted. // Saund_16.10 //

children.text: ākāsayoniḥ pavano yathā hi yathā śamīgarbhaśayo hutāśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as wind is born from space, just as fire lies hidden within the <s>Śamī</s> wood,

children.text: āpo yathāntarvasudhāśayāś ca duḥkhaṃ tathā cittaśarīrayoni // Saund_16.11 //
children.translated_text: and just as waters lie hidden within the earth — so suffering is born from mind and body. // Saund_16.11 //

children.text: apāṃ dravatvaṃ kaṭhinatvam urvyā vāyoś calatvaṃ dhruvam auṣṇyam agneḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as fluidity is the nature of water, hardness of earth, movement of wind, and heat certainly of fire,

children.text: yathā svabhāvo hi tathā svabhāvo duḥkhaṃ śarīrasya ca cetasaś ca // Saund_16.12 //
children.translated_text: so too is suffering the nature of the body and of the mind. // Saund_16.12 //

children.text: kāye sati vyādhijarādi duḥkhaṃ kṣuttarṣavarṣoṣṇahimādi caiva /
children.translated_text: When there is a body, there is suffering from disease, old age, and the like, as well as from hunger, thirst, rain, heat, cold, and so forth;

children.text: rupāśrite cetasi sānubandhe śokāratikrodhabhayādi duḥkham // Saund_16.13 //
children.translated_text: and when there is a mind attached to form and accompanied [by its objects], there is suffering from grief, discontent, anger, fear, and the like. // Saund_16.13 //

children.text: pratyakṣam ālokya ca janmaduḥkhaṃ duḥkhaṃ tathātītam apīti viddhi /
children.translated_text: Having observed directly the suffering of birth, know that past suffering too was like this;

children.text: yathā ca tad duḥkham idaṃ ca duḥkhaṃ duḥkhaṃ tathānāgatam apy avehi // Saund_16.14 //
children.translated_text: and just as that [past] suffering and this [present] suffering [are], so understand that future suffering too [will be]. // Saund_16.14 //

children.text: bījasvabhāvo hi yatheha dṛṣṭo bhūto 'pi bhavyo 'pi tathānumeyaḥ /
children.translated_text: For just as the nature of a seed is seen here [in the present], so the past and future [seeds] are to be inferred similarly;

children.text: pratyakṣataś ca jvalano yathoṣṇo bhūto 'pi bhavyo 'pi tathoṣṇa eva // Saund_16.15 //
children.translated_text: and just as fire is directly [experienced as] hot, so too [was it] in the past and [will it be] in the future — hot indeed. // Saund_16.15 //

children.text: tan nāmarūpasya guṇānurūpaṃ yatraiva nirvṛtti udāravṛtta /
children.translated_text: O one of noble conduct, wherever there is satisfaction in accordance with the qualities of name-and-form,

children.text: tatraiva duḥkhaṃ na hi tadvimuktaṃ duḥkhaṃ bhaviṣyaty abhavad bhaved vā // Saund_16.16 //
children.translated_text: right there is suffering; for what is free from that [name-and-form] neither has been, will be, nor could be suffering. // Saund_16.16 //

children.text: pravṛttiduḥkhasya ca tasya loke tṛṣṇādayo doṣagaṇā nimittam /
children.translated_text: And the host of faults beginning with <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) is the cause of that suffering which consists in [continued] activity in the world;

children.text: naiveṣvaro na prakṛtir na kālo nāpi svabhāvo na vidhir yadṛcchā // Saund_16.17 //
children.translated_text: it is neither a lord (<s>Īśvara</s>), nor primordial nature (<s>Prakṛti</s>), nor time, nor inherent nature, nor fate, nor chance. // Saund_16.17 //

children.text: jñātavyam etena ca kāraṇena lokasya doṣebhya iti pravṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: And by this reason it should be known that the world's [continued] activity arises from the faults;

children.text: yasmān mriyante sarajastamaskā na jāyate vītarajastmaskaḥ // Saund_16.18 //
children.translated_text: for those who possess <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> die [and are reborn], while one who is free from <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> is not born. // Saund_16.18 //

children.text: icchāviṣeśe sati tatra tatra yānāsanāder bhavati prayogaḥ /
children.translated_text: When there is a specific desire, the employment of vehicles, seats, and the like follows accordingly;

children.text: yasmād atas tarṣavaśat tathaiva janma prajānām iti veditavyam // Saund_16.19 //
children.translated_text: therefore, know that the birth of beings likewise follows from the power of craving (<s>tarṣa</s>). // Saund_16.19 //

children.text: sattvāny abhiṣvaṅgavaśāni dṛṣṭvā svajātiṣu prītiparāṇy atīva /
children.translated_text: Seeing that beings are subject to attachment, exceedingly delighting in their own kind,

children.text: abhyāsayogād upapāditāni tair eva doṣair iti tāni viddhi // Saund_16.20 //
children.translated_text: know that they have been brought into being through habitual practice by those very faults. // Saund_16.20 //

children.text: krodhapraharṣādibhir āśrayāṇām utpadyate ceha yathā viśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a specific condition arises in substrates here due to anger, joy, and the like,

children.text: tathaiva janmasv api naikarūpo nirvartate kleśakṛto viśeṣaḥ // Saund_16.21 //
children.translated_text: so too a multiform specific condition produced by the <s>kleśas</s> manifests in [various] births. // Saund_16.21 //

children.text: doṣādhike janmani tīvradoṣa utpadyate rāgiṇi tīvrarāgaḥ /
children.translated_text: In a birth predominated by fault, one of intense fault is born; in one [predominated by] passion, one of intense passion;

children.text: mohādhike mohabalādhikaś ca tadalpadoṣe ca tadalpadoṣaḥ // Saund_16.22 //
children.translated_text: in one predominated by delusion, one of intense delusion; and in one of lesser fault, one of lesser fault. // Saund_16.22 //

children.text: phalaṃ hi yādṛk samavaiti sākṣāt tadāgamād bījam avaity atītam /
children.translated_text: For just as one directly perceives the fruit [in the present], from that [fruit] one infers the past seed;

children.text: avetya bījaprakṛtiṃ ca sākṣād anāgataṃ tatphalam abhyupaiti // Saund_16.23 //
children.translated_text: and having directly ascertained the nature of the seed, one anticipates the future fruit. // Saund_16.23 //

children.text: doṣakṣayo jātiṣu yāsu yasya vairāgyatas tāsu na jāyate saḥ /
children.translated_text: In whichever births one's faults are exhausted, one is not born there, through dispassion;

children.text: doṣāśayas tiṣṭhati yasya yatra tasyopapattir vivaśasya tatra // Saund_16.24 //
children.translated_text: and wherever the residue of faults remains, there is the arising of that helpless [being]. // Saund_16.24 //

children.text: taj janmano naikavidhasya saumya tṛṣṇādayo hetava ity avetya /
children.translated_text: Therefore, O gentle one, having understood that craving and the rest are the causes of manifold birth,

children.text: tāṃś chindhi duḥkhād yadi nirmumukṣā kāryakṣayaḥ kāraṇasaṃkṣayād dhi // Saund_16.25 //
children.translated_text: cut them off if you wish to be freed from suffering — for the effect ceases with the cessation of the cause. // Saund_16.25 //

children.text: duḥkhakṣayo hetuparikṣayāc ca śāntanaṃ śivaṃ sākṣikuruṣva dharmam /
children.translated_text: And through the thorough cessation of the cause, [comes] the cessation of suffering — realize directly the <s>Dharma</s> that is peaceful, auspicious,

children.text: tṛṣṇāvirāgaṃ layanaṃ nirdohaṃ sanātanaṃ trāṇam ahāryam āryam // Saund_16.26 //
children.translated_text: the dispassion from craving, the resting place, the freedom from harm, the eternal, the refuge, the inviolable, the noble. // Saund_16.26 //

children.text: yasmin na jātir na jarā na mṛtyur na vyādhayo nāpriyasaṃprayogaḥ /
children.translated_text: Wherein there is no birth, no old age, no death, no disease, no unwanted conjunction,

children.text: necchāvipanna priyaviprayogaḥ kṣemaṃ padaṃ naiṣṭhikam acyutaṃ tat // Saund_16.27 //
children.translated_text: no frustrated desire, no separation from the beloved — that is the final, secure, imperishable state of well-being. // Saund_16.27 //

children.text: dīpo yathā nirvṛtim abhyupeto naivāvaniṃ gacchati nānatarikṣam /
children.translated_text: Just as a lamp that has reached extinction goes neither to the earth nor to the sky,

children.text: diśaṃ na kāṃ cid vidiṣaṃ na kāṃ cit snehakṣayāt kevalam eti śāntim // Saund_16.28 //
children.translated_text: nor to any direction or intermediate direction, but through the exhaustion of fuel simply attains peace;

children.text: evaṃ kṛtī nirvṛtim abhyupeto naivāvaniṃ gacchati nāntarikṣam /
children.translated_text: so too the accomplished one who has reached <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation) goes neither to the earth nor to the sky,

children.text: diśaṃ na kāṃ cid vidiśaṃ na kāṃ cit kleśakṣayāt kevalam eti sāntim // Saund_16.29 //
children.translated_text: nor to any direction or intermediate direction, but through the exhaustion of the <s>kleśas</s> simply attains peace. // Saund_16.29 //

children.text: asyābhyupāyo 'dhingamāya mārgaḥ prajñātrikalpaḥ praśamadvikalpaḥ /
children.translated_text: The path for attaining this [cessation] is of threefold constitution with respect to wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) and twofold with respect to tranquility (<s>praśama</s>);

children.text: sa bhāvanīyo vidhivad budhena śīle śucau tripamukhe sthitena // Saund_16.30 //
children.translated_text: it is to be cultivated properly by the wise one who is established in pure <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct), the threefold opening. // Saund_16.30 //

children.text: vākkarma samyak sahakāyakarma yathāvad ājīvanayaś ca śuddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Right speech, together with right action, and a pure livelihood as prescribed —

children.text: idaṃ trayaṃ vṛttavidhau pravṛttaṃ śīlāśrayaṃ karmaparigrahāya // Saund_16.31 //
children.translated_text: these three, operating in the domain of conduct, are grounded in <s>śīla</s> and serve to discipline actions. // Saund_16.31 //

children.text: satyeṣu duḥkhādiṣu dṛṣṭir āryā samyagvitarkaś ca parākramaś ca /
children.translated_text: The noble vision (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>) regarding the truths beginning with suffering, right thought, and right effort —

children.text: idaṃ trayaṃ jñānavidhau pravṛttaṃ prajñāśrayaṃ kleśaparikṣayāya // Saund_16.32 //
children.translated_text: these three, operating in the domain of knowledge, are grounded in wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) and serve to destroy the <s>kleśas</s>. // Saund_16.32 //

children.text: nyāyena satyādhigamāya yuktā samyak smṛtiḥ samyag atho samādhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Right mindfulness and right concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), properly applied for the attainment of the truths —

children.text: idaṃ dvayaṃ yogavidhau pravṛttaṃ śamāśrayaṃ cittaparigrahāya // Saund_16.33 //
children.translated_text: these two, operating in the domain of <s>yoga</s>, are grounded in tranquility and serve to discipline the mind. // Saund_16.33 //

children.text: kleśāṅkurān na pratanoti śīlaṃ bījāṅkurān kāla ivāvṛttaḥ /
children.translated_text: Moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) does not allow the shoots of the <s>kleśas</s> to sprout, like the [unsuitable] season [that prevents] seed-shoots;

children.text: śucau hi śīle puruṣasya doṣā manaḥ salajjā iva dharṣayanti // Saund_16.34 //
children.translated_text: for in one of pure conduct, faults assail the mind only with shame, as it were. // Saund_16.34 //

children.text: kleśāṃs tu viṣkambhayate samādhir vegān ivādrir mahaot nadīnām /
children.translated_text: Concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), however, suppresses the <s>kleśas</s>, as a mountain [suppresses] the currents of great rivers;

children.text: sthite samādhau hi na dharṣayanti doṣā bhujaṅgā iva mantrabaddhāḥ // Saund_16.35 //
children.translated_text: for when concentration is established, faults do not assail, like serpents bound by mantras. // Saund_16.35 //

children.text: prajñā tv aśeṣeṇa nihanti doṣāṃs tīradrumān prāvṛṣi nimnageva /
children.translated_text: But wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) destroys the faults completely, as a river [destroys] the trees on its banks in the rainy season;

children.text: dagdhā yayā na prabhavanti doṣā vajrāgninevānusṛtena vṛkṣāḥ // Saund_16.36 //
children.translated_text: burned by which, the faults do not arise again, like trees [consumed] by fire following a thunderbolt. // Saund_16.36 //

children.text: triskandham etaṃ pravigāhya mārgaṃ praspaṣṭam aṣṭāṅgam ahāryam āryam /
children.translated_text: Having entered this path of three divisions, clearly eightfold, inviolable, and noble,

children.text: duḥkhasya hetūn prajahāti doṣān prāpnoti cātyantaśivaṃ padaṃ tat // Saund_16.37 //
children.translated_text: one abandons the faults that are the causes of suffering and attains that supremely auspicious state. // Saund_16.37 //

children.text: asyopacāre dhṛtir ārjavaṃ ca hrīr apramādaḥ praviviktatā ca /
children.translated_text: In the practice of this [path], there is steadfastness, uprightness,

children.text: alpecchatā tuṣṭir asaṃgatā ca lokapravṛttāv aratiḥ kṣamā ca // Saund_16.38 //
children.translated_text: modesty, vigilance, seclusion, few desires, contentment, non-attachment, dissatisfaction with worldly ways, and patience. // Saund_16.38 //

children.text: yāthātmyato vindati yo hi duḥkhaṃ tasyodbhavaṃ tasya ca yo nirdodham /
children.translated_text: For one who truly understands suffering, its arising, and its cessation —

children.text: āryeṇa mārgeṇa sa sāntim eti kalyāṇamitraiḥ saha vartamānaḥ // Saund_16.39 //
children.translated_text: By the Noble Path, he attains peace, dwelling in the company of virtuous friends. // Saund 16.39 //

children.text: yo vyādhito vyādhim avaiti samyag vyādher nidānaṃ ca tadauṣadhaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: One who is sick and rightly understands the sickness, the cause of the sickness, and its remedy —

children.text: ārogyam āpnoti hi so 'cireṇa mitrair abhijñair upacaryamāṇaḥ // Saund_16.40 //
children.translated_text: He indeed attains health before long, being treated by knowledgeable friends. // Saund 16.40 //

children.text: tad vyādhisaṃjñāṃ kuru duḥkhasatye doṣeṣv api vyādhinidānasaṃjñām /
children.translated_text: Therefore, apply the notion of sickness to the truth of suffering, the notion of the cause of sickness to the faults (<s>doṣas</s>),

children.text: ārogyasaṃjñāṃ ca nirdohasatye bhaiṣajyasaṃjñām api mārgasatye // Saund_16.41 //
children.translated_text: The notion of health to the truth of cessation, and the notion of medicine to the truth of the path. // Saund 16.41 //

children.text: tasmāt pravṛttiṃ parigaccha duḥkhaṃ pravartakān apy avagaccha doṣān /
children.translated_text: Therefore, comprehend suffering as origination; understand too the faults (<s>doṣas</s>) as the originators;

children.text: nivṛttim āgaccha ca tannirodhaṃ nivartakaṃ cāpy avagaccha mārgam // Saund_16.42 //
children.translated_text: Attain cessation as the stopping of that; and understand the path as the means of stopping. // Saund 16.42 //

children.text: śirasy atho vāsasi saṃpradīpte satyāvabodhāya matir vicāryā /
children.translated_text: When one's head or garment is ablaze, one's mind should be directed toward the realization of the truths;

children.text: dagdhaṃ jagat satyanayaṃ hy adṛṣṭvā pradahyate saṃprati dhakṣyate ca // Saund_16.43 //
children.translated_text: For the world, burned [by suffering], not having seen the method of the truths, is being burned now and will be burned hereafter. // Saund 16.43 //

children.text: yadaiva yaḥ paśyati nāmarūpaṃ kṣayīti taddarśanam asya samyak /
children.translated_text: The very moment one sees that name-and-form is subject to destruction — that is his right seeing;

children.text: samyak ca nirvedam upaiti paśyān nandīkṣayāc ca kṣayam eti rāgaḥ // Saund_16.44 //
children.translated_text: And seeing rightly, he attains disenchantment, and from the waning of delight, passion comes to an end. // Saund 16.44 //

children.text: tayoś ca nandīrajasoḥ kṣayeṇa samyag vimuktaṃ pravadāmi cetaḥ /
children.translated_text: And through the waning of those two — delight and passion — I declare the mind to be rightly liberated;

children.text: samyag vimuktir manasaś ca tābhyāṃ na cāsya bhūyaḥ karaṇīyam asti // Saund_16.45 //
children.translated_text: And for the mind rightly liberated from those two, there is nothing further to be done. // Saund 16.45 //

children.text: yathāsvabhāvena hi nāmarūpaṃ tad dhetum evāstagamaṃ ca tasya /
children.translated_text: For one who knows name-and-form according to its true nature, its cause, and also its cessation,

children.text: vijānataḥ paśyata eva cāhaṃ bravīmi samyak kṣayam āsravāṇām // Saund_16.46 //
children.translated_text: And who also sees — I declare the right destruction of the <s>āsravas</s> (outflows). // Saund 16.46 //

children.text: tasmāt paraṃ saumya vidhāya vīryaṃ śīghraṃ ghaṭasv āsravasaṃkṣayāya /
children.translated_text: Therefore, O gentle one, mustering supreme effort, strive swiftly for the destruction of the <s>āsravas</s>,

children.text: duḥkhān anityāṃś ca nirātmakāṃś ca dhātūn viśeṣeṇa parīkṣamāṇāḥ // Saund_16.47 //
children.translated_text: Examining especially the elements (<s>dhātus</s>) as painful, impermanent, and devoid of self. // Saund 16.47 //

children.text: dhātūn hi ṣaḍ bhūsalilānalādīn sāmānyataḥ svena ca lakṣaṇena /
children.translated_text: For one who understands the six elements — earth, water, fire, and the rest — both in their general and specific characteristics,

children.text: avaiti yo nānyam avaiti tebhyaḥ so 'tyantikaṃ mokṣam avaiti tebhyaḥ // Saund_16.48 //
children.translated_text: And understands no other [thing] apart from them — he understands ultimate liberation from them. // Saund 16.48 //

children.text: kleśaprahāṇāya ca niścitena kālo 'bhyupāyaś ca parīkṣitavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: And for one resolved upon the abandonment of defilements, the right time and method must be examined;

children.text: yogo 'py akāle hy anupāyataś ca bhavaty anarthāya na tadguṇāya // Saund_16.49 //
children.translated_text: For practice at the wrong time or without proper method leads to harm, not to its intended benefit. // Saund 16.49 //

children.text: ajātavatsāṃ yadi gāṃ duhīta naivāptuyāt kṣīram akāladohī /
children.translated_text: If one were to milk a cow that has not yet calved, milking at the wrong time, one would not obtain milk;

children.text: kāle 'pi vā syān na payo labheta mohena śṛṅgād yadi gāṃ duhīta // Saund_16.50 //
children.translated_text: Or even at the right time, one would get no milk if, through delusion, one milked the cow by the horn. // Saund 16.50 //

children.text: ārdrāc ca kāṣṭhā jvalanābhikāmo naiva prayatnād api vahnim ṛcchet /
children.translated_text: And one desiring fire from wet wood would never obtain fire even with effort;

children.text: kāṣṭhāc ca śuṣkād api pātganena naivāgnim āpnoty anupāapūrvam // Saund_16.51 //
children.translated_text: And even from dry wood, through mere friction, one would never get fire without the proper method. // Saund 16.51 //

children.text: tad deśakālau vidhivat parīkṣya yogasya mātrām api cābhyupāyam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, having duly examined the place and time, the measure and method of practice,

children.text: balābale cātmani saṃpradhārya kāryāḥ prayatno na tu tadviruddhaḥ // Saund_16.52 //
children.translated_text: And having assessed one's own strengths and weaknesses — effort should be applied, not what contradicts it. // Saund 16.52 //

children.text: pragrāhakaṃ yat tu nimittam uktam uddanyamāne hṛdi tan na sevyam /
children.translated_text: The object of meditation that has been prescribed as stimulating should not be practiced when the mind is agitated;

children.text: evaṃ hi cittaṃ praśamaṃ na yāti [na vahri] nā vahnir iveryamāṇaḥ // Saund_16.53 //
children.translated_text: For thus the mind does not attain tranquility, like a fire that is being fanned. // Saund 16.53 //

children.text: śamāya yat syān niyataṃ nimittaṃ jātoddhave cetasi tasya kālaḥ /
children.translated_text: An object that is invariably calming — its time is when the mind has become agitated;

children.text: evaṃ hi cittaṃ praśamaṃ niyacchet pradīpyamāno 'gnir ivodakena // Saund_16.54 //
children.translated_text: For thus the mind is brought to tranquility, like a blazing fire [doused] with water. // Saund 16.54 //

children.text: śamāvahaṃ yan niyataṃ nimittaṃ sevyaṃ na tac cetasi līyamāne /
children.translated_text: An object that is invariably calming should not be practiced when the mind is sinking into torpor;

children.text: evaṃ hi bhūyo layameti cittam anīryamāṇo 'gnir ivālpasāraḥ // Saund_16.55 //
children.translated_text: For thus the mind sinks further into torpor, like a fire of little fuel that is not stirred. // Saund 16.55 //

children.text: pragrāhakaṃ yan niyataṃ nimittaṃ layaṃ gate cetasi tasya kālaḥ /
children.translated_text: An object that is invariably stimulating — its time is when the mind has sunk into torpor;

children.text: kriyāsamarthaṃ hi manas tathā syān mandāyamāno 'gnir ivendhanena // Saund_16.56 //
children.translated_text: For thus the mind becomes capable of action, like a weakening fire [revived] with fuel. // Saund 16.56 //

children.text: aupekṣikaṃ nāpi nimittam iṣṭaṃ layaṃ gate cetasi soddhave vā /
children.translated_text: Nor is the equanimous object desirable when the mind has sunk into torpor or is agitated;

children.text: evaṃ hi tīvraṃ janayed anartham upekṣito vyādhir ivāturasya // Saund_16.57 //
children.translated_text: For thus it would generate severe harm, like a disease that is neglected in a sick person. // Saund 16.57 //

children.text: yat syād upekṣāniyataṃ nimittaṃ sāmyaṃ gate cetasi tasya kālaḥ /
children.translated_text: An object suited to equanimity — its time is when the mind has reached equilibrium;

children.text: evaṃ hi kṛtyāya bhavet prayogo ratho vidheyāśva iva prayātaḥ // Saund_16.58 //
children.translated_text: For thus the practice would serve its purpose, like a chariot driven by well-trained horses. // Saund 16.58 //

children.text: rāgoddhavyākulite 'pi citte maitropasaṃhāravidhir na kāryaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the mind is agitated by the turbulence of passion, the method of cultivating <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) should not be applied;

children.text: rāgātmako muhyati maitrayā hi senhaṃ kaphakṣobha ivopayujya // Saund_16.59 //
children.translated_text: For one of a passionate nature is bewildered by loving-kindness, like one afflicted with <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) aggravation who takes unctuous [food]. // Saund 16.59 //

children.text: rāgoddhate cetasi dhairyam etya niṣevitavyaṃ tv aśubhaṃ nimittam /
children.translated_text: When the mind is agitated by passion, one should steadfastly practice the meditation on the <s>aśubha</s> (impure/unattractive);

children.text: rāgātmako hy evam upaiti śarma kaphātmako rūkṣam ivopayujya // Saund_16.60 //
children.translated_text: For one of a passionate nature thus attains peace, like one of a phlegmatic constitution who takes dry [food]. // Saund 16.60 //

children.text: vyāpādadoṣeṇa manasy udīrṇe na sevitavyaṃ tv aśubhaṃ nimittam /
children.translated_text: When the mind is stirred by the fault of ill-will, the meditation on the <s>aśubha</s> (impure) should not be practiced;

children.text: dveṣātmakasya hy aśubhā vadhāya pittātmanas śīta ivopacāraḥ // Saund_16.61 //
children.translated_text: For for one of a hateful nature, the <s>aśubha</s> leads to violence, like cold treatment for one of a bilious constitution. // Saund 16.61 //

children.text: vyāpādadoṣakṣubhite tu citte sevyā avapakṣopanayena maitrī /
children.translated_text: But when the mind is disturbed by the fault of ill-will, <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) should be practiced, through the method of introducing the opposite;

children.text: dveṣātmano hi praśamāya maitrī pittātmanaḥ śīta ivopacarāḥ // Saund_16.62 //
children.translated_text: For <s>maitrī</s> pacifies one of a hateful nature, like cool treatment for one of a bilious constitution. // Saund 16.62 //

children.text: mohānubaddhe manasaḥ pracāre maitrāśubhā caiva bhavaty ayogaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the mind's activity is bound by delusion, both <s>maitrī</s> and <s>aśubha</s> meditation are inappropriate;

children.text: tābhyāṃ hi saṃmoham upaiti bhūyo vāyvātmako rūkṣam ivopanīya // Saund_16.63 //
children.translated_text: For through those two, one falls further into confusion, like one of a windy constitution who takes dry [food]. // Saund 16.63 //

children.text: mohātmaikāyāṃ mansaḥ pravṛttau sevyas tv idaṃ pratyayatāvihāraḥ /
children.translated_text: When the mind is engaged in a deluded manner, one should practice the contemplation of dependent origination (<s>idaṃpratyayatā</s>);

children.text: mūḍhe manasy eṣa hi śāntimārgo vāyvātmake snigdha ivopacāraḥ // Saund_16.64 //
children.translated_text: For this is the path of peace for a deluded mind, like unctuous treatment for one of a windy constitution. // Saund 16.64 //

children.text: ulkāmukhastaṃ hi yathā suvarṇaṃ suvarṇakāro dhamatīha kāle /
children.translated_text: Just as a goldsmith blows upon gold placed at the mouth of a torch at the [right] time,

children.text: kāle pariprokṣayate jalena krameṇa kāle samupekṣate ca // Saund_16.65 //
children.translated_text: Sprinkles it with water at the [right] time, and observes it at the [right] time in sequence — // Saund 16.65 //

children.text: dahet suvarṇaṃ hi dhamann akāle jale kṣipan saṃśamayed akāle /
children.translated_text: He would burn the gold if blowing at the wrong time, would cool it prematurely if plunging it in water at the wrong time,

children.text: na cāpi samyak paripākam enaṃ nayed akāle samupekṣamāṇaḥ // Saund_16.66 //
children.translated_text: And would not bring it to proper refinement if observing it at the wrong time — // Saund 16.66 //

children.text: saṃpragrahasya praśamasya caiva tathaiva kāle samupekṣaṇasya /
children.translated_text: Similarly, the right object for stimulation, for calming, and likewise for equanimity in due time

children.text: samyaṅnimittaṃ manasā tv avekṣyaṃ nāśo hi yatno 'py anupāyapūrvaḥ // Saund_16.67 //
children.translated_text: Must be discerned by the mind; for effort without the proper method is destruction. // Saund 16.67 //

children.text: ity evam anyāyanivartanaṃ ca nyāyaṃ ca tasmai sugato babhāṣe /
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) spoke to him of the turning away from wrong paths and the right path;

children.text: bhūyaś ca tat tac caritaṃ viditvā vitarkahānāya vidhīn uvāca // Saund_16.68 //
children.translated_text: And furthermore, having understood his various dispositions, he taught methods for the abandonment of discursive thoughts (<s>vitarka</s>). // Saund 16.68 //

children.text: yathā bhiṣak pittakaphānilānāṃ ya eva kopaṃ samupaiti doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a physician, for whichever <s>doṣa</s> (humor) among bile, phlegm, and wind becomes aggravated,

children.text: śamāya tasyaiva vidhatte vyadhatta doṣeṣu tathairva buddhaḥ // Saund_16.69 //
children.translated_text: Prescribes [a remedy] for the pacification of that very [humor] — so did the <s>Buddha</s> [act] with regard to the [mental] faults. // Saund 16.69 //

children.text: ekena kalpena sacen na hanyāt svabhyastabhāvād aśubhān vitarkān /
children.translated_text: If by one method one cannot destroy the unwholesome thoughts that have been repeatedly practiced,

children.text: tato dvitīyaṃ kramam ārabheta na tv eva heyo guṇavān prayogaḥ // Saund_16.70 //
children.translated_text: Then one should undertake a second approach; but a beneficial practice should never be abandoned. // Saund 16.70 //

children.text: anādikālopacitātmakatvād balīyasaḥ kleśagaṇasya caiva /
children.translated_text: Because the host of defilements, accumulated since beginningless time, is powerful,

children.text: samyakprayogasya ca duṣkaratvāc chettuṃ na śakyāḥ sahasā hi doṣāḥ // Saund_16.71 //
children.translated_text: And because right practice is difficult — faults cannot be cut off all at once. // Saund 16.71 //

children.text: añvyā yathāṇyā vipulāṇir anyā nirvāhyate tadviduṣā nareṇa /
children.translated_text: Just as one thorn is extracted by another, larger thorn, by a man skilled in that [art],

children.text: tadvad tad evākuśalaṃ nimittaṃ kṣipen nimittāntarasevanena // Saund_16.72 //
children.translated_text: So too should one dispel an unwholesome object by resorting to another [wholesome] object. // Saund 16.72 //

children.text: tathāpy athādhyātmanavagrahatvān naivopaśāmyed aśubho vitarkaḥ /
children.translated_text: But if, even so, the unwholesome thought does not subside due to its deep inner hold,

children.text: heyaḥ sa taddoṣaparīkṣaṇena saśvāpado mārga ivādhvagena // Saund_16.73 //
children.translated_text: It should be abandoned by examining its faults, like a dangerous road [avoided] by a traveler. // Saund 16.73 //

children.text: yathā kṣudhārto 'pi viṣeṇa pṛktaṃ jijīviṣur necchati bhoktum annam /
children.translated_text: Just as a hungry person, wishing to live, does not desire to eat food mixed with poison,

children.text: tathaiva doṣāvaham ity avetya jahāti vidvān aśubhaṃ nimittam // Saund_16.74 //
children.translated_text: So too, knowing it to be productive of faults, the wise one abandons the unwholesome object. // Saund 16.74 //

children.text: na doṣataḥ paśyati yo hi doṣaṃ kas taṃ tato vārayituṃ samarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: For who is able to restrain one who does not see fault as fault?

children.text: guṇaṃ guṇe paśyati yaś ca yantra sa vāryamāṇo 'pi tataḥ prayāti // Saund_16.75 //
children.translated_text: And one who sees virtue in virtue — even when restrained, he proceeds [toward it]. // Saund 16.75 //

children.text: vyapatrapante hi kulaprasūtā mahaḥpracārair aśubhaiḥ pravṛttaiḥ /
children.translated_text: For those born of noble families are ashamed when shameful thoughts of wide range have arisen,

children.text: kaṇṭhe manasvīva yuvā vapuṣmān acākṣuṣair aprayatair viṣaktaiḥ // Saund_16.76 //
children.translated_text: Like a self-respecting, handsome young man [ashamed] by unclean, impure [garlands] hung upon his neck, invisible [to him]. // Saund 16.76 //

children.text: nirdhūyamānās tv atha leśato 'pi tiṣṭheyur evākuśalā vitarkāḥ /
children.translated_text: But if unwholesome thoughts persist even to the slightest degree, even when being shaken off,

children.text: kāryāntarair adhyayanakriyād yaiḥ sevyo vidhir vismaraṇāya teṣām // Saund_16.77 //
children.translated_text: The method of occupying oneself with other activities such as study etc. should be practiced to forget them. // Saund 16.77 //

children.text: svaptavyam apy eva vicakṣaṇena kāyaklamo vāpi niṣevitavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The discerning one should even go to sleep, or physical exhaustion should be resorted to,

children.text: na tv eva saṃcintyam asannimittaṃ yatrāvasaktasya bhaved anarthaḥ // Saund_16.78 //
children.translated_text: But one should never intentionally dwell upon an unwholesome object, attachment to which would bring harm. // Saund 16.78 //

children.text: yathā hi bhīto niśi taskarebhyo dvāraṃ priyebhyo 'pi na dātum icchet /
children.translated_text: Just as one who is afraid of thieves at night would not wish to open the door even to loved ones,

children.text: prājñas tathā saṃharati prayogaṃ samaṃ śubhasyāpy aśubhasya doṣaiḥ // Saund_16.79 //
children.translated_text: So the wise one curtails his practice equally of both the wholesome and the unwholesome [when the faults of the latter threaten]. // Saund 16.79 //

children.text: evaṃprakārair api yady upāyair nivāryamāṇā na parāñmukhāḥ syuḥ /
children.translated_text: If, even by such methods, when being restrained, they do not turn away,

children.text: tato yathāsthūlanibarhaṇena suvarṇadoṣā iva te praheyāḥ // Saund_16.80 //
children.translated_text: Then they should be abandoned by coarse suppression, like impurities in gold. // Saund 16.80 //

children.text: drutaprayāṇaprabhṛtīṃś ca tīkṣṇāt kāmaprayogāt parikhidyamānaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a man, weary from forced marches and similar hardships, seeks a fierce pleasure-resort,

children.text: yathā naraḥ saṃśrayate tathaiva prājñena doṣeṣv api varitavyam // Saund_16.81 //
children.translated_text: Even so should the wise one deal with the faults. // Saund 16.81 //

children.text: te ced alabdhapratipakṣabhāvā naivopaāmyeyur asadvitarkāḥ /
children.translated_text: If, not having found their antidote, the unwholesome thoughts still do not subside,

children.text: muhūrtam apy aprativadhyamānā gṛhe bhujaṅgā iva nādhivāsyāḥ // Saund_16.82 //
children.translated_text: They should not be tolerated even for a moment without being opposed, like snakes in a house. // Saund 16.82 //

children.text: dante 'pi dantaṃ praṇidhāya kāmaṃ tālvagram utpīḍya ca jihvayāpi /
children.translated_text: Setting tooth against tooth, pressing the palate firmly with the tongue,

children.text: cittena cittaṃ prarigṛhya cāpi kāryaḥ prayatno na tu te 'nuvṛttāḥ // Saund_16.83 //
children.translated_text: And restraining the mind with the mind — effort must be made, and they must not be indulged. // Saund 16.83 //

children.text: kim atra citram yadi vītamoho vanaṃ gataḥ svasthamanā na muhyet /
children.translated_text: What wonder is it if one free from delusion, gone to the forest, with a calm mind, is not bewildered?

children.text: ākṣipyamāṇo hṛdi tannimittair na kṣobhyate yaḥ sa kṛtī sa dhīraḥ // Saund_16.84 //
children.translated_text: He who, though his heart is assailed by those provocative objects, is not shaken — he is the accomplished one, he is the steadfast. // Saund 16.84 //

children.text: tad āryasatyādhigamāya pūrvaṃ viśodhayānena nayena mārgam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, for the realization of the Noble Truths, first purify the path by this method,

children.text: yātrāgataḥ śatruvinigrahārthaṃ rājevy lakṣmīm ajitāṃ jigīṣan // Saund_16.85 //
children.translated_text: Like a king who sets out on a campaign to subdue the enemy, desiring to conquer unattained sovereignty. // Saund 16.85 //

children.text: etāny araṇyāny abhitaḥ śivāni yogānukūlāny ajaneritāni /
children.translated_text: These forests round about are auspicious, favorable to <s>yoga</s>, free from the disturbance of crowds;

children.text: kāyasya kṛtvā pravivekamātraṃ kleśaprahāṇāya bhajasva mārgam // Saund_16.86 //
children.translated_text: Having achieved bodily seclusion, pursue the path for the abandonment of defilements. // Saund 16.86 //

children.text: kauṇḍinyananadakṛmilāniruddhās tipyopasenau vimalo 'tha rādhaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>, <s>Nandaka</s>, <s>Kṛmila</s>, <s>Aniruddha</s>, <s>Tiṣya</s>, <s>Upasena</s>, <s>Vimala</s>, and then <s>Rādha</s>;

children.text: bāṣpottarau dhautakimoharājau kātyāyanadravyapinindavatsāḥ // Saund_16.87 //
children.translated_text: <s>Bāṣpa</s>, <s>Uttara</s>, <s>Dhautaki</s>, <s>Moharāja</s>, <s>Kātyāyana</s>, <s>Dravya</s>, and <s>Pilindavatsa</s>; // Saund 16.87 //

children.text: bhaddālibhadrāyaṇasarpadāsasubhūtigodattsujātavatsāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhaddāli</s>, <s>Bhadrāyaṇa</s>, <s>Sarpadāsa</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>Godatta</s>, <s>Sujāta</s>, <s>Vatsa</s>;

children.text: saṃgrāmajidbhadrajidaśvajic ca śroṇaś ca śoṇaś ca sa koṭikarṇaḥ // Saund_16.88 //
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃgrāmajit</s>, <s>Bhadrajit</s>, <s>Aśvajit</s>, and <s>Śroṇa</s>, and <s>Śoṇa</s>, and that <s>Koṭikarṇa</s>; // Saund 16.88 //

children.text: kṣemājito nandakanandamātā vupālivāgīśayaśāoyaśodāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Kṣemājita</s>, <s>Nandaka</s>, <s>Nandamātā</s>, <s>Upāli</s>, <s>Vāgīśa</s>, <s>Yaśas</s>, and <s>Yaśodā</s>;

children.text: mahāhvayo valkalirāṣṭrapālau sudarśaanasvāgatameghikāś ca // Saund_16.89 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mahāhvaya</s>, <s>Valkali</s>, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, <s>Svāgata</s>, and <s>Meghika</s>; // Saund 16.89 //

children.text: sa kapphinaḥ kāśyapa auruvilvo mahāmahākāśyapatiṣyanandāḥ /
children.translated_text: That <s>Kapphiṇa</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s> of <s>Uruvilvā</s>, <s>Mahā[-kāśyapa]</s>, <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, <s>Tiṣya</s>, <s>Nanda</s>;

children.text: pūrṇaś ca pūrṇaś ca sa pūrṇakaś ca śonāparāntaś ca sa pūrṇa eva // Saund_16.90 //
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇa</s>, and <s>Pūrṇa</s>, and that <s>Pūrṇaka</s>, and <s>Śoṇa</s> of <s>Aparānta</s>, and that [other] <s>Pūrṇa</s> too; // Saund 16.90 //

children.text: śāradvatīputrasubāhucundāḥ kondeyakāpyabhṛgukuṇṭhadhānāḥ /
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Śāradvatī</s>, <s>Subāhu</s>, <s>Cunda</s>; <s>Kondeya</s>, <s>Kāpya</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Kuṇṭhadhāna</s>;

children.text: saśaivalau revatakauṣṭhilau ca maudgalyagotraś ca gavāṃ patiś ca // Saund_16.91 //
children.translated_text: Together with <s>Śaivala</s>, <s>Revata</s>, and <s>Kauṣṭhila</s>, and one of <s>Maudgalya</s> lineage, and <s>Gavāṃpati</s>; // Saund 16.91 //

children.text: yaṃ vikramaṃ yogavidhāv akurvaṃs tam eva śīghraṃ vidhivat kuruṣva /
children.translated_text: Whatever effort they made in the discipline of <s>yoga</s> — make that same [effort] swiftly and according to the method;

children.text: tataḥ padaṃ prāpsyasi tair avāptaṃ sukhāvṛtais tvaṃ nivataṃ niyataṃ yaśaś ca // Saund_16.92 //
children.translated_text: Then you shall attain the state attained by them, who are enveloped in happiness — steadfast peace and certain glory. // Saund 16.92 //

children.text: dravyaṃ yathā syāt kaṭukaṃ rasena tac copayuktaṃ madhuraṃ vipāke /
children.translated_text: Just as a substance may be pungent in taste yet, when consumed, sweet in its final effect,

children.text: tathaiva vīryaṃ kaṭukaṃ śrameṇa tasyārthasiddhyai madhuro vipākaḥ // Saund_16.93 //
children.translated_text: So too is effort pungent through exertion, but for the accomplishment of its purpose, sweet is its final effect. // Saund 16.93 //

children.text: vīryaṃ paraṃ kāryakṛtau hi mūlaṃ vīryād ṛte kā cana nāsti siddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Supreme effort is indeed the root in the accomplishment of any task; without effort, there is no achievement whatsoever;

children.text: udeti vīryād iha sarvasaṃpan nirvīryatā cet sakalaś ca pāpmā // Saund_16.94 //
children.translated_text: From effort arises all prosperity in this world; and from lack of effort, all evil. // Saund 16.94 //

children.text: alabdhasyālābho niyatam upalabdhasya vigamas
children.translated_text: Non-attainment of what has not been attained, and the loss of what has been attained —

children.text: tathaivātmāvajñā kṛpañam adhikebhyaḥ paribhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Likewise, self-contempt, humiliation from superiors, pitiable state,

children.text: tamo nistejastvaṃ śrutiniyamatuṣṭivyuparamo
children.translated_text: darkness, loss of vigor, cessation of the satisfaction of hearing and discipline —

children.text: nṛṇāṃ nirvīryāṇāṃ bhavati vinipātaś ca bhavati // Saund_16.95 //
children.translated_text: all this befalls powerless men, and downfall too befalls them. (16.95)

children.text: nayaṃ śrutvā śakto yad ayam abhivṛddhiṃ na labhate
children.translated_text: That one who, having heard the doctrine, is unable to gain progress,

children.text: paraṃ dharmaṃ jñātvā yad upari nivāsaṃ na labhate /
children.translated_text: that one who, having known the supreme <s>Dharma</s>, does not attain the higher abode,

children.text: gṛhaṃ tyaktvā muktau yad ayam upaśāntiṃ na labhate
children.translated_text: that one who, having renounced the household, does not attain tranquility in liberation —

children.text: nimittaṃ kausīdyaṃ bhavati puruṣasyātra na ripuḥ // Saund_16.96 //
children.translated_text: the cause is laziness, not an enemy, for a man in this world. (16.96)

children.text: anikṣiptotsāho yadi khanati gāṃ vāri labhate
children.translated_text: If one digs the earth with unflagging effort, one obtains water;

children.text: prasaktaṃ vyāmathnan jvalanam araṇibhyāṃ janayati /
children.translated_text: by persistently churning, one generates fire from the fire-sticks;

children.text: prayuktā yoge tu dhruvam upalabhante śramaphalaṃ
children.translated_text: those yoked to <s>yoga</s> assuredly obtain the fruit of their exertion —

children.text: drutaṃ nityaṃ yānto girim api hi bhindanti saritaḥ // Saund_16.97 //
children.translated_text: rivers, flowing swiftly and constantly, even split mountains. (16.97)

children.text: kṛṣṭvā gāṃ paripālya ca śramaśatair aśnoti sasyaśāriyaṃ
children.translated_text: By plowing the earth and tending it through hundreds of labors, one enjoys the wealth of grain;

children.text: yatnena pravigāhya sāgarajalaṃ ratnaśriyā krīḍati /
children.translated_text: by plunging with effort into the ocean waters, one plays with the splendor of jewels;

children.text: śatrūṇām avadhūya vīryam iṣubhir bhuṅkte narendraśriyaṃ
children.translated_text: by shaking off the valor of enemies with arrows, one enjoys the splendor of a king —

children.text: tad vīryaṃ kuru śāntaye viniyataṃ vīrye hi sarvardddhayaḥ // Saund_16.98 //
children.translated_text: therefore exert your vigor, directed toward peace, for in vigor lie all attainments. (16.98)

body.text: Saundarananade mahākāvya āryasatyavyākhyāno nāma ṣoḍaśaḥ sargaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the sixteenth canto of the <s>Saundarananda</s> <s>mahākāvya</s>, named 'The Exposition of the Noble Truths.'
CANTO XVII

children.text: athaivam ādesitatattvamārgo nandas tadā prāptavimokṣamārgaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Nanda</s>, having been shown the path of truth in this way, having attained the path to liberation,

children.text: sarveṇa bhāvena gurau praṇamya kleśaprahāṇāya vanaṃ jagāma // Saund_17.1 //
children.translated_text: bowing to the Guru with his whole being, went to the forest for the abandonment of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). (17.1)

children.text: tatrāvakāśaṃ mṛdunīlaśaṣpaṃ dadarśa sāntaṃ taruṣaṇḍavantam /
children.translated_text: There he saw a secluded spot with soft blue grass, possessing clusters of trees,

children.text: niḥśabdayā nimnagayopagūḍhaṃ vaiḍūryanīlodakayā vahantyā // Saund_17.2 //
children.translated_text: embraced by a silent stream flowing with waters blue as <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl). (17.2)

children.text: sa pādayos tatra vidhāya śaucaṃ śucau śive śrīmati vṛkṣamūle /
children.translated_text: Having performed the purification of his feet there, at a beautiful, auspicious, glorious tree-root,

children.text: mokṣāya baddhvā vyavasāyakaṣāṃ paryaṅkam aṅkāvahitam babandha // Saund_17.3 //
children.translated_text: fastening the girdle of resolution for liberation, he bound his legs in the cross-legged posture. (17.3)

children.text: ṛjuṃ samagraṃ praṇidhāya kāyaṃ kāve smṛtiṃ cābhimukhīṃ vidhāya /
children.translated_text: Setting his body upright and complete, directing mindfulness inward toward the object,

children.text: sarvendriyāṇy ātmani saṃnidhāya sa tatra yogaṃ pryataḥ prapede // Saund_17.4 //
children.translated_text: withdrawing all the senses into the self, he there earnestly entered into <s>yoga</s>. (17.4)

children.text: tataḥ sa tattvaṃ nikhilaṃ cikīṣur mokṣānukūlāṃś ca vidhīṃś cikīrṣan /
children.translated_text: Then he, desiring to know the truth in its entirety, and wishing to practice the methods favorable to liberation,

children.text: jñānena lokyena śamena caiva cacāra cetaḥparikarmabhūmau // Saund_17.5 //
children.translated_text: traversed the ground of mental purification with worldly knowledge and with tranquility. (17.5)

children.text: saṃdhāya dhairyaṃ praṇidhāya vīryaṃ vyapohya saktiṃ parigṛhya śaktim /
children.translated_text: Summoning firmness, directing vigor, repelling attachment, grasping [true] power,

children.text: praśāntacetā niyamasthacetāḥ svasthas tato 'bhūd viṣayeṣv anāsthaḥ // Saund_17.6 //
children.translated_text: with mind at peace, with thoughts established in discipline, he became self-possessed, indifferent to sense objects. (17.6)

children.text: ātaptabuddheḥ prahitātmano 'pi svabhyastabhāvād atha kāmasaṃjñā /
children.translated_text: Then, even though his intellect was heated [with effort] and his self was directed [to the goal], the perception of desire (<s>kāmasaṃjñā</s>),

children.text: paryākulaṃ tasya manaś cakāra prāvṛṭsu vidyuj alam āgateva // Saund_17.7 //
children.translated_text: due to its habitual nature, threw his mind into confusion — like lightning arriving suddenly in the rainy season. (17.7)

children.text: sa paryavasthānam avetya sadyaś cikṣepa tāṃ dharmavighātgakartrīm /
children.translated_text: Recognizing that obstruction at once, he cast away that destroyer of <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: priyām api krodhapāritacetā nārīm ivodvṛttaguṇāṃ manasvī // Saund_17.8 //
children.translated_text: as a man of spirit, whose mind is stirred to anger, casts off a beloved woman whose virtues have gone astray. (17.8)

children.text: ārabdhavīryasya manaḥśamāya bhūyas tu tasyākuśalo vitarkaḥ /
children.translated_text: But for him who had begun to exert vigor for the calming of the mind, an unwholesome thought-pattern (<s>vitarka</s>)

children.text: vyādhipraṇāśāya niviṣṭabuddher upadravo ghora ivājagāma // Saund_17.9 //
children.translated_text: arose again — like a terrible complication befalling one whose mind was set on destroying a disease. (17.9)

children.text: sa tadvighātāya nimittam anyad yogānukūlaṃ kuśalaṃ prapede /
children.translated_text: For the destruction of that [obstruction], he resorted to another wholesome object favorable to <s>yoga</s>,

children.text: ārtāyanaṃ skṣīṇabalo balsthaṃ nirasyamāno balināriṇeva // Saund_17.10 //
children.translated_text: as one whose strength is diminished, being repelled by a powerful enemy, takes refuge with a strong ally. (17.10)

children.text: puraṃ vidhāyānuvidhāya daṇḍaṃ mitrāṇi saṃgṛhya ripūn vighṛhya /
children.translated_text: Just as a king, having fortified a city, having organized the army, having gathered allies and repelled enemies,

children.text: rājā yathāpnoti hi gām apūrvāṃ nītir mukukṣor api saiva yoge // Saund_17.11 //
children.translated_text: obtains new territory — that very same strategy applies to one who seeks liberation in <s>yoga</s>. (17.11)

children.text: vimokṣakāmasya hi yogino 'pi manaḥ puraṃ jṇānavidhiś ca daṇḍaḥ /
children.translated_text: For a <s>yogin</s> who desires liberation, the mind is the city, the method of knowledge is the army,

children.text: guṇāś ca mitrāṇy arayaś ca doṣā bhūmir vimuktir yatate yadartham // Saund_17.12 //
children.translated_text: virtues are allies and faults are enemies; liberation is the territory for which one strives. (17.12)

children.text: sa duḥkhajālān mahato mukukṣur vimokṣamārgādhigame vivikṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: He, desiring release from the great net of suffering, eager to attain the path to liberation,

children.text: panthānam āryaṃ paramaṃ didṛkṣuḥ śamaṃ yayau kiṃ cid upāttacakṣuḥ // Saund_17.13 //
children.translated_text: wishing to see the supreme noble path, attained some tranquility with partially opened eyes [of wisdom]. (17.13)

children.text: yaḥ syān niketas tamaso 'niketaḥ śrutvāpi tattvaṃ sa bhavet pramattaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who would be a dwelling-place of darkness, though dwelling-less, having heard the truth, would become heedless;

children.text: yasmāt tu mokṣāya sa pātrabhūtas tasmān manaḥ svātmani saṃjahāra // Saund_17.14 //
children.translated_text: but since he was a worthy vessel for liberation, therefore he withdrew the mind into his own self. (17.14)

children.text: saṃbhārataḥ pratyayataḥ svabhāvād āsvādato doṣaviśeṣataś ca /
children.translated_text: In terms of their constituents, their causes, their intrinsic nature, their savor, their particular faults,

children.text: athātmavān niḥsaraṇātmataś ca dharmeṣu cakre vidhivat parīkṣām // Saund_17.15 //
children.translated_text: and their means of escape — that self-possessed one conducted a proper examination of the <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena). (17.15)

children.text: sa rūpiṇaṃ kṛtsnam arūpiṇaṃ ca sāraṃ didṛkṣur vicikāya kāyam /
children.translated_text: He, wishing to see the essence, analyzed the body — both what has form and what is formless;

children.text: athāśuciṃ duḥkham anityam asvaṃ nirātmakaṃ caiva cikāya kāyam // Saund_17.16 //
children.translated_text: then he discerned the body as impure, suffering, impermanent, without ownership, and without self. (17.16)

children.text: anityatas tatra hi śūnyataś ca nirātmato duḥkhata eva cāpi /
children.translated_text: For therein, by the worldly path of entry upon the way, [contemplating] impermanence, emptiness,

children.text: mārgapravekeṇa sa laukikena kleśadrumaṃ saṃcalayāṃ cakāra // Saund_17.17 //
children.translated_text: selflessness, and suffering — he caused the tree of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) to shake. (17.17)

children.text: yasmād abhūtvā bhavatīha sarvaṃ bhūtvā ca bhūyo na bhavaty avaśyam /
children.translated_text: Since everything in this world, having not been, comes into being, and having been, inevitably ceases to be,

children.text: sahekutaṃ ca kṣayihetumac ca tasmād anityaṃ jagad ity avindat // Saund_17.18 //
children.translated_text: and since it arises with a cause and is subject to a cause of destruction — therefore he realized: 'The world is impermanent.' (17.18)

children.text: yataḥ prasūtasya ca karmayogaḥ prasajyate bandhavighātahetuḥ /
children.translated_text: Since for one who is born, the connection with <s>karma</s> ensues, which is the cause of bondage and its destruction,

children.text: duḥkhapratīkāravidhau sukhākhye tato bhavaṃ duḥkham iti vyapaśyat // Saund_17.19 //
children.translated_text: and since what is called 'happiness' is [really] a remedy for suffering — therefore he saw: 'Existence is suffering.' (17.19)

children.text: yataś ca saṃskarāgataṃ viviktaṃ na kārakaḥ kaś cana vedako vā /
children.translated_text: Since what has come into being through <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) is devoid [of self], and there is no agent or experiencer whatsoever,

children.text: sāmagryathaḥ saṃbhavati pravṛttiḥ śūnyaṃ tato lokam imaṃ dadarśa // Saund_17.20 //
children.translated_text: and since activity arises from the assemblage [of conditions] — therefore he saw this world as empty. (17.20)

children.text: yasmān nirīhaṃ jagad asvatantraṃ naiśvaryam ekaḥ kurute kriyāsu /
children.translated_text: Since the world is without will, not self-directed, and no single being exercises sovereignty over actions,

children.text: tat tat pratītya prabhavanti bhāvā nirātmakaṃ tena viveda lokam // Saund_17.21 //
children.translated_text: and since things arise in dependence on this and that — thereby he understood the world as selfless. (17.21)

children.text: tataḥ sa vātaṃ vyajanād ivoṣṇe kāṣṭhāśritaṃ nirmathanād ivāgnim /
children.translated_text: Then he — like [one obtaining] a breeze from a fan in the heat, like [one obtaining] fire lodged in wood through churning,

children.text: antaḥkṣitisthaṃ khananād ivāmbho lokattaraṃ vartima durāpam āpa // Saund_17.22 //
children.translated_text: like [one obtaining] water hidden within the earth through digging — attained the supramundane path, difficult to attain. (17.22)

children.text: sajjñānacāpaḥ smṛtivarma baddhvā viśuddhaśīlavratavāhanasthaḥ /
children.translated_text: With the bow of right knowledge strung, having bound the armor of mindfulness, mounted on the vehicle of pure conduct and moral observances,

children.text: kleśāribhiś cittaraṇājirasthaiḥ sārdhaṃ yuyustsur vijayāya tasthau // Saund_17.23 //
children.translated_text: he stood ready to fight for victory against the enemies, the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), stationed on the battlefield of the mind. (17.23)

children.text: tataḥ sa bodhyaṅgaśitāttaśastraḥ samyakpradhānottamavāhanasthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, with sharp weapons whetted by the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), mounted on the supreme vehicle of right exertion (<s>samyakpradhāna</s>),

children.text: mārgāṅgamātaṅgavatā balena śanaiḥ śanaiḥ kleśacumūṃ jagāhe // Saund_17.24 //
children.translated_text: with the force of an elephant of the path-factors, he gradually entered the army of the <s>kleśas</s>. (17.24)

children.text: sa smṛtyupasthānamayaiḥ pṛṣatkaiḥ śatrūn viparyāsamayān kṣaṇena /
children.translated_text: With the arrows of the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), in an instant, the enemies consisting of the perversions (<s>viparyāsa</s>),

children.text: duḥkhasya hetūṃś caturaś caturbhiḥ svaiḥ svaiḥ pracārāyatanair dadāra // Saund_17.25 //
children.translated_text: the four causes of suffering — he pierced them with four [arrows], each in its own proper sphere. (17.25)

children.text: āryair balaiḥ pañcabhir eva pañca cetaḥkhilāny apratimair babhañja /
children.translated_text: With the five noble powers (<s>bala</s>), he shattered the five hardened clots of the mind, unmatched [in force];

children.text: mithyāñganāgāṃś ca tathāṅganāgair vinirdudhāvāṣṭabhir eva so 'ṣṭau // Saund_17.26 //
children.translated_text: and with eight noble elephants [of the Eightfold Path], he drove out the eight false elephants [of wrong views]. (17.26)

children.text: athātmadṛṣṭiṃ sakalāṃ vidhūya caturṣu satyeṣv akathaṃ kathaḥ san /
children.translated_text: Then, having completely demolished the view of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>), being without doubt regarding the Four Truths,

children.text: viśuddhaśīlavratadṛṣṭadharmā dharmasya pūrvāṃ phalabhūmim āpa // Saund_17.27 //
children.translated_text: with purified conduct, observances, and vision of <s>Dharma</s>, he attained the first fruit-stage of the <s>Dharma</s>. (17.27)

children.text: sa darśanād āryacatuṣṭayasya kleśaikadeśasya ca viprayogāt /
children.translated_text: Through the vision of the noble fourfold [truths], and through separation from a portion of the <s>kleśas</s>,

children.text: pratyātmikāc cāpi viśeṣalābhāt pratyakṣato jñānisukhasya caiva // Saund_17.28 //
children.translated_text: and through the personal attainment of distinction, and through direct perception of the bliss of knowledge — (17.28)

children.text: dārḍhyāt prasādasya dhṛteḥ sthiratvāt satyeṣv asaṃmūḍhatayā caturṣu /
children.translated_text: through the firmness of faith, the stability of resolve, through freedom from confusion regarding the Four Truths,

children.text: śīlasya cācchidratayottamasya niḥsaṃśayo dharmavidhau babhūva // Saund_17.29 //
children.translated_text: and through the flawlessness of his supreme moral conduct — he became free from doubt regarding the method of <s>Dharma</s>. (17.29)

children.text: kudṛṣṭijālena sa viprayukto lokaṃ tathābhūtam avekṣamāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Freed from the net of wrong views, seeing the world as it truly is,

children.text: jñānāśrayāṃ prītim upājagāma bhūyaḥ prasādaṃ ca gurāv iyāya // Saund_17.30 //
children.translated_text: he attained a joy rooted in knowledge, and developed even greater faith in the Guru. (17.30)

children.text: yo hi pravṛttiṃ niyatām avaiti naivānyahetor iha nāpy ahetoḥ /
children.translated_text: For one who understands that arising is determined, not from another cause nor without cause,

children.text: pratītya tat tat samavaiti tat tat sa naiṣṭhikaṃ paśyati yaś ca dharmam /
children.translated_text: and who comprehends each thing in dependence on each [condition] — he sees the <s>Dharma</s> in its finality,

children.text: tasyopadeṣṭāram athāryavaryaṃ sa prekṣate buddham avāptacakṣuṅ // Saund_17.32 //
children.translated_text: and then he beholds the <s>Buddha</s>, the supreme among the noble ones, as his teacher, with eyes [of wisdom] attained. (17.32)

children.text: yathopadeśena śivena mukto rogād arogo bhiṣajaṃ kṛtajñaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as one freed from disease by auspicious treatment, healthy, grateful to the physician,

children.text: anusmaran paśyati cittadṛṣṭyā maitryā ca śāstrajñatayā ca tuṣṭaḥ // Saund_17.33 //
children.translated_text: remembers and sees him with the eye of the mind, pleased both by his friendliness and by his knowledge of the healing art — (17.33)

children.text: āryeṇa mārgeṇa tathaiva muktas tathāgataṃ tattvavid āryatattvaḥ /
children.translated_text: so too, freed by the Noble Path, the knower of truth, noble in truth,

children.text: anusmaran paśyati kāyasākṣī maitryā ca sarvajñatayā ca tuṣṭaḥ // Saund_17.34 //
children.translated_text: remembers and sees the <s>Tathāgata</s> as a bodily witness, pleased both by his friendliness and by his omniscience. (17.34)

children.text: sa nāśakair dṛṣṭigatair vimuktaḥ paryantam ālokya punarbhavasya /
children.translated_text: Freed from destructive views, having seen the limit of rebirth,

children.text: bhaktvā ghṛṇāṃ kleśavijṛmbhiteṣu mṛtyor na tatrāsa na durgatibhyaḥ // Saund_17.35 //
children.translated_text: feeling revulsion toward the outbursts of the <s>kleśas</s>, he feared neither death nor the lower realms. (17.35)

children.text: tvaksnāyumedorduhirāsthimāṃsakeśādināmedhyagaṇena pūrṇam /
children.translated_text: Filled with the impure collection of skin, sinews, fat, blood, bones, flesh, hair, and the like —

children.text: tataḥ sa kāyaṃ samavekṣamāṇaḥ sāraṃ vicintyāṇv api nopalebhe // Saund_17.36 //
children.translated_text: then, examining the body, he did not find even a particle of essence. (17.36)

children.text: sa kāmarāgapratighau sthirātmā tenaiva yogena tanū cakāra /
children.translated_text: He, steady of self, attenuated desire-passion and aversion through that very <s>yoga</s>;

children.text: kṛtvā mahoraskatanus tanū tau prāpa dvitīyaṃ phalam āryadharme // Saund_17.37 //
children.translated_text: having made those two thin — like a great serpent shedding its skin — he attained the second fruit of the noble <s>Dharma</s>. (17.37)

children.text: sa lobhacāpaṃ parikalpabāṇaṃ rāgaṃ mahāvairiṇam alpaśeṣam /
children.translated_text: That great enemy, desire (<s>rāga</s>), with its bow of greed and arrows of fantasy, [now] with little remainder,

children.text: kāyasvabhāvādhigatair bibheda yogāyudhāstrair aśubhāpṛṣatkaiḥ // Saund_17.38 //
children.translated_text: he shattered with the weapons and arrows of <s>yoga</s>, gained through [contemplation of] the true nature of the body. (17.38)

children.text: dveṣāyudhaṃ krodhavikīrṇabāṇaṃ vyāpādam antaḥprasavaṃ sapatnam /
children.translated_text: Ill-will (<s>vyāpāda</s>), that internal enemy, armed with hatred, scattering arrows of anger,

children.text: maitrīpṛṣatkair dhṛtitūṇasaṃsthaiḥ kṣamādhanurjyāvisṛtair jaghāna // Saund_17.39 //
children.translated_text: he slew with the arrows of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), placed in the quiver of steadfastness, released from the bowstring of patience (<s>kṣamā</s>). (17.39)

children.text: mūlāny atha trīṇy āsudhasya vīras tribhir vimokṣāyatanaiś cakarta /
children.translated_text: Then the hero cut the three roots of evil with the three gateways to liberation,

children.text: camūmukhasthān dhṛtakārmukāṃs trīn arīn ivāris tribhir āyasāgraiḥ // Saund_17.40 //
children.translated_text: as a warrior [cuts down] three bow-bearing enemies at the front of the army with three iron-tipped [arrows]. (17.40)

children.text: sa kāmadhātoḥ samtikramāya pārṣṇigrahāṃs tān abhibhūya śatrūn /
children.translated_text: Having transcended the realm of desire (<s>kāmadhātu</s>), having overcome those rear-guard enemies,

children.text: yogād anāgāmiphalaṃ prapadya dvārīva nirvāñapurasya tasthau // Saund_17.41 //
children.translated_text: and attaining through <s>yoga</s> the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>), he stood as if at the gate of the city of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. (17.41)

children.text: kāmair vikitaṃ malinaiś ca dharmair vitarkavac cāpi vicāravac ca /
children.translated_text: Free from desires and from impure <s>dharmas</s>, still possessed of thought-application (<s>vitarka</s>) and sustained thought (<s>vicāra</s>),

children.text: vivekajaṃ prītisukhopapannaṃ dhyānaṃ tataḥ sa prathamaṃ prapede // Saund_17.42 //
children.translated_text: born of seclusion, endowed with joy and happiness — he then attained the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). (17.42)
