children.text: kāmāgnidhāhena sa vipramukto hlādaṃ paraṃ dhyānasukhād avāpa /
children.translated_text: Released from the burning of the fire of desire, he experienced supreme delight from the happiness of <s>dhyāna</s>,

children.text: sukhaṃ vigāhyāpsv iva gharmakhinnaḥ prāpyeva cārthaṃ cipulaṃ daridraḥ // Saund_17.43 //
children.translated_text: as one tormented by heat [experiences delight] upon plunging into cool waters, or as a poor man upon obtaining great wealth. (17.43)

children.text: tatrāpi taddharmagatān vitarkān guṇāguṇe ca prasṛtān vicārān /
children.translated_text: But even therein, the thought-applications pertaining to those <s>dharmas</s>, and the sustained reflections spreading toward merit and demerit,

children.text: buddhvā manaḥkṣobhakarān aśāntāṃs tadviprayogāya matiṃ cakāra // Saund_17.44 //
children.translated_text: knowing them to be disturbers of the mind and not peaceful, he set his intention toward their abandonment. (17.44)

children.text: kṣobhaṃ prakurvanti yathormayo hi dhīraprasannāmbuvahasya sindhoḥ /
children.translated_text: For just as waves disturb a calm, clear-watered river,

children.text: ekāgrabhūtasya tahtormibhūtāś cittāmbhasaḥ kṣobhakarā vitarkāḥ // Saund_17.45 //
children.translated_text: so thought-applications (<s>vitarka</s>), like waves, are disturbers of the mind-water that has become one-pointed. (17.45)

children.text: khinnasya suptasya ca nirvṛtasya bādhaṃ yathā saṃjanayanti śabdāḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as sounds cause disturbance to one who is weary, asleep, and at rest,

children.text: adhyātmam aikāgryam upāgatasya bhavanti bādhāya tathā vitarkāḥ // Saund_17.46 //
children.translated_text: so thought-applications become a hindrance to one who has attained inner one-pointedness. (17.46)

children.text: athāvitarkaṃ kramaśo 'vicāram ekāgrabhāvān manasaḥ prasannam /
children.translated_text: Then, gradually without thought-application, without sustained thought, with the mind clear from one-pointedness,

children.text: samādhijaṃ prītsukhaṃ dvitīyaṃ dhyānaṃ tad ādhyātmaśivaṃ sa dadhyau // Saund_17.47 //
children.translated_text: he meditated on the second <s>dhyāna</s>, born of concentration, possessed of joy and happiness, inwardly serene. (17.47)

children.text: tad dhyānam āgamya ca cittamaunaṃ lebhe parāṃ prītim alabdhapūrvām /
children.translated_text: And having attained that <s>dhyāna</s> and the silence of mind, he obtained supreme joy never before obtained;

children.text: prītau tu tatrāpi sa doṣadarśī yathā vitarkeṣv abhavat tathaiva // Saund_17.48 //
children.translated_text: but even in that joy, he saw faults, just as he had in the thought-applications. (17.48)

children.text: prītiḥ parā vastuni yatra yasya viparyayāt tasya hi tara duḥkham /
children.translated_text: For wherever one has supreme delight in any object, from its reversal comes suffering for that person;

children.text: prītāv ataḥ prekṣya sa tatra doṣān prītikṣaye yogam upāruroha // Saund_17.49 //
children.translated_text: therefore, seeing faults in delight there, he ascended to the <s>yoga</s> of the waning of delight. (17.49)

children.text: prītedr virāgāt sukham āryajuṣṭaṃ kāyena vindann atha saṃprajānan /
children.translated_text: Then, through dispassion toward delight, experiencing the happiness enjoyed by the noble ones through the body, fully conscious,

children.text: upekṣakaḥ sa smṛtimān vyahārṣīd dhyānaṃ tṛtīyaṃ pratilabhya dhīraḥ // Saund_17.50 //
children.translated_text: equanimous, mindful, he rejoiced — the steadfast one, having attained the third <s>dhyāna</s>. (17.50)

children.text: yasmāt paraṃ tatra sukhaṃ sukhebhyas tataḥ paraṃ nāsti sukhapravṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: Since the pleasure therein is supreme among pleasures and beyond it there is no further engagement in pleasure,

children.text: tasmād babhāṣe śubhakṛtsnabhūmiṃ parāparajñaḥ parameti maitryā // Saund_17.51 //
children.translated_text: therefore the knower of higher and lower declared the <s>śubhakṛtsna</s> ("all-pervading purity") stage to be the highest, through <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness). (17.51)

children.text: dhyāne 'pi tatrātha dadarśa doṣaṃ mene paraṃ śāntam aniñjam eva /
children.translated_text: Then, even in that <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), he perceived a fault and considered the supreme [state] to be tranquil and unmoving alone;

children.text: ābhogato 'pīñjayati sma tasya cittaṃ pravṛttaṃ sukham ity ajasram // Saund_17.52 //
children.translated_text: for even through [subtle] mental engagement, the pleasure that had arisen constantly agitated his mind. (17.52)

children.text: yatreñjitaṃ spanditam asti tatra yatrāsti ca spanditam asti duḥkham /
children.translated_text: Where there is agitation, there is fluctuation; and where there is fluctuation, there is suffering;

children.text: yasmād atas tat sukham iñjakatvāt praśāntikāmā yatayas tyajanti // Saund_17.53 //
children.translated_text: therefore, since that [pleasure] involves agitation, ascetics who desire tranquility abandon it. (17.53)

children.text: atha prahāṇāt sukhaduḥkhayoś ca manovikārasya ca pūrvam eva /
children.translated_text: Then, through the prior abandonment of both pleasure and pain and of mental disturbance,

children.text: dadhyāv upekṣāmṛtimad viśuddhaṃ dhyānaṃ tathāduḥkhasukhaṃ caturtham // Saund_17.54 //
children.translated_text: he meditated upon the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> — pure, possessing equanimity and mindfulness, free from both suffering and pleasure. (17.54)

children.text: yasmāt tu tasmin na sukhaṃ na duḥkhaṃ jñānaṃ ca tatrāsti tad arthacāri /
children.translated_text: Since therein there is neither pleasure nor pain, and there is knowledge that operates purposefully,

children.text: tasmād upekṣāsmṛtipāriśuddhir nirucyate dhyānavidhau caturthe // Saund_17.55 //
children.translated_text: therefore in the method of <s>dhyāna</s>, the fourth is declared to be the purity of equanimity and mindfulness. (17.55)

children.text: dhyānaṃ sa niśritya tataś caturtham arhattvalābhāya matiṃ cakāra /
children.translated_text: Then, relying on the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, he set his mind toward the attainment of <s>arhatva</s> (arhatship),

children.text: saṃdhāya maitraṃ balavantam āryaṃ rājeva deśān ajitān jigīṣuḥ // Saund_17.56 //
children.translated_text: having marshaled the powerful, noble force of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), like a king intent on conquering unconquered territories. (17.56)

children.text: ciccheda kārtsnyena tataḥ sa pañca prajñāsinā bhāvanayeritena /
children.translated_text: Then, with the sword of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) set in motion by <s>bhāvanā</s> (meditation), he completely severed the five

children.text: ūrdhvaṅgamāny uttamabandhanāni saṃyojanāny uttamabandhanāni // Saund_17.57 //
children.translated_text: upper fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>), the supreme bonds that lead upward. (17.57)

children.text: bodhyaṅganāgair api saptabhiḥ sa saptaiva cittānuśayān mamarda /
children.translated_text: With the seven elephants of the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), he crushed the seven latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>) of the mind,

children.text: dvīpān ivopasthitavipraṇāśān kālo grahaiḥ saptabhir eva sapta // Saund_17.58 //
children.translated_text: as <s>Kāla</s> (Time/Death) [destroys] seven islands on the verge of destruction with [its] seven planets. (17.58)

children.text: agnidrumājyāmbuṣu yā hi vṛttiḥ kavandhavāvyagnidivākarāṇām /
children.translated_text: For just as a headless torso, wind, fire, and the sun have their respective functions upon fire-wood, ghee, and water —

children.text: doṣeṣu tāṃ vṛttim iyāya nando nirvāpaṇotpāṭanadāhaśoṣaiḥ // Saund_17.59 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s> exercised that same function upon the defilements: extinguishing, uprooting, burning, and desiccating them. (17.59)

children.text: iti trivegaṃ trijhaṣaṃ trivīcam ekāmbhasaṃ pañcarayaṃ dvikūlam /
children.translated_text: Thus, the ocean of suffering — with three currents, three aquatic creatures, three waves,

children.text: dvigrāham aṣṭāṅgavatā plavena duḥkhārṇavaṃ custaram uttatāra // Saund_17.60 //
children.translated_text: one body of water, five streams, two banks, and two crocodiles — he crossed by the vessel endowed with the eightfold [path], so difficult to cross. (17.60)

children.text: arhattvam āsādya sa satkriyārho nirutsuko niṣpraṇayo nirāśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having attained <s>arhatva</s> (arhatship), worthy of honor, free from agitation, free from affection, free from expectation,

children.text: vibhīr viṣug vītamado virāgaḥ sa eva dhṛtyānya ivābabhāse // Saund_17.61 //
children.translated_text: fearless, free from affliction, free from pride, free from passion — he, though the same person, appeared like another through his composure. (17.61)

children.text: bhrātuś ca śāstuś ca tayānuśiṣṭyā nandas tataḥ svena ca vikrameṇa /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Nanda</s>, through the instruction of both his brother and his teacher, and by his own effort,

children.text: praśāntacetāḥ paripūrṇakāryo vāṇīm imām ātmagatāṃ jagāda // Saund_17.62 //
children.translated_text: with tranquil mind, his purpose fully accomplished, uttered these words to himself: (17.62)

children.text: namo 'stu tasmai sugatāya yena hitaiṣiṇā me karuṇatmakena /
children.translated_text: "Homage to that <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), by whom, benevolent and compassionate toward me,

children.text: bahūni duḥkhāny apavartitāni sukhāni bhūyāṃsy upasaṃhṛtāni // Saund_17.63 //
children.translated_text: many sufferings have been removed and abundant joys have been bestowed. (17.63)

children.text: ahaṃ hy anāryeṇa śarīrajena duḥkhātmake vartmani kṛṣyamāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: For I, being dragged along the path of suffering born from the body, by ignoble [impulses],

children.text: nivartitas tadvacanāṅkuṣena darpānvito nāga ivāṅkuśena // Saund_17.64 //
children.translated_text: was turned back by the goad of his words, like a maddened elephant by a goad. (17.64)

children.text: tasyājñayā kāruṇikasya śāstur hṛdistham utpāṭya hi rāgaśalyam /
children.translated_text: By the command of that compassionate teacher, having uprooted the thorn of passion lodged in my heart,

children.text: adyaiva tāvat sumahat sukhaṃ me sarvakṣaye kiṃ bata nirvṛtasya // Saund_17.65 //
children.translated_text: even now I have attained supremely great happiness — what then when all [defilements] are destroyed and I am at peace? (17.65)

children.text: nirvāpya kāmāgnim ahaṃ hi dīptaṃ dhṛtyambunā pāvakam ambuneva /
children.translated_text: For having extinguished the blazing fire of desire with the water of fortitude, as [one extinguishes] a fire with water,

children.text: hlādaṃ paraṃ sāṃpratam āgato 'smi śītaṃ hradaṃ gharma ivāvatīrṇaḥ // Saund_17.66 //
children.translated_text: I have now attained supreme delight, like one who has descended into a cool lake in the heat. (17.66)

children.text: na me priyaṃ kiṃ cana nāpriyaṃ me na me 'nurodho 'sti kuto virodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Nothing is dear to me and nothing is hateful; I have no attachment, whence then aversion?

children.text: tayor abhāvāt sukhito 'smi sadyo himātapābhyām iva vipramuktaḥ // Saund_17.67 //
children.translated_text: Through the absence of both, I am at once happy, as if freed from both cold and heat. (17.67)

children.text: mahābhayāt kṣemam ivopalabhya mahāvarodhād iva vipramokṣam /
children.translated_text: As if having found safety from great danger, as if gaining freedom from a great imprisonment,

children.text: mahārṇavāt pāram ivāplavaḥ san bhīmāndhakārād iva ca prakāśam // Saund_17.68 //
children.translated_text: as if one without a raft having reached the far shore of a great ocean, and as if [finding] light from a terrible darkness — (17.68)

children.text: rogād ivārogyam asahyarūpād ṛṇād ivānṛṇyam anantasaṃkhyāt /
children.translated_text: as if [gaining] health from an unbearable disease, as if [gaining] freedom from debt of immeasurable amount,

children.text: dviṣatsakāśad iva cāpayānaṃ durchikṣayogāc ca yathā subhikṣam // Saund_17.69 //
children.translated_text: as if [gaining] departure from the presence of enemies, and as if abundance after enduring famine — (17.69)

children.text: tadvat parāṃ śāntim upāgato 'haṃ yasyānubhāvena vināyakasya /
children.translated_text: just so have I attained supreme peace, through the power of that guide;

children.text: karomi bḥūyaḥ punar uktam asmai namo namo 'rhāya tathāgatāya // Saund_17.70 //
children.translated_text: therefore I pay homage to him again and yet again: homage, homage to the <s>Arhat</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>!" (17.70)

children.text: yenāhaṃ girim upanīya rukmaśṛṅgaṃ svargaṃ ca plavagavadhūnidarśanena /
children.translated_text: "He who, having led me to the gold-peaked mountain and to heaven through the sight of the monkey-maidens,

children.text: kāmātmā tridivacarībhir aṅganābhir niṣkṛṣṭo yuvatimaye kalau nimagnaḥ // Saund_17.71 //
children.translated_text: drew me — desire-natured as I was, sunk in the evil [snare] of young women — out [of it] by means of the celestial <s>apsaras</s> women. (17.71)

children.text: tasmāc ca vyasanaparād anarthapaṅkād utkṛṣya kramaśithilaḥ karīva paṅkāt /
children.translated_text: And from that calamity-prone, harmful mire, he drew me out, step by step, like an elephant from mud,

children.text: śānte 'smin virajasi vijvare viśoke saddharme vitamasi naiṣṭhike vimuktaḥ // Saund_17.72 //
children.translated_text: and released me into this peaceful, dustless, fever-free, grief-free, darkness-free, ultimate true <s>dharma</s>. (17.72)

children.text: taṃ vande param anukampakaṃ maharṣiṃ mūrdhnāhaṃ prakṛtiguṇajñam āśayajñam /
children.translated_text: I bow with my head to that supremely compassionate great sage, the knower of innate dispositions and intentions,

children.text: saṃbuddhaṃ daśabalinaṃ bhiṣakpradhānaṃ trātāraṃ punar api cāsmi saṃnatas tam // Saund_17.73 //
children.translated_text: the awakened one, the one of ten powers, the chief of physicians, the savior — and I bow to him yet again." (17.73)

body.translated_text: Thus ends the seventeenth canto, titled "The Attainment of the Deathless," in the <s>Saundarananda</s> <s>mahākāvya</s>.
CANTO XVIII

children.text: atha dvijo bāla ivāptavedaḥ kṣipraṃ vaṇik prāpta ivāptalābhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, like a young <s>Brahmin</s> who has mastered the <s>Vedas</s>, like a merchant who has swiftly obtained his profit,

children.text: jitvā ca rājanya ivārsainyaṃ nandaḥ kṛtārtho gurum abhyagacchat // Saund_18.1 //
children.translated_text: and like a prince who has conquered the enemy army — <s>Nanda</s>, his purpose accomplished, approached the teacher. (18.1)

children.text: draṣṭuṃ sukhaṃ jñānasamāptikāle gurur hi śiṣyasya guroś ca śiṣyaḥ /
children.translated_text: For at the time of the completion of knowledge, the teacher is a joy to behold for the student, and the student for the teacher;

children.text: pariśramas te saphalo mayīti yato didṛkṣāsya munau babhūva // Saund_18.2 //
children.translated_text: "My effort has borne fruit in you" — thus arose his desire to see the sage. (18.2)

children.text: yato hi yenādhigato viśeṣas tasyottamāṅge 'rhati kartumiḍyām /
children.translated_text: For since it is through whom one has attained distinction that one deserves to pay homage at the head,

children.text: āryaḥ sarāgo 'pi kṛtajñabhāvāt prakṣīṇamānaḥ kimu vītarāgaḥ // Saund_18.3 //
children.translated_text: even a noble person with attachment does so out of gratitude — how much more one whose pride is diminished and who is free from passion? (18.3)

children.text: yasyārthakāmaprabhavā hi bhaktis tato 'sya sā tiṣṭhati rūḍhamūlā /
children.translated_text: For one whose devotion arises from worldly gain and desire, that devotion stands with shallow roots;

children.text: dharmānvayo yasya tu bhaktirāgas tasya prasādo hṛdayāvagāḍhaḥ // Saund_18.4 //
children.translated_text: but one whose devotion follows <s>dharma</s>, his reverence is deeply embedded in the heart. (18.4)

children.text: kāṣāyavāsāḥ kanakāvadātas tataḥ sa mūrdhnā gurave praṇeme /
children.translated_text: Then he, wearing ochre robes, golden in complexion, bowed to the teacher with his head,

children.text: vāteritaḥ pallavatāmrarāgaḥ puṣpojjvalaśrīr iva karṇikāraḥ // Saund_18.5 //
children.translated_text: like a <s>karṇikāra</s> tree, stirred by the wind, with its tender crimson sprouts and its glory blazing with flowers. (18.5)

children.text: athātmanaḥ śiṣyaguṇasya caiva mahāmuneḥ śāstṛguṇasya caiva /
children.translated_text: Then, in order to demonstrate both the virtues of himself as a student and the virtues of the great sage as a teacher,

children.text: saṃdarśanārthaṃ sa na mānahetoḥ svāṃ kāryasiddhiṃ kathayāṃ babhūva // Saund_18.6 //
children.translated_text: and not out of pride, he proceeded to narrate his own attainment of the goal. (18.6)

children.text: yā dṛṣṭiśalyo hṛdayāvagāḍhaḥ prabho bhṛśaṃ mām atudat sutīkṣṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: "The thorn of wrong views (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>) that was deeply embedded in my heart, O Lord, which pierced me most painfully,

children.text: tvadvākyasaṃdaṃśamukhena me sa samuddhṛtaḥ śalyahṛteva śalyaḥ // Saund_18.7 //
children.translated_text: has been extracted by the forceps of your words, as a surgeon extracts a thorn. (18.7)

children.text: kathaṅkathābhāvagato 'smi yena chinnaḥ sa niḥsaṃśaya saṃśayo me /
children.translated_text: I have arrived at the state beyond doubt, for that uncertainty of mine has been cut away without remainder;

children.text: tvacchāsanāt satpatham āgato 'smi sudeśikasyeva pathi pranaṣṭaḥ // Saund_18.8 //
children.translated_text: through your teaching I have reached the right path, like one lost on a road [who finds] an excellent guide. (18.8)

children.text: yat pītam āsvādavaśendriyeṇa darpeṇa kandarpaviṣaṃ mayāsīt /
children.translated_text: The poison of <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love) that I had drunk, with senses enslaved to relish,

children.text: tan me hataṃ tvadvacanāgadena viṣaṃ vināśīva mahāgadena // Saund_18.9 //
children.translated_text: has been destroyed by the antidote of your words, as poison [is destroyed] by a great antidote. (18.9)

children.text: kṣayaṃ gataṃ janma nirastajanman saddharmacaryām uṣito 'smi samyak /
children.translated_text: Birth has come to an end, O you who have eliminated birth; I have duly lived the life of the true <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: kṛtsnaṃ kṛtaṃ me kṛtakārya kāryaṃ lokeṣu bhūto 'smi na lokadharmā // Saund_18.10 //
children.translated_text: all that was to be done has been done by me, O accomplished one; I exist in the worlds but am not subject to worldly conditions. (18.10)

children.text: maitrīstanīṃ vyañjanacārusāsnāṃ saddharmadugdhāṃ pratibhānaśṛṅgām /
children.translated_text: Having deeply drunk from your cow — whose udder is <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), whose dewlap is beautiful with the marks [of excellence], who yields the milk of the true <s>dharma</s>, whose horns are ready speech —

children.text: tavāsmi gāṃ sādhu nipīya tṛptas tṛṣeva gām uttamavatsavarṇaḥ // Saund_18.11 //
children.translated_text: I am satisfied, like a young bull of the finest color [drinking] from a cow, when thirsty. (18.11)

children.text: yat paśyataś cādhigamo mamāyaṃ tan me samāsena mune nibodha /
children.translated_text: What I have attained while you were watching — hear that from me in brief, O sage;

children.text: sarvajña kāmaṃ viditam tavaitat svaṃ tūpacarāṃ pravivakṣur asmi // Saund_18.12 //
children.translated_text: O omniscient one, you surely know this already, yet I wish to declare my own service. (18.12)

children.text: anye 'pi santo vimumukṣavo hi śrutva vimokṣāya nayaṃ parasya /
children.translated_text: For even other virtuous ones who desire liberation, having heard the method for liberation from another,

children.text: muktasya rogād iva rogavantas tenaiva mārgeṇa sukhaṃ ghaṭānte // Saund_18.13 //
children.translated_text: like those afflicted with disease [hearing] from one cured of disease, strive happily along that very path. (18.13)

children.text: urvyādikān janmani vedmi dhātūn nātmānam urvyādiṣu teṣu kiṃ cit /
children.translated_text: I know the elements (<s>dhātu</s>) such as earth and the like in [this cycle of] birth, but I know no self whatsoever in those [elements];

children.text: yasmād atas teṣu na me 'sti saktir bahiś ca kāyena samā matir me // Saund_18.14 //
children.translated_text: since therefore I have no attachment to them, my attitude toward what is external is the same as toward the body. (18.14)

children.text: skandhāṃś ca rūpaprabhṛtīn daśārdhān paśyāmi yasmāc capalān asārān /
children.translated_text: And since I see the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) beginning with <s>rūpa</s> (form) to be unstable, insubstantial,

children.text: anātmakāṃś caiva vadhātmakāṃś ca tasmād vimukto 'smy aśivebhya ebhyaḥ // Saund_18.15 //
children.translated_text: without a self, and of a destructive nature — therefore I am freed from these inauspicious [aggregates]. (18.15)

children.text: yasmāc ca paśyāmy udayaṃ vyayaṃ ca sarvāsv avasthāsv aham indriyāṇām /
children.translated_text: And since I see the arising and passing away of the senses in all their states,

children.text: tasmād anityeṣu nirātmakeṣu duḥkheṣu me teṣv api nāsti saṃgaḥ // Saund_18.16 //
children.translated_text: therefore I have no attachment even to these, which are impermanent, without a self, and full of suffering. (18.16)

children.text: yataś ca lokaṃ samjanmaniṣṭhaṃ paśyāmi niḥsāram asac ca sarvam /
children.translated_text: And since I see the world, from birth to its final end, to be entirely insubstantial and unreal,

children.text: ato dhiyā me manasā vibaddham asmīti me neñjitam asti yena // Saund_18.17 //
children.translated_text: therefore my mind is bound by wisdom [in such a way] that I have no agitation from the [notion] "I am." (18.17)

children.text: caturvidhe naikavidhaprasaṃge yato 'ham āhāravaidhāv asaktaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since I am unattached to the fourfold method of sustenance (<s>āhāra</s>), which involves manifold engagement,

children.text: amūrchitaś cāgrathitaś ca tatra tribhyo vimukto 'smi tato bhavebhyaḥ // Saund_18.18 //
children.translated_text: and since I am without craving and without being bound therein — I am freed from the three [kinds of] becoming. (18.18)

children.text: aniśritaś cāpratibaddhacitto dṛṣṭaśutādau vyavahāradharme /
children.translated_text: And since I am without reliance and with unfettered mind regarding what is seen, heard, and so forth — the things of conventional existence —

children.text: yasmāt samātmānugataś ca tatra tasmād visaṃyogagato 'smi muktaḥ // Saund_18.19 //
children.translated_text: and since I am equanimous and self-possessed therein, I have reached the state of dis-junction and am liberated. (18.19)

children.text: ity evam uktvā gurubāhumānyāt sarveṇa kāyena sa gāṃ nipannaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, out of great reverence for the teacher, he prostrated on the ground with his entire body,

children.text: praverito lohitacandanākto haimo mahāstambha ivābhāse // Saund_18.20 //
children.translated_text: and anointed with red sandalwood, he appeared like a great golden pillar set in motion. (18.20)

children.text: tataḥ pramādāt prasṛtasya pūrvaṃ śrutvā dhṛtiṃ vyākaraṇaṃ ca tasya /
children.translated_text: Then, having heard the steadfastness and declaration of one who had formerly gone astray through heedlessness,

children.text: dharmānvayaṃ cānugataṃ prasādaṃ meghasvaras taṃ munir ābabhāṣe // Saund_18.21 //
children.translated_text: and [seeing] his devotion that followed the <s>dharma</s>, the sage addressed him with a voice like thunder: (18.21)

children.text: uttiṣṭha dharme sthita śiṣyajuṣṭe kiṃ pādayor me patito 'si mūrdhnā /
children.translated_text: "Rise, O you who stand firm in the <s>dharma</s> beloved by disciples — why have you fallen at my feet with your head?

children.text: abhyarcanaṃ me na tathā praṇāmo dharme yathaiṣā pratipattir eva // Saund_18.22 //
children.translated_text: Prostration is not so much a worship to me as this very practice of the <s>dharma</s> itself. (18.22)

children.text: adyāsi supravrajito jitātmann aiśvaryam apy ātmani yena labdham /
children.translated_text: Today you have truly gone forth, O conqueror of the self, by which mastery has been won even over yourself;

children.text: jitātmanaḥ pravrajanaṃ hi sādhu calātmano na tv ajitendriyasya // Saund_18.23 //
children.translated_text: for the going forth of one who has conquered the self is noble, but not so for one of unsteady self and unconquered senses. (18.23)

children.text: adyāsi śaucena pareṇa yukto vākkāyacetāṃsi śucīni yat te /
children.translated_text: Today you are endowed with supreme purity, since your speech, body, and mind are pure;

children.text: ataḥ punaś cāprayatām asaumyāṃ yat saumya no vekṣyasi garbhaśayyām // Saund_18.24 //
children.translated_text: and therefore, gentle one, you shall not again behold the unpleasant, impure bed of the womb. (18.24)

children.text: adyārthavat te śrutavac chrutaṃ tac chrutānurūpaṃ pratipadya dharmam /
children.translated_text: Today your learning is meaningful, having practiced the <s>dharma</s> in accordance with what was learned;

children.text: kṛtaśruto vipratipadyamāno nindyo hi nirvīrya ivāttaśastraḥ // Saund_18.25 //
children.translated_text: for one who is learned yet acts contrary [to his learning] is blameworthy, like a powerless one who has taken up weapons. (18.25)

children.text: aho dhṛtis te 'viṣayātmakasya yat tvaṃ matiṃ mokṣavidhāv akārṣīḥ /
children.translated_text: Ah, what fortitude in you, who are not of the nature of sense objects, that you directed your mind toward the method of liberation!

children.text: yāsyāmi niṣṭhām iti bāliśo hi janmakṣayāt trāsam ihābhyupaiti // Saund_18.26 //
children.translated_text: For a fool, [thinking] "I shall reach the end," becomes fearful of the destruction of birth in this [life]. (18.26)

children.text: diṣṭyā durāpaḥ kṣaṇasaṃnipāto nāyaṃ kṛto mohavaśena moghaḥ /
children.translated_text: Fortunately, this conjunction of the [right] moment, so hard to attain, has not been rendered fruitless through delusion;

children.text: udeti duḥkhena gato hy adhastāt kūrmo yugacchidra ivārñavasthaḥ // Saund_18.27 //
children.translated_text: for one who has gone below rises [again] with difficulty, like a turtle in the ocean [finding] the hole in a yoke. (18.27)

children.text: nirjitya māraṃ yudhi durnivāram adyāsi loke raṇaśīrṣūraḥ /
children.translated_text: Having conquered <s>Māra</s>, so hard to withstand in battle, today you are a hero on the battlefield in the world;

children.text: śūro 'py āsūraḥ sa hi veditavyo doṣair amitrair iva hanyate yaḥ // Saund_18.28 //
children.translated_text: for even a brave warrior is to be considered no hero if he is slain by the faults, which are like enemies. (18.28)

children.text: nirvāpya rāgāgnim udīrṇam adyāsi loke raṇaśīrṣaśūraḥ /
children.translated_text: Having extinguished the blazing fire of passion, today you are [truly] a hero on the battlefield in the world;

children.text: duḥkhaṃ hi śete śayane 'py udāre kleśāgninā cetasi dhayamānaḥ // Saund_18.29 //
children.translated_text: for one who is consumed in his mind by the fire of afflictions sleeps in misery even on the finest bed. (18.29)

children.text: abhyucchrito dravyamadena pūrvam adyāsi tṛṣnoparamāt samṛddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Formerly exalted through pride in possessions, today you are truly prosperous through the cessation of craving;

children.text: yāvat satarṣaḥ puruṣo hi loke tāvat samṛddho 'pi sadā daridraḥ // Saund_18.30 //
children.translated_text: for as long as a person in this world has craving, so long, even if prosperous, he is always poor. (18.30)

children.text: adyāpadeṣṭuṃ tava yuktarūpaṃ śuddhodhano me nṛpatiḥ piteti /
children.translated_text: Today it is fitting for you to declare: "The king <s>Śuddhodana</s> is my father" —

children.text: bhraṣṭasya dharmāt pitṛbhir nipātād aślāghaniyo hi kulāpadeśaḥ // Saund_18.31 //
children.translated_text: for the claim of noble lineage is not praiseworthy for one who has fallen from the <s>dharma</s> [upheld by] his ancestors. (18.31)

children.text: diṣṭyāsi śāntiṃ paramām upeto nistīrṇakāntāra ivāptasāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Fortunately, you have attained supreme peace, like one who has traversed a wilderness and reached the essence;

children.text: sarvo hi saṃsāragato bhayārto yathaiva kāntāragatas tathaiva // Saund_18.32 //
children.translated_text: for everyone in <s>saṃsāra</s>, stricken with fear, is just as if traversing a wilderness." (18.32)

children.text: āraṇyakaṃ kbhaikṣacaraṃ vinītaṃ dkraṣyāmi nandaṃ nibhṛtaṃ kadeti /
children.translated_text: 'When shall I see <s>Nanda</s>, disciplined, wandering for alms, living in the forest, restrained, and calm?' —

children.text: āsīt purastāt tvayi me didṛkṣā tathāsi diṣṭyā mama darśanīyaḥ // Saund_18.33 //
children.translated_text: such was my desire to see you before; and now, by good fortune, you are worthy of being seen. (18.33)

children.text: bhavaty arūpo 'pi hi darśanīyaḥ svalaṅkṛtaḥ śreṣṭhatamair guṇaiḥ svaiḥ /
children.translated_text: For even one who is formless becomes worthy of being seen, being well-adorned with the most excellent qualities of his own;

children.text: doṣaiḥ parīto malinīkarais tu sudarśanīyo 'pi virūpa eva // Saund_18.34 //
children.translated_text: but one beset by defiling faults is indeed misshapen, even if outwardly most handsome. (18.34)

children.text: adya prakṛṣtā tava buddhimattā kṛtsnaṃ yayā te kṛtam ātmakāryam /
children.translated_text: Today your wisdom is supreme, by which you have entirely accomplished the task of the self;

children.text: śrutonnatasyāpi hi nāsti buddhir notpadyate śreyasi yasya buddhiḥ // Saund_18.35 //
children.translated_text: for even one exalted in learning lacks true wisdom, if wisdom does not arise in him regarding what is truly beneficial. (18.35)

children.text: unmīlitasyāpi janasya madhye nimīlitasyāpi tathaiva cakṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: Among people, both the one with eyes open and the one with eyes closed have the [same physical] eye;

children.text: prajñāmayaṃ yasya hi nāsti cakṣuś cakṣur na tasyāsti sacakṣuṣo 'pi // Saund_18.36 //
children.translated_text: but for one who does not possess the eye made of wisdom, there is no [true] eye, even though he has [physical] eyes. (18.36)

children.text: duḥkhapratīkāranimittam ārtaḥ kṛṣyādibhiḥ khedam upaiti lokaḥ /
children.translated_text: Afflicted, seeking a remedy for suffering, the world undergoes hardship through farming and the like;

children.text: ajasram āgacchati tac ca bhūyo jñānena yasyādya kṛtas tvayāntaḥ // Saund_18.37 //
children.translated_text: yet that [suffering] returns again and again unceasingly — [the cycle] to which you have now put an end through knowledge. (18.37)

children.text: duḥkhaṃ na me syāt sukham eva me syād iti pravṛttaḥ stataṃ hi lokaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Let there be no suffering for me; let there be only happiness for me' — thus the world constantly strives,

children.text: na vetti tac caiva tathā yathā syāt prāptaṃ tvayādyāsulabhaṃ yatāvat // Saund_18.38 //
children.translated_text: yet it does not know that [happiness] in such a way that it might truly be [attained]; you have now attained what is so difficult to attain, in its entirety. (18.38)

children.text: ity evamādi sthirabuddhicittas tathāgatenābhihito hitāya /
children.translated_text: Thus and in other such ways addressed by the <s>Tathāgata</s> for his benefit, <s>Nanda</s>, with steady mind and intellect,

children.text: staveṣu nindāsu ca nirvyapekṣaḥ kṛtāñjalir vākyam uvāca nandaḥ // Saund_18.39 //
children.translated_text: indifferent to praise and blame alike, spoke with joined palms: (18.39)

children.text: aho viśeṣeṇa viṣeṣadarśiṃs tvayānukampā mayi darṣiteyam /
children.translated_text: 'Ah, O discriminating seer, you have shown extraordinary compassion to me,

children.text: yat kāmapaṇke bhagavan nimagnas trāto 'smi saṃsārabhayād akāmaḥ // Saund_18.40 //
children.translated_text: for, <s>Bhagavan</s>, I who was sunk in the mire of desire have been rescued, unwilling though I was, from the terror of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence). (18.40)

children.text: bhrātrā tvayā śreyasi daiśikena pitrā phalasthena tataiva mātrā /
children.translated_text: 'By you as a brother, a guide to the good, by you as a father established in the goal, and thereby as a mother —

children.text: hato 'bhaviṣyaṃ yadi na vyamokṣyaṃ sārthāt paribhraṣṭa ivākṛtārthaḥ // Saund_18.41 //
children.translated_text: I would have perished had I not been liberated, like one who has fallen from a caravan, his purpose unaccomplished. (18.41)

children.text: śāntasya tuṣṭasya sukho viveko vijñātattvasya parīkṣakasya /
children.translated_text: 'For one who is at peace, contented, who has known the truth, who is a discerning examiner,

children.text: prahīṇamānasya ca nirmadasya sukhaṃ virāgatvam asaktabuddheḥ // Saund_18.42 //
children.translated_text: who has abandoned pride and is free from intoxication — sweet is dispassion for one of unattached mind. (18.42)

children.text: ato hi tattvaṃ parigamya samyañ nirdhūya doṣān adhigamya śāntim /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, having fully understood the truth, having shaken off the faults, having attained peace,

children.text: svaṃ nāśrayaṃ saṃprati cintayāmi na taṃ janaṃ nāpsaraso na devān // Saund_18.43 //
children.translated_text: I now contemplate my own refuge — not that person [<s>Sundarī</s>], not the <s>Apsarases</s>, not the gods. (18.43)

children.text: idaṃ hi bhuktvā suci śāmikaṃ sukhaṃ na me manaḥ kāṃṣati kāmjaṃ sukham /
children.translated_text: 'For having tasted this pure, tranquil happiness, my mind does not long for the happiness born of desire,

children.text: mahārham apy annam adaivāhṛtaṃ divaukaso bhuktavataḥ sudhām iva // Saund_18.44 //
children.translated_text: just as one who has eaten the divine <s>sudhā</s> (ambrosia) would not [crave] even costly food prepared by mortals. (18.44)

children.text: aho 'ndhavijñānanimīlitaṃ jagat paṭāntare paśyati nottamaṃ sukham /
children.translated_text: 'Alas, the world, its understanding blinded by darkness, sees beyond the curtain, yet sees not the supreme happiness;

children.text: sudhīram adhyātmasukhaṃ vyapāsya hi śramaṃ tathā kāmasukhārtham ṛcchati // Saund_18.45 //
children.translated_text: for, forsaking the profound happiness of the inner self (<s>adhyātmasukha</s>), it undergoes such toil for the sake of sensual pleasure. (18.45)

children.text: yathā hi ratnākaram etya durmatir vihāya ratnāny asato maṇin haret /
children.translated_text: 'Just as a foolish person, having reached a mine of gems, would cast aside the gems and take a worthless bead,

children.text: apāsya saṃbodhisukhaṃ tahottamaṃ śramaṃ vrajet kāmasukhopaabdhaye // Saund_18.46 //
children.translated_text: so one would, discarding the supreme happiness of <s>saṃbodhi</s> (awakening), undergo toil for the attainment of sensual pleasure. (18.46)

children.text: aho hi satteṣv atimaitracetasas tathāgatasyānujighṛkṣutā parā /
children.translated_text: 'Ah, how supreme is the compassion of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, who has an exceedingly friendly mind toward beings;

children.text: apāsya yad dhyānasukhaṃ mune paraṃ parasya duḥkhoparamāya khidyase // Saund_18.47 //
children.translated_text: for, O sage, having set aside the supreme happiness of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), you undergo hardship for the cessation of others' suffering. (18.47)

children.text: mayā na śakyaṃ pratikartum adya kiṃ gurau hitaiṣiṇy anukampake tvayi /
children.translated_text: 'What can I now do in return to my teacher — you who are beneficent and compassionate —

children.text: samuddhṛto yena bhavārṇavād ahaṃ mahārṇavāc cūrṇitanaur ivormibhiḥ // Saund_18.48 //
children.translated_text: by whom I have been pulled out from the ocean of existence, like one whose ship was shattered by waves out of the great sea?' (18.48)

children.text: tato munis tasya niśamya hetumat prahīṇasarvāsravasūcakaṃ vacaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the sage, hearing his reasoned speech, indicative of the destruction of all <s>āsravas</s> (outflows),

children.text: idaṃ babhāṣe vadatām anuttamo yad arhati śrīghana eva bhāṣitum // Saund_18.49 //
children.translated_text: spoke thus — he, the supreme among speakers, [saying] what only one dense with splendor can speak: (18.49)

children.text: idaṃ kṛtārthaḥ paramārthavit kṛtī tvam eva dhīmann abhidhātum arhasi /
children.translated_text: 'It is you, O wise one — accomplished, knowing the supreme truth, one who has acted — who are worthy to declare this,

children.text: atītya kāntāram avāptasādhanaḥ sudaiśikasyeva kṛtaṃ mahāvaṇik // Saund_18.50 //
children.translated_text: like a great merchant who, having crossed the wilderness and attained his goal, [proclaims] the deed of a good guide.' (18.50)

children.text: avaiti buddhaṃ naradamyasārthiṃ kṛtī yathārhann upśāntamānasaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'A doer who, as an <s>Arhat</s>, understands the <s>Buddha</s> — the charioteer who tames men — with pacified mind, truly knows [him];

children.text: na dṛṣṭasatyo 'pi tathāvabudhyate pṛthagjanaḥ kiṃ bata buddhimān api // Saund_18.51 //
children.translated_text: but even one who has seen the truth does not so understand — how much less a common person, even if intelligent!' (18.51)

children.text: rajastamobhyāṃ parimuktacetasas tavaiva ceyaṃ sadṛsī kṛtajñatā /
children.translated_text: 'This gratitude, befitting you alone, whose mind is freed from <s>rajas</s> (passion) and <s>tamas</s> (darkness);

children.text: rajaḥprakarṣeṇa jagaty avasthite kṛtajñabhāvo hi kṛtajña durlabhaḥ // Saund_18.52 //
children.translated_text: for in a world established in the prevalence of <s>rajas</s>, the quality of gratitude, O grateful one, is rare.' (18.52)

body.text: ato 'sti bhūyas tvayi me vivakṣitaṃ nato hi bhaktaś ca niyogam arhasi // Saund_18.53 //
body.translated_text: 'Therefore there is something more I wish to say to you; for one who is bowed and devoted is worthy of a commission.' (18.53)

children.text: avāptakāryo 'si parāṃ gatiṃ gato na te 'sti kiṃ cit karaṇīyam aṇv api /
children.translated_text: 'You have accomplished your task, you have reached the highest state; there is nothing whatsoever, however small, left for you to do;

children.text: ataḥparaṃ saumya carānukampayā vimokṣayan kṛcchragatān parān api // Saund_18.54 //
children.translated_text: henceforth, gentle one, act out of compassion, liberating also others who are in distress.' (18.54)

children.text: ihārtham evārabhate naro 'dhamo vimadhyamas tūbhayalaukikīṃ kriyām /
children.translated_text: 'The lowest man undertakes action solely for this world; one below the middle undertakes action for both worlds;

children.text: kriyām amutraiva phalāya madhyamo viśiṣṭadharmā punar apravṛttaye // Saund_18.55 //
children.translated_text: the middling one undertakes action for its fruit in the next world; but one of exceptional <s>dharma</s> [acts] for the cessation of action [itself].' (18.55)

children.text: ihottamebhyo 'pi mataḥ sa tūttamo ya uttamaṃ dharmam avāpya naiṣṭhikam /
children.translated_text: 'But among even the highest, he is deemed the most excellent who, having attained the ultimate, supreme <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: acintayitvātmagataṃ pariśramaṃ śamaṃ parebhyo 'py upadeṣṭum icchati // Saund_18.56 //
children.translated_text: without considering his own exertion, wishes to teach peace to others also.' (18.56)

children.text: vihāya tasmād iha kāryam ātmanaḥ kuru sthirātman parakāryam apy atho /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, setting aside your own [completed] task here, O steadfast one, undertake now the task of others as well;

children.text: bhramatsu sattveṣu tamovṛtātmasu śrutapradīpo niśi dhāryatām ayam // Saund_18.57 //
children.translated_text: among beings who wander about, their selves enveloped in darkness, let this lamp of learning be held aloft in the night.' (18.57)

children.text: bravītu tāvat puri vismito janas tvayi sthite kurvati dharmadeśanāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Let the astonished people in the city say, when you stand there delivering <s>dharma</s> teachings:'

children.text: aho batāścaryam idaṃ vimuktaye karoti rāgī yad ayam kathām iti // Saund_18.58 //
children.translated_text: 'Oh, how wonderful! This man of passion gives a discourse on liberation!' (18.58)

children.text: dhruvaṃ hi saṃśrutya tava sthiraṃ mano nivṛttanānāviṣayair manorathaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For surely, hearing of your steadfast mind, with its fantasies turned away from the various sense objects,

children.text: vadhūr gṛhe sāpi tavānukurvatī kariṣyate strīṣu virāgiṇīḥ kathāḥ // Saund_18.59 //
children.translated_text: your wife at home too, emulating you, will give discourses on dispassion among women.' (18.59)

children.text: tvayi paramadhṛtau niviṣṭatattve bhavanagatā na hi raṃsyate dhruvaṃ sā /
children.translated_text: 'When you are established in truth, of supreme resolve, she at home will surely find no delight,

children.text: manasi śamadamātmaike vivikte matir iva kāmasukhaiḥ parīkṣakasya // Saund_18.60 //
children.translated_text: like the mind of an examiner [that finds no delight] in sensual pleasures, when the mind is solitary, devoted to tranquility and self-control.' (18.60)

children.text: ity arhataḥ paramakāruṇikasya śāstur mūrdhnā vacaś ca caraṇau ca samaṃ gṛhītvā /
children.translated_text: Thus, having received the words and the feet of the <s>Arhat</s>, the supremely compassionate teacher, upon his head,

children.text: svasthaḥ praśāntahṛdayo vinivṛttakāryaḥ pārśvān muneḥ pratiyayau vimadaḥ karīva // Saund_18.61 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s>, at ease, with pacified heart, his task accomplished, departed from the sage's side — like an elephant freed from rut. (18.61)

children.text: bhikṣarthaṃ samaye viveśa sa puraṃ dṛṣṭīr janasyākṣipan lābhālābhasukhāsukhādiṣu samaḥ svasthendriyo niḥspṛhaḥ /
children.translated_text: At the proper time, he entered the city for alms, captivating the gaze of the people; equal in gain and loss, happiness and unhappiness, with senses composed and free from craving,

children.text: nirmokṣāya cakāra tatra ca kathāṃ kāle janāyārthine naivonmārgagatān parān paribhavan nātmānam utkarṣayan // Saund_18.62 //
children.translated_text: he gave discourses there at the right time to people who sought [them], for the sake of liberation — neither disdaining others who had gone astray, nor exalting himself. (18.62)

children.text: ity eṣā vyupaśāntaye na rataye mokṣārthagarbhā kṛtiḥ śrotṝṇāṃ grahaṇārtham anyamanasāṃ kāvyopacārāt kṛtā /
children.translated_text: Thus this work, pregnant with the purpose of liberation, has been composed for the sake of tranquility and not for entertainment, employing the devices of poetry for the comprehension of listeners whose minds are elsewhere;

children.text: yan mokṣāt kṛtam anyad atra hi mayā tat kāvyadharmāt kṛtaṃ pātuṃ tiktam ivauṣadhaṃ madhuyutaṃ hṛdyaṃ kathaṃ syād iti // Saund_18.63 //
children.translated_text: whatever has been done herein by me other than for liberation has been done for the sake of poetic convention — [wondering] how bitter medicine mixed with honey might become agreeable. (18.63)

children.text: prāyeṇālokya lokaṃ viṣayaratiparaṃ mo kṣāt pratihataṃ kāvyavājena tattvaṃ kathitam iha mayā mokṣaḥ param iti /
children.translated_text: Observing that the world, for the most part devoted to the pleasure of sense objects, is repelled by liberation, I have here told the truth by the device of poetry — that liberation is the supreme [goal];

children.text: tad buddhvā śāmikaṃ yat tad avahitam ito grāhyaṃ na lalitaṃ pāṃsubhyo dhātujebhyo niyatam upakaraṃ cāmīkaram iti // Saund_18.64 //
children.translated_text: therefore, having understood this, what is peaceful therein should be grasped with attention, and not the ornamental — just as gold is certainly a beneficial extract from mineral-bearing dust. (18.64)

body.translated_text: Thus ends the eighteenth canto, entitled 'The Pronouncement of Authority,' in the <s>Saundarananda</s> <s>mahākāvya</s>.

body.text: āryasuvarṇākṣīputrasya sāketakasya bhikṣor ācāryabhadantāśvaghoṣasya mahākaver mahāvādinaḥ kṛtir iyam //
body.translated_text: This is the work of the noble <s>Aśvaghoṣa</s>, son of <s>Suvarṇākṣī</s>, of <s>Sāketa</s>, a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk), a revered master, a great poet and great debater.
